_doc: Provinces v2 (branch provinces-v2, 2026-11-23 night; proposal): each province's land, places (existing and new, design/world/provinces-v2/), lore and start record, from tools/design/map/province_stats_v2.py with the Provinces GDD formulas F1-F6. Production in the dump's per-class units for seed 7; population in settlement-weight units (w_size x livability); development = built levels + population units (a display index, not in the GDD). Each province also carries land_qi (mean tile base element shares) and variant_max (strongest tile per variant, 0-100 scale), and top-level land_element_means (Provinces rule 3a).

provinces.name: Băng Tâm
provinces.lore: Red badlands, dry steppe and the first snow mountains meet around Cựu Các, the Desert Pavilion, the old seat of Băng Tâm Các. Herders, well-diggers and the sect's own servants live here, and the land yields little but stone, wool and qi. Disciples at the pavilion drink only its ice-cold well water, and Ôn Sa Ngọc keeps the pavilion's trade and its desert recruits.

places.name: Cựu Các
places.look: Out of red badlands at the desert's edge rises a tall white pavilion of stacked celadon-glazed roofs, pale stone terraces climbing to it. Even at midsummer frost rims its eaves, and a thin cold mist spills from the round well-house at its foot, where the water keeps ice all year. Far beyond, the snow ranges of Ngọc Hồ Sơn stand white against the sky.

places.name: Tẩy Kiếm Tuyền
places.look: A cold spring wells up in a rock basin on the mountainside, its stone rim cut with long grooves where blades have been laid.
places.lore: A Metal vein rises here with the water. Băng Tâm's sword cultivators wash a new sword in it before they first draw it in earnest.

provinces.name: Bình Thủy
provinces.lore: A low green headland of grass and bamboo over the strait, the island's door to the mainland. Its people are ferry hands, rope-makers and innkeepers, many of them born somewhere else, and they live by Bình Thủy Môn's crossing. On the headland stands the Strangers' Hall, the sect's old seat, where newcomers sleep their first night, and every dusk the green lanterns on its mast are lit, so that a homesick traveller can read the name of his own village among them.

places.name: Khách Tương Đường
places.look: A low green headland over the strait carries halls rising in grey-tile tiers to one high hall, now a hostel for travellers. On the point stands a tall mast hung with green lanterns, lit every dusk, and below it the ferries come and go from the quay.

places.name: Tha Hương Tuyền
places.look: A round warm pool in the grass behind the headland, rimmed with flat stones worn smooth by bathers and ringed by small wooden name boards.
places.lore: New disciples of Bình Thủy Môn bathe here on their first night and nail the name of their home village to a board beside the pool. It is said the water tastes faintly of whatever home the bather left.

provinces.name: Củng Tinh
provinces.lore: Open high plain more than a thousand metres up, cut by a river and dotted with mountain lakes. Herders and a few barley farmers live around the abbey of Củng Tinh Quán, which keeps the star-iron mine at Vẫn Tinh. On still nights the star-readers watch Tinh Lạc Hồ, and the herders keep their fires low so as not to spoil the water's stars.

places.name: Củng Tinh Quán
places.look: On a high open shoulder of the plain, beside a round mountain lake, stands a quiet abbey (quán) of low walls and dark tile. In the middle of its main court, on a raised stone platform open to the sky, turns a great bronze armillary of nested rings, green with age, that follows the Northern Dipper through the year.

places.name: Vẫn Tinh Khoáng
places.look: On the high plain, a shallow round crater lined with dark, rust-streaked rock holds a timber headframe and winch over the deepest shaft at its centre. Small stone cairns mark the crater rim.

places.name: Phong Văn Hồ
places.look: A small, shallow lake on the high plain just west of Tinh Lạc Hồ, its surface always wrinkled by the wind.
places.lore: Unlike its neighbour it holds no stars, for the wind never lets it lie still. Củng Tinh's novices are sent to watch it first, to learn what a broken reflection looks like.

provinces.name: Cửu Cao
provinces.lore: Reed marsh and wet woodland along a slow river, with a little steppe and one bare spur of mountain at the edge. Its people cut reed, net marsh fish and keep the roosts of Cửu Cao Phái, whose cranes are the only sky traffic here. Since 874 the crane riders have also held the holdings the Pivot took from Phá Quân Môn, and the marsh villages pay their dues in reed and fish to the sect rather than to the Pivot's clerks.

places.name: Cửu Cao Phái
places.look: Out of a reed marsh rise slender red-lacquered crane-roost towers, each topped with a broad platform of woven reed where the great birds stand and preen. Behind them, terraced halls climb a low wooded rise to a four-roof pagoda. The cry of cranes overhead never quite stops.

places.name: Hạc Tê Lâm
places.look: Tall pines on a low rise above the marsh, their crowns flattened and white with droppings where cranes stand at dusk.
places.lore: Young cranes of Cửu Cao Phái roost here before they are trusted on the towers. The riders forbid felling any tree a crane has stood on.

provinces.name: Dạ Quang
provinces.lore: Steppe, sand and salt pans run to the coast around the red-earth fort of Dạ Quang Môn. Its riders and horse-breeders guard the caravans they once robbed, and the land yields horses, salt and the pale stone of the night-glowing cups. The broken fortress of Cô Thành stands on its salt pan, a reminder of the Desert Road War.

places.name: Dạ Quang Môn
places.look: A squat fort of rammed red earth sits on the open steppe, ringed by horse lines and sabre racks. Over its gate, on a pillar, stands a great stone cup carved from a pale stone that glows faint green after dusk. Around it the steppe is trampled bare by hooves.

places.name: Cô Thành
places.look: On a white salt pan that was once a desert lake stands a square fortress, its walls glazed black and cracked by fire. One corner tower still rises to its full height; the rest have slumped. Salt crust creeps up the foot of the walls like frost.

places.name: Xích Sa Mạch
places.look: A patch of red sand in the desert that stays hot after sunset, shimmering faintly in the dark.
places.lore: A Fire vein lies under the red sand. Dạ Quang's riders temper their blood sabres here, and Băng Tâm lets them.

provinces.name: Hàm Nguyệt
provinces.lore: Birch and pine shore along the western end of Hạo Nguyệt Hồ, where the long lake is calmest. Its people fish, tend pearl beds and cut birch for Hàm Nguyệt Trang, which rules the shore for Tùng Đào Cung. The sect's moon halls stand on piles over the still pool of Trầm Bích Đàm, while its Shore House on the lake keeps the pearl houses and the boats. Pearls and spirit fish are its wealth, and every fisher here knows the old saying that the moon in the lake is easier to catch than the one in the sky.

places.name: Ngạn Đường
places.look: A low manor of dark timber and grey tile stands among birches on the lake shore, its slim piers reaching out over still water. Just off the piers a perfect ring of white stones breaks the surface, enclosing a circle of water so calm it holds the moon whole; the manor calls it the Moon Net.

places.name: Hàm Nguyệt Trang
places.look: Dark timber halls under grey tile stand on tall piles over the middle of a round, still pool behind a bar, joined by long covered walkways, and birches ring the shore. The water is so calm that every roof and the full moon lie in it twice.
places.lore: Hàm Nguyệt Trang is a small water-arts sect (tông môn) sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, living on spirit fish (linh ngư) and lake pearls. Its founder Đới Thiềm Quang raised the moon halls on piles over Trầm Bích Đàm in 412, because the moon lies stillest here, and sank the Sunken Disc under them to hold the moonlit qi. Its mistress Kiều Nguyệt Châu has led it since 1150 and doubled the pearl harvest. The sect keeps its boats and its pearl trade at the Shore House on the lake.

places.name: Cựu Châu Trấn
places.look: Low stone footings and the stumps of pier posts on a bare shore, half buried in sand and birch saplings, with heaps of old mussel shells grown over by moss.
places.lore: Pearl farmers built this town soon after the great pearl of 470 was found. When the lake froze to its bed in 748, the town's pearl beds died, and by the next year its people had moved to Hàm Nguyệt Trang's shore.

provinces.name: Hồng Đậu
provinces.lore: Coastal rain forest and open grass at the western edge of Tiêu Vũ Lâm, where the forest road comes down to the sea at Nhã Môn, the gracious door of Hồng Đậu Trang. Its people gather rattan, honey and resin and fish the shallows, and many serve the manor as gardeners and porters without asking what grows in the back garden over the vein of Tiêu Âm Mạch, where the mistress has kept her rooms since 1110. Vines of red beans run wild along every path, and children are taught early not to put them in their mouths.

places.name: Nhã Môn
places.look: Where the rain forest meets the sea, a walled manor of red-lacquered halls rises in three terraces, half buried in glossy leaves. Its entrance is a perfect round moon gate of red lacquer, so thickly wreathed in vines of scarlet, black-eyed beans that the lacquer barely shows. A path of crushed shell leads to it from the forest road.

places.name: Lan Tân Trấn
places.look: On a wooded stretch of shore, house footings and a fallen harbour wall lie under creepers, with orchids rooted in the cracks of the old landing steps.
places.lore: Lan Tân was a small port that shipped orchids and resin from the forest until Thôn Hải's raiders burned it in 779. No one came back after the Pirate Purge, and Hồng Đậu Trang later carried off the dressed stone of its walls for its own terraces.

places.name: Hồng Đậu Trang
places.look: Under a ring of old wild banana plants, red-bean trellises climb over faintly warm green ground, and a low house of black wood stands among them, where gardeners in grey bend over the beds. The rain falls softer here.
places.lore: Hồng Đậu Trang is a minor ma đạo sect under Thính Vũ Lâu, a house of poisons and charms. Its mistress Nghê Hồng Đậu has kept her own rooms and her canon here since 1110, in the banana shade over a spirit vein (linh mạch) of Wood (Mộc) qi, where the red beans grow on trellises first planted in 912 and rewoven as the Red Trellis array. Only a cart track from the manor on the forest road reaches it, and visitors who sit too long in the shade wake with a headache and no memory of the hour. Those who stay too long at the manor are said to end up tending the beans.

provinces.name: Hồng Lô
provinces.lore: A steep coast of snow, black rock and smoking volcanic slopes around the valley of Hồng Lô Cốc. Few mortals live here beyond the valley's servants and ash-gatherers; the land yields sulphur-yellow ores, hot water and furnace heat. The alchemists still sail out to the volcanic isles whenever they smoke, as they did in 1185.

places.name: Hồng Lô Cốc
places.look: A steep coastal valley of snow and black rock opens onto a grey sea, its terraces climbing to a squat red-brick furnace tower. Snow never settles in a wide ring around the tower; the bare dark ground there steams, and the stack glows at night like a coal.

places.name: Hồ Tâm Thang
places.gloss: Hot Water at the Lake's Heart
places.look: A small rocky islet sits in the middle of a cold mountain lake. Its hot springs have built a staircase of white and rust-orange mineral terraces down to the water, each step a steaming pool.

places.name: Kê Quan Khoáng
places.look: Orange-red crusts of realgar coat a steaming volcanic crater wall, cut into ledges where miners chip the ore into baskets.
places.lore: Hồng Lô Cốc works the mine for realgar, the red cockscomb stone, which its alchemists use to drive poison from pills. Miners wear wet cloth over their faces, and a fresh hand who forgets it does not forget twice.

provinces.name: Lạc Hà
provinces.lore: A low swell of steppe and grass along the river, crowned by the ochre terraces and rose-tiled halls of Cựu Hà Viện, the Old Glow Court, Lạc Hà Tông's old seat and now its outer gate. Its people serve the sect as farmers, boatmen and servants, and every evening the whole land turns to watch the sun go down through the Sunset Ring. An Earth vein under the steppe near the court is said to be strongest in the hour of the evening glow.

places.name: Cựu Hà Viện
places.look: The road climbs a low swell of steppe to a sect (tông môn) of long ochre earth terraces and rose-tiled halls, every one of them turned to the west. On the westernmost terrace stands the Sunset Ring, a great round stone gate with no doors and no wall, through which the whole sect watches the sun go down each evening. Below, the river shoals of Hạc Đinh Thị shine in the low light.

places.name: Tề Phi Mạch
places.look: A low rise of steppe below the seat where, at dusk, the sunset clouds and the wild ducks seem to fly together overhead.
places.lore: An Earth vein runs under the rise, named for the line in which the sunset clouds fly with the lone wild duck. Lạc Hà's inner disciples cultivate here at evening, and it is strongest in the hour of the glow.

provinces.name: Lãng Đào
provinces.lore: Low wooded ground at the river mouth around the gate of hulls of Lãng Đào Môn. Its people are ferrymen, rope-tarrers and boat-builders who carry the river trade for Tùng Đào. On the shore stand the wrecked piers of Phá Chu Trấn, whose feuding boatmen were the reason the ferrymen banded together in 790.

places.name: Lãng Đào Môn
places.look: On low wooded ground just back from the river stands a sect gate made of two great river-boat hulls, upturned and set on end so their keels meet overhead in a pointed arch. Behind it, tarred timber halls and rope sheds climb a gentle rise, and a path of crushed shell runs down toward the landing at Đào Sa Thị. The whole place smells of pitch and wet hemp.

places.name: Phá Chu Trấn
places.look: On the shore, rotted piers and the hulls of boats lie broken in the sand, among the stone footings of a small town.
places.lore: The boatmen's town where the families of the river fought over landings. In 786 a feud ended with half the town burned, and the survivors were among those who banded together as Lãng Đào Môn four years later.

places.name: Tẩy Sa Tuyền
places.look: A clear spring bubbles up through white sand in the woods behind the gate of hulls, its pool ringed with oar blades driven into the ground.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring. Lãng Đào's disciples wash their oars in it before a voyage and plant an old oar beside it when they retire.

provinces.name: Lê Hoa
provinces.lore: Ice fields and the highest rock on the continent rise straight from a cold shore here, with a strip of rimed forest at their foot. The nuns of Lê Hoa Am are nearly the only people: the white nuns keep the Upper Hermitage on a shelf of the glacier of Lăng Tuyệt Phong, and the grey sisters hold the Gate Hermitage in the rimed pear orchard below. They live on the cold jade they cut high on the mountain and on the gifts of the villages below. Băng Tâm disciples pass through on their way to climb Lăng Tuyệt Phong before a long seclusion, and since Chúc Long Sơn rumbled in 1199 the hermitage has watched the north.

places.name: Môn Am
places.look: A small hermitage of white-plastered halls climbs a steep slope beside the ice fields, inside an orchard of old pear trees whose branches are white with rime most of the year. From below, the rimed orchard looks like a hillside in full blossom even in deep winter. A single three-roof bell pagoda stands above the trees.

places.name: Lê Hoa Am
places.look: The highest summit on the continent, a white glacier pyramid standing clear above a sea of cloud, with a cairn of pale stones on its very top. On a shelf of rock and ice on its flank a small hermitage of white-plastered halls hangs a bronze bell, ringed by frost-white stones.

places.name: Hàn Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A narrow adit cut into a glacier-polished wall far above the clouds, its mouth hung with prayer strips stiff with frost.
places.lore: The nuns of Lê Hoa Am cut cold jade (hàn ngọc) here, a stone that stays cold in the hand. Only nuns may enter, and they work in silence.

provinces.name: Lễ Tuyền
provinces.lore: Low grassland by the shore of Triêu Hà Hồ and the gulf, where the brewers of Lễ Tuyền Phái keep the Spring House. Its people farm rice, tend the school's herb beds and carry its wine jars to the boats. Envoys of the Pivot come each year for the wine, and a warm spring nearby is where they are made to wait.

places.name: Tuyền Phòng
places.look: A low rise on the open grassland by the shore of Triêu Hà Hồ carries a short stack of pale timber halls and a three-roofed pagoda. Below the pagoda a round basin of white stone brims with spring water under one enormous wutong (ngô đồng) tree, its broad leaves always beaded wet. Stoneware jars sealed with red clay stand in rows on the lowest terrace, warming in the sun.

places.name: Cam Lộ Thang
places.look: A warm spring in the grass near the lake, edged with white stone and shaded by a small roofed pavilion.
places.lore: Lễ Tuyền Phái bathes its fever patients here before they drink the wine. The Pivot's envoys are given the pavilion while the jars are sealed.

provinces.name: Mục Vân
provinces.lore: A small stretch of coastal grass and steppe around the racing track of Mục Vân Trang. Its people are grooms, riders and herders of the manor's spirit horses. An Earth vein under the pasture is said to be why the manor's foals run faster than any on the plain.

places.name: Mục Vân Trang
places.look: A manor seat on a low rise near the coast of the open plain, its halls climbing in tiers to a tall stable tower under a sweeping grey roof. Around the foot of the rise runs a great oval racing track of packed earth, and on it pale spirit horses (linh mã) move like clouds.

places.name: Trì Vân Mạch
places.look: A low swell of pasture where the grass grows thick and silver-green and the spirit foals of Mục Vân graze in their first year.
places.lore: An Earth vein runs under the pasture, and the manor says a foal raised on it never tires. Khấu Mục Vân lets only his own riders cultivate here, at dawn, among the horses.

provinces.name: Nam Phố
provinces.lore: Old forest on the river mouth shore around the cloud-painted hall of Nam Phố Đường. Its people are scribes, paper makers and ink grinders. Golden pheasants nest in the meadow by the hall, and the scribes buy their tail feathers for fine brushes.

places.name: Nam Phố Đường
places.look: Under old forest near the southern shore stands one long hall whose beams and rafters are painted, end to end, with drifting clouds, so that through the open doors the roof seems to float. Lines of yellow paper hang drying between the trunks, and the smell of cinnabar ink and pine soot carries far down the road.

places.name: Cẩm Kê Nguyên
places.look: A grassy meadow by the hall where red and gold pheasants strut among the paper-drying lines.
places.lore: Spirit golden pheasants nest here, and their spurs can open a man's leg. The scribes of Nam Phố Đường buy their moulted tail feathers for fine brushes and leave the birds alone.

provinces.name: Hòa Thử
provinces.lore: Coastal fields of millet climb from the sea into forested hills and a few bare heights. Its farmers keep the stilted granaries that fed Yên Ba Thành through the winter of 860, and still sell to the city first. The hill above the fields is Thúy Vi's, and its disciples climb it to sit among the trees.

places.name: Hòa Thử Thôn
places.look: Low farmhouses sit among millet and grain fields on the coast. Beside them stand rows of small granary huts raised on mushroom-shaped stone stilts, keeping the grain clear of damp and rats.

places.name: Thúy Bình Phong
places.look: A forested hill with a long flat face of trees stands behind the millet fields like a green screen.
places.lore: Wood qi gathers in the trees on its face, and Thúy Vi disciples sit there to cultivate. The farmers of Hòa Thử say it shelters their fields from the north wind.

provinces.name: Ẩn Loan
provinces.lore: Open grassland and woods end in cliffs over a narrow hidden cove. The few households live by goats, fishing and saying little to strangers, as they have since the pirates left in 781. A small spirit vein in the grass draws Thúy Vi's herb-gatherers each spring.

places.name: Ẩn Loan Thôn
places.look: A few houses cling above a narrow cove hidden between cliffs, out of sight from the open sea. A steep stair cut into the rock leads down from the village to the mouth of a sea cave at the water's edge.

places.name: Phương Phỉ Nhãn
places.look: A round hollow in the grassland stays green and flowering long after the grass around it has turned brown.
places.lore: A small wood vein rises in the hollow, and herbs grow there twice as fast as anywhere on the cape. Thúy Vi's gatherers pick it each spring and leave the roots.

provinces.name: Ô Đề
provinces.lore: A long stretch of coastal forest with a few limestone knolls and marshy hollows, under the crow ridge of Ô Đề Thôn. Its people fish, cut oak and feed the crows at the new year. Inland lie the walls of a town whose wells turned salt after the earthquake of 1033.

places.name: Ô Đề Thôn
places.look: A small fishing village of grey roofs lies on the shore under a long ridge. On the ridge top a single huge bare oak stands black against the sky, its branches crowded with roosting crows.

places.name: Lão Tượng Lâm
places.look: Broad old oaks grow down to the shore below the crow ridge, their branches black with roosting birds at dusk.
places.lore: The crows of Ô Đề roost here when the great oak is full. Villagers cut oak for boats only where no crows sit.

places.name: Song Tỉnh Trấn
places.look: Empty stone houses stand around two well-heads in an overgrown square, a crack running across the ground between them.
places.lore: The town grew up around two sweet wells on the coast road. The earthquake of 1033 split the ground and turned both wells salt, and the town was empty within a year.

provinces.name: Lâm Tuyền
provinces.lore: Wooded coastal slopes above the bamboo pipe line of Lâm Tuyền Thôn. Its villagers fish and keep the spring that cured the coughing sickness of 760. The woods above ring with cicadas all summer.

places.name: Lâm Tuyền Thôn
places.look: A coastal village of grey roofs lies under wooded slopes, with a long line of split bamboo pipes running down from the woods on wooden trestles. The pipes end in a row of stone troughs in the village square, always running.

places.name: Thiền Minh Lâm
places.look: A sunny wooded slope above the pipe line, loud with cicadas all summer.
places.lore: The spring of Lâm Tuyền rises under these trees. Villagers say that if the cicadas fall silent at noon, someone is fouling the water.

provinces.name: Thu Diệp
provinces.lore: Steep mountain, limestone and maple forest falling to the sea around Thu Diệp Thôn. The village lives by fishing and by the red leaves it sells as bookmarks in Lam Yên Thị. A summit of red maples above it is the source of the best leaves.

places.name: Thu Diệp Thôn
places.look: A small village of grey roofs by the shore stands in front of a grove of maples that burns crimson every autumn. Wooden frames of pressed leaves dry in rows along the house walls.

places.name: Hồng Phong Đỉnh
places.look: A steep summit of limestone and maple turns crimson from crown to foot each autumn.
places.lore: Wood qi gathers in its maples, and the leaves from its top are the ones scholars pay most for. Only mortals of Thu Diệp may pick them.

provinces.name: Bạch Hoa
provinces.lore: Coastal forest climbing from the sea into steep hills, its lower slopes a pied grove of white birch and black stumps left by the fire of 548. Its people strip birch bark for writing sheets and boxes and fish the coast. The fire's dead town, Hỏa Tẫn Trấn, still stands burned on the shore.

places.name: Bạch Hoa Thôn
places.look: A small coastal village of grey roofs stands in a bright grove of white birches. Among the pale trunks the black stumps of old burned trees still stand, so the grove is pied black and white.

places.name: Ngân Hồ Cương
places.look: A birch-crowned knoll riddled with fox earths, silver-grey fur caught on the brambles around every hole.
places.lore: Silver foxes den here, clever enough to rob the bark-strippers' lunches. Villagers say a fox that steals from you brings luck if you let it go.

places.name: Hỏa Tẫn Trấn
places.look: On the coast, charred posts and blackened stone hearths stand among young birches, the ground still dark with old ash.
places.lore: A timber town that burned with the forest in the great fire of 548. Its survivors moved inland, and the birches that grew over the burn gave Bạch Hoa its name.

provinces.name: Thanh Tùng
provinces.lore: River forest in the hills west of the palace, around the memorial pines of Thanh Tùng Thôn. Its people are woodsmen and river folk, many of them children of Hổ Khiếu's survivors. They neither cut nor tap the old pines of the forest above the village.

places.name: Thanh Tùng Thôn
places.look: A river village of grey roofs sits beside a grove of tall pines planted in neat rows, each with a small flat stone at its foot. The rows run from the riverbank to the forest edge like ranks of soldiers.

places.name: Cổ Cái Lâm
places.look: Old pines with vast flat crowns that touch overhead, leaving the forest floor dim and soft with needles.
places.lore: These are the oldest pines near Thanh Tùng, and the villagers neither cut nor tap them. The survivors of Hổ Khiếu say their dead walk here.

provinces.name: Tùng Phong
provinces.lore: High river forest in the south of the pine sea, where Vạn Hác Viện's students practise among the villagers. Its people are woodsmen, hunters and zither-string twisters. Striped tigers hold the ridge above, and the wind strings warn the hamlet when the wind turns toward it.

places.name: Tùng Phong Thôn
places.look: A small river village of grey roofs lies in the pines. Between two great pines at its edge long strings are stretched, and they hum and moan whenever the wind blows, a sound that carries over the whole hamlet.

places.name: Ban Hổ Lĩnh
places.look: A pine ridge above Tùng Phong, its bark clawed at head height and its paths marked with great striped hairs.
places.lore: Tigers hold the ridge, and when the wind turns toward the hamlet the wind strings hum a warning. Vạn Hác's students say a well-played zither keeps them away.

provinces.name: Tuyết Ốc
provinces.lore: River forest on the upper river, where the snow lies so deep that the houses of Tuyết Ốc Thôn are built half under it. Its people trap, fish and dig snow tunnels door to door all winter. Behind the village lies a forest where the drifts are deeper than a man is tall.

places.name: Tuyết Ốc Thôn
places.look: In winter the village almost vanishes: low turf-roofed houses sunk half into the ground, chimneys smoking through the drifts. Each house is marked by a tall red-painted door-pole so neighbours can find each other under the snow. In summer the poles stand oddly tall over a cluster of grassy mounds by the upper river.

places.name: Thâm Tuyết Lâm
places.look: A fir forest where the snow lies deeper than a man is tall all winter, only the treetops showing above the drifts.
places.lore: The villagers of Tuyết Ốc tunnel into it for firewood. Hunters say bears and stranger beasts sleep under the snow here until the thaw.

provinces.name: Hàn Mai
provinces.lore: Wide river forest around Hàn Mai Thôn and its plum. Its people farm the river flats, fish and gather wild plums from the woods. Above the village stands the Plum Gate, the old seat and outer gate of Ngạo Tuyết Phái, founded in 1105; the school's sword hall moved to Thạch Khẩu Trấn in 1162, and every winter its outer disciples come down to train barefoot under the plums.

places.name: Hàn Mai Thôn
places.look: A handful of grey-tile houses sits around a small snowy square, and in the middle of the square grows one gnarled winter plum behind a low bamboo fence. In the cold months its red blossoms are the only colour for days of travel. Villagers bow to it on their way down to the river.

places.name: Dã Mai Lâm
places.look: A wood of wild plum trees on the slope above the village, their red blossoms opening through the snow.
places.lore: The villagers of Hàn Mai say the plums grew from the seeds of their own tree. The swordsmen of Ngạo Tuyết Phái train among them in the blossom season.

places.name: Mai Môn
places.look: A plain grey plank gate under a small tiled roof stands at the end of a garden of about two hundred old plum trees, with a few low grey-tiled buildings and a stone yard before it. In the first winter a line of children waits in the snow under the red blossom to have their roots read.
places.lore: Mai Môn, the Plum Gate, is the old seat of Ngạo Tuyết Phái, a small school of sword cultivators sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, and is now its outer gate. Every child's root is read here in the first winter, and the founder turns away anyone without Metal; Mạc Chiết Chi keeps the gate and the school's graves. Every winter the outer disciples come down to it and train barefoot under the plums. A swordsman who learned his art watching the plum bloom through the snow founded the school here in 1105, and its plum-blossom sword forms are quick and light.

provinces.name: Bạch Lang
provinces.lore: River forest around the old den of the white wolf king that Thôi Khinh Hồng slew. Its people hunt, fish and lime the den's boulders white each spring. Grey wolves still prowl a knoll nearby, and the village watches them closely.

places.name: Bạch Lang Thôn
places.look: The village circles a hollow at its heart, ringed with white-limed boulders: the old den of the white wolf king. Children run between the houses with wolf-tooth charms clicking at their necks. A path from the hollow leads down to the river, where women beat laundry on flat stones.

places.name: Lang Hồi Cương
places.look: A forested knoll above the river, its moss cut by wolf trails and its foot littered with gnawed deer bones.
places.lore: Grey wolves have come back to this knoll in the centuries since the white wolf king fell. The villagers of Bạch Lang say the year they leave the den's boulders grey, the wolves will come down.

provinces.name: Ba Quang
provinces.lore: A strip of forest coast and small stepped lakes below the ridges. Its people fish the lakes and the shore and ferry Cửu Cao's riders over the water. The ruins of an older port lie on the coast to the east, a reminder of why Ba Quang builds well back from the tide line.

places.name: Ba Quang Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the shore of a chain of small mountain lakes stepping down a grassy slope, its boats drawn up on the gravel. At midday the lakes throw so much light that the village seems to stand in a blaze. Flat reed rafts lie on the beach, ready for the evening nets.

places.name: Kiêu Minh Lâm
places.look: A dim stand of old oaks between the lakes, hung with owl pellets and silent by day.
places.lore: Spirit owls with wings as wide as a boat hunt here at night and take lambs and dogs. Ba Quang's fishermen will not row past it after dark.

places.name: Cựu Tân Trấn
places.look: Stone footings and a broken quay on the shore, half buried in sand and shingle, with sea grass growing in the old streets.
places.lore: A small port that ferried goods along the coast from 420. In 968 a storm tide drove over the quay and took half the town; the rest moved inland to the lakes of Ba Quang.

provinces.name: Hạc Quy
provinces.lore: Gentle forested river country with marsh meadows where the cranes come down each year. Villagers farm millet and beans and keep the landing pool clear for the birds. A small Wood vein lies in the woods west of the village, and the crane riders rest their mounts on it after long flights.

places.name: Hạc Quy Thôn
places.look: A quiet marsh-edge village of reed-thatched and grey-tile houses on a slow river. In the meadow beyond, the villagers keep a crescent-shaped landing pool dug in the turf and edged with flat grey stepping stones, where the cranes come down each year. They clear its weed by hand all summer.

places.name: Hạc Tức Mạch
places.look: A hollow in the woods where the pines grow twice as thick as their neighbours and the moss is bright green even in winter.
places.lore: A small vein (linh mạch) whose qi (linh khí) runs to Wood. Cửu Cao's riders rest tired cranes here, and the birds sleep a whole day after.

provinces.name: Lộc Uyển
provinces.lore: High meadows and open forest where the steppe begins, under Thiên Xu's old ban on hunting. Its people keep goats, gather shed antlers and cut hay. On a wooded rise stand the empty halls of Bạch Lộc Quán, the little abbey that first asked the Pivot to protect the deer.

places.name: Lộc Uyển Thôn
places.look: A hillside village of log houses above a high meadow where deer gather each spring. At the meadow's edge stands a black stone stele carrying Thiên Xu's ban on hunting, and shed antlers are heaped around its foot. A rail fence keeps the village goats off the deer's grass.

places.name: Lão Du Lâm
places.look: A line of old elms along the edge of the steppe, bent away from the wind, with deer trails worn through the grass beneath.
places.lore: The elms shelter Lộc Uyển's deer from the steppe wind in early spring. Villagers gather the elm seed in famine years and grind it into cakes.

places.name: Bạch Lộc Quán
places.look: Low moss-grown halls on a wooded rise, their roofs fallen in, with a stone deer standing headless in the court.
places.lore: Hermits who fed the wild deer founded this small abbey in 370 and asked the Pivot to ban hunting in the meadow, which it did in 380. Its last master died in 612 without a disciple, and the halls were left to the deer.

provinces.name: Đỗ Quyên
provinces.lore: Low forest and reed swamp run down to a grey shore of black shingle. The people fish and cut timber and leave the red azalea slopes untouched, because they hold the flowers to be the dead of the old eruption. Băng Tâm takes its tax here in dried fish and fir planks.

places.name: Đỗ Quyên Thôn
places.look: A fishing village sits on a grey shore under steep slopes that turn blood-red with azaleas each spring. Its low houses are roofed with dark stone slabs against the wind, and its boats lie hauled up on black volcanic shingle. In bloom the slope looks like a fire about to come down on the roofs.

places.name: Hàn Sam Lâm
places.look: Dark firs stand close on low ground behind the shore, their roots in black volcanic grit.
places.lore: The woodcutters of Đỗ Quyên cut their planks here and leave the azalea slopes alone. Old trees still carry scorch marks from the eruption.

provinces.name: Hoàng Oanh
provinces.lore: A sheltered coastal valley of willow and fir, warmer than the land around it, where orioles spend the winter. Its people fish and weave the straw bird shelters, and they sell willow baskets up and down the coast. Nuns of Lê Hoa Am come down in the cold months only to hear the birds.

places.name: Hoàng Oanh Thôn
places.look: In a sheltered coastal valley, a ring of grey-tile houses stands among bare willows hung with woven straw bird shelters. All winter the shelters flash yellow with orioles, and their song carries down to the boats. Snow lies on the ridges all around.

places.name: Dã Liễu Lâm
places.look: A tangle of grey willows and firs fills the valley floor, bare branches hung with straw bird shelters.
places.lore: The orioles of Hoàng Oanh roost here in winter. The village cuts willow for baskets only in spring, after the birds have gone.

provinces.name: Ngư Đàm
provinces.lore: Dry steppe around an oasis of fish ponds beside a barren salt sea. Its people raise carp and dates and send live fish to the seat in water jars. An Earth vein lies under the pond fields.

places.name: Ngư Đàm Thôn
places.look: Behind a bitter salt shore where nothing swims, a small oasis holds a grid of square fish ponds edged with mud brick and shaded by date palms. Low flat-roofed houses of the same brick line the dikes between the ponds. Children with wooden clappers chase the herons off the shallows.

places.name: Hoàng Thổ Mạch
places.look: A low mound of yellow earth among the fish ponds, where the grass grows thicker than anywhere in the desert.
places.lore: An Earth vein lies under the pond fields. The villagers say it is why their fish grow so fat.

provinces.name: Liên Đường
provinces.lore: A small green hollow of spring-fed grassland on the coast. Its people live on lotus root and seed and on what caravans spend when they stop to look. Dạ Quang's riders water their horses here and leave the flowers alone.

places.name: Liên Đường Thôn
places.look: In the middle of the open steppe, a hollow of spring-fed ponds blooms pink and white with lotus all summer. A few mud-brick houses with reed roofs stand on the banks, and a wooden viewing pier reaches out over the leaves. Caravans halt on the rise above just to look.

places.name: Lục Ba Đàm
places.look: A clear spring-fed pool among grass, its surface rippling green with lotus leaves.
places.lore: This is the largest of the Liên Đường ponds and the source of the rest. Dạ Quang's riders water horses at its lower end only.

provinces.name: Mã Minh
provinces.lore: Grassland behind the range where herders have run horses since 100. They sell remounts to Băng Tâm's caravans and anyone who pays. The old wells to the west lie under the sand of 1050.

places.name: Mã Minh Thôn
places.look: Round corrals of piled dry stone ring a cluster of felt tents and mud houses on the steppe behind the range. The neigh of horses carries far over the grass. To the west a low hump of sand covers the old wells where the village once stood.

places.name: Mục Thảo Mạch
places.look: A meadow on the steppe where the grass stays green even in drought, crossed by horse trails.
places.lore: A Wood vein lies under the meadow. Mã Minh's herders graze their best mares here.

provinces.name: Tiều Lộ
provinces.lore: River forest on the edge of Vô Tung Lâm, running down to the shore. Its woodcutters are the only people who can find the forest paths after a night's snow, and they sell timber and guiding. It answers to Trạc Anh Đài.

places.name: Tiều Lộ Thôn
places.look: A woodcutters' village where the forest comes down to the shore, its log houses under grey-tile roofs around a small timber jetty. At the forest's edge a fan of red-painted marker posts leads off among the trees, each one the start of a different path into Vô Tung Lâm.

places.name: Ngân Hùng Cương
places.look: A forested rise with great dens dug under the roots, and white fur caught on the bark.
places.lore: White bears from Vô Tung Lâm come here to den. In 1180 hunters took one alive and sold it in Mộc Lan.

places.name: Thoa Lạp Trấn
places.look: Burned stone foundations on the shore, overgrown with fir saplings.
places.lore: Hàn Giang Môn's fishers built this town around 320, named after their founder's rain cape and hat. It burned in the War of the Frost Coast in 498.

provinces.name: Lâm Ẩn
provinces.lore: A small stretch of old fir forest on a quiet inlet. Its people are trackers whom hunters from Mộc Lan hire. The ruin of a trackers' academy lies in the woods.

places.name: Lâm Ẩn Thôn
places.look: A coastal village so deep in old firs that from the sea only its chimney smoke shows above the canopy. A single long plank jetty runs out of the trees into a quiet inlet.

places.name: Lão Sam Lâm
places.look: Huge old firs close over the inlet, and the forest floor is deep with needles.
places.lore: Lâm Ẩn's children learn to track here. The firs are so tall that village smoke barely clears them.

places.name: Tầm Tung Viện
places.look: A ruined timber hall in the firs, with tracks of every beast carved into its stone threshold.
places.lore: Students of the hermit who taught Lâm Ẩn's children founded this academy in 800. In 1040 its masters went into Vô Tung Lâm together and did not come back.

provinces.name: Lô Hoa
provinces.lore: Forest and reed marsh on the grassy south coast. Its people cut reeds for thatch, mats and quilts and sell the reed-flower down the coast. Blue lynxes hunt in the woods behind.

places.name: Lô Hoa Thôn
places.look: A marsh village on the grassy coast, its stilt houses standing in a sea of reeds. In summer the reeds flower white and the whole marsh looks snowed over, with only grey roofs and winding boat channels showing through.

places.name: Thanh Ly Lâm
places.look: A thick wood of fir and alder behind the reed marsh, where the trunks are scored with claw marks at shoulder height.
places.lore: Blue-grey spirit lynxes hunt marsh birds and deer here, and their coats fetch a high price in Liên Giang. Lô Hoa's reed-cutters never go in alone at dusk, and they hang reed bells at the wood's edge to hear the cats pass.

provinces.name: Bối Sa
provinces.lore: Flat grass and dry steppe running down to a white shell beach. Its fishers and shell-gatherers trade old shell money for small things and new shells to the mainland. A warm pool behind the dunes is where the shell-sorters soak their hands after the cold season's work.

places.name: Bối Sa Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on a gleaming white beach on the island's grassy coast. On the sand above the tide line stands a small mound-shrine built entirely of white shells, with the village's drying mats spread around it.

places.name: Ôn Bối Trì
places.look: A shallow warm pool in the grass behind the dunes, its bottom white with old shells.
places.lore: The shell-gatherers of Bối Sa soak their cracked hands here after the cold season. They throw in one shell from every catch, so the floor rises a little every year.

provinces.name: Lãng Thạch
provinces.lore: Grassy shore and bamboo thickets around the split sea stack of Wave Rock. The village answers to Bình Thủy Môn and lives by fishing and by rowing visitors into the sea cave of old Cô Phàm charts. Inland of the harbour, on the crab flats of Cự Ngao Chử, the sect keeps its Tide Hall on stilts. Great claw crabs come up out of the surf onto the grass, and the fishers count them a worse nuisance than storms.

places.name: Lãng Thạch Thôn
places.look: A small village behind a sea stack on the island coast. The stack, Wave Rock, stands split in two from crown to waterline, and through the gap shows the dark mouth of a sea cave.

places.name: Bình Thủy Môn
places.look: The Tide Hall stands on agarwood stilts above low brackish flats of grey grass, cut by creeks that fill and empty with the tide. A raft track runs off toward Wave Rock, and giant crabs still roam the mud around the stilts.
places.lore: Bình Thủy Môn, founded in 520 by strangers far from home and sworn to Lạc Hà Tông, has kept its Tide Hall here since 1116, on agarwood stilts above the crab flats of Cự Ngao Chử. Its head Bùi Phiêu Bình chose the flats for the Still Moon Tide Scripture, a canon that fills at the turn of the tide, and in 1115 he fought the Claw King for two tides and killed it at slack water. He drove its shell plates into the mud as the Slack-Water Weirs, and the sect's boats moor at Lãng Thạch. The old hall above the landing is now the Strangers' Hall.

provinces.name: Dương Liễu
provinces.lore: Dunes and coastal grass held in place by long rows of willows, with forest on the higher ground behind. The villagers fish and tend their willow rows, which they began planting after the sands buried Hải Khúc Trấn. Sand pythons lie up in the warm dunes, and children are taught to walk only on the willow paths.

places.name: Dương Liễu Thôn
places.look: A village on the island's dunes, its grey roofs sheltered behind long rows of wind-bent willows planted along the sand ridges. Their roots bind the dunes, and from the sea the village looks hedged in green.

places.name: Phục Mãng Cương
places.look: A warm bare dune ridge beyond the willow rows, its sand marked with long curving trails.
places.lore: Sand pythons as thick as a man lie buried in the warm sand and take what walks over them. The villagers of Dương Liễu say the willows are the only thing the snakes will not cross.

provinces.name: Tình Sa
provinces.lore: A sunny river mouth of grass and bamboo, with the empty quays of Bích Không Cảng on its shore. Its fishers dry their catch on the sandbar beside the driftwood whale. A hot spring inland is where the islanders go to wash after a storm has passed, and they say it always rises clearer when the rain stops.

places.name: Tình Sa Thôn
places.look: A village of low grey roofs on a broad, sunny sandbar at a river mouth. On the bar lies a long driftwood effigy of a whale, built by the villagers and weathered silver.

places.name: Bích Không Cảng
places.look: The empty harbour below Đàm Ảnh Thành: long stone quays running out into blue water, lined with bare mooring posts and not one boat. At the root of the quays stands the roofless shell of a great sail loft, its rafters open to the sky.

places.name: Vũ Tễ Tuyền
places.look: A steaming pool in open grass that clouds over in wet weather and runs clear as glass when the rain stops.
places.lore: The islanders read the weather by it: when the pool clears, the storm is over. Fishers of Tình Sa will not put out until they have seen it clear.

provinces.name: Nguyệt Loan
provinces.lore: Grass, bamboo and broad-leaf forest round the crescent cove where the island's fleets run from storms. Its people fish, mend boats and keep the storm shed hung with carved moons. Inland under the cassia trees runs a quiet spirit vein that Lạc Hà's disciples visit when they come over to the island.

places.name: Nguyệt Loan Thôn
places.look: A fishing village around a perfect crescent cove, its arms of rock nearly closing at the mouth. Inside rides a crowded fleet of island boats, their masts thick as reeds.

places.name: Quế Ảnh Mạch
places.look: A grove of old cassia trees in the forest above the cove, where the moonlight falls through the leaves in sharp silver patches.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the cassias, strongest on moonlit nights. Lạc Hà's disciples who come over to the island sit here when the moon is full and say the sea is quieter in their meridians.

provinces.name: Điền Viên
provinces.lore: Forest and garden fields on the plain coast where Nhạn Thanh's scholars retire to farm. The village answers to Mục Vân Trang and lives by vegetables, orchards and letters written for herders. A quiet Wood vein under its orchards draws old scholars who have taken up cultivation late.

places.name: Điền Viên Thôn
places.look: A village of gardens and fields on the plain coast, its grey roofs half hidden by orchard walls. In nearly every garden wall is a round moon gate, and through them show the small studies of retired scholars.

places.name: Ẩn Canh Mạch
places.look: A small wood behind the scholars' gardens, its floor soft with leaf mould and a stone seat at its centre.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the wood, gentle enough for those who come to cultivation late. Retired scholars of Nhạn Thanh sit here after their morning in the fields, and a few have reached Luyện Khí in old age.

provinces.name: Yến Quy
provinces.lore: Grass and forest on the plain coast around the old farm where the swallows return each spring. Its farmers plant by the birds. A warm spring in the fields is where the swallows bathe before they nest.

places.name: Yến Quy Thôn
places.look: A small farm village on the plain coast, its grey roofs gathered around one old farmstead. The old farm's roof ridge is lined end to end with little clay swallows, and the real birds perch among them.

places.name: Yến Ngữ Thang
places.look: A warm pool in the fields edged with reeds, crowded each spring with swallows dipping and calling.
places.lore: The swallows of Yến Quy bathe here before they nest. The farmers say a year when they bathe late is a year to plant carefully.

provinces.name: Chu Tân
provinces.lore: Low wet grass and forest on a shore below the level of the high tide, round the old ford whose river has wandered away. The village answers to Mục Vân Trang and hauls travellers and herds across the tidal creek. A warm pool by the old ford is where the ferrymen thaw out after winter crossings.

places.name: Chu Tân Thôn
places.look: A ferry village on the low, wet shore, below the level of the sea at high tide. Two tall carved ferry posts stand at the old ford, joined by a heavy rope across a narrow tidal creek, with a flat barge crawling along it.

places.name: Ôn Tân Trì
places.look: A steaming pool on the wet shore beside the old ferry posts, lower than the sea at high tide but never flooded by it.
places.lore: The ferrymen of Chu Tân thaw out here after winter crossings. The tide rises all around it and stops at its rim, and no one knows why.

provinces.name: Lô Cảng
provinces.lore: Grass and forest around the reed harbour where Lạc Hà keeps its western watch. Watchmen and fishers share the land and the tower lights a fire at strange sails. A hot spring inland warms the watchmen after their nights on the tower.

places.name: Lô Cảng Thôn
places.look: A village of reed-thatched boat sheds around a sheltered reed harbour on the plain coast. Out of the reeds rises a tall timber watchtower flying Lạc Hà's sunset-red banner, the sect's western watch.

places.name: Hàn Thú Thang
places.look: A walled hot spring in the grass inland of the reed harbour, with a small guardroom beside it.
places.lore: Lạc Hà built the guardroom when it raised the western watch, so the watchmen could warm themselves after a night on the tower. A watchman who leaves his post for the spring is made to bathe in the sea instead.

provinces.name: Diêm Điền
provinces.lore: Flat grass and forest along a coast of glittering salt pans, the oldest on the continent. Its people rake salt and sell it up and down the plain. On the shore lie the drowned walls of Triều Một Trấn, a town the sea took.

places.name: Diêm Điền Thôn
places.look: A village at the edge of a vast glittering grid of salt pans on the flat west coast. Between the shallow white squares stand rows of shining salt cones, raked up by hand.

places.name: Hàm Thủy Thang
places.look: A hot salty spring in the grass behind the salt pans, its rim crusted white.
places.lore: Its water is saltier than the sea, and the salt-makers once boiled it for salt in winter. Now they soak their aching backs in it after the summer raking.

places.name: Triều Một Trấn
places.look: Low broken walls standing in shallow water on the grassy shore, visible only at low tide.
places.lore: Salt traders built the town on the shore in 350, before any sect held the plain. In 988 a storm surge broke its sea wall and drowned the lower streets, and its people moved up the coast to Diêm Điền. At low tide the salt-makers still walk out to its gate.

provinces.name: Khê Thanh
provinces.lore: Grass, forest and steppe along a clear chattering brook that runs to the bay. Its villagers keep the banks clean for Thiên Bảo Trai, which rinses its finest refinings here. On the steppe shore lie the burned walls of Hoa Ổ Viện, a hall of Lạc Anh Phái lost in the fighting for the Petal Shore.

places.name: Khê Thanh Thôn
places.look: A village on a clear grassland brook, its grey roofs strung along the water. Over the brook stand a row of small covered rinsing sheds on stilts, where the water chatters loudly over the stones beneath them.

places.name: Hoa Ổ Viện
places.look: Burned walls and a fallen gate on the steppe shore, with a few old peach trees still growing in the empty courtyard.
places.lore: Lạc Anh Phái built this hall in 280 to graft its peach trees. When Lạc Hà and Thính Vũ fought over the empty Petal Shore it burned with the orchards in 618, and no one rebuilt it. The peach trees in its courtyard still flower each spring.

places.name: Chu Hoa Mạch
places.look: A wood by the brook where red flowers grow on the forest floor all year.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the wood, named for the old line about vermilion blooms by the water. Thiên Bảo's apprentices rest here between rinsings.

provinces.name: Khê Đầu
provinces.lore: Open grass where the brook rises from a carp-head spout, with the burned ruins of Kim Cốc Thành and Hồng Vũ Thành on its land. Its villagers guard the spring and herd a few cattle. Hornets nest in the old walls, and the scavengers who sift Kim Cốc's ash go in with smoke pots.

places.name: Khê Đầu Thôn
places.look: A small village at the head of a brook on the grassland, where the water rises from the ground. The spring pours from a stone spout carved as a carp's head into a round basin, and the brook starts from its overflow.

places.name: Kim Cốc Thành
places.look: The burned shell of a merchant city on the bay shore, its walls blackened and its streets choked with ash and weeds. At its heart stands the charred skeleton of a great garden pavilion, a few gold-glazed tiles still clinging to its broken ridge.

places.name: Hồng Vũ Thành
places.look: Burned walls among wild peach trees on the Petal Shore, inland of the bay. In spring the peaches bloom through the roofless halls, and red petals drift down over the black stones like red rain.

places.name: Độc Phong Nguyên
places.look: Open grass by the brook head where the air hums and grey paper nests hang from every bush.
places.lore: Spirit hornets as long as a thumb nest here, and a dozen stings can kill. The villagers of Khê Đầu smoke them back from the spring each summer.

provinces.name: Hải Môn
provinces.lore: Grass, bamboo and a little jungle on the bay coast by the great rock arch. Its fishers time everything by the tide through the arch. Troops of spirit monkeys live in the bamboo hills and raid the drying racks.

places.name: Hải Môn Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the bay coast beside a great natural rock arch, the Sea Gate. Twice a day the tide runs through the arch in a white rush, and the village boats wait on the inner side for the slack.

places.name: Quần Hầu Lĩnh
places.look: A bamboo ridge loud with chattering, where the canes bend under the weight of monkeys.
places.lore: Troops of spirit monkeys live in the bamboo and raid the fish racks of Hải Môn. They throw stones well enough to break a skull, and the fishers keep dogs.

provinces.name: Tân Khẩu
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo round the harbour mouth where the refugees of Vô Định Thành settled in 805. Its people fish and keep their blank wall turned to the plain. A hot spring behind the village is called the spring of forgetting, and the old ones bathe there in silence.

places.name: Tân Khẩu Thôn
places.look: A village at the mouth of a harbour on the bay coast, its houses all facing the sea. On the landward side they join into one long blank wall with no windows, turned against the plain.

places.name: Vong Ưu Tuyền
places.look: A clear warm pool in the grass behind the village, with a single stone bench beside it.
places.lore: The refugees of Vô Định Thành called it the spring of forgetting. The old ones bathe there in silence, and no one speaks while they are in the water.

provinces.name: Hoa Khê
provinces.lore: Forest and grass along the flower brook, with a little bamboo. Its cottages keep the custom of the lovers' slips and pay their dues to Nam Phố Đường. Wild plum trees line the river and fill it with petals in spring.

places.name: Hoa Khê Thôn
places.look: A handful of grey-roofed cottages along a clear brook in open grassland, with wild plum and pear on its banks. Just below the last house a low fence of bamboo stakes crosses the brook, and in spring it catches a pink drift of petals and paper slips.

places.name: Lạc Mai Lâm
places.look: A wood of wild plums along the river that turns white with blossom before the snow is gone.
places.lore: Its petals float down to the flower brook each spring and catch on the lovers' fence. The village's old women say a slip that catches in the plum petals is the luckiest of all.

provinces.name: Ngân Than
provinces.lore: Forest and grass on a gravel river bend, rising to wooded hills. Its panners wash the shallows for the silver of Lạc Hà's coin. The wind in the forest on the hills sounds like flutes, and the panners say it keeps the count.

places.name: Ngân Than Thôn
places.look: A low village on a gravel bend of the river, its shallows lined with long wooden sluice boxes where flecks of silver glint under the moving water. Heaps of washed grey gravel stand in rows behind the houses.

places.name: Sảng Lại Lâm
places.look: A forest on the hills where the wind through the hollow branches sounds like many flutes.
places.lore: Its name comes from the old line about clear pipes sounding and a clean wind rising. The silver panners of Ngân Than say the forest keeps the count when their singers tire.

provinces.name: Phương Thảo
provinces.lore: Forest and sea meadow behind low dunes at a river mouth. Its people cut the sweet grass for the mats of Lạc Hà's meditation halls. A wood of sea pines shelters the meadow from the salt wind.

places.name: Phương Thảo Thôn
places.look: A fishing village behind low dunes, where long swathes of golden-green sweet grass are laid out to dry in neat combed rows across the sea meadow. Open-sided weaving sheds face its small harbour.

places.name: Yển Tùng Lâm
places.look: A wood of low, wind-bent pines behind the dunes, their crowns all leaning away from the sea.
places.lore: The sea pines shelter the sweet grass meadow from the salt wind. The grass cutters of Phương Thảo say that the day the pines fall the grass will lose its scent.

provinces.name: Thủy Khẩu
provinces.lore: Grass, forest and steppe where the brook joins the river at the hand-dug channel. Its people live by the boat trade and lift a spadeful each winter so the river will remember. A sweet hot spring rises in the grass nearby.

places.name: Thủy Khẩu Thôn
places.look: Where a slow brook mouths into the main river stands a small village of grey roofs beside a dead-straight channel, dug by hand and banked with long ridges of spoil planted with willows. A stone tablet stands where the channel opens onto the river.

places.name: Cam Lộ Tuyền
places.look: A warm spring in the grass above the river, its water sweet enough to drink.
places.lore: The boatmen of Thủy Khẩu fill their jars here before going downriver. Lạc Hà's cooks send for it to brew the tea of the evening rites.

provinces.name: Mộc Hương
provinces.lore: River forest and steppe on the northern edge of the plain, grown with scented incense trees. Its woodcutters cut only fallen and dying trees for the Pivot Hall's fires. Spirit horses run wild on the steppe beyond the groves, and the villagers keep well away from their herd.

places.name: Mộc Hương Thôn
places.look: A woodcutters' village of steep grey roofs under groves of tall incense trees on a river bank. Low clay curing kilns stand in a row along the water, and their thin blue smoke hangs over the river and smells sweet a long way downstream.

places.name: Thiết Đề Nguyên
places.look: Open steppe beyond the incense groves, beaten bare in long tracks by a running herd.
places.lore: A herd of wild spirit horses with hooves hard as iron runs here and tramples anything in its way. Mộc Hương's woodcutters stay inside the groves when they hear it.

provinces.name: Thụ Âm
provinces.lore: Dry steppe with a little forest and badland along a river, around the great tree of Thụ Âm Thôn. Its people keep goats and grow millet on the river flats. The roots of the great tree are said to reach down to an Earth and Wood vein under the steppe.

places.name: Thụ Âm Thôn
places.look: A village sheltering whole under the canopy of one vast old tree, its roofs dappled and its lanes always cool. From the far edge of the shade, on clear days, villagers can see a grey haze lying low over the plain beyond.

places.name: Khô Tỉnh Trấn
places.look: Mud-brick walls on the steppe around a deep stone well, dry to the bottom, with empty houses roofless around it.
places.lore: A caravan halt that grew into a town around its well from 530. The well failed in the drought of 940, and the people left for the river.

places.name: Bàn Căn Mạch
places.look: A dip in the steppe where great roots break the surface in coils, though no tree stands near.
places.lore: Its qi (linh khí) runs to Earth and Wood. The villagers of Thụ Âm say these are the roots of their great tree, and that the tree drinks from the vein.

provinces.name: Thủy Đối
provinces.lore: Grassland on a fast river running down to the inland sea. Its people farm wheat and work the water mills that grind Thanh Mạch's grain for Tinh Hán Thành. A Water vein lies in the grass above the mills.

places.name: Thủy Đối Thôn
places.look: A village on a fast stream where a row of waterwheels drives long wooden trip-hammers that rise and fall into stone mortars, thudding all day under open sheds. Flour dust whitens the roofs.

places.name: Thanh Lưu Mạch
places.look: A spring in the grass above the mills, so clear that its pebbles seem to float.
places.lore: A small vein (linh mạch) whose qi (linh khí) runs to Water. The millers say their wheels turn smoother on the stream it feeds, and they never let cattle drink at its head.

provinces.name: Thanh Mạch
provinces.lore: Rolling steppe and grassland along a river, the wheat land of Ngọc Hành. Its farmers grow the grain the mills of Thủy Đối grind. A vein by the river is said to make the wheat ripen evenly.

places.name: Thanh Mạch Thôn
places.look: A farming village on a low rise above a river, its houses gathered around a round threshing floor of polished stone on the hilltop, with a heavy stone roller standing upright at its centre. Green wheat falls away on every side.

places.name: Kim Tuệ Mạch
places.look: A riverside field where the wheat always ripens first and stands tallest.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth and Wood. The village threshes the first sheaf from it before any other, and seed from this field is traded for twice its weight in common grain.

provinces.name: Châu Bạng
provinces.lore: A small stretch of rocky coast and low mountain on the inland sea. Its people dive for pearls in the shallows and burn shell and limestone for lime. A low humped hill shelters the village from the sea wind.

places.name: Châu Bạng Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the inland sea whose house walls are set all over with oyster shells, so the whole village glitters white and pearl-grey in the sun. Diving boats are drawn up on a beach of broken shell.

places.name: Thạch Hôi Khoáng
places.look: A white limestone quarry by the sea, with kilns burning shell and stone into lime.
places.lore: Its lime makes the mortar of Tinh Hán's walls and the packing between the ribs of the bone reef. The burners' eyes are always red, and they wash them in sea water each evening.

places.name: Quy Bối Sơn
places.look: A low, humped hill of grey rock on the shore, shaped like a turtle's back, its seaward side white with spray.
places.lore: It shelters Châu Bạng from the sea wind. Its qi runs to Water, calm and slow, and divers sit on its crown before the season to steady their breath.

provinces.name: Đào Khê
provinces.lore: Rolling grass and wild peach below the northern ridges, watered by the brook that runs past the old palace platform of Cửu Thiều Cung. Its farmers grow peaches, millet and a little rice, and make peach wine they will not sing over. Phượng Minh sends a disciple each spring to sweep the platform, and nobody asks why the palace bothers.

places.name: Đào Khê Thôn
places.look: A small village beside a brook below the ridges, built at the edge of a wide terraced stone platform where wild peach trees grow straight out of the cracks between old paving slabs. Broken stone column bases stand in rows among the trees.

places.name: Đào Hoa Thang
places.look: A warm pool in the grass below the peach orchard, its surface covered with pink petals every spring.
places.lore: The villagers of Đào Khê bathe here after the peach harvest. Like the orchard above it, no one sings at the pool.

provinces.name: Hà Loan
provinces.lore: A wide floodplain of grass and reeds where the river loops to the gulf, flooded every autumn. Its stilt villages grow rice in the drained season and trade from boats in the wet one. Phượng Minh's bird keepers have lately settled in the jungle edge above the floods.

places.name: Hà Loan Thôn
places.look: A village on a wide river bend, every house raised high on timber stilts above the floodplain and joined by plank walks. Boats are tied under the houses, ready for autumn.

places.name: Noãn Ba Tuyền
places.look: A shallow warm spring on the floodplain, ringed by a low mud wall that the autumn flood tops every year.
places.lore: When the flood comes, the warm water spreads over the plain and the fish crowd to it, and Hà Loan's boat traders call it their best season.

places.name: Bách Vũ Các
places.look: On the jungle edge above the floodplain, a tall pavilion of red timber stands among great netted aviaries, loud with peacocks, pheasants and messenger birds.
places.lore: A minor sect of spirit bird keepers sworn to Phượng Minh Cung, founded in 1110 by bird catchers who said that all birds bow to the phoenix and so should serve its palace. It raises messenger birds for the palace and sells feather fans and talisman feathers; it is one of the younger vassals of the south and still eager to prove itself.

provinces.name: Bích Lãng
provinces.lore: A low coast of bamboo groves sinking below the level of the gulf, held back by basket walls of stone. Its people fish and cut bamboo for Trúc Thực Viên, which keeps the coast. Up the river, the empty halls of a Cửu Thiều flute school still stand in the bamboo.

places.name: Bích Lãng Thôn
places.look: A fishing village lying just below the level of the gulf behind a seawall of great woven bamboo baskets packed with stones, stacked in a long curve. Bamboo groves crowd the houses, and jade-green waves break against the baskets.

places.name: Tử Trúc Lâm
places.look: A grove of dark purple-stemmed bamboo, so dense that it is dim at noon and rustles without wind.
places.lore: Trúc Thực Viên cuts the purple cane for the basket walls of Bích Lãng, since it rots slower than any other in salt water.

places.name: Trúc Địch Viện
places.look: Roofless halls by the river among the bamboo, their walls pierced with rows of small round holes like the stops of a flute.
places.lore: A flute school of Cửu Thiều Cung where its disciples learned the bamboo pipes. When the palace made its last stand in 340 the students went up to the palace's last stand and did not come back, and the school was never reopened.

provinces.name: Thủy Điền
provinces.lore: The oldest rice country of the plain, flooded paddies and dry steppe along a river under the western hills. Its farmers have planted here since 140 and still set the plain's first seedling each spring. A spirit vein runs under the dry ground beyond the paddies.

places.name: Thủy Điền Thôn
places.look: A handful of grey-tile houses on a low dyke between flooded paddies, beside the river. On the bank a great bamboo waterwheel, its rim strung with tube buckets, creaks round and lifts water into the oldest fields on the plain.

places.name: Hòa Miêu Mạch
places.look: A patch of dry steppe beyond the paddies where grass grows green in the driest month.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein under the dry ground. Thủy Điền's farmers raise their first seedlings here before planting them out.

provinces.name: Âu Lộ
provinces.lore: A low marsh coast and oak woods on the eastern gulf, loud with nesting birds. Its people fish from the shore; their forebears were the pearl divers of Châu Lệ Cảng and never dived again. A water vein lies in the woods behind the marsh.

places.name: Âu Lộ Thôn
places.look: A low marsh shore of the eastern gulf, where a stand of dead trees is white with nesting gulls and herons and loud from dawn to dusk. The village houses sit back from the waterline on the landward edge of the marsh, and on their walls hang old diving baskets and weighted ropes, dry for centuries.

places.name: Thanh Âu Nhãn
places.look: A small clear spring in the oak woods behind the marsh, where gulls come to drink and bathe.
places.lore: A Thủy (water) vein rises here. The old divers' families say the pearls of Châu Lệ came from the same water.

provinces.name: Ngân Hạnh
provinces.lore: Grass and oak woods on a river at the western edge of the plain, rising to the hills. Its people farm rice and roast ginkgo nuts for the road. In the woods toward the hills stand the walls of a music town that emptied when Cửu Thiều fell.

places.name: Ngân Hạnh Thôn
places.look: A forest village on a small river among the oak woods at the plain's edge, its grey roofs gathered under one colossal ginkgo (ngân hạnh) that dwarfs them. In autumn the tree turns gold in a single night, and by morning the roofs are carpeted yellow.

places.name: Ngọc Quản Trấn
places.look: Low walls in the oak woods at the foot of the hills, with a carved stone stage still standing in the old square.
places.lore: A town of Cửu Thiều Cung where jade pipes were cut and played. When the palace fell its people left within a year, like those of Vân Môn, and the woods took it.

places.name: Kim Diệp Mạch
places.look: A low grassy mound near the river, ringed by young ginkgo trees that turn gold before any others.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein. The villagers say the great ginkgo of Ngân Hạnh draws its long life from it.

provinces.name: Lý Hoa
provinces.lore: A broad sandy coast of grass and steppe on the eastern gulf, with the burned pearl harbour of Châu Lệ Cảng on its shore. Its people fish and grow white plums. Since the pirate years a hall of watchers has kept the coast, and its lantern still burns over the old oyster beds.

places.name: Lý Hoa Thôn
places.look: A fishing hamlet on a sandy beach, its boats drawn up below an orchard of white plum (lý hoa) that runs right down to the high-tide line. In early spring the orchard is so white that beach and blossom are hard to tell apart, and grey snow geese sit among the branches.

places.name: Châu Lệ Cảng
places.look: A curve of low coast where a beach of heaped white oyster shells glitters under rows of charred pier pilings standing in the shallows. Behind them the burned shells of warehouses and a broken harbour wall slope down into the sea.

places.name: Vọng Triều Đường
places.look: A walled hall of grey stone on the steppe shore, with a tall lantern tower facing the sea and the burned piers of Châu Lệ.
places.lore: A minor sect founded in 790 by survivors of the pirate years, sworn to Phượng Minh, which keeps watch on the eastern gulf and lays sea-ward formations against storms and raiders. Its lantern burns every night over the old oyster beds, and its head swears no harbour on this coast will burn again.

places.name: Bạch Nhạn Huyệt
places.look: A shallow hollow in the steppe where the snow geese land each spring, the grass pale and stiff.
places.lore: A Kim (metal) vein lies under the hollow. The fishers say the geese come for it, not for the plum blossom.

provinces.name: Hoàng Ngưu
provinces.lore: Open grass and steppe on the gulf where yellow oxen graze in loose herds. Its herders breed the oxen that plough the plain and pull its barges. On the shore of Triêu Hà Hồ stands the Dawn Hall, where the healers of Lễ Tuyền Phái have lived since 1141. A warm spring in the steppe is where the oxen are washed before the spring blessing.

places.name: Hoàng Ngưu Thôn
places.look: A cattle village on the open plain, its grey roofs gathered beside a great round corral of piled fieldstone. Yellow oxen graze in loose herds all around, and the grass near the corral is worn to bare earth.

places.name: Ngưu Dục Trì
places.look: A broad warm pool in the steppe, its banks trodden bare by hooves.
places.lore: Hoàng Ngưu's herders wash the ox with painted horns here before walking it round the corral on the first day of spring.

places.name: Lễ Tuyền Phái
places.look: A wide shallow lake lies so still at dawn in the open grassland that the first clouds lie doubled on it, a rose mist lifting off the water. On its shore stands the Dawn Hall, pale timber halls at the water's edge with herb terraces behind, and in the eastern shallows lies a low flat platform of weathered stone, half awash.

provinces.name: Kiều Bạn
provinces.lore: Grassy river country with stands of bamboo, crossed by the forest road at the roofed bridge of Kiều Bạn. Farmers grow rice and sugar cane on the bottoms and cut bamboo on the low hills, and the inns at the bridge buy whatever they bring. It is the first stop on the road from the west, and the Tower keeps a toll clerk at the bridge's southern end.

places.name: Kiều Bạn Thôn
places.look: Where the forest road crosses a slow river, a roofed timber bridge with deep eaves carries the traffic, and under those eaves hang rows of worn straw sandals. A cluster of grey-tile houses and an inn crowd its northern end.

places.name: Thảo Tâm Nhãn
places.gloss: Eye in the Heart of the Grass
places.look: In an open meadow a round patch of grass stays bright green through the dry months, and at its centre a small clear spring wells up without a sound.
places.lore: A minor spirit eye of Wood (Mộc) qi a short walk from the bridge at Kiều Bạn. Travellers resting at the bridge come to sit by it, and the village charges a copper for the privilege.

provinces.name: Bình Độ
provinces.lore: Rolling grass and rain forest along a slow, wide river, with bamboo on the higher ground. Villagers farm rice and longans and run the calm ferry at Bình Độ, which carries most of the traffic between Thu Trì and the inland towns. Drums are forbidden on the riverbank for a day's walk either side of the ferry.

places.name: Bình Độ Thôn
places.look: A ferry landing on a wide, slow forest river, where a broad flat raft with a small thatched sleeping shelter on its deck is poled across from a village of grey-tile houses. The water here is glassy and barely moves.

places.name: Long Nhãn Lâm
places.look: Tall old longan trees, their trunks split and hollow with age, stand widely spaced across the grassland like an orchard gone wild.
places.lore: The ferry village says the first ferryman of Bình Độ planted it, and no one owns it now. In summer the whole village picks the fruit together and dries it for the markets of Thu Trì.

provinces.name: Hoa Điền
provinces.lore: Low flower meadows and forest between the river and the sea, kept in long strips of colour for the bees. Its honey, wax and flower oils go down to Thu Trì Thành, and buyers for the Night Rain Market pay well for the honey of the poison flowers at the forest edge. A warm spring in the jungle behind the fields is the province's other wealth.

places.name: Hoa Điền Thôn
places.look: A river village set among sweeping fields of flowers in long strips of purple, yellow and white. Along the village edge runs a wall of stacked hollow-log beehives, humming loudly all summer.

places.name: Ôn Vũ Thang
places.look: In the jungle above the flower fields a steaming pool lies among ferns, and when rain falls on it the drops hiss and raise a thin warm mist.
places.lore: The beekeepers of Hoa Điền bathe here to ease the stings of the season, and the water is said to draw out venom. Hồng Đậu Trang has offered twice to buy the spring, and the village has refused twice.

provinces.name: Yên Kiều
provinces.lore: Damp jungle and meadow along a misty river, held by Hồng Đậu Trang as the approach to its manor. Its villagers fish, grow taro and chew the areca nut of the groves around them, and they work for the manor as boatmen and guides. Guests of the manor cross the misty bridge here, and the villagers say not all of them are counted coming back.

places.name: Yên Kiều Thôn
places.look: A river village in low meadows, where a long, narrow bridge of grey stone slabs on many low piers runs out across a misty river and fades into fog before it reaches the other side. On rainy days its far end cannot be seen at all.

places.name: Tân Lang Lâm
places.look: Ranks of tall, slender areca palms rise out of the meadow grass, their crowns so high that the rain reaches the ground long after it starts.
places.lore: The villagers of Yên Kiều cut areca nuts here to chew with betel leaf, and Hồng Đậu Trang, which owns the grove, sends each guest a lacquered box of them on arrival. Those who chew the manor's nuts say they taste faintly of beans.

provinces.name: Ương Ca
provinces.lore: Wooded hills and bamboo above a river, terraced for rice wherever the slope allows. Its farmers sing the oldest planting song in the south, and sing it louder each spring to drown the autumn singing from the graves of Lôi Trạch. A grove of lightning-struck paulownia above the terraces supplies the zither makers of Không Mông.

places.name: Ương Ca Thôn
places.look: A hill village above a river, its grey-tile houses at the top of a stair of curving rice terraces. At the head of the terraces stands a round stone stage open to the sky, where the singers stand at planting.

places.name: Tiêu Đồng Lâm
places.look: Above the rice terraces stands a wood of paulownia trees, nearly every trunk split and blackened by lightning yet still in leaf.
places.lore: Lightning finds these trees every storm season, and wood that has been struck and lived holds Wood qi with a spark of thunder in it. The zither makers of Không Mông pay the most for the charred ends, which they say give the truest note.

provinces.name: Song Khê
provinces.lore: Low bamboo country and grass between two brooks, west of the old Lôi Trạch marsh. Villagers cut bamboo, grow rice and keep the joined dippers at the meeting of the brooks, where couples come from as far as Thu Trì. Hornets as long as a thumb nest in the bamboo, and the ruin of a drummers' hall stands empty on the grass.

places.name: Song Khê Thôn
places.look: A village where two brooks, one clear and one tea-brown from the forest, run together in a Y below the houses. On the point of land where they meet stands a tiny roofed shrine with two bamboo dippers tied together by a red cord.

places.name: Hoàng Phong Cốc
places.look: A shallow bamboo valley where paper nests the size of rain barrels hang from the stems, and the air hums from end to end.
places.lore: Spirit-touched hornets as long as a thumb nest here, led by a queen no one has seen. The villagers of Song Khê smoke out a nest each autumn for its grubs and wax and are stung for their trouble.

places.name: Kích Cổ Đường
places.look: On open grass stand the stone footings of a round hall, its floor cut with rings of empty sockets where great drums once stood.
places.lore: Kích Cổ Đường was a small school of drummers sworn to Khải Lôi Môn, whose drums answered the Gate's thunder at every festival. When the Gate fell in 480 the school had no one left to answer, and its last drummers scattered two years later.

provinces.name: Thượng Độ
provinces.lore: Bamboo and jungle along the upper river, where the ferry rope crosses between its carved stone posts. Its people raft bamboo downstream and keep the charred post that shows how near Phượng Minh's raiders came to the Tower's heart. A grove of purple bamboo above the ferry is cut for flutes.

places.name: Thượng Độ Thôn
