places.look: A ferry village on the upper river, where a ferry boat is hauled across on a rope strung between two tall carved stone posts. The post on the near bank is charred black to its top.

places.name: Địch Trúc Lâm
places.look: On the slope above the ferry, slender bamboo with dark purple stems grows in a dense grove, glossy after rain.
places.lore: The flute makers of the south cut their best stems here. The ferry village cuts only in the dry months, saying a stem cut in rain will always sound wet.

provinces.name: Hà Châu
provinces.lore: Grass, bamboo and jungle on both banks of a broad river, with the raw new isle in midstream that Thính Vũ and Xuyên Lâm both claim. Villagers fish, grow rice and row out each morning to see whose flag has moved. Lightning-blackened ebony trees stand alone in the meadows, and no one will cut them.

places.name: Hà Châu Thôn
places.look: A river village of grey roofs on the bank, facing a raw new isle of grey mud and gravel that has risen in the middle of the river. Two rival boundary flags flap on the isle, one at either end.

places.name: Hắc Đàn Mộc
places.look: A few great ebony trees stand alone in the river meadows, each blackened from crown to root where lightning has run down it.
places.lore: The struck ebony is harder than iron and holds a trace of thunder. Hà Châu will not cut a living tree, and takes only the limbs the storms bring down.

provinces.name: Cúc Viên
provinces.lore: Flat steppe and grass on the northern coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, around the flower village that hid Phượng Minh's scouts in 586. Its people grow chrysanthemums for the palace's autumn rites and fish the shore. A warm spring at the village edge is banked with flowers.

places.name: Cúc Viên Thôn
places.look: A small harbour village on a flat coast, its grey roofs half hidden by banked beds of yellow and bronze chrysanthemums that fill every slope and yard. In autumn the gardens grow so thick that the paths between them cannot be seen.

places.name: Hoàng Cúc Thang
places.look: A warm pool at the village edge, banked so thick with yellow chrysanthemums that its steam smells of them.
places.lore: The villagers soak chrysanthemum heads in it for a tea they sell to Phượng Minh for the autumn rites.

provinces.name: Tang Âm
provinces.lore: Grass and low hills on the coast road where the silk caravans rest under the great mulberry. Its people keep inns, fodder yards and stables. A wood vein runs under the caravan yard, and carters say it is why the tree never ages.

places.name: Tang Âm Thôn
places.look: A harbour village on the coast road whose heart is a single vast old mulberry tree, its crown spread wide over a dusty caravan yard. Carts and pack animals stand in its shade, and the village houses face inward toward it.

places.name: Tang Căn Mạch
places.look: The dusty caravan yard under the great mulberry, where the ground stays cool even at noon.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein runs under the yard. Carters say it is why the old tree never ages.

provinces.name: Hồ Tâm
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo behind the coastal dunes, around the round lake that breathes with the tide. Its people fish the lake and the sea. Giant crabs crowd the dune shore, and the villagers trap them for the markets.

places.name: Hồ Tâm Thôn
places.look: Behind the coastal dunes lies a round lake cut off from the sea, and the village sits on a small island in its middle, joined to the shore by a stone causeway. In the shallows beside the island stands a tall stone pillar notched with water marks, by which the villagers read the lake's strange tide. Their sea boats are dragged over the dunes to the beach.

places.name: Cự Giải Chử
places.look: A flat grassy shore between the lake and the dunes, riddled with burrows and littered with broken shells as big as shields.
places.lore: Spirit crabs with claws that can snap an oar live in the burrows. Hồ Tâm's villagers trap the small ones and leave the old ones alone.

provinces.name: Lô Châu
provinces.lore: Jungle, hills and reed marsh on a river in the west of Đan Huyệt Châu. Its people cut reed and have done so since before the pirates came. A forest of water pines grows along the river above the village.

places.name: Lô Châu Thôn
places.look: A river village on a low island of reed marsh, its houses raised on stilts with walls of bundled reeds lashed tight under grey-tile roofs. Paths of reed mats float between them, and the marsh around is cut into neat bays where reed is harvested.

places.name: Thủy Tùng Lâm
places.look: A grove of tall water pines on the wet grass by the river, their knobbed roots rising out of the mud like rows of kneeling stones.
places.lore: Lô Châu's reed cutters take its wood for the stilts of their houses, since water pine does not rot in the marsh. When the village was rebuilt in 782, every new stilt came from this grove, and the stumps are still counted as its founders.

provinces.name: Yên Ba
provinces.lore: The broad forested lowland around Yên Ba Thành, cut by a river, limestone knolls and patches of marsh, is the most crowded land on the cape. Timber, grain, fish and the trade of every cape village pass through its port. Thúy Vi's formation keeps the sea fog off the upper town but not off the woods, where the haze lies green all morning.

places.name: Yên Ba Thành
places.look: A walled port city stands where a river meets the sea, its quays and lower streets often lost in a drifting blue-green mist. Above the haze rises a slender pagoda of green-glazed tile at the end of the harbour mole, and a bronze horn at its top sounds through the fog to guide the ships home.

places.name: Lục Âm Lâm
places.look: A deep broadleaf forest just inland of Yên Ba, where the blue-green haze hangs under the canopy all morning.
places.lore: The city's carpenters and charcoal makers work its edges under licence from Thúy Vi. Children of Yên Ba are told the mist in the trees is the sect's breath.

provinces.name: Hàn Tân
provinces.lore: River forest, marsh and tundra edge around the ford and port of Hàn Tân Thành. Fishers and ferrymen live by the river and the cold sea, and fir timber goes out by boat. On the marsh coast lie the drowned quays of a town emptied under Tùng Đào's resin tax.

places.name: Hàn Tân Thành
places.look: A walled port city of grey roofs stands on bleak tundra coast where a broad river meets the sea at a shallow ford. Across the ford march a line of tall stone pillars, each with a lamp niche, marking the safe crossing for wagons and boats alike.

places.name: Lãnh Sam Lâm
places.look: Dark firs stand close on the low ground by the ford, snow caught in their branches long into spring.
places.lore: Ferrymen cut ford poles and boat timber here. Under Tùng Đào the firs were tapped for resin, and the old scars still show on the trunks.

places.name: Lô Khẩu Trấn
places.look: Rotted wooden quays and the stumps of house posts stand in a reed marsh on the coast, with a stone shrine above the water.
places.lore: A fishing town at a reedy inlet, it emptied when its fishers left for the hills under Tùng Đào's resin tax from 674. With no one to dredge it, the marsh took the quays.

provinces.name: Tùng Gian
provinces.lore: The small river mouth around Tùng Gian Thành, Tùng Đào's first city and port. Its land is all city, harbour and pine grove, with a clear spring running over the stones by the river. Timber, resin and pilgrims pass through its moon gate.

places.name: Tùng Gian Thành
places.look: A walled city at a river mouth on the coast, its grey roofs half hidden among tall pines that grow inside and along its walls. In the wall facing the palace ridge stands a huge round moon gate, and from the harbour road the moon rises framed in it among the pines.

places.name: Thạch Thượng Tuyền
places.look: A clear spring runs over flat river stones under pines just outside Tùng Gian Thành, and at night the moon shines through the pines on it.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring, named for Vương Duy's line of the clear spring that flows over the stones. Townsfolk fetch its water for the Night of a Thousand Pines.

provinces.name: Đào Thanh
provinces.lore: River land and steep forest around Đào Thanh Thành, the busiest city on the river. Timber merchants, river traders and the families of Tùng Đào's outer disciples live here. A spirit vein above the city hums with the pine waves.

places.name: Đào Thanh Thành
places.look: A walled river city under endless pine, its quays set high up the bank on tall stone steps. Below them, at low water, a row of old drowned quay pillars stands in the current like a broken fence, marking where the city once met the river. When the wind turns, the forest above roars like surf, and the streets go quiet to listen.

places.name: Đào Âm Mạch
places.look: A pine-covered hill above the city where the wind in the crowns roars like surf, and the ground underfoot trembles faintly with it.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the hill. The townsfolk of Đào Thanh climb up on windy evenings to hear the pines.

provinces.name: Khai Dương
provinces.lore: The forest country around the port of Khai Dương Thành, cut by a river that reaches the sea under the city walls. Farms and timber lots feed the city, and its quays ship timber, furs and Dao Quang iron along the northern coast. The woods inland are kept for the city's shipwrights and its morning fires.

places.name: Khai Dương Thành
places.look: A walled port city where the northern road meets a river mouth and the sea. Its east gate tower carries a great polished bronze disc that catches the first light before dawn, so the gate seems to burn while the streets below are still dark. Masts crowd the river quays under the walls.

places.name: Thần Hi Lâm
places.look: An oak and beech forest on the east side of Khai Dương, so open that the first light runs far under its trees.
places.lore: Khai Dương's bakers gather their kindling here before dawn. The city keeps it as a common wood, and no one may fence it.

provinces.name: Trường Vân
provinces.lore: Steppe and grassland around the river mouth where Trường Vân Thành stands, Băng Tâm's door to the sea since 470. Caravan guards, chandlers and the sect's officers fill it, and goods pass from camel to ship under the long gallery. Its guard families have never forgiven Hạng Dạ Bôi, who was born among them.

places.name: Trường Vân Thành
places.look: A walled harbour city at the edge of the desert, where a river reaches the sea under the snow mountains. A long roofed caravan gallery runs straight through the city from the land gate to the docks, so goods pass from camel to ship without seeing the sun. On cloudy days a faint shimmer of a ward formation hangs over the walls, and long clouds lie on the peaks behind.

places.name: Trấn Sa Đường
places.look: A walled compound of pale mud brick on a rise in the steppe, with a sabre yard and a long stable.
places.lore: The caravan guard families of Trường Vân founded this hall in 1125, after Dạ Quang Môn was made to guard the caravans. They train guards in sabre and desert craft, and they watch Dạ Quang's riders more closely than the road.

places.name: Quy Vân Mạch
places.look: A low rise on the steppe where morning mist gathers and lingers until noon.
places.lore: An Earth vein lies under the rise, and its qi draws the mist. Trường Vân's guards say the long clouds over the mountains come home here.

provinces.name: Liên Giang
provinces.lore: Forest around the cold river mouth where Hàn Giang Môn built Liên Giang Thành in 350. Its people fish and pay their tax in ice-fish, as they have since the frost coast fell in 498. A new school of ice-hole cultivators keeps Hàn Giang's old practice alive under Băng Tâm's licence.

places.name: Liên Giang Thành
places.gloss: City Where the Rain Meets the River
places.look: A grey port city where a cold river meets the sea, its walls running down both banks to the harbour. Across the river mouth stretches a long roofed bridge of dark timber and grey tile, its eaves hung with racks of silver ice-fish drying in the rain.

places.name: Lãnh Giang Phái
places.look: Timber halls stand on the bank above the river mouth, and in winter a line of holes runs across the river ice with disciples sitting motionless beside them.
places.lore: Liên Giang's fishers founded this school in 1140 to revive Hàn Giang's ice-hole cultivation under Băng Tâm's licence. Its disciples still leave a fish on Hàn Giang's fallen gate after a good catch.

places.name: Bạch Âu Đường
places.look: A burned hall on the shore, its seaward wall gone and gull nests in the rafters.
places.lore: A small sect of sea cultivators founded this hall in 640. Thôn Hải Môn's pirates burned it in 779, two years before the Pirate Purge destroyed them.

places.name: Dạ Vũ Tuyền
places.look: A spring among the riverside firs that wells up highest on rainy nights.
places.lore: A Water vein rises here. Liên Giang's people say a child bathed in it will never drown.

provinces.name: Đàm Ảnh
provinces.lore: The broad grass and bamboo country around Đàm Ảnh Thành, the island's old Cô Phàm city on its river mouth. It lives by fish, trade and the painters who come to paint the sky upside down in the pool. A Water vein lies under the land nearby, and some say it is why the pool never ripples.

places.name: Đàm Ảnh Thành
places.look: A low walled port city on the island's grassy shore where a river meets the sea. In its heart lies a large round pool, so still that the clouds and the city's roofs lie upside down in it, ringed with open pavilions where painters set up their easels.

places.name: Nhàn Vân Quán
places.look: A low abbey of grey roofs on the steppe shore, its long open galleries hung with silk scrolls of clouds that seem to drift when the sea wind moves them.
places.lore: Painters who came to Đàm Ảnh Thành for its pool founded the abbey in 905, under Lạc Hà Tông, and learned to paint with qi in the ink. Their scrolls can hold a reflection, hide a doorway or show a cloud that is not there. Every disciple must first paint the pool of Đàm Ảnh well enough that a heron tries to land on it.

places.name: Tinh Di Mạch
places.look: A hollow in the grass with a ring of still, dark pools, in which the stars can be seen to move across the night.
places.lore: A Water vein runs under the land here, and the painters of Đàm Ảnh say it feeds the stillness of the city's pool. Its name comes from the old line about things changing and stars moving through the autumns.

provinces.name: Nhạn Thanh
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grass around Nhạn Thanh Thành, the wool market of the western plain, where a river meets the sea. Its herders drive their flocks to the city, and its lake is where the wild geese come down each autumn. On the steppe shore stands Nhạn Trận Môn, the gate that drills the plain's levies.

places.name: Nhạn Thanh Thành
places.gloss: City of the Wild Geese's Cry
places.look: A walled city where a river meets the sea on the dry steppe coast, its grey roofs crowded around wool warehouses. Over the main gate rises a tower whose two upswept roofs spread like the wings of a goose in flight, and the wild geese pass over it in long formations each autumn.

places.name: Lạc Nhạn Hồ
places.look: A broad shallow lake in the grass with level sandy shores, covered each autumn with wild geese.
places.lore: The geese that fly in formation over Nhạn Thanh come down here to rest each autumn. As in the city, no one may shoot a goose on the lake, and the herders say the geese know it.

places.name: Nhạn Trận Môn
places.look: A walled gate seat on the steppe shore, its parade ground marked with lines of white stones in the shape of a goose formation.
places.lore: Survivors of Chiết Kích Nguyên founded the gate in 806 under Lạc Hà Tông, swearing that Lạc Hà's disciples would never again fight in loose order. Its disciples drill in formations modelled on the flight of the wild geese, and every spring they drill the plain's levies. Their banner shows a goose formation breaking off at the cold.

provinces.name: Tử Điện
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo round Tử Điện Thành, Lạc Hà's armoury city on the bay, where a river meets the sea. Its people are smiths, guards and fishers, the most disciplined in the bay. In the bamboo hills behind the city a Wood vein runs under a grove of purple-stemmed bamboo.

places.name: Tử Điện Thành
places.look: A walled port city on the bay where a river meets the sea, its grey roofs packed tight inside strong walls. Above them rises a tall armoury tower roofed in violet-glazed tile, and on clear evenings the faint violet shimmer of its ward array (trận pháp) hangs over the whole city.

places.name: Tử Trúc Mạch
places.look: A grove of purple-stemmed bamboo in the hills behind the city, its canes dark as old lacquer.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the grove, and its bamboo grows purple only here. The armoury of Tử Điện cuts it for arrow shafts and keeps a guard on the grove.

provinces.name: Tinh Hán
provinces.lore: Steppe and grassland around Tinh Hán Thành, Thiên Xu's port on the inland sea, where a river meets the shore. Farms and pasture feed the city, and the ore of Ngọc Hành goes out from its quays. A Water vein by the shore rises and falls with the tide.

places.name: Tinh Hán Thành
places.look: Thiên Xu's port on the inland sea sits where a river meets the shore, a walled grid of grey roofs behind a long curving breakwater. The breakwater is the reef itself: a line of great white arched ribs, the bones of the old sea-serpent, rising out of the water with stone packed between them. At night the harbour lamps and the Milky Way in the water make the city seem set among stars.

places.name: Triều Tịch Mạch
places.look: A pool in the steppe near the shore that rises and falls with the tide, though it does not touch the sea.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Water. Tinh Hán's formation masters know of it but have never drawn on it, saying a vein that keeps the sea's time will not keep a city's.

provinces.name: Lai Nghi
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grass around Phượng Minh's port city at the river mouth, with the broken walls of Vân Môn Thành upriver. Its people farm, herd and work the gulf trade. A fire vein under the steppe is said to stir when the nine tiers play at dawn.

places.name: Lai Nghi Thành
places.look: A walled port city at a river mouth on the dry eastern steppe, its harbour mole curving out into the gulf. On the mole rises a terrace of nine stepped stone tiers, each crowned with a bronze bell frame, so that the whole stair glints at sunrise. A faint shimmer over the walls marks the city's guardian array (hộ thành trận).

places.name: Vân Môn Thành
places.look: Low grass-grown walls on the river, broken into a rough square, with the stumps of towers at the corners. In the middle stands the one thing still upright: a tall frame of two carved stone pillars and a crossbeam, where the stone chime Vân Môn Khánh hung in the city's hall.

places.name: Cửu Tấu Mạch
places.look: A low ring of standing stones on the steppe outside the city, the grass inside it scorched brown.
places.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein. Lai Nghi's musicians say it warms when the welcome is played nine times at dawn; no one has proved otherwise.

provinces.name: Thu Trì
provinces.lore: The rich coastal lowland around Thu Trì Thành, where the river meets the sea below wooded hills: rice paddies, fish ponds and jungle on the slopes. Night rain on the hills fills the city's pools and the fields together, and the province lives on the port and the Night Rain Market. It is the Tower's richest holding, and its most watched.

places.name: Thu Trì Thành
places.look: A walled port city where a river meets the sea below wooded hills, built in steps so that tiers of square stone pools descend through its streets from the upper town to the harbour. After night rain on the hills every pool brims and spills into the next, and the whole city murmurs. Over the lower terraces hang the dark oiled-paper awnings of the Night Rain Market, and a guardian array (hộ thành trận) shimmers faintly on the walls.

places.name: Quế Hương Thang
places.look: A cluster of hot pools steams in the jungle under cassia trees, whose fallen bark floats on the water and scents the whole hollow.
places.lore: Buyers for the Night Rain Market come up from Thu Trì to bathe here by day, before the market opens at dark. The bathhouse keeper, like the innkeepers below, never asks a name.

places.name: Vũ Linh Đường
places.look: On a grassy hill above Thu Trì a long, low hall stands under deep eaves hung with hundreds of small bronze bells on chains, each ringing its own note as the rain strikes it.
places.lore: Vũ Linh Đường is a small school of array-makers (trận pháp sư) who build bell-and-chain warning arrays for the Tower's walls and roads; its founder was a smith who cast rain-chains for the Tower. It keeps the warding bells on the walls of Thu Trì Thành, and its disciples can tell from the bells alone where the rain, or a stranger, is falling.

provinces.name: Không Mông
provinces.lore: The valley mouth around Không Mông Thành: rice meadows, bamboo and broadleaf woods on the hills, nearly always under fine rain. Many of its families descend from the people of Lôi Trạch and still beat the thunder-day drums each spring. A drizzle-fed spirit spring above the city is shared by the Tower's resident disciples and the city's painters.

places.name: Không Mông Thành
places.look: A walled port city in a low valley mouth by the sea, almost always seen through fine hazy rain. Every street is roofed by long covered arcades of grey tile on red-painted posts, so that one can cross the whole city without getting wet. Above the arcades rise the older halls of Khải Lôi's time, their roof ridges capped in green bronze.

places.name: Vi Vũ Tuyền
places.look: In the meadow above Không Mông a clear spring rises in a stone basin, and a fine drizzle hangs over it even when the valley is dry.
places.lore: A Water (Thủy) vein shared, by long custom, between the Tower's resident disciples and the city's painters. The painters wet their ink stones here and say the drizzle never ruins a picture.

provinces.name: Ngũ Thải
provinces.lore: Grass, jungle and bamboo at the river mouth around the five-coloured port city. Its people glaze tile, fish and trade along the coast. A fire vein near the city is where Hùng Phần Vũ is said to have first sat as a boy.

places.name: Ngũ Thải Thành
places.look: A walled port city at a river mouth on the warm southern coast, its wards roofed in glazed tile of five colours, red, yellow, green, white and black, so that from the hills it looks like a bird's spread wing. A gate tower painted with a five-coloured bird faces the harbour.

places.name: Thải Vũ Mạch
places.look: A low grass rise outside the city walls, where a small shrine holds a red feather under glass.
places.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein. The city says Hùng Phần Vũ first sat here as a boy, and its young come to sit where he sat.

provinces.name: Lam Yên
provinces.lore: Forested foothills climbing to high ground below Thúy Vi Tông, inland and nearly always in haze. Carters, stallholders and herb growers live along the stair road of Lam Yên Thị. A wood spring below the market feeds the herb plots of the lower slopes.

places.name: Lam Yên Thị
places.look: A broad stone stair climbs from the valley into the mountain haze below Thúy Vi Tông, lined on both sides with stalls under indigo cloth awnings. On misty days the awnings fade into the haze one step at a time, so the market seems to climb into cloud.

places.name: Dưỡng Mộc Tuyền
places.look: A clear spring rises in a ring of unusually tall trees below the market stair, its runnels feeding terraced herb plots.
places.lore: Wood qi rises with the water, and herbs watered from it grow fast and strong. Lam Yên's herb growers share its water by an old rota.

provinces.name: Tùng Hạ
provinces.lore: Wide pine sea along the road to the palace, with Tùng Hạ Thị's ring market at its heart. Caravans, woodcutters and pilgrims fill its roads, and wolves follow the caravans in hard winters. Since 1191 the new Tuần Tùng Đường keeps the road watch from the hills above the market.

places.name: Tùng Hạ Thị
places.look: In a wide clearing under old pines, a market stands in a perfect ring: round stall-houses with low grey cone roofs set shoulder to shoulder around an open circle. A single gate in the ring opens onto the road through the pine sea.

places.name: Tuần Tùng Đường
places.look: On a pine-covered hill above the road, a long timber hall with a watchtower at each end, bows racked under the eaves and wolf pelts on the walls.
places.lore: Tuần Tùng Đường is a young sect of road wardens sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, founded after wolves followed the caravans to Tùng Hạ Thị in 1190. Its wardens guard the caravans through the pine sea with staff and bow, and take their fee in coin and salt.

places.name: Tùng Âm Mạch
places.look: On a hill above the ring market, a stand of pines sings in even the lightest wind, and the ground under them is warm.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under these pines, and pilgrims to the palace stop here to listen first. Tùng Đào's disciples say it is the vein that makes the pines sing.

provinces.name: Đào Sa
provinces.lore: Sand flats, bog and forest at the river mouth, around the stilt market of Đào Sa Thị. Its people wash gold, fish and work the landing. A poplar wood holds the dunes behind the flats.

places.name: Đào Sa Thị
places.look: Where the river spreads its sand into the sea, a market sprawls across the flats on stilts. Rows of wooden washing cradles stand in the shallows, rocked by washers in wide straw hats, and at low tide the whole flat glitters with fine gold. Along the landing lie the charred ribs of burned ferries, left where they sank.

places.name: Bạch Dương Lâm
places.look: A wood of tall white poplars on the dunes behind the sand flats, their leaves flickering silver in the sea wind.
places.lore: The poplars hold the dunes against the wind and keep the sand off the washing cradles. The gold-washers gather firewood here.

provinces.name: Tống Khách
provinces.lore: Forest and low mountains around the market where travellers leaving the frost coast are seen off. Its people sell furs, dried fish and warm wine for the road. The sword sage Tư Không Hạc Niên has lived here since 1130 and teaches no one.

places.name: Tống Khách Thị
places.look: A forest market strung along the road on a gentle rise, its stalls tucked under dark fir eaves. At the eastern end stands a small eight-sided farewell pavilion over a stone table, where a single cup is always set out full.

places.name: Bình Minh Hồ
places.look: A small lake in the mountains above the market, its still water catching the first light.
places.lore: Travellers leaving at dawn stop here for a last look. The lake is named from the poem: at dawn I see my guest off.

provinces.name: Tương Phùng
provinces.lore: Grass and dry steppe along the quay where the floating market of Tương Phùng Thị rides the tide. Its people are boatmen, stall-keepers and brokers who never know who the next ferry will bring. On the point beyond the market stands the empty hall of a school of wanderers that ended without an heir.

places.name: Tương Phùng Thị
places.look: A market built half on the water at the quay below Bình Thủy Môn: boats lashed side by side into a floating raft of stalls that rises and falls with the tide. Planks run between them, and faded green awnings drift like duckweed on the strait.

places.name: Phiêu Bồng Quán
places.look: A small roofless abbey on the steppe point, its walls whole but its doors gone and its courtyard full of wind-blown grass.
places.lore: Wanderers who would not settle founded a small school here in 860 and taught that a cultivator should belong to no place. In 1102 its last master died with no disciple willing to stay, and he left its books to Bình Thủy Môn. The abbey has stood empty since, and travellers waiting for the ferry still sleep in it.

places.name: Bình Tung Mạch
places.look: A shallow green pond in the grass behind the market, its surface thick with duckweed that drifts in rings with no wind to move it.
places.lore: A Water vein lies under the pond, and its qi wanders like the duckweed, never strongest in the same place two days running. Bình Thủy's disciples say it suits their sect better than any steady vein would.

provinces.name: Vật Hoa
provinces.lore: Dry steppe, red badlands and a river below Thiên Bảo Trai, around the market of the land's riches. Its people are traders, carters and caravan guards. Scorpions as long as a forearm live in the badland gullies, and the market sells their venom to alchemists.

places.name: Vật Hoa Thị
places.look: A busy open market on the dry steppe below Thiên Bảo Trai, rows of awnings around a central square. In the square stands a great bronze steelyard on a stone frame, taller than a house, where any trader may have goods weighed in public.

places.name: Hạt Vĩ Cương
places.look: A dry steppe ridge whose rocks are pocked with burrows and littered with cast-off shells.
places.lore: Spirit scorpions as long as a forearm live here. The venom gatherers of Vật Hoa Thị catch them at night with lamps and sell the venom to alchemists.

provinces.name: Hạc Đinh
provinces.lore: Steppe and grass where the river spreads into shallows below the sect, around the islet market of Hạc Đinh Thị. Its people trade pills, river fish and talismans among the cranes. An Earth vein lies under a long sandy isle in the shallows.

places.name: Hạc Đinh Thị
places.look: Where the river spreads into shallows below Lạc Hà's seat, the market (phường thị) sits on a scatter of sandbar islets joined by plank causeways, its stalls under reed awnings. White cranes stand in the shallows between the islets and do not move for the crowds.

places.name: Trường Châu Mạch
places.look: A long sandy isle in the shallows above the market, its steppe grass thick and green.
places.lore: An Earth vein lies under the isle, named for the old line about the long isle of the prince. The cranes of Hạc Đinh roost here at night, and the sect's disciples wade out to cultivate among them.

provinces.name: Thiên Quyền
provinces.lore: Mountain flanks and grassy steppe at the foot of Thiên Xu Tông's seat, around the market of Thiên Quyền Thị. Traders, weighers and carters live by the market, and a copper mine above it supplies the bronze for the market's weights. Every road to the seat passes through here, and every load is weighed.

places.name: Thiên Quyền Thị
places.look: At the foot of the Pivot's mountain, a square market of grey stone halls opens around a tall timber gantry from which hangs a giant bronze steelyard, its beam as long as a boat. Every large sale in the market is weighed on it in public view.

places.name: Hoàng Đồng Khoáng
places.look: A small mine of brassy, glittering ore high on the mountain, with a casting shed at the path's foot.
places.lore: Its copper is cast into the bronze weights of Thiên Quyền Thị. A weight cast here is tested against the standard before it leaves the shed.

places.name: Thạch Quyền Phong
places.look: A squat, flat-topped mountain above the market, shaped like the weight of a steelyard.
places.lore: The market's weighers say it is the counterweight that keeps the heart in balance. Its qi runs to Earth.

provinces.name: Thiều Âm
provinces.lore: A narrow river valley of bamboo at the foot of Phượng Minh's ridges, with bare rock rising steeply behind it. Its people make and sell instruments at Thiều Âm Thị and hire out as players for rites across the south. Since 1195 the palace has watched the market's musicians more closely than its traders.

places.name: Thiều Âm Thị
places.look: At the foot of Phượng Minh's ridges, a market of bamboo-roofed stalls lines a river among bamboo groves, and every lane is hung with curtains of bamboo flutes and pipes drying on strings, clicking and whistling in the wind. A raised music stage stands over the water.

places.name: Minh Cầm Phong
places.look: A sharp grey peak above the market, its face cut by long straight cracks like the strings of a zither.
places.lore: In a high wind the cracks hum, and Thiều Âm's makers climb it to tune by the sound. Its qi runs Kim (metal), hard and ringing.

provinces.name: Hạnh Hoa
provinces.lore: Mountain and dry steppe along the river below the Tower's southern road, with apricot orchards on the bank and bare rock above. The market at Hạnh Hoa Thị sells the flowers, felt and ore of the uplands, and the sick come to wait for the healer Giả Hồi Xuân. A tin mine and an old stockade of Khải Lôi's time stand in the hills over the road.

places.name: Hạnh Hoa Thị
places.look: A market town on the river below the southern road to Thính Vũ Lâu, built of deep, narrow lanes between tall grey-tile houses. From every eave hang woven baskets of apricot blossom (hạnh hoa), so after rain the lanes are roofed in pink and white. Apricot trees crowd the river bank behind the stalls.

places.name: Hắc Tích Khoáng
places.look: Low tunnels open at the foot of a mountain wall above the river, with heaps of dark, heavy tin ore by the sluices.
places.lore: Tin has been dug here since 720 and is sold in Hạnh Hoa Thị for the bronze of the Tower's rain-chains. The ore is washed in the river, and the water below the mine runs grey.

places.name: Quy Nhạn Phong
places.look: A red-brown badland peak above the apricot market, its crest notched like a gate.
places.lore: Wild geese fly through the notch each spring and autumn, and the market of Hạnh Hoa sets its seasons by them. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

places.name: Thạch Môn Trại
places.look: Two tall stone gate pillars stand alone on a mountain saddle over the road, with the outlines of a stockade wall in the grass around them.
places.lore: Khải Lôi Môn built the stockade to guard its western road, and the Tower kept it after the Gate fell. Once the Pivot's judgement on the Petal Shore had settled the west, the Tower let its garrison go, and only the gate pillars stand.

provinces.name: Quy Điểu
provinces.lore: Low pine forest running down to the shore around Quy Điểu Trấn, loud with birds every autumn. Townsfolk and woodsmen live by the pearl market, fowling and timber. The winter ice market draws pearl buyers from all three of Tùng Đào's lands.

places.name: Quy Điểu Trấn
places.look: A walled lakeside town of grey roofs whose shore is lined with rows of tall birch poles, each crowned with a straw nest-basket. In autumn every pole and roof ridge is crowded with returning birds; in winter the market tents stand out on the ice beyond the harbour wall.

places.name: Bách Điểu Lâm
places.look: A low pine and birch wood behind Quy Điểu Trấn whose every branch is crowded with birds in autumn, the ground white with droppings and feathers.
places.lore: The homing flocks rest here before settling on the town's nest poles. Fowlers take only what the town allows, and a feather-gatherer who robs a nest is fined a pearl.

provinces.name: Mục Ca
provinces.lore: Wooded hills and open grass run down to the sea around the sheepfolds of Mục Ca Thành. Herders and their flocks own the grass; the woods give firewood and a small spirit vein that Thúy Vi keeps for its disciples. On a hill west of the city stand the broken halls of a flute sect that once sang with the herders.

places.name: Mục Ca Thành
places.look: A walled city of low grey roofs sits on open coastal grassland, hunched against the wind. Around its walls a ring of round dry-stone sheepfolds lies across the grass like beads on a string, and at dusk the herders' songs carry from fold to fold.

places.name: Địch Thanh Viện
places.look: On a wooded hilltop the roofless halls of a small academy stand among trampled walls, flutes of bone still lying in the grass.
places.lore: A sect of flute cultivators founded by herders' children, sworn to Thúy Vi, who learned to call beasts as the herders called their flocks. In 1012 its master's flute drove a herd of spirit cattle mad, and they trampled the halls; the survivors went back to the folds of Mục Ca.

places.name: Bàn Căn Huyệt
places.look: In a wooded hollow the roots of a few huge old oaks coil over one another into a knot as tall as a house.
places.lore: Wood qi pools in the knot of roots, and Thúy Vi keeps the hollow for disciples posted to Mục Ca. Herders will not graze their flocks near it, saying the roots move at night.

provinces.name: Bạch Sa
provinces.lore: A coastal strip of firs and grass behind the white beach of Bạch Sa Trấn. The Thẩm clan rules the town and the fishing, and its woodcutters supply the net frames and boats. Since 1120 strangers come through asking about tides and streams, and the woods behind the beach are where they ask.

places.name: Bạch Sa Trấn
places.look: A small walled town of whitewashed walls and grey roofs sits on a beach of dazzling white sand. Along the shore stand long rows of whitewashed net-drying frames, so many that from the sea the town seems fenced in white lattice.

places.name: Sam Ảnh Lâm
places.look: Dark straight firs stand close behind the white beach, so their shadows reach the sand in the afternoon.
places.lore: The Thẩm clan cuts net poles and boat timber here and nowhere else. Strangers asking about the hidden valley's stream are often seen walking its paths, looking at the brooks.

provinces.name: Bách Diệp
provinces.lore: River-mouth forest and steep mountain around the cypress grid of Bách Diệp Trấn. The town lives by cypress resin and incense and the coast trade. A squared summit above the town is said to have been the students' model for the grid.

places.name: Bách Diệp Trấn
places.look: A walled town of grey roofs at a river mouth stands inside a vast grid of ancient cypresses planted in straight rows. From any approach the dark columns of the trees march out in lines, and the town sits at the centre of the pattern.

places.name: Kỳ Bàn Phong
places.look: A flat-topped rocky peak above the cypress town, its summit crossed by natural cracks in a square grid.
places.lore: Earth qi gathers in its stone, and Không Sơn's students are said to have laid out the cypress grid by copying its cracks. Players climb it to play a game on the summit.

provinces.name: Tiều Ca
provinces.lore: Forested ridges, limestone gorges and a small volcanic shoulder on the south coast, below Không Sơn's boundary stones. Woodcutters send timber down the flume of Tiều Ca Trấn, and miners dig alum from the volcanic rock. Their songs echo back from the gorge, but only below the stones.

places.name: Tiều Ca Trấn
places.look: A walled timber town of grey roofs sits on the coast below steep forested ridges. A long wooden log flume runs from the ridge tops straight down to the harbour, and logs rattle along it into the water.

places.name: Hồi Âm Cốc
places.look: A deep limestone valley opens onto the coast, its walls so close that every shout comes back three times.
places.lore: The woodcutters of Tiều Ca sing here freely, for it lies below the boundary stones. Their songs echo up the gorge and, they say, reach the old academy anyway.

places.name: Phàn Thạch Khoáng
places.look: Pale altered rock on a volcanic shoulder is cut into pits, with leaching vats and white crusts below them.
places.lore: Miners dig alum stone and boil it for dyers and tanners along the coast. Thúy Vi's alchemists buy the purest crystals to clear their pill waters.

provinces.name: Lộc Minh
provinces.lore: Low river forest and coast around Lộc Minh Trấn, the carvers' town held by Lãng Đào Môn. Its people carve, ferry and fish. Deep in its pines lie the clawed walls of Hổ Khiếu Trấn, and giant otters hold the river bend below the town.

places.name: Lộc Minh Trấn
places.look: A walled town of grey roofs lies on a low river mouth at the forest's edge, every beam end of its timber houses carved. At the end of its ferry pier stands a life-sized stag carved from pine, head raised as if calling across the water.

places.name: Hổ Khiếu Trấn
places.look: Deep in the pine sea, on a river bend, the walls of a small town have sunk under moss and young trees. Its timber watchtower lies toppled across the gate, scored with claw marks as long as a man is tall.

places.name: Cự Thát Chử
places.look: Low sandbars in a river bend below Lộc Minh, littered with fish bones and slick slides into the water.
places.lore: Otters as long as boats hunt the river bend and steal from the ferry nets. Lãng Đào's ferrymen toss them a fish as they pass, and the otters let them by.

provinces.name: Cổ Độ
provinces.lore: Hill forest and bamboo along the southern river around Cổ Độ Thành and its ferry stair. Its people ferry, smith and drag the old chain links of Thiết Tỏa Quan from the river. A bamboo spirit vein lies in the hills, and an older iron town stands empty upslope.

places.name: Cổ Độ Thành
places.look: A walled city stands among bamboo groves on the bank of the southern river, where a broad stone ferry stair runs down into the water. At the top of the stair, set upright on a stone plinth, stands a single huge rusted iron link from a sunken chain, taller than a man.

places.name: Luyện Thiết Trấn
places.look: On a hillside above the river, the slumped stone bellies of old smelting furnaces stand among pines, slag heaps grown over with moss.
places.lore: This town smelted iron for Tùng Đào, and its furnaces made much of the chain for Thiết Tỏa Quan. After the War of the Pivot the palace stopped buying iron, and within a generation the town was empty.

places.name: Trúc Căn Mạch
places.look: A bamboo grove on a hillside above Cổ Độ grows taller and greener than any around it, its stems creaking in the still air.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the grove, and its bamboo grows a man's height in a night in spring. The smiths of Cổ Độ cut their tongs' handles from it.

provinces.name: Hà Bạn
provinces.lore: River forest around Hà Bạn Trấn and its herb mills, which answer to Thải Chi Cốc. Its people fish, grind herbs and ship them downriver. Upslope lie the silted streets of Cựu Hà Trấn, left dry when the river changed course.

places.name: Hà Bạn Trấn
places.look: A low riverside town whose fishing lanes all end at the water. At its upstream corner a great timber waterwheel turns beside a mill house, grinding roots from Thải Chi Cốc into powder, and its creak carries to the road. Herb sacks stand stacked on the short jetties, waiting for boats.

places.name: Cự Miết Chử
places.look: Muddy shoals in a slow bend of the river, where flat leathery shells as wide as doors bask in the sun and slide into the water at a footstep.
places.lore: Giant softshell turtles live in the bend and snap at the oars of passing boats. Hà Bạn's fishermen go wide of the shoals, and alchemists pay well for a shell.

places.name: Cựu Hà Trấn
places.look: On a dry rise, the silted streets of a small town lie under grass, with a stone landing stair that ends in a meadow.
places.lore: A town on the old course of the river, left dry when the river changed course. Its people moved to the new bank, and Hà Bạn Trấn grew there.

provinces.name: Lâm Hạ
provinces.lore: Shaded beech and pine forest around the granary town of Lâm Hạ Trấn. Its people are granary-keepers, coopers and rat-catchers. The giant rats of a knoll nearby are the reason the granaries stand on stone staddles.

places.name: Lâm Hạ Trấn
places.look: The town sits so deep in the shade of old beeches that its roofs are green with moss even in summer. Between the houses stand round timber granaries raised on squat stone staddles shaped like mushrooms, so that no rat can climb them. At noon the lanes are cool and dim, and smell of grain dust.

places.name: Thử Vương Cương
places.look: A knoll riddled with rat holes the width of a man's arm, its grass stripped and grain husks heaped at the burrow mouths.
places.lore: Giant rats live here and raid the granaries of Lâm Hạ whenever a staddle cracks. The town's rat-catchers hunt them with terriers and smoke.

provinces.name: Bích Khê
provinces.lore: Forested hills around the green brook of Bích Khê Trấn, with a few steppe clearings on the high ground. Jade-pickers and carvers live by the brook, woodcutters by the hills. Downstream the brook runs through a stand of firs that the town forbids anyone to fell.

places.name: Bích Khê Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on a brook so green it looks dyed. Below the walls the stream runs over shallow stone weirs where jade-pickers kneel, sorting pebbles into baskets by colour. Polishing wheels hum in the workshops along the main street.

places.name: Khê Sam Lâm
places.look: Straight red-barked firs stand in the shallows of the green brook, their roots knotted like knees above the water.
places.lore: Bích Khê Trấn forbids felling these firs, since their roots hold the brook bed where the jade pebbles lie. Carvers say the best stones are found where the knees are thickest.

provinces.name: Thanh Bách
provinces.lore: Rolling forest and steppe on the northern road around Thanh Bách Thành. Its farms grow wheat and millet on the clearings, and ore carts from the southern mountains roll through it to the coast. The old cypress wood north of the city gives the city its name and its coffins.

places.name: Thanh Bách Thành
places.look: A walled city of grey roofs and dark, narrow cypresses on the northern road, a cypress standing over every courtyard. Outside its north wall lies a small round crater pond, glassy black at the rim, where a star fell in 980. Ore carts and officials' carriages pass through its gates all day.

places.name: Cổ Bách Lâm
places.look: A dark wood of ancient cypresses north of Thanh Bách Thành, their trunks twisted and grey and their scent heavy in the air.
places.lore: Thanh Bách cuts its coffin wood here, one tree for each official who dies in office. The oldest trees are tied with red cord and may never be cut.

provinces.name: Hòe Âm
provinces.lore: River forest between the sea and the ice mountains, crossed by the old locust avenue that carries the hermitage's supplies uphill. Hunters, fishers and carters live here and answer to Lê Hoa Am. Every hunter still looks for the sealed cave with the sword's cold light that a man of the town found in 930 and lost again.

places.name: Hòe Âm Trấn
places.look: A small harbour town where a river reaches the sea, and from its back gate an avenue of ancient locust trees climbs toward the mountains, their crowns meeting overhead in a green tunnel. Fishing boats and the hermitage's supply carts share one narrow quay. In early summer the locust blossom drops on the road like pale snow.

places.name: Hào Trư Cương
places.look: A low forested rise where the bark of every trunk is torn and black quills as long as arrows lie in the leaf litter.
places.lore: A spirit porcupine the size of an ox lives here and throws its quills like darts. Hòe Âm's hunters buy the quills for fletching and never go for the beast itself.

places.name: Tầm Kiếm Đường
places.look: A long timber hall with a stone hearth stands on a wooded bluff over the sea, its walls hung with mountain maps marked in red.
places.lore: A Tiêu-clan hunter turned away from Lê Hoa Am's gate founded this hall in 1162 to take the men the hermitage will not. Its members hunt, guide and search the mountain for the sealed cave of 930, and Lê Hoa Am tolerates them under Băng Tâm's licence.

provinces.name: Hồi Lan
provinces.lore: Steppe running to the desert coast behind the hooked breakwater of Hồi Lan Thành. Southern ships trade here for wool, salt and northern furs. A warm spring in the steppe is where the merchants bathe off the road dust.

places.name: Hồi Lan Thành
places.look: A harbour city on the desert coast, built behind a long curved breakwater that hooks out into the sea and turns the waves back on themselves. Sand-coloured walls enclose low warehouses under pale grey roofs. Ships from the south crowd the still water inside the hook.

places.name: Ôn Thạch Thang
places.look: Warm water fills a ring of smooth stones in the steppe, steaming in the cold mornings.
places.lore: Hồi Lan's merchants bathe here to wash off the road. The spring's mild Fire qi is good for joints stiffened by the desert cold.

provinces.name: Mộc Lan
provinces.lore: Flat forest on the frost coast around Mộc Lan Thành, Băng Tâm's younger port. Its people trade furs, timber and live beasts from Vô Tung Lâm. The fallen gate of Hàn Giang Môn lies in the snow nearby.

places.name: Mộc Lan Thành
places.look: A walled harbour city on the flat frost coast, its grey roofs low against the sea wind. A double row of old magnolia trees runs the length of the harbour wall, and in spring their white blossoms line the quay like snow that will not melt. Inland, the white cone of Sương Diễm Sơn stands over the city.

places.name: Hàn Giang Môn
places.look: A broken sect seat on the frost coast: a stone gate arch fallen on its side and half buried in snow, behind it the stumps of halls stepping up a low bank. A fishing rod carved along the fallen lintel shows where the wind has swept the snow away.

places.name: Xuân Hàn Lâm
places.look: A forest of fir and wild magnolia, where snow lingers among the white blossoms in spring.
places.lore: Mộc Lan's people come here in spring to see the magnolias. The cold lingers longest in this wood.

provinces.name: Kê Minh
provinces.lore: Grassy steppe and forest on the frost coast around Kê Minh Trấn. Its fishers set out at the first cockcrow and its herders graze sheep on the grass. A dew-fed Wood vein lies inland.

places.name: Kê Minh Trấn
places.look: A small walled port town on the grassy frost coast, low grey roofs around a single harbour. Above its gate stands a tall pole topped by a bronze rooster, green with age, that turns with the wind.

places.name: Hiểu Lộ Mạch
places.look: A meadow on the coastal steppe that is soaked with dew every dawn, even in the dry months, its grass greener than the land around it.
places.lore: A Wood vein lies under the meadow and draws the dew. Kê Minh's herders graze their lambs here, and they drive them out at the first cockcrow so the grass is still wet when they eat.

provinces.name: Xích Ngạn
provinces.lore: Red cliffs and rolling grass on the island's high coast, the land of the rust-red sails. Its people quarry and grind the red rock for pigment and fish from the cove below the cliff stair. On the headland stands the ruin of the hall where Cô Phàm's watchers once waited for the fleet.

places.name: Xích Ngạn Trấn
places.look: A small walled town atop red cliffs on the island's east coast, its grey roofs bright against the rust-red rock. A long stair cut into the cliff face zigzags down to a cove where the boats are drawn up.

places.name: Sài Quần Nguyên
places.look: Open red-earthed grass above the cliffs, crossed by worn trails and littered with old bones.
places.lore: Packs of rust-red spirit dholes hunt the grass inland of Xích Ngạn, the colour of the rock they run over. The townsfolk drive their goats in at dusk and keep fires on the cliff stair.

places.name: Vọng Phàm Quán
places.gloss: Abbey of the Watch for Sails
places.look: A broken hall of red stone on the steppe headland, its roof fallen in and a stone platform facing the open sea.
places.lore: Cô Phàm Các built this watch hall in 430 for its watchers to call the fleet home. After the fleet was lost in 705 the last watchers kept the vigil for three more years, then went down to Xích Ngạn and did not come back. The townsfolk say a lamp is sometimes seen on the platform on stormy nights.

provinces.name: Hải Yến
provinces.lore: Flat grass coast with patches of jungle, where the sea swallows nest under the town's double eaves. Families here own eaves the way others own fields and sell the nests to alchemists. In the jungle behind the town a Wood vein runs under the shade where the swallows hunt insects at dusk.

places.name: Hải Yến Trấn
places.look: A fishing town of low grey roofs on the flat island shore. Every house wears deep double eaves, and under them the sea swallows' nests cluster so thickly that the eaves look whitewashed; at dusk the air above the town is a whirl of birds.

places.name: Lục Âm Mạch
places.look: A dim stand of jungle behind the town where the canopy closes overhead and the air is cool and green even at noon.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the shade, and the sea swallows of Hải Yến hunt the insects that swarm over it at dusk. The town's nest harvesters rest here at midday and say they never grow sick.

provinces.name: Triều Âm
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass around Lạc Hà Tông's own walled harbour at the river mouth, where the bored breakwater sings with the tide. Its people are sailors, customs men and fishers, and Lạc Hà's ships call here first. Crocodiles bask on the shoals upriver, and the city's boatmen keep to the far bank.

places.name: Triều Âm Thành
places.look: A walled city on the island's western shore at a river mouth, grey roofs stepping up from the water. Along its sea front runs a stone breakwater bored with round holes that moan and sing as the tide pushes through.

places.name: Ngạc Bối Chử
places.look: Muddy jungle shoals on the river upstream of the city, where long grey backs lie motionless in the shallows.
places.lore: Spirit crocodiles bask here, some longer than a river boat. Triều Âm's boatmen keep to the far bank and throw them the fish offal from the market, which keeps them fat and lazy.

provinces.name: Thanh Điền
provinces.lore: Forest and fields so wide around Thanh Điền Trấn that its farmers ride to work. The town answers to Mục Vân Trang and holds a horse fair on the night its head was born. On the coast lie the ruins of Di Hà Trấn, a river town whose river left it.

places.name: Thanh Điền Trấn
places.look: A small walled market town in a sea of bright green fields that run to the horizon. Outside its gate stretches a long row of hitching rails where the farmers' horses wait, since the fields are too far to walk.

places.name: Di Hà Trấn
places.look: A ring of grass-grown walls on the coast with a stone river quay that now faces a dry meadow.
places.lore: Boatmen built the town in 430 on the plain's widest river, the same river that once ran past Chu Tân's ford. The river wandered away over the years, and by 860 the quay faced only grass and the last boatmen had left. Herders now shelter their flocks in its walls.

places.name: Thanh Miêu Mạch
places.look: A wood of young trees among the fields, where the seedlings always sprout a fortnight before the rest.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the wood, and the farmers of Thanh Điền bring their seed rice here to sprout. Mục Vân Trang lets them, as long as they keep their horses out.

provinces.name: Thảo Đường
provinces.lore: Farms, fish ponds and forest round Thảo Đường Thành, the granary of the western plain. Its people grow rice and hemp and raise fish and ducks in the grass-banked ponds. On the coast lies Dã Độ Trấn, the older ferry town that emptied when the city was built.

places.name: Thảo Đường Thành
places.look: A walled city on the flat coastal plain, its grey roofs low among farms. Outside the walls lies a chequerboard of grass-banked ponds, each a square of sky, with fish and ducks raised in every one.

places.name: Bảo Thụ Lâm
places.look: A wood of tall old trees between the fish ponds, their autumn leaves so bright they look lacquered.
places.lore: The city's first farmers left the wood standing as a windbreak for the ponds. Families of Thảo Đường call a promising child a jewel tree after it, from the old saying.

places.name: Dã Độ Trấn
places.look: Roofless houses on the grassy shore beside a silted landing, where a rotten ferry boat lies across the mud.
places.lore: Ferrymen founded the town in 500 on the coast creek. When Thảo Đường Thành rose in 680 its trade drew the ferrymen away, the landing silted, and by 712 only the boat was left. The coast says the boat turns on its own when the tide comes in.

provinces.name: Ngư Lương
provinces.lore: Forest and grass where a plain river spills into the sea through the great zigzag weir. Its families keep the fish of their own stretch of weir. Upstream a white elm wood gives the timber for the weir's frames.

places.name: Ngư Lương Trấn
places.look: A small walled town where a plain river spills into the sea. Across the river mouth runs a great zigzag weir of stone and bamboo, the largest on the plain, its traps glinting with fish.

places.name: Bạch Du Lâm
places.look: A wood of pale-barked elms on the grass upstream of the weir, cut in rows and growing back in rows.
places.lore: The fishers of Ngư Lương cut its elms for the weir's frames and replant one for each they fell. Each stretch of weir has its own rows of trees.

provinces.name: Liễu Ngạn
provinces.lore: Grass and forest on a flooding river behind the willow levee. Its people farm the flood land and beat the drum when the river passes the red mark. Giant spirit turtles haul out on the river shoals, and the levee guards keep an eye on them as well as on the water.

places.name: Liễu Ngạn Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on a river through flat grassland, set behind a high earthen levee. On the levee stands a tall stone flood-pillar cut with the marks of every great flood, the highest painted red; willows line the bank on either side.

places.name: Bạch Miết Chử
places.look: Grassy shoals on the river where huge flat shells lie in the sun like stepping stones.
places.lore: Spirit soft-shelled turtles as wide as a door haul out here. Their bite takes off a hand, and the levee guards of Liễu Ngạn chase them back into the river when they come near the levee.

provinces.name: Hòa Phong
provinces.lore: Almost all open grass on the bay coast, swept by the gentle sea breeze. Its people keep guesthouses for the sick and fish the bay. An orchid-scented Wood vein in the grass inland is where its healers sit before they treat the gravely ill.

places.name: Hòa Phong Trấn
places.look: A small port town on the open bay coast, its grey roofs low and airy. On every roof stands a tall woven wind-scoop turned toward the sea, so the whole town seems to lean into the breeze.

places.name: Huệ Phong Mạch
places.look: A hollow in the open grass where wild orchids grow and the breeze carries their scent toward the town.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the hollow, and the healers of Hòa Phong sit here before they treat the gravely ill. They say the breeze over it carries its qi to the sick.

provinces.name: Ngũ Cốc
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo round Ngũ Cốc Thành, the bay's grain port. Its people are guildsmen, porters and the descendants of Kim Cốc merchants. Spirit rats as large as dogs burrow on the rise behind the granaries, and every grain guild pays a rat-catcher.

places.name: Ngũ Cốc Thành
places.look: A walled port city on the bay coast, its quay lined with granaries. Along the waterfront stands a row of tall round grain towers, each roofed differently for its grain, with wooden chutes running down to the ships.

places.name: Thạc Thử Cương
places.look: A low grassy rise behind the granaries, honeycombed with burrows as wide as a barrel.
places.lore: Spirit rats as large as dogs burrow here and raid the grain towers at night, as in the old song of the great rats. Every grain guild of Ngũ Cốc pays its own rat-catcher and blames the others' rats.

provinces.name: Phong Lâm
provinces.lore: Red maple forest where the river meets the sea, round the harbour town kept by Nam Phố Đường. Its people are clerks, timber hands and fishers, and the swallows nest on the Tạ clan hall. Great owls live in the maples and are left alone, since they keep the town's granaries clear of rats.

places.name: Phong Lâm Trấn
places.look: A walled harbour town among red maples where a river meets the sea, its grey-tile roofs half hidden in leaves. At its centre stands the old Tạ clan hall, its deep eaves lined end to end with the mud nests of swallows, so that in spring the hall seems to breathe birds.

places.name: Phong Kiêu Lâm
places.look: A dark stand of old maples above the town where pellets and bones lie thick under the branches.
places.lore: Spirit owls as large as a child roost here and hunt the river land by night. They take rats from the granaries and the occasional lamb, and the townsfolk count the bargain fair.

provinces.name: Tang Ma
provinces.lore: Forest and grass along the river, planted with mulberry and blue-flowering hemp around Tang Ma Thành. Its people weave silk and twist the ropes the ferrymen trust. A wild mulberry wood gives the silkworms of the poorest families their leaves, and since 1187 the alchemists of Yên Quang Các have kept their furnaces there.

places.name: Tang Ma Thành
places.look: A walled city on a river among endless rows of mulberry and blue-flowering hemp. Its river channels are crossed not by stone but by a lattice of swaying hemp-rope bridges slung between timber towers, which hum when the wind blows. Rope walks run along the outer wall, where long strands are twisted under open sheds.

places.name: Yên Quang Các
places.look: Low furnace-houses of grey tile and unpainted timber stand under old wild mulberry trees, and a thin line of sweet steam goes up at dusk. In summer the ground beneath the trees is purple with fallen fruit.
places.lore: Yên Quang Các, the Pavilion of the Hazy Light, is a minor sect of alchemists (luyện đan) sworn to Lạc Hà Tông. In 1187 its head Tào Mộ Tử moved the furnaces and beds here, carrying the founder's furnace with its coals lit so that the fire never went out. The mulberry gives three medicines, the leaf, the root bark and the mistletoe that grows on it. The poorest families of Tang Ma still pick leaves here for their silkworms, and the old seat on the steppe is now the Dusk Field.

provinces.name: Thạch Kiều
provinces.lore: Rolling steppe and desert edge on a river, around Thạch Kiều Thành, the first city of the heart. Caravans from four coasts meet here, and the farms on the river flats feed the city. Out on the desert edge lie the buried halls of Minh Sa Các, a small sect the sand took back.

places.name: Thạch Kiều Thành
places.look: The first city of the heart sits astride a river in rolling steppe, a walled grid of grey roofs crossing the water on one great stone bridge. The bridge wears its age plainly: its old central arches are dark, almost black, while the wide new deck and outer arches added in 1050 are pale grey. Bell towers stand at both ends.

places.name: Minh Sa Các
places.look: The roof ridge of a pavilion standing out of a dune on the desert edge, its halls filled with sand to the eaves.
places.lore: A small sect that studied the humming of the dunes was founded here in 560. The dunes crept over its halls for three centuries, and in 893 its last disciples gave up digging and went to Thạch Kiều.

places.name: Kiều Cơ Mạch
places.look: A low swell of steppe where bare grey bedrock breaks through the grass in smooth domes.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, solid and slow. The builders of Thạch Kiều's bridge are said to have cut its first stones here.

provinces.name: Song Kiều
provinces.lore: Grassland, forest and mountain along the river road around Song Kiều Trấn, where the miners' ore has been weighed in public since 235. Carters, assayers and the Ôn clan's toll keepers live here. A warm spring on the grassland is where the carters rest their oxen.

places.name: Song Kiều Trấn
places.look: A walled town on the river road where two humpbacked stone bridges cross the river side by side, one for carts going in and one for carts going out, with a small toll house on a pier between them. In the square behind stands a row of open ore scales under a long tiled roof.

places.name: Xuân Thủy Thang
places.look: A warm, shallow spring in the grassland with stone troughs where oxen stand.
places.lore: Carters rest their oxen here after the ore road. The Ôn clan charges nothing for it, which surprises everyone who knows the clan.

places.name: Chân Kim Các
places.look: A two-storey stone pavilion in a forest clearing, its yard full of crucibles and its doors bound in bronze.
places.lore: Assayers and refiners of spirit ore founded this pavilion in 980 beside Song Kiều's open scales, sworn to Thiên Xu. They test and refine ore for the mines of Ngọc Hành, and their stamp on an ingot is taken at Thiên Quyền Thị without a second weighing.

provinces.name: Mạch Điền
provinces.lore: Flat wheat and pasture where a river meets the gulf, with dry steppe inland and a fringe of jungle on the shore. Its wheat has fed Phượng Minh's palace since 530. Farmers soak their aching backs in a warm spring by the sea after harvest.

places.name: Mạch Điền Trấn
places.look: A walled town in flat wheat country where a river meets the gulf, dominated by one tall granary raised on a ring of mushroom-shaped staddle stones, its steep thatched roof the highest thing on the plain. Wheat barges tie up at a timber quay below.

places.name: Hải Ôn Tuyền
places.look: A warm spring bubbling up among rocks at the edge of the wheat, where its water runs out into the gulf.
places.lore: The wheat farmers of Mạch Điền soak here after harvest, and the water tastes faintly of salt.

provinces.name: Thanh Khê
provinces.lore: Bamboo hills falling to the gulf around Phượng Minh's port city, with a clear brook running through them to the harbour. Its people build boats, cut bamboo and work the ships of the coast. Above the city lies an empty town the fever took in 812, and the harbour of healing still remembers it.

places.name: Thanh Khê Thành
places.look: Phượng Minh's port on the gulf sits where a clear brook runs into the sea, a walled grid of grey roofs around a wide harbour. All along the harbour wall hangs an unbroken row of red lanterns, lit every night, so from far out at sea the city shows as a glowing line on the water.

places.name: Kim Trúc Lâm
places.look: A hill forest of golden-yellow bamboo above the port, the canes glowing in the evening light.
places.lore: Thanh Khê's shipwrights cut its canes for masts and lantern poles; every lantern on the harbour wall hangs from golden bamboo.

places.name: Cựu Khê Trấn
places.look: Grass-grown walls in the bamboo above the port, with a row of small grave mounds outside the gate.
places.lore: A town of bamboo cutters built ten years after the port, emptied by a fever in 812 that killed half its people before Lễ Tuyền's healers came. The survivors moved down to Thanh Khê and never went back up.

provinces.name: Hoàng Vân
provinces.lore: Rice land and oak forest on the river where the plain lies flattest, around Phượng Minh's granary city. Its farmers bring their harvest to the round granaries by barge. Spirit boars come out of the forest at harvest, and the granary keepers pay hunters to meet them.

places.name: Hoàng Vân Thành
places.look: A broad walled city on the river where the rice plain lies flattest, crowned inside its walls by a ring of tall round granaries capped in yellow-glazed tile. At harvest a haze of rice chaff hangs over the roofs and turns gold in the low sun, which gives the city its name. Grain barges crowd the river quay below the granary gates.

places.name: Dã Trư Lâm
places.look: Oak forest with its floor torn up in long furrows and the trunks rubbed bare and muddy.
places.lore: Spirit boars with tusks like sickles live here and raid the rice at harvest. Hoàng Vân's keepers pay a bounty for every pair of tusks.

provinces.name: Đạo Hương
provinces.lore: Rice fields and woods running from a river to the gulf, with steep hills behind. The Vương family has planted a new field here every generation since 520. A clear lake in the woods reflects the hills so exactly that the Vương paint it on their betrothal letters.

places.name: Đạo Hương Trấn
places.look: A small walled town of grey-tile roofs in a sea of rice, the smell of ripening grain heavy on the river wind. Along the field road outside the east gate stands a long row of carved stone stakes, one for each generation of the Vương family, each beside the paddy that generation planted.

places.name: Minh Kính Hồ
places.look: A still lake in the woods behind the rice fields, reflecting the hills so exactly that the shore line is hard to see.
places.lore: The Vương of Đạo Hương paint it on their betrothal letters; the one sent to the Tạ in 1199 bore it too.

provinces.name: Lục Dã
provinces.lore: Green meadows and steppe on the gulf with hills to the west, given to Lễ Tuyền Phái for its herb gardens in 662. Its people grow and dry healing herbs. A millstone town in the hills above was buried by a landslide in 1062.

places.name: Lục Dã Trấn
places.look: A walled town in open green meadows, ringed by a chequer of square herb beds in a dozen shades of green, each bordered by a low stone channel of spring water. In the morning the beds steam faintly and smell of mint and bitter root.

places.name: Bạc Hà Đàm
places.look: A spring-fed pool in the meadows, its shallow edges thick with wild mint.
places.lore: Lễ Tuyền's herb growers draw water for the beds from it, and the meadows smell of its mint after rain.

places.name: Thạch Ma Trấn
places.look: Half-buried walls in a landslide scar on the hillside, with round millstones lying among the rubble.
places.lore: A quarry town that cut millstones for the rice mills of the plain. In the great rains of 1062 the hillside slid and buried it in a night; the survivors went down to Lục Dã.

provinces.name: Bình Dã
provinces.lore: An open plain cleared from the forest, ringed by bamboo and broadleaf woods, where rain comes less often than anywhere else in the south. Forest folk bring their wet harvests to dry on the great yard of Bình Dã Trấn, and the plain grows sesame and millet that would rot elsewhere. In the bamboo south of the town stand the empty halls of a school that left when the Tower opened its doors to the ma đạo.

places.name: Bình Dã Trấn
places.look: A walled town in an open plain cleared from the forest, its grey roofs gathered around a huge paved yard of sun-baked brick. On dry days the yard is covered edge to edge with mats of drying tea, herbs, cloth and grain brought in from the wet country around.

places.name: Mãng Đằng Lâm
places.look: A dark patch of broadleaf forest north of the drying yards, so thick with hanging vines that it is hard to tell which of them are moving.
places.lore: Spirit-touched rock pythons as long as a ferry raft lair here and slide out onto Bình Dã's warm yard on the rare dry nights. The yard-keepers sweep it with long poles before dawn.

places.name: Trúc Ẩn Viện
places.look: Deep in a bamboo grove, a walled compound of grey-tile halls stands roofless, its courtyards grown solid with bamboo that has split the paving.
places.lore: Trúc Ẩn Viện was a small righteous (chính đạo) school of scholars and zither players under the Tower's lordship. When the Night Rain Edict opened the Tower to the ma đạo arts, its masters packed their books and walked north in 906, and the bamboo took the halls they left.

provinces.name: Xuân Thảo
provinces.lore: A small, rich stretch of river meadow, bamboo and jungle around Xuân Thảo Thành, on the forest half of the Petal Shore that the Pivot gave the Tower. The burned orchards are long grown over, and peaches still fruit here and there among the banana trees. Farmers plant a peach stone at the corner of every new field for luck.

places.name: Xuân Thảo Thành
places.look: A city on a river at the forest's edge, enclosed by thick earthen walls whose tops are capped with living turf, green even in the dry months. Inside, grey-tile roofs stand among young trees, and in the meadows outside the walls old blackened stumps lie grown over with grass.

places.name: Thanh Hoàng Lâm
places.look: Along the river near Xuân Thảo Thành, giant bamboo grows so straight and close that from the water it looks like a green wall.
places.lore: The city cuts its scaffolding and water pipes here, and every pole taken must be replaced with a planted shoot. Charred stumps from the Petal Shore fighting still stand among the bamboo.

provinces.name: Lãng Hoa
provinces.lore: Grass and wind-bitten steppe on the coast around Lãng Hoa Thành, at the mouth of a river. Its fishers and salt-boilers came down to the shore after the Pirate Purge, and its children still race the spray along the sea wall. A spirit eye of sea air on the steppe behind the city is the province's one cultivation ground.

places.name: Lãng Hoa Thành
places.look: A walled port city on a dry, wind-bitten steppe coast at the mouth of a river. Its sea wall is pierced with rows of carved stone blowholes, and when the waves strike, white spray bursts from them in plumes like flowers along the whole waterfront. Behind the wall, grey roofs climb a low rise toward a watch hall.

places.name: Hải Khí Nhãn
places.look: On the dry steppe behind Lãng Hoa a shallow salt hollow glitters white, and the air over it smells of the sea though the shore is out of sight.
places.lore: A small spirit eye of Water (Thủy) qi carried inland on the sea wind. The salt-boilers of Lãng Hoa say it is where the spray flowers go when they vanish.

provinces.name: Vọng Hải
provinces.lore: Coastal bamboo and grass at a river mouth below low sea cliffs, held by Xuyên Lâm Môn. Its people fish, cut bamboo and keep the cliff watchtowers manned, though no pirate has come in centuries. Armoured scale-beasts dig their burrows in the bamboo behind the town.

places.name: Vọng Hải Trấn
places.look: A walled town in coastal bamboo at a river mouth, below a line of low sea cliffs. Along the cliff tops stand tall watchtowers with stone footings and bamboo upper storeys, each with a signal frame looking out over the gulf.

places.name: Lân Giáp Cốc
places.look: A bamboo hollow behind the town honeycombed with burrows, the earth around them scored by heavy claws and littered with shed scales.
places.lore: Pangolin-kind beasts with spirit-hard scales burrow here and dig up the anthills of the coast. Xuyên Lâm's guides teach their apprentices to roll one over with a staff without being cut.

provinces.name: Phong Đăng
provinces.lore: Fertile river meadows, bamboo and jungle on the coast, the best grain land of the Tower's south. The Lục family's carts are weighed first on the great steelyard each year, and the Tower collects its grain tax here before anywhere else. Thunder bamboo grows in the groves, and in the hills above, a small school calls the rain for the harvest.

places.name: Phong Đăng Trấn
places.look: A walled harbour town in fertile river meadows by the sea, its fields heavy with grain. In its main gate hangs a huge wooden steelyard balance, its beam as long as a boat, where grain carts are weighed for the tax before they enter.

places.name: Lôi Trúc Lâm
places.look: A low coastal grove of thick-stemmed bamboo, where new shoots stand in dense ranks after every storm.
places.lore: Thunder bamboo sprouts at the sound of the first spring thunder, and its shoots hold a spark of it. Phong Đăng digs the shoots for the table and sells the oldest stems to the Tower's smiths for quenching rods.

places.name: Cốc Vũ Quán
places.look: On a bamboo hill above Phong Đăng an open-sided abbey stands beside a stone rain altar, and bamboo gutters carry water from its roofs down to small terraces of spirit rice.
places.lore: Cốc Vũ Quán is a small school that calls the rain for the farmers of the south and grows spirit rice (linh mễ) on its terraces. Each year it sends a priest to bless the first cart on Phong Đăng's great steelyard, and it has kept clear of the Tower's ma đạo arts without ever refusing them aloud.

provinces.name: Thạch Cơ
provinces.lore: Flat grass and steppe on the northern gulf around the port that grew from the fleet's jetty. Its people work the ships and the shipyard. An earth vein under the shore is said to be why the jetty stood for four centuries before the storm.

places.name: Thạch Cơ Thành
places.look: A walled harbour city on a flat stretch of coast, built around a long stone jetty that juts far out into the gulf. Most of the jetty is grey, sea-worn stone, but its outer end has been rebuilt in bright red stone that stands out against the water.

places.name: Bàn Thạch Huyệt
places.look: A flat shelf of bedrock in the grass behind the harbour, with a ring of old fleet mooring stones set round it.
places.lore: A Thổ (earth) vein lies under the rock. Sailors say it is why the old jetty stood for four centuries.

provinces.name: Tang Điền
provinces.lore: Red-soiled grass and steppe on the coast, planted in mulberry since 200. Its people raise silkworms and reel silk, and the town belongs to Phần Vũ Đường. A vein runs under the red earth, and the silk women say it is what puts fire in the thread.

places.name: Tang Điền Trấn
places.look: A walled coastal town on rust-red earth, surrounded by long rows of mulberry bushes. Among the rows stand low two-storey silkworm sheds with slatted wooden walls, and in season the whole town smells of boiling cocoons.

places.name: Xích Nhưỡng Mạch
places.look: A field of rust-red earth among the mulberry rows, warm underfoot on cold mornings.
places.lore: A Thổ (earth) vein touched with fire. The silk women say it is what puts fire in the thread.

provinces.name: Tuyết Lộc
provinces.lore: A cold strip of forest, lichen tundra and frozen bog on the snowy north shore, grazed by the reindeer of Tuyết Lộc Thôn. Herders trade hides and antler for salt with the Băng Tâm fishers who share this shore since the Long Lake War. Snow leopards still come down from the bogs in hard winters.

places.name: Tuyết Lộc Thôn
places.look: A handful of low log houses with grey tile and turf roofs sit on the snowy north shore of the lake, entered through a gate arch built entirely of shed reindeer antlers. Herds graze the lichen between the houses and the water's edge.

places.name: Tuyết Báo Cương
places.look: A low wooded knoll above the bogs, its rocks scored with claw marks and the snow around it trampled into tracks that lead nowhere near the village.
places.lore: Snow leopards den among its rocks, kin, the herders say, to the spirit beast Hàm Nguyệt Trang hunted across the ice in 610. Herders keep their reindeer well away from it.

provinces.name: Hàn Yên
provinces.lore: A small stretch of pine and birch on the shore around Hàn Yên Thôn, where winter smoke hangs frozen over the chimneys. Its people fish through the ice and cut firewood. The village bell still calls the children in before dusk, a habit kept since the snow-leopard hunt of 610.

places.name: Hàn Yên Thôn
places.look: A huddle of grey-roofed houses with tall stone chimneys sits on the lake shore, where on still winter mornings the smoke hangs frozen in pale columns. At the ice edge stands a lone post with a bronze bell, rung at every dusk.

places.name: Ngưng Yên Nhãn
places.look: A small round hollow in the pines behind Hàn Yên Thôn, where a thin column of mist rises and hangs frozen in the air on still winter days.
places.lore: A small spirit vein of Water qi, cold and clear, wells up here; villagers say it is why the village smoke freezes. Hàm Nguyệt Trang's disciples come to sit in its mist.

provinces.name: Noãn Ốc
provinces.lore: A sheltered shore of pine around the domed stone houses of Noãn Ốc Thôn and its hot spring. Its people fish and rent bath hours to old cultivators who come to soak their bones each winter. Tùng Đào counts the hamlet among the warmest places of its cold north.

places.name: Noãn Ốc Thôn
