places.look: Domed stone houses, thick-walled and half sunk into the ground, cluster on the lake shore like loaves of bread, each capped with a small grey tile roof. Between them a timber bath-house stands over a hot spring, its steam visible far across the ice.

places.name: Ôn Thủy Mạch
places.look: A line of snow-free ground runs through the pines behind Noãn Ốc Thôn, steaming faintly, with green moss even in midwinter.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here with a faint warmth in it, and it feeds the hot spring found under the snow in 1015. Old cultivators who soak at Noãn Ốc say the vein, not the spring, is what eases their bones.

provinces.name: Mạch Lãng
provinces.lore: Wheat on warm volcanic ash, walled in black lava stone, fills the open land between the woods and the sea. The farmers of Mạch Lãng Thôn are the oldest on the cape, and their wheat feeds Mục Ca and Yên Ba. Sea pines grow along the shore where the ash thins to sand.

places.name: Mạch Lãng Thôn
places.look: A few grey-roofed farmhouses stand among wheat fields that ripple like waves over dark volcanic soil. Low walls of black lava stone divide the gold fields into long strips running down to the sea.

places.name: Hải Tùng Lâm
places.look: A strip of twisted sea pines grows on the sandy shore below the black-walled wheat fields.
places.lore: The farmers of Mạch Lãng planted the first rows to keep the salt wind off their wheat, and the forest has grown on by itself. Its pine cones are roasted at the harvest feast.

provinces.name: Phong Phàm
provinces.lore: A small windy headland of grass and wind-bent woods above the boat sheds of Phong Phàm Thôn. Its people are sailors and pilots, hired by merchants up and down the coast. Every tree on the point leans the same way, and the pilots read the wind in them as well as in their streamers.

places.name: Phong Phàm Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs sits on a windy headland above its boat sheds. On the point stands a tall mast hung with long cloth streamers of many colours, which the sailors read before every launch.

places.name: Khuynh Mộc Lâm
places.look: On the windy headland every tree leans inland at the same angle, like a crowd bending away from the sea.
places.lore: The pilots of Phong Phàm say the trees lean a little further before a storm. Young pilots are sent to sit under them for a season to learn the wind.

provinces.name: Phần Vũ
provinces.lore: Grass, jungle and steep volcanic ground on the east coast, where Phần Vũ Đường, vassal of Phượng Minh Cung, tempers its disciples in the vents and Chúc Dung Khẩu smokes over the sea. Few farm here; its people serve the hall and its burned. On the slope stands the Fire Court (Hỏa Đình), raised in 592 on the ashes of the fire-silk town of Hỏa Ti, which has been the court of Phượng Minh Cung since 1162; the quarter keeps the name Hỏa Ti.

places.name: Phần Vũ Đường
places.look: On the grassland inland from the red cliffs, a field of smoking volcanic vents opens in the ground, and around the largest a hall of red-brown stone climbs in tiers. The vent pits nearest the hall have stone sitting ledges cut into their lips, worn smooth by bodies. Above them a tall mast of black stone flies the crimson war banner Xích Hà Kỳ.

places.name: Chúc Dung Khẩu
places.look: On the east coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, a low volcanic cone of black rock opens in a wide crater whose lip is shaped like an open mouth. Inside, lava glows orange, and a thin tongue of it creeps down a notch in the rim, hissing where it meets wet rock.

places.name: Phượng Minh Cung
places.look: Red-lacquered halls with golden-brown roofs climb the black volcanic rock below the smoking vent of Chúc Dung Khẩu, with faint lines of red silk glowing from the vent's lip down to the roofs. The old fire-silk quarter of Hỏa Ti still crowds the slope below them.
places.lore: Phượng Minh Cung, the Palace of the Phoenix's Call, is the great sect of fire and wood in the south; in 1162 its head Hoa Triêu Dương moved the court, the treasury and the Hall of Spoils here from the ridge, which is now the Wutong Court. Ngô Thê Đồng had raised the Fire Court (Hỏa Đình) on the ashes of Hỏa Ti Trấn in 592, after the fire-silk town burned in the fighting that destroyed Xích Thành Môn, and sent his inner gate down to it. He laid the town's last unburned silk as the Nest Array, carrying the vent's fire into the court, and swore that no silk would be reeled at these vents again. The ash-born, children born at the Fire Court since 592, run the palace.

provinces.name: Phất Y
provinces.lore: A high green valley among grey peaks and dry steppe, with the gorge of Vạn Trùng Hạp cutting through it. Phất Y Cốc's swordsmen live here and hire out across the heart. Their whetstones are cut from a quarry above the valley.

places.name: Phất Y Cốc
places.look: In a high green valley ringed by grey peaks, a modest sect of plain timber halls stands behind a tall stone gate whose name board is left deliberately blank. Swordsmen pass in and out beneath the empty board without a word.

places.name: Vạn Trùng Hạp
places.look: A deep, twisting gorge where the river races white between ranks of steep ridges folded one behind another like stacked screens. A narrow plank road on timber beams socketed into the cliff runs along one wall above the rapids.

places.name: Lệ Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A grey quarry of fine sandstone high on the mountain, its slabs split and stacked by the path to the valley.
places.lore: Phất Y Cốc's whetstones are cut here. Every disciple cuts and dresses his own first stone, and carries it until it is worn through.

provinces.name: Phượng Minh
provinces.lore: The high ridges of Thê Ngô Lĩnh, planted with wutong on every terrace, where the Wutong Court, the old seat of Phượng Minh Cung, stands around its great tree. No farmers live here; the slopes belong to the palace's disciples, gardeners and musicians. Its first elder Vu Ngô Đồng keeps the court, since the head Hoa Triêu Dương moved down to the Fire Court in 1162, and on a shoulder below the palace the broken fort that held the ridge for Cửu Thiều is left as it fell.

places.name: Ngô Đồng Đình
places.look: High on the ridges of Thê Ngô Lĩnh, a palace of red-lacquered halls and stacked golden-brown pagoda roofs climbs around one colossal ancient wutong (ngô đồng) tree, whose broad green crown rises above the highest roof. Wutong groves fill the terraces below.

places.name: Triều Phượng Đỉnh
places.gloss: Summit Where the Birds Pay Homage to the Phoenix
places.look: The highest summit of the palace ridges, a bare red crest above the wutong where flocks of birds circle at dawn.
places.lore: The saying is that a hundred birds come to pay homage to the phoenix, and here they do circle every morning. Its qi runs strong Hỏa (fire), and Phượng Minh's elders keep its crest for themselves.

places.name: Minh Cổ Bảo
places.look: A broken stone fort on a shoulder of the ridge, its drum tower split and its gate choked with fallen wutong leaves.
places.lore: Cửu Thiều Cung's guard fort on the ridge road, whose drums warned the palace when Thiên Xu came south. It fell in 340 in the War of the Nine Shao, and Phượng Minh has left it as it fell.

provinces.name: Thải Chi
provinces.lore: Swamp, forest and tundra at the river's northern mouth around Thải Chi Cốc. Its people grow herbs and gather marsh plants, and the valley's orphans learn their letters in the drying sheds. Poison leeches infest the marsh, and gatherers wrap their legs.

places.name: Thải Chi Cốc
places.look: A shallow forest valley opens off the road, its floor striped with herb beds that step down toward the river below. At the valley mouth sit four moss-grey stone hermits in a row, each cradling a lingzhi in its lap and facing the road as if judging who may enter. The air smells of bitter roots and the smoke of drying sheds.

places.name: Độc Điệt Trạch
places.look: A cold marsh of black water and grey reeds where leeches as long as a hand ripple through the shallows toward any footstep.
places.lore: Poison leeches infest the marsh, and their bite leaves a numb welt for days. Thải Chi's herb gatherers wrap their legs in oiled cloth, and the valley's alchemists collect the leeches for a blood-thinning draught.

provinces.name: Thiên Bảo
provinces.lore: Red badlands and dry steppe round the seat of Thiên Bảo Trai, with the red gold mine of Xích Kim and the burned ruin of Vô Định Thành at the edge of the poisoned plain. Its people are refiners, miners and furnace hands. A Metal vein on the badlands shines at night like buried swords, and the Trai guards it closely.

places.name: Thiên Bảo Trai
places.look: A tall sect seat on a dry steppe rise above the bay, its stacked pagoda roofs ridged in gilt bronze that burns in the evening sun. Around its base a ring of refining furnace chimneys trails thin smoke in green, copper and violet.

places.name: Xích Kim Khoáng
places.look: An open-cut mine in the dry badlands, its terraces cut into rock banded with streaks of red gold. At sunset the whole pit glows the colour of Lạc Hà's evening sky.

places.name: Vô Định Thành
places.gloss: City of the Vô Định River
places.look: A burned city on the dry steppe at the edge of the poisoned plain, its walls broken and its streets empty; of the river that named it, only a dry stream bed under a broken footbridge is left. A grey-green bank of miasma lies against the ruins like fog that never lifts, and above it a charred bell tower still holds its bronze bell, green with verdigris.

places.name: Long Quang Mạch
places.look: A high badland ridge where at night a pale light rises from cracks in the red rock, like the glow of buried swords.
places.lore: A Metal vein runs under the ridge, named for the old line in which the dragon light of buried swords shoots up at the stars. Thiên Bảo Trai holds it and lets its refiners cultivate here before great workings.

provinces.name: Thiên Xu
provinces.lore: The bare mountain of Thiên Xu Tông's seat and its green slopes, the heart of the Bắc Thần Phúc Địa over Tử Vi Mạch. No mortal village stands inside the seat's wards; servants and disciples live on its terraces. Array stone for the sect's formations is quarried just below the halls.

places.name: Thiên Xu Tông
places.look: High on a bare mountain above the heart of the continent, seven terraced halls step down a curving ridge in the bent line of the Northern Dipper, each a little lower than the last. The first and highest, the Pivot Hall, carries a slender black-iron spire that catches the last light long after the valleys are dark. Around the seat the slopes are strangely green for such a height, the mark of the Bắc Thần Phúc Địa.

places.name: Trận Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A neat old quarry below the lowest hall, its walls cut in square steps, with a few round stone blanks still stacked and never carved.
places.lore: The Pivot's array discs were once cut from this stone, close-grained and heavy with the blessed land's qi. The good seam is spent; the last blanks were weighed at Thiên Quyền Thị and never sent for carving.

places.name: Xu Trụ Phong
places.look: A sheer pillar of grey rock above the seat's terraces, green with moss to a height no moss should reach.
places.lore: It stands over Tử Vi Mạch inside the blessed land, and its qi runs to Metal and Earth. Only the Pivot's elders may meditate on its summit.

provinces.name: Thính Vũ
provinces.lore: The Rain Tower's own ground, the old seat of Thính Vũ Lâu: a dormant volcanic cone and the bare high mountains around it, falling through dry steppe to the coast. Banana groves terrace the cone's flanks and the grey lake Tàn Hà Hồ lies at its foot; no village stands within sight of the Tower, and its only people are disciples, servants and the masters who came by night. Quan Vũ Thanh keeps the founder's tower here since the court moved east in 1166-1170. Rain clouds break on the cone almost every night, so the Tower sits in rain while the steppe below stays dry.

places.name: Vũ Lâu
places.look: Out of the rain forest rises a dormant volcanic cone, dark with banana groves on its terraced flanks, and on its crown a slender many-eaved tower, the tallest thing in the south. From every eave of every storey hang long bronze rain-chains, so that in a downpour the whole tower runs with water and rings like a struck bell. No lamp burns in any window.

places.name: Lâm Linh Đỉnh
places.look: A bare dark summit just north of the Tower's cone, crowned by a single bronze bell hung from a stone frame, its rim worn bright by the rain.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi gathers on this crag, and Thính Vũ's sword disciples come here in long rains to listen to the bell ring under the drops until they strike in time with it. The bell was cast for Phó Tiêu Tương and is never struck by hand.

provinces.name: Thối Tinh
provinces.lore: Steep mountain flanks and a little badland along a river, around the forges of Thối Tinh Môn. Smiths, coal carriers and ore porters live on its slopes. An anvil-shaped peak rises above the forges, and the coal for them is dug below.

places.name: Thối Tinh Môn
places.look: On a steep mountain flank, a sect of soot-dark stone halls climbs beside a stream led through a long cascade of stone quenching troughs, each spilling into the next. White steam bursts from the troughs whenever a blade is plunged, and the whole slope seems to smoke.

places.name: Thạch Thán Khoáng
places.look: A black adit below the forges, with coal baskets carried up a stair cut in the slope.
places.lore: Its hard black coal feeds Thối Tinh Môn's forges. The porters climb the stair a hundred times a day and are paid by the basket.

places.name: Thiết Châm Phong
places.look: A flat-topped peak of dark rock above the forges, shaped like an anvil and often ringed with forge smoke.
places.lore: Thối Tinh Môn's smiths say the sky hammers stars on it. Its qi runs to Metal, hard and ringing, and smiths sit on its flat top to temper their own bodies before forging a great blade.

provinces.name: Thu Phần
provinces.lore: Quiet bamboo hills inland from the ruins of Lôi Trạch, covered in old grave mounds and held by Thu Phần Các. Few living people stay here besides the pavilion's disciples; the villagers of Ương Ca keep away, and woodcutters come only by day. Among the graves grows bamboo that sprang from roots the tribulation lightning scorched.

places.name: Thu Phần Các
places.look: On a quiet bamboo hill inland from the ruins of Lôi Trạch, a pavilion of dark weathered wood with two small towers rises above slopes covered in old grave mounds. Between the bamboo, countless thin wooden slips, each brushed with a line of an old poem, hang on strings across the graves and clack softly in the wind.

places.name: Kiếp Trúc Lâm
places.look: Among the grave mounds a grove of grey-green bamboo grows in twisted stems, each joint marked with a black scorch ring.
places.lore: The grove sprang from roots scorched by the lightning of Hầu Xuân Lôi's tribulation, and its bamboo still holds a trace of that thunder. Thu Phần Các cuts the slips for its poems from it, and no one else may.

provinces.name: Thúy Vi
provinces.lore: The twin summits of the Cliff Hall, the old seat of Thúy Vi Tông, and the forested mountains around them, with no coast and no river, high and always half in haze. Herb terraces and the green jade of Bích Ngọc Khoáng are its wealth, and the founder's grave and pine stay on the ridge under the grand elder Cù Thúy Bách. Disciples walk the white spiral Haze Walk from dawn to dusk before they take their vows.

places.name: Thúy Vi Nhai Đường
places.look: Twin summits rise out of the blue-green haze, their herb terraces and white-walled halls half empty, and a twisted pine grows sideways out of the rock by the gate. A broad white stone path still winds in a spiral around the higher summit, its pale upper turns showing above the clouds.

places.name: Bích Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A stepped quarry face is cut into a forested hill, its terraces banded with bright green stone. A cart ramp zigzags down the cut to the road at its foot.

places.name: Quy Tịch Phong
places.look: A bare rock peak rises south of the twin summits, standing clear above the haze on most days.
places.lore: Earth qi gathers in its rock, and Thúy Vi's elders go up it for closed-door cultivation. From its top the whole spiral of the Haze Walk can be seen.

provinces.name: Trạc Anh
provinces.lore: River forest on the frost coast around the terrace of Trạc Anh Đài. Fishers and sea hunters live here and swear their oaths only when the stream runs clear. The sect takes timber from the woods for its drying poles.

places.name: Trạc Anh Đài
places.look: A low wooded rise above a clear, cold stream, its halls stepping up in grey-tiled tiers among birch and fir. At its foot lies the terrace that gives the sect its name: a broad granite platform running out into the water, strung with long bamboo poles where rows of dyed hat strings hang drying in the wind.

places.name: Thương Lãng Lâm
places.look: Birch and fir along a clear stream, with stumps where drying poles have been cut.
places.lore: Trạc Anh Đài cuts its drying poles here. The wood is named from the song: when the water is clear, wash your hat strings in it.

provinces.name: Trúc Thực
provinces.lore: A low coastal plain of grass and seed bamboo where Trúc Thực Viên grows the phoenix's grain. Its people are spirit farmers and their hired hands, and its seed and beast feed go to keepers across the south. Bamboo rats the size of dogs raid the beds every seeding year.

places.name: Trúc Thực Viên
places.look: On a low grassy plain, terraced beds of tall golden bamboo bow under heavy tassels of seed, and between them long swept earthen floors are spread with seed drying in the sun. A plain hall roofed with split bamboo stands at the centre.

places.name: Trúc Thử Nguyên
places.look: A stretch of grassland pocked with burrow mounds, the bamboo around it gnawed to stumps.
places.lore: Spirit bamboo rats the size of dogs breed here and raid Trúc Thực Viên's beds whenever the seed is heavy. The garden's disciples hunt them each seeding year, and the rats come back each year.

provinces.name: Tùng Đào
provinces.lore: The palace ridge and the endless pines around it, rising to a thousand metres. Its people are the palace's servants, foresters and the families of outer disciples, and pilgrims climb the ridge only to listen. A spirit vein of wood and water qi below the gallery is where new disciples first learn to hear the pine waves.

places.name: Tùng Đào Cung
places.look: Out of an endless sea of pines a long ridge rises, crowned with stacked halls of dark timber and blue-grey tile. Along the crest runs an open-sided roofed gallery so long that it follows the ridge out of sight, and the wind through the pines sounds in it like surf.

places.name: Thính Đào Nhãn
places.gloss: Eye Where One Hears the Waves
places.look: Just below the long gallery, a round hollow among the pines holds a still pool, and the sound of the pines falls into it like surf.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood and Water qi rises in the pool. New disciples of Tùng Đào sit by it to learn to hear the pine waves before they are taught a single art.

provinces.name: Vạn Hác
provinces.lore: Ravine-broken pine forest climbing into high mountain, around Vạn Hác Viện and its pillar pavilion. Zither makers, malachite miners and the academy's students are its people. The rockfall that buried Cầm Tượng Trấn in 1012 still scars one ravine wall.

places.name: Vạn Hác Viện
places.look: Deep in the pine sea the ground breaks into ravine after ravine. Over the deepest, on a single pillar of rock rising from its floor, stands a hexagonal pavilion, and the academy's halls step along the ravine rim around it.

places.name: Thạch Lục Khoáng
places.look: On a high slope of the pine sea, small mine mouths open between the exposed roots of giant old pines. Heaps of green malachite spoil lie below them, bright against the brown needles.

places.name: Bích Hác Sâm
places.look: High on the ravine rims, a dark forest of fir and pine clings to the edges, its roots hanging over the drops.
places.lore: Vạn Hác's students climb here to play into the ravines and hear the echoes return. Zither makers take their soundboard wood only from trees that have fallen into the ravines.

places.name: Cầm Tượng Trấn
places.look: At the foot of a ravine wall, broken workshop roofs and half-carved zither bodies lie under a slope of fallen rock.
places.lore: Zither makers settled here to serve Vạn Hác Viện soon after its founding. In 1012 the ravine wall gave way and buried half the town, and the survivors moved to the academy rim.

provinces.name: Vân Khởi
provinces.lore: High mountain shoulders and forest above the south coast, where the abbey of Vân Khởi Quán follows its stream to where the water ends. Hermits, teachers and a few mica diggers live here. Below the abbey stands an empty fort built against Thôn Hải's pirates.

places.name: Vân Khởi Quán
places.look: High on a mountain shoulder a small abbey of grey stone halls follows a thin stream uphill to the point where it vanishes into a cleft in the rock. Beside that spot a wooden platform juts out over the drop, and below it the clouds rise from the valleys.

places.name: Vân Mẫu Khoáng
places.look: On a bare mountain slope a fan of glittering silver mica tailings spills down from a dark mine mouth, shining like a cloud resting on the rock. Above it thin seams in the cliff catch the light.

places.name: Thủy Cùng Phong
places.look: A high rocky peak stands above the abbey, the thin stream rising toward it and vanishing into a cleft halfway up.
places.lore: Earth qi gathers in the stone above the place where the water ends. Abbot Tống Tọa Vân sends his oldest students up it to sit and watch the clouds rise.

places.name: Quan Lan Bảo
places.look: A square stone fort stands on a mountain spur above the sea, its gate open and its watch platform broken.
places.lore: Thúy Vi built it to watch for Thôn Hải's pirate sails on the south coast. After the Pirate Purge of 781 it was no longer needed, and the garrison left within a decade.

provinces.name: Xuyên Lâm
provinces.lore: A high shoulder of Kinh Trập Sơn above the rain forest, mostly bare mountain with bamboo on its lower slopes, where Xuyên Lâm Môn keeps its gate. Its people are the school's guides and their households, and they live by leading travellers through the forest. Above the gate rises the peak where the school tests its new guides.

places.name: Xuyên Lâm Môn
places.look: On a high shoulder of Kinh Trập Sơn above the rain forest, a sect gate of plain grey stone stands at the head of a long stair that drops straight into the trees. Beside it an open-sided gatehouse holds racks of worn hardwood guide staffs, one taken down for every traveller led through the forest. Above the gate, small halls climb the ridge on narrow terraces.

places.name: Thiết Trượng Phong
places.look: Above Xuyên Lâm Môn's gate a thin, straight peak of dark rock rises like a staff planted in the ridge.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs through its dark rock. A new guide of Xuyên Lâm must climb it with a staff and no rope before leading a traveller through the forest.

provinces.name: Tang Du
provinces.lore: High grass, forest and a strip of steppe on the island's sunset coast, where the last light lies longest. Its few villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below the cliffs. Above the village lie the sand-choked lanes of Hải Khúc Trấn, a town the dunes walked over.

places.name: Hải Khúc Trấn
places.look: The tops of walls and a gate arch sticking out of drifted sand on a grassy coastal hill, the lanes between them filled to the windowsills.
places.lore: Fishers built the town on a bend of the coast in 430. Storm after storm blew the beach sand up the hill into its wells and lanes, and in 748 the last families left it. Two years later the people of Dương Liễu began planting willows on their own dunes, so that the same would not happen to them.

places.name: Tà Dương Mạch
places.look: A low grassy rise where the evening light falls level across a field of warm, ochre stones.
places.lore: An Earth vein runs under the rise, strongest in the hour of the evening glow, which suits Lạc Hà's arts. The sect's disciples on the island come here at dusk to cultivate.

places.name: Tang Du Thôn
places.look: A few stone houses on the steppe shore, their doors all turned to the sunset and goat pens on the slope behind.
places.lore: The village is named for the old saying that the setting sun among the mulberries and elms is late, but not too late. Its people keep goats and fish, and old islanders come here to live out their last years facing the evening.

provinces.name: Thanh Đằng
provinces.lore: Deep inland jungle with no river and no coast, hung everywhere with rattan. Its villagers cut and split the canes and weave the baskets and ropes that the coast towns buy. Banyans stand so thick on the high ground that their roots make the paths.

places.name: Long Tu Lâm
places.look: A high jungle of giant banyans whose hanging roots have grown into trunks, so that one tree stands like a grove.
places.lore: The paths through it run along the roots, never on the ground. Rattan cutters say one banyan here has swallowed a whole hut, and that its roof can still be seen inside the trunk.

places.name: Thanh Đằng Thôn
places.look: Stilted houses in a jungle clearing, their walls woven of split rattan and bundles of green cane stacked under every floor.
places.lore: The villagers cut the rattan of the inland jungle and weave the baskets, ropes and fish traps the coast towns buy. A child here learns to split cane before it learns to count.

provinces.name: Trầm Hương
provinces.lore: Jungle coast where old agarwood trees grow, the island's richest wood. Its town lives by the resin trade, and its finest kỳ nam wood goes to Lạc Hà's meditation halls as incense. Gatherers who go into the old groves mark their trees with knots of red cord, and stealing a marked tree is the worst crime the town knows.

places.name: Kỳ Nam Lâm
places.gloss: Forest of the Kỳ Nam Agarwood
places.look: An old jungle of tall pale-barked trees, many tied with knots of red cord and scarred where resin has been cut.
places.lore: The finest agarwood, kỳ nam, forms only in old wounded trees here, and a single piece can buy a house. Each gatherer marks his trees with red cord, and the cords are older than most of the gatherers.

places.name: Trầm Hương Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on the jungle shore whose air is heavy with incense smoke from the resin sheds along its quay.
places.lore: The town lives by the agarwood of the jungle behind it, graded and sold by weight in its sheds. Its best kỳ nam goes to Lạc Hà Tông's meditation halls, and a merchant who sells false agarwood here is banished from the island.

provinces.name: Xướng Vãn
provinces.lore: Jungle and coastal grass on a low shore of the island's far end. Its fishing boats come in singing at dusk, as boats do all over Lạc Hà's lands, and the village keeps the song even in bad years. Wild plantain groves on the grass behind the beach feed the village through the lean season.

places.name: Ba Tiêu Lâm
places.look: A thicket of wild plantains on the coastal grass, their broad torn leaves rattling in the sea wind.
places.lore: The wild plantains feed the village in lean years, and rain on the leaves can be heard from the beach. Children are sent to gather the fruit and told never to go past the last tree.

places.name: Xướng Vãn Thôn
places.look: A fishing village of thatched houses on a grassy shore, its boats drawn up in a long row with their bows toward the sunset.
places.lore: Its boats come in singing at dusk, as fishing boats do all over Lạc Hà's lands. In 803, when the boats fell silent after Chiết Kích Nguyên, the village kept silent for a year, and it still sings one verse fewer than its neighbours.

provinces.name: Hồng Thụ
provinces.lore: Jungle running down into a mangrove shore. Its villagers catch crabs, burn mangrove charcoal and gather the island's shellfish. Flying foxes the size of eagles roost in the jungle behind the village and strip its fruit trees at night.

places.name: Phi Hồ Lâm
places.look: A patch of jungle whose trees hang thick with dark folded shapes by day, and roar with wings at dusk.
places.lore: Spirit fruit bats as broad as eagles roost here in thousands and strip the island's orchards at night. A bitten hunter runs a fever for a month, and the villagers leave the roost alone.

places.name: Hồng Thụ Thôn
places.look: Houses on stilts among the mangrove roots, joined by plank walks, with charcoal kilns smoking on the firmer ground behind.
places.lore: Its people catch mud crabs, gather shellfish and burn mangrove charcoal for the island's smiths. They cut only every third tree, so the mangrove will keep the sea out.

provinces.name: Phương Lân
provinces.lore: Jungle and mangrove on a low shore that dips below the sea. Two fishing clans share the village and have never quarrelled, which the island thinks a wonder. Behind them lies a drowned forest of water pines, cut for boat timber that does not rot.

places.name: Nịch Tùng Lâm
places.look: A drowned forest below the level of the sea, where straight water pines stand knee-deep in black water beside the mangrove.
places.lore: The wood of the water pine does not rot, and the boatwrights of Lan Chu pay well for it. Cutters go in only at low tide, by boat, and leave before the water rises.

places.name: Phương Lân Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on a low shore with a single long boat shed shared down the middle by two clans.
places.lore: Two fishing clans have shared the village since it was founded and have never once gone to the elders with a quarrel. The island says it is the only village where a borrowed net always comes back mended.

provinces.name: Nam Minh
provinces.lore: The island's jungle tip, where the mist rises off the deep sea and the mist leopards of Vụ Báo Lâm hunt inland. Its one village fishes the deep water off the point. No one goes inland by the leopards' paths, and Bình Thủy's ferrymen warn travellers away from them.

places.name: Vụ Báo Lâm
places.look: A steaming jungle in the island's interior, its canopy drowned in white mist most mornings. Out of the mist rises a single black rock outcrop, where the leopards bask when the sun burns through.

places.name: Nam Minh Thôn
places.look: A small fishing village on the jungle point, facing a sea so deep it shows dark blue right up to the rocks.
places.lore: Its fishers take the deep-water fish no one else on the island can reach. They never go inland, since the mist leopards of Vụ Báo Lâm hunt the paths behind the village.

provinces.name: Ngưu Đẩu
provinces.lore: Rolling inland grass rising to forested heights, the highest farmland on the island. Its villagers raise water buffalo and say their herds were named after the stars over the hills. Spirit porcupines den in the forest above, and their quills are sold to the talisman makers of the mainland.

places.name: Hào Trư Lĩnh
places.look: A forested ridge whose paths are littered with black and white quills as long as a forearm.
places.lore: Spirit porcupines den here and can shoot their quills across a clearing. The talisman makers of the mainland buy the quills as pens, and the hunters who gather them wear buffalo-hide coats.

places.name: Ngưu Đẩu Thôn
places.look: A hill village of grey roofs on open grass, its buffalo pens ringed with stone walls.
places.lore: The villagers raise water buffalo and name their herds after the stars of the Ox and the Dipper, which stand over the hills in autumn. The old line says a dragon light once shot up toward those stars, and the village children still watch for it.

provinces.name: Mộ Sơn
provinces.lore: Inland hills of grass, bamboo and forest that turn purple at dusk. Its villagers grow tea on the slopes and graze cattle on the tops. A hot spring in the hills is said to make the greedy greedier and the honest clearer, and the villagers drink from it only at weddings.

places.name: Tham Tuyền
places.look: A small hot spring in a cleft of the grassy hills, its water bright and sweet-smelling.
places.lore: The old saying holds that whoever drinks from the spring of greed turns greedy, and that a clean heart only finds it refreshing. The villagers drink from it only at weddings, to show the families have nothing to hide.

places.name: Mộ Sơn Thôn
places.look: A village of tea terraces on a grassy hillside that turns purple at dusk.
places.lore: Its villagers grow tea and graze cattle on the hilltops. They pick the tea only in the hour before sunset, and Lạc Hà's disciples say it is the only tea that tastes of the evening glow.

provinces.name: Vọng Hương
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo along the strait coast beside Bình Thủy's headland. Its fishers dry cuttlefish and sell it to the ferry passengers. Travellers fresh off the crossing wash the road off in its hot spring before they go on.

places.name: Tẩy Trần Tuyền
places.gloss: Spring that Washes off the Dust
places.look: A warm spring in the grass a short walk from the ferry road, with a bathhouse of bamboo built over it.
places.lore: Travellers fresh off the strait crossing wash the road off here before going on. Bình Thủy Môn pays for the bathhouse, and a newcomer's first bath is free.

places.name: Vọng Hương Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the strait coast, its racks of drying cuttlefish lined up facing the mainland across the water.
places.lore: The villagers dry cuttlefish and sell it to ferry passengers, many of them homesick. On clear days the mainland can be seen from the beach, and the old men sit and look at it.

provinces.name: Lục Trúc
provinces.lore: Inland bamboo forest, with a little grass where the groves thin. Its people cut bamboo for houses, rafts and paper and dig the shoots in spring. Jade-scaled bamboo vipers live in the deepest groves, and cutters wear thick leggings of buffalo hide.

places.name: Bích Lân Lâm
places.look: The deepest groves of the bamboo forest, where green shapes lie along the canes and drop at a footstep.
places.lore: Spirit bamboo vipers as green as the canes live here, and their bite stops a heart in minutes. Cutters wear buffalo-hide leggings and tap the canes ahead with a long pole.

places.name: Lục Trúc Thôn
places.look: Bamboo houses deep in a bamboo forest, with paper pulp vats steaming in the clearings.
places.lore: Its people cut bamboo for houses and rafts, dig shoots in spring and make a coarse paper that Nam Phố Đường buys for practice talismans. The old line about green bamboo in a garden is painted over the village gate.

provinces.name: Phù Can
provinces.lore: Bamboo forest coming down to a sheltered coast. Its villagers build bamboo rafts and fish traps and float cut cane along the shore to the towns. The great grove inland is so old that no one has ever found its far edge on foot.

places.name: Vạn Can Lâm
places.look: An endless bamboo forest whose canes stand so close that the light inside is green and the wind sounds like rain.
places.lore: No one has walked to its far edge, and cutters work only its rim. Bình Thủy's disciples train their footwork on the canes, running along the tops without touching the ground.

places.name: Phù Can Thôn
places.look: A coastal village where bamboo rafts are lashed together on the beach and stacked cane floats moored in the shallows.
places.lore: Its villagers build rafts and fish traps and float cut bamboo along the shore to the towns. A raft here is lashed with rattan from Thanh Đằng and lasts three seasons.

provinces.name: Lan Chu
provinces.lore: Bamboo and grass on a calm stretch of coast, the island's boatbuilding shore. Its town builds the light fishing boats of Cô Vụ Đảo and is famous for carving an orchid on each prow. Wild buffalo with iron-hard horns graze the grass behind the yards and must be driven off before the timber carts can pass.

places.name: Bạo Ngưu Nguyên
places.look: Open grass behind the boatyards, churned into wallows and grazed short by heavy beasts.
places.lore: Wild spirit buffalo with horns hard as iron graze here and charge anything that comes near their calves. The town's carters drive them off with drums before the timber carts go through.

places.name: Lan Chu Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on a calm shore whose slips are crowded with half-built fishing boats, each with an orchid carved on the prow.
places.lore: The town builds the light fishing boats of Cô Vụ Đảo from bamboo and water pine. The orchid on each prow is the builder's mark, and a boat without one will not be bought.

provinces.name: Đê Hạ
provinces.lore: Low grass and bamboo on a shore that lies below the sea at high tide, kept dry by an earth dyke. Its people grow rice and raise fish in the ditches behind the dyke. Every year spirit sea turtles come ashore to lay their eggs on the beach outside it, and the villagers keep well clear.

places.name: Hải Quy Chử
places.look: A stretch of grassy shore pitted with great sand nests, each as wide as a cart.
places.lore: Spirit sea turtles come ashore each year to lay their eggs, and the mothers bite through a boat's side. The villagers of Đê Hạ keep away until the young have gone to sea.

places.name: Đê Hạ Thôn
places.look: A village of rice fields and fish ditches below a long earth dyke, the sea higher than its roofs at high tide.
places.lore: Its people grow rice and raise fish behind the dyke and send every household to mend it after a storm. A crack in the dyke is called before a fire.

provinces.name: Phong Sào
provinces.lore: Inland jungle with no river and no coast, the island's dark heart. Its villagers climb the tallest trees to take wild honey and wax. A Wood vein runs under the high canopy nearby, and the bees there are said to be larger and calmer than anywhere else.

places.name: Phong Vương Mạch
places.look: A high knoll in the jungle where the canopy closes into one green roof, humming with large slow bees.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the knoll, and the bees over it are larger and calmer than anywhere else on the island. The honey hunters of Phong Sào leave its combs alone and say the vein belongs to the bees.

places.name: Phong Sào Thôn
places.look: A village in a jungle clearing, its houses hung with wax combs and long bamboo ladders leaning on the tallest trees.
places.lore: Its villagers climb the jungle giants to take wild honey and wax, which they trade to the alchemists of Hải Yến. A honey hunter sings to the bees as he climbs, and no one else may use his song.

provinces.name: Vụ Vũ Lâm
provinces.lore: The wooded isle of Phù Chử Đảo, forest from shore to crown, ringed by a raft of wild ducks so thick the water looks feathered. No one lives here and no sect holds it; egg-gatherers row over from the plain coast each spring, wait for the ducks to part before landing, and take only a few eggs from each nest. The forest floor is soft with moulted down, which gives the wood its name.

places.name: Phù Chử Đảo
places.look: A low wooded isle off the plain coast, its trees dark against the water. Around it floats a thick, shifting raft of wild ducks, so dense the water looks feathered.

provinces.name: Bạch Thảo
provinces.lore: Grass and dry steppe on the coast, rising to bare hills inland. Its herders run sheep on the pale autumn grass and fish the shore. A warm spring in the steppe is where the herds drink in winter.

places.name: Ẩm Câu Tuyền
places.look: A steaming spring in a dip of the steppe, its overflow running into a long stone trough.
places.lore: The herders water their flocks here in winter when the ponds freeze. Mục Vân's couriers always stop to water their horses, and the trough's stones are worn by hooves.

places.name: Bạch Thảo Thôn
places.look: A herding village on the steppe shore, its sheep pens of piled stone and the autumn grass around it bleached white.
places.lore: Its herders run sheep on the pale grass and fish the shore in winter. Their wool goes to Nhạn Thanh and is said to be the whitest on the plain.

provinces.name: Thanh Phong
provinces.lore: Wide grass and steppe on a low coast where the sea and the sky meet in one colour. Its town ships wool and hides along the plain coast. A Water vein near the shore is named for the old line about autumn water and the endless sky.

places.name: Nhất Sắc Mạch
places.look: A flat grassy shore where on calm evenings the sea and the sky turn the same colour and the horizon disappears.
places.lore: A Water vein runs under the shore, named for the line in which the autumn water and the endless sky are one colour. Lạc Hà's disciples cultivate here at the hour of the evening glow.

places.name: Thanh Phong Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on the steppe shore, its wool sheds open to the sea wind.
places.lore: The town ships wool and hides along the plain coast. Its name comes from the old line about clear breezes rising, and the merchants say the breeze keeps the moth out of their wool.

provinces.name: Song Tỉnh
provinces.lore: Dry inland steppe with patches of grass, far from any river or coast. Its herders live by two deep wells and move their flocks between them. An Earth vein under the open steppe draws Mục Vân's riders to cultivate on long journeys.

places.name: Khoáng Dã Mạch
places.look: A bare rise in the steppe where the grass grows short and the ground hums faintly underfoot.
places.lore: An Earth vein runs under the rise, steady and broad. Mục Vân's couriers break their journeys here to cultivate an hour before riding on.

places.name: Song Tỉnh Thôn
places.look: A cluster of felt tents and stone pens around two deep stone wells in the open grass.
places.lore: The herders move between the two wells with the seasons and never let one run dry. A quarrel over water here is settled by the oldest woman of the village.

provinces.name: Vãn Chu
provinces.lore: Grass and steppe on the coast, with a few red badland gullies inland. Its fishers put out in the evening and come home singing in the dark. Black vultures nest on the high ground and follow the herds.

places.name: Hắc Thứu Đài
places.look: A grassy terrace of high ground streaked white with droppings, where huge black birds sit hunched on the rocks.
places.lore: Spirit vultures nest here and take lambs and sick sheep from the herds. Herders say they gather over any flock that is about to suffer a loss, and drive their sheep home when they see them.

places.name: Vãn Chu Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the grassy coast where the boats put out at sunset, each with a lamp at the stern.
places.lore: Its fishers go out in the evening and come home singing in the dark, guided by the lamps. In 803 they stayed ashore, and they still stay ashore on that dusk every year.

provinces.name: Mộ Cảnh Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The westernmost isles: the grassy hump of Tịch Chiếu Đảo with its stone bench and cairns, and a smoking volcanic cone of forest and bare rock farther out. No settlement has ever stood here; boats from the mainland bring Lạc Hà's dying elders to Tịch Chiếu and do not wait. The cone holds Hỏa Ngọc Mạch on Thúy Vi's sealed chart, and only that sect's short guarded voyages ever land on it.

places.name: Tịch Chiếu Đảo
places.look: The westernmost island, a low grassy hump in the open sea. On its western cliff stands a single long stone bench facing the sunset, and behind it the grass is dotted with small cairns of grey stones.

places.name: Hỏa Ngọc Mạch
places.look: Far out in the western sea a black volcanic island rises in a steep cone, steam leaking from its flanks. Down the cone's sides run seams of fire jade that glow red-green through the rock at dusk, as if the mountain were cracked over a lamp.

provinces.name: Chung Phàm
provinces.lore: A small high spur of steppe and grass over the sea, the last stop for boats going out to the far west. Its little town sells water, salt fish and rope to the boats. Its people say they live at the edge of the world, and that the sunset is nearer to them than to anyone.

places.name: Chung Phàm Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on a high steppe spur over the sea, its water tanks cut into the rock.
places.lore: It is the last stop for boats going out to the far west, and it sells them water, salt fish and rope. Its people claim the sunset is nearer to them than to anyone on the continent.

provinces.name: Bình Sa
provinces.lore: Grass and forest rising from level sands to high ground. Its villagers fish and herd on the shore flats. Wild stallions run on the uplands and are the terror of herders and the prize of Mục Vân's horse-breakers.

places.name: Liệt Mã Cương
places.look: An open grassy ridge high above the coast, its turf torn by hooves.
places.lore: Wild spirit stallions run here and kill any horse that strays into their herd. Mục Vân's horse-breakers come each year to try to take one, and come back with fewer riders than they took.

places.name: Bình Sa Thôn
places.look: A village on flat sands at the shore, its houses raised on low mounds against the spring tides.
places.lore: Its villagers fish the shore flats and herd sheep on the grass behind. Geese come down on the level sand each autumn, and the village holds a feast when the first ones land.

provinces.name: Hòa Lũng
provinces.lore: Wide coastal grass, mostly ploughed, with a little steppe and forest. Its farmers grow rice and millet on raised ridges against the floods. A Wood vein under the level grass makes the ridges green earlier than anywhere on the plain.

places.name: Bình Vu Mạch
places.look: A wide patch of open grass that turns green weeks before the rest of the plain each spring.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the level grass, gentle and wide. The farmers of Hòa Lũng plant first beside it and say the vein wakes the plain.

places.name: Hòa Lũng Thôn
places.look: A farm village on the coastal grass, its fields raised on long ridges with ditches between.
places.lore: Its farmers grow rice and millet on ridges that stand above the floods. The village sends its grain by cart to Thảo Đường Thành.

provinces.name: Thán Ổ
provinces.lore: Inland grass and steppe with woods in its hollows. Its villagers burn charcoal in the woods and sell it to the towns. On the steppe stand the empty halls of Phù Dao Quán, a school that ended after the cold year of 1120.

places.name: Phù Dao Quán
places.look: Empty halls of grey stone on the open steppe, their doors banging in the wind and the courtyard drifted with dust.
places.lore: A small school sworn to Lạc Hà Tông founded the abbey in 760 to cultivate on the open steppe. The cold year of 1120 killed its herds and its old master, and in 1121 its few disciples went to serve Mục Vân Trang. Herders shelter in its halls in storms.

places.name: Thiên Cao Mạch
places.look: A broad rise of steppe under an enormous sky, with a single stone cairn on its crown.
places.lore: An Earth vein runs under the rise, named for the old line in which heaven is high and earth far-reaching. The disciples of Phù Dao Quán cultivated here, and their cairn still stands.

places.name: Thán Ổ Thôn
places.look: A village of black-roofed huts in a wooded hollow, its charcoal mounds smoking under turf.
places.lore: Its people burn charcoal in the woods and carry it to the towns of the plain. Each family has its own wood and cuts it in turn so the trees grow back.

provinces.name: Di Tân
provinces.lore: Grass and forest rising from the coast to high wooded ground. Its town is a crowded harbour for the plain's coast boats. A Wood vein high in the forest draws Lạc Hà disciples, and on the shore lie the ruins of Ngư Hỏa Trấn, broken by the storm of 870.

places.name: Ngư Hỏa Trấn
places.look: A broken sea wall and roofless houses on a grassy shore, with rows of rusted lamp hooks along the old quay.
places.lore: Fishers built the town in 610, and its boats fished at night by lamplight. The great storm of 870 broke its sea wall and sank its fleet in the harbour, and the survivors moved to Di Tân. Fishers still see lights on the water off the old quay.

places.name: Thanh Vân Mạch
places.look: A high forest shoulder above the coast where the clouds come down through the trees.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the forest, named for the old line about never letting the will for the blue clouds fall. Lạc Hà's young disciples are sent here to cultivate before their first trial.

places.name: Di Tân Trấn
places.look: A small walled harbour town on the grassy coast, its harbour so packed with coast boats that one can walk across it.
places.lore: Its name comes from the old line about boats crowding the ford. It is the busiest harbour on the plain coast after Nhạn Thanh, and its harbour master settles mooring quarrels by lot.

provinces.name: Mục Địch
provinces.lore: Wide inland grass and steppe, the heart of the open plain. Its herders follow their flocks and call them with bamboo flutes. Grass wolves hunt the flocks in winter, and the herders sleep beside their sheep.

places.name: Thảo Lang Nguyên
places.look: Rolling high grass where the wind shows long tracks through the blades and old wolf dens open on the slopes.
places.lore: Spirit wolves the colour of dry grass hunt here and are hard to see until they move. In winter they come down on the flocks, and the herders sleep beside their sheep with fire pots.

places.name: Mục Địch Thôn
places.look: A herding village of felt and timber on open grass, its flocks moving around it to the sound of bamboo flutes.
places.lore: Its herders call their flocks with flutes, each family with its own tune. A sheep that answers the wrong tune is given back without a word.

provinces.name: Phùng Nghênh
provinces.lore: Grass and steppe on the coast, with an Earth vein on the rise inland. Its town is known for its inns and its welcome to travellers from a thousand miles away. Herders say no stranger has ever slept outside in Phùng Nghênh.

places.name: Trường Phong Mạch
places.look: An open grassy rise inland of the town where the wind never stops and the grass lies flat.
places.lore: An Earth vein runs under the rise, and the wind over it is said to carry the qi far across the plain. Travellers staying at Phùng Nghênh come up to cultivate before setting out.

places.name: Phùng Nghênh Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on the grassy coast whose main street is nothing but inns, each with a lantern at the door.
places.lore: Its name comes from the old line about welcomes from a thousand miles away. The town's custom is that no stranger sleeps outside, and the innkeepers take turns to house those who cannot pay.

provinces.name: Hoàng Trần Hoang
provinces.lore: High dry badlands and steppe with a few bare peaks, where the wind lifts yellow dust every afternoon. No one lives here; there is no water and the poisoned plain lies not far beyond its hills. Thiên Bảo's prospectors cross it for the Earth vein on its high steppe and leave before dark.

places.name: Ốc Thổ Mạch
places.look: A broad shelf of high steppe among the badlands where the soil lies deep and dark among bare red rock.
places.lore: A heavy Earth vein runs under the shelf, the only green ground for a day's walk. Thiên Bảo's prospectors cultivate here on their way through and never stay the night.

provinces.name: Viên Nhật Nguyên
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and desert under high bare mountains on the border with Thính Vũ Lâu. No one lives here but Lạc Hà's watch on the ridge of Trường Hà Mạch. The plain takes its name from the same line as the vein, the long river and the round setting sun, which here sinks straight into the flat land.

places.name: Trường Hà Mạch
places.look: A high bare mountain on the border, its slope split by a long seam of amber-gold rock that winds down the face like a river. In the setting sun the seam glows as if the river ran with fire.

provinces.name: Thu Tân
provinces.lore: Steppe and grass rising from the bay shore to high bare mountains. Its villagers fish the shore and graze goats on the slopes. An Earth vein high on the steppe is wrapped most mornings in ranks of mist.

places.name: Vụ Liệt Mạch
places.look: A high steppe shoulder where the morning mists lie in long even ranks along the slope.
places.lore: An Earth vein runs under the shoulder, and its qi holds the mists in place until noon. Lạc Hà's disciples climb up to cultivate in the mist.

places.name: Thu Tân Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the bay shore below bare hills, its boats drawn up on a gravel beach.
places.lore: Its villagers fish the bay in autumn when the water runs clearest and graze goats on the hills the rest of the year. The bay is said to be most like its name here.

provinces.name: Đào Ẩn
provinces.lore: Inland grass, jungle and bamboo behind Tử Điện Thành. Its villagers grow longans and send them to the bay cities in summer. Peach trees still fruit wild among the jungle here, from the orchards of the Petal Shore.

places.name: Thúy Bình Mạch
places.look: A grassy rise backed by a wall of jungle that stands like a green screen.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the rise. The villagers of Đào Ẩn say their trees fruit best on the side facing it.

places.name: Đào Ẩn Thôn
places.look: A village in a jungle clearing ringed by longan orchards, heavy with brown fruit in summer.
places.lore: Its villagers grow longans and dry them on bamboo trays for the bay cities. Wild peaches from the old Petal Shore orchards grow among their trees.

provinces.name: Ngư Võng
provinces.lore: Coastal grass with jungle along the bay, beside the web-hung wood of Thiên Chu Lâm. Its villagers fish with nets and mend them on the beach. No sect holds the spider wood, and the villagers burn back its edge every spring.

places.name: Thiên Chu Lâm
places.look: A low, steaming jungle by the bay, its canopy sagging under sheets of silver web strung from tree to tree. In the evening light the webs shine like sails across the whole wood.

places.name: Ngư Võng Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the jungle shore where nets hang drying on poles all along the beach.
places.lore: Its villagers fish with nets and burn back the edge of Thiên Chu Lâm each spring. They say a spider web and a net are the same thing, and that the village must stay quicker.

provinces.name: Hoàng Long
provinces.lore: Open grass on the bay coast, flat and low. Its town builds and paints the dragon prows of the bay's ships. A Water vein near the shore runs under a spring-fed stream that never fails in drought.

places.name: Lưu Thủy Mạch
places.look: A spring-fed stream in the grass that runs clear and full even in the driest summer.
places.lore: A Water vein feeds the stream, named for the old tune of flowing water. Musicians of the bay come to play beside it.

places.name: Hoàng Long Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on the flat coast whose slipways hold half-carved dragon prows painted yellow.
places.lore: Its name comes from the old line about ships with blue bird and yellow dragon prows. Its carvers make the prows for the bay's ships, and a ship launched without one is thought unlucky.

provinces.name: Châu Liêm
provinces.lore: Grass and jungle along the bay coast. Its town strings shell beads into curtains that hang in every rich house of the bay. A hot spring inland is where its bead-drillers rest their eyes.

places.name: Ngọc Lộ Thang
places.look: A warm spring in the grass whose steam leaves beads of dew on the reeds around it.
places.lore: The bead-drillers of Châu Liêm bathe their tired eyes in the water. They say it keeps an old driller's sight sharp.

places.name: Châu Liêm Trấn
places.look: A small walled town on the bay coast whose doorways all hang with curtains of shell beads that click in the wind.
places.lore: Its drillers string shell beads into curtains for the rich houses of the bay, after the old line about pearl curtains rolled up at dusk. A bride's curtain takes her family a year to make.

provinces.name: Liệt Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Badlands and high split crags, with no water and no roads. No one lives here but iron miners in summer. Its high peak can be seen from Thiên Bảo Trai, and the poisoned plain lies beyond its far side.

places.name: Mặc Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Adits cut into a high crag, their spoil heaps black against the red badlands.
places.lore: Miners dig black iron here in summer and carry it down on mules to Thiên Bảo's furnaces. In winter the mine is shut and the wind has it.

places.name: Trùng Tiêu Phong
places.look: A sheer grey peak above the badlands whose tip often stands above the clouds.
places.lore: Its name comes from the old line about peaks rising above the layered heavens. Its bare rock carries Metal qi, and Thiên Bảo's refiners climb it to temper blades in its cold wind.

provinces.name: Hàn Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High cold mountains above the badlands, the highest ground in the bay's lands. Few live here but the bell-casters of Minh Loan Các, whose pavilion has stood on Tằng Loan Phong since 1188; otherwise only jade cutters climb up in summer. Thiên Bảo Trai buys every stone they bring down.

places.name: Lam Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A cold high working where blue-green jade shows in the rock face under a crust of frost.
places.lore: Jade cutters climb up each summer and work until the first snow. Thiên Bảo Trai buys every stone they bring down and sells the best at its auctions.

places.name: Minh Loan Các
places.look: Black casting sheds stand on a ledge of a tall peak of pale rock, with a frame of bells hung under their eaves, and ridge after ridge falls away below. The note of a bell rung here is heard on every ridge.
places.lore: Minh Loan Các, the Pavilion of the Singing Bells, is the bell-casting sect of Lạc Hà Tông's bay, whose ward bells drive off beasts, warn of attack and ring on every ship and caravan of the bay. In 1188 its head Yến Bội Ngọc moved the casting floor and the inner pavilion up this mountain, after the casting master Ngụy Trầm Âm cast the Cloud Bridge bells on this shoulder, next to the blue jade mine, and they rang true. A ring of tuned bells, the Hundred-Bell Eaves, rings in the mountain wind under the pavilion's roofs, though it is still a little under half hung. The peak's name comes from the old line about layered ranges rising green to the heavens.

provinces.name: Liên Chu
provinces.lore: Dry steppe with badland gullies along a river. Its villagers keep the pontoon bridge that carries the caravan road to Vật Hoa Thị. Giant lizards bask on the gully rocks and take stray goats.

places.name: Hoàng Tích Cương
places.look: A ridge of yellow rock in the steppe where great lizards lie motionless in the sun.
places.lore: Spirit lizards as long as a cart bask here and take stray goats and sheep. Their hides are sold to Thiên Bảo's armourers.

places.name: Liên Chu Thôn
places.look: A steppe village on a river where a bridge of boats lashed together carries the caravan road.
places.lore: Its villagers keep the pontoon bridge and take a small toll for Thiên Bảo Trai. When the river floods they cut the bridge loose and haul it back afterwards.

provinces.name: Mã Độ
provinces.lore: Steppe and grass along a river where horses can wade across. Its villagers breed hardy steppe ponies and sell them to the caravans. Herds of wild spirit asses run on the steppe and kick any rider who comes too close.

places.name: Dã Lư Nguyên
places.look: Open steppe crossed by dusty trails and the dung heaps of wild herds.
places.lore: Herds of wild spirit asses run here, fast as a horse and vicious. They kick riders from the saddle and kill ponies that stray into the herd.

places.name: Mã Độ Thôn
places.look: A steppe village by a shallow river ford, its corrals full of shaggy ponies.
places.lore: Its villagers breed hardy steppe ponies and sell them to the caravans. A caravan that buys its ponies here is said never to lose one to thirst.

provinces.name: Hàm Phong
provinces.lore: Dry steppe on the bay coast, swept by a salty wind. Its villagers fish and dry their catch in the wind. A hot spring inland runs red over the rocks.

places.name: Lưu Đan Trì
places.look: A hot pool in the steppe whose overflow runs down the rocks in a bright red stain.
places.lore: Its name comes from the old line about vermilion flowing from the pavilion's eaves. Its iron water stains the rocks red, and the fishers soak their sore joints in it.

places.name: Hàm Phong Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the steppe coast where racks of split fish dry in a constant salty wind.
places.lore: Its fish dry in the salt wind in a single day, and the bay's caravans buy them for the road.

provinces.name: Bạch Dương
provinces.lore: Wide steppe with patches of grass and desert, from the bay coast far inland. Its herders run white sheep between wells. On the coast stands Chung Bến, the Bell Wharf, the old coast hall of Minh Loan Các, whose ward bells ring on the bay's ships and the caravans.

places.name: Kim Sa Tuyền
places.look: A warm spring in the steppe whose bed glitters with golden grains of mica.
places.lore: Prospectors once dug the spring for gold and found only mica. The herders of Bạch Dương water their sheep here in winter.

places.name: Chung Bến
places.look: A walled bell-yard of grey stone and tile stands on the steppe shore, its foundry smoking among hundreds of bronze bells hung on timber frames that ring together in the sea wind. Beyond it the bay's ships lie at the wharf.
places.lore: Chung Bến, the Bell Wharf, is the coast hall of Minh Loan Các, where bell-casters founded the pavilion in 960 under Lạc Hà Tông, after the old line about jade pendants and singing bells. Its casting floor moved up Tằng Loan Phong in 1188 and the hall was left to the ships. Ships are fitted and caravans buy their ward bells here, and the steward Ông Hải Linh keeps the note ledger, which records every bell the pavilion has sold by its note.

places.name: Bạch Dương Thôn
places.look: A cluster of felt tents and stone pens around a deep well on the open steppe.
places.lore: Its herders run white sheep between the wells of the steppe and sell the wool at Vật Hoa Thị. They move camp by the stars.

provinces.name: Hà Khúc
provinces.lore: Steppe and grass along a winding river. Its villagers farm the bends and fish the pools. Golden eagles nest on the high ground and take lambs.

places.name: Hoàng Điêu Đài
places.look: A rocky terrace on the high steppe where great eagles sit on the stones and the ground is strewn with bones.
places.lore: Spirit golden eagles nest here and take lambs and foals. Mục Vân Trang's riders have tried to tame their chicks and never succeeded.

places.name: Hà Khúc Thôn
places.look: A steppe village on a tight bend of the river, its fields laid out inside the loop.
places.lore: Its villagers farm the bend and fish the deep pools. When the river cuts a new bend, the village moves its fields and keeps its houses.

provinces.name: Xích Thổ
provinces.lore: Steppe, desert and salt flats along a river that runs to the sea, rising to bare heights. Its villagers farm the red earth by the river and gather salt from the brine lake. Herders avoid the far heights, which look toward the poisoned plain.

places.name: Bạch Lỗ Hồ
places.look: A shallow brine lake on the salt flats, ringed with white crust and too salty for any fish.
places.lore: The villagers of Xích Thổ rake salt from its shores and sell it to the caravans. Its water holds a body up like a raft.

places.name: Xích Thổ Thôn
places.look: A steppe village of red mud houses by a river, with salt carts lined up outside.
places.lore: Its villagers farm the red earth by the river and gather salt from the brine lake. They never take their flocks to the far heights.

provinces.name: Thạch Trụ Lâm
provinces.lore: A coast of grey karst pillars and forest, honeycombed with caves where beasts den. No one lives here; Lạc Hà holds the Jade Milk Spring but sends its disciples only in groups. Lime-cutters come for the cave stone and leave before dark.

places.name: Ngọc Nhũ Tuyền
places.look: Among grey karst pillars, a stair of milky-green pools steps down a slope, each held in a pale lip of stone the warm water has laid down over the centuries. Steam drifts between the pillars on cool mornings.

places.name: Chung Nhũ Quật
places.look: A deep cave among the karst pillars whose roof hangs with milky stone icicles, many of them cut short.
places.lore: Cutters take the stalactite stone here for the alchemists, who grind it into pills for the lungs. They work in groups and leave before dark, for other caves in the pillars are dens.

provinces.name: Than Đầu
provinces.lore: Steppe, forest, grass and red badlands climbing from a river to high bare ground. Its villagers fish the rapids and ferry goods past them. A Metal vein on the high badlands draws Lạc Hà's sword disciples.

places.name: Thiết Cốt Mạch
places.look: A ridge of dark badland rock where seams of grey metal stand out like bones.
places.lore: A Metal vein runs under the ridge, hard and cold. Lạc Hà's sword disciples cultivate here to temper their bodies before taking up a blade.

places.name: Than Đầu Thôn
places.look: A steppe village by a stretch of rocky river rapids, with a hauling path cut along the bank.
places.lore: Its villagers fish the rapids and haul the boats past them on ropes for a toll. The boatmen sing as they haul, and the songs are older than the village.

provinces.name: Sùng A Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest, high mountains, steppe and badlands, the highest ground in Ngư Ca Xuyên. No one lives here; its slopes are too steep to farm and the mountain apes drive off hunters. Lạc Hà's disciples climb it to look out over the whole river land.

places.name: Sơn Tiêu Nhai
places.look: A high cliff of bare rock where red-faced apes sit on the ledges and hurl stones at anyone below.
places.lore: Spirit mountain apes live on the cliff and drive off hunters and climbers. They are said to remember a face and stone that person for years.

provinces.name: Lô Địch
provinces.lore: Wide steppe and grass along the river below Lạc Hà's old seat. Its villagers fish and play reed flutes at dusk, answering the songs of the boats. On the steppe lies the Dusk Field, Vãn Điền, the old seat of Yên Quang Các, where the pickers still gather herbs in the evening glow.

places.name: Hà Quang Tuyền
places.look: A hot spring on a steppe rise whose steam glows rose-red at sunset.
places.lore: Lạc Hà's disciples bathe here after cultivating at dusk. The herbalists of Yên Quang Các water their evening herbs from it.

places.name: Vãn Điền
places.look: A small walled yard of grey stone and grey tile stands quiet on the steppe, with a gate-house, a plain hall with a lantern before it and a drying shed hung with herb bundles. Behind it a gentle hillside slopes away, where the founder's grave lies and pickers walk in a slow line at sunset.
places.lore: Vãn Điền, the Dusk Field, is the old seat of Yên Quang Các, now its outer gate, where the pickers walk the steppe at sunset beside Hà Quang Tuyền, the Spring of the Evening Glow. The grand elder Diêm Tử Tô lives here beside the founder's grave and would not move, and Văn Đương Quy keeps the field with him. Two of Lạc Hà's alchemists founded the pavilion here in 1065, after the old line about the haze and light congealing as the evening hills turn purple. The sect moved its furnaces and beds to Dã Tang Lâm in 1187.

places.name: Lô Địch Thôn
places.look: A river village of reed-thatched houses where reed flutes hang drying from the eaves.
places.lore: Its fishers play reed flutes at dusk, answering the songs of the boats on the river. In 803 the flutes fell silent with the boats, and the village still plays one tune less on that dusk.

provinces.name: Mộ Tử Nguyên
provinces.lore: Badlands and dry steppe whose hills turn purple at dusk, as the old line says the evening hills do. No one lives here; there is no water. An Earth vein in the badlands draws Lạc Hà's disciples to cultivate at sunset.

places.name: Ngưng Tử Mạch
places.look: A hollow among badland hills where the dusk light pools in a deep purple long after sunset.
places.lore: An Earth vein runs under the hollow, and it holds the purple of the evening hills longest. Lạc Hà's disciples cultivate here in the last light.

provinces.name: Hồng Nham Hoang
provinces.lore: High red badlands and bare mountains with no water and no road. No one lives here but copper miners in summer. A boiling spring among the crags is the only water for a day's walk.

places.name: Phí Thạch Tuyền
places.look: A boiling spring among red crags, its water bubbling up through stones too hot to touch.
places.lore: It is the only water for a day's walk in the waste. Copper miners cool its water in jars overnight before they drink.

places.name: Tử Đồng Khoáng
places.look: Shallow pits in the red badlands, half filled with sand, beside old heaps of green-stained rock.
places.lore: Lạc Hà once dug its coin and bell copper here, but the shallow ore is nearly spent. A few miners still pick over the heaps in summer; in winter the pits are left to the wind.

provinces.name: Vạn Động Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and karst full of caves and winding gorges. No one lives here; the caves are dens and the gorges flood. Gypsum cutters come in the dry season for the white stone the alchemists use.

places.name: Oanh Hồi Hạp
places.look: A narrow karst gorge that winds back and forth between grey walls, so that a walker sees the same pillar three times.
places.lore: Its name comes from the old line about islands and isles winding round. The gorge floods in the rains, and gypsum cutters cross it only in the dry season.

places.name: Bạch Cao Động
places.look: A cave in the karst whose walls are crusted with soft white gypsum, scraped in long grooves.
places.lore: Cutters scrape gypsum here for the alchemists, who use it in cooling pills, and for the plaster of fine halls. The cave is cold even in summer.

provinces.name: Hầu Đầu
provinces.lore: Forest and karst on high ground with no river. Its villagers grow wood-ear mushrooms on cut logs and gather herbs. Wild spirit boars root through the forest and break the mushroom racks.

places.name: Cuồng Trư Lâm
places.look: A high forest whose floor is rooted up and torn, with tusk marks on the trunks.
places.lore: Spirit boars as heavy as an ox root here and charge anything that moves. They break the mushroom racks of Hầu Đầu, and the village hires Lạc Hà's outer disciples to drive them back each autumn.

places.name: Hầu Đầu Thôn
places.look: A forest village where stacks of cut logs lean in the shade, studded with dark wood-ear mushrooms.
places.lore: Its villagers grow wood-ear mushrooms on cut logs and gather herbs in the high forest. Their dried mushrooms go down to Hạc Đinh Thị.

provinces.name: Hôi Diêu
provinces.lore: Forest and karst with a little bamboo. Its villagers burn the karst stone into lime for the plaster of Lạc Hà's halls. Beside the village lies Hãm Thạch Trấn, a town that sank into the ground.

places.name: U Lan Cốc
places.look: A narrow karst valley where wild orchids grow on the damp walls.
places.lore: The orchids grow only in its shade, and herbalists climb its walls for them. The lime-burners leave its stone alone.

places.name: Hãm Thạch Trấn
places.look: A ring of broken walls in the forest around a deep round pit where the town's centre used to be.
places.lore: Lime-burners built the town in 340 on the edge of the karst. In 912 the ground under its market fell into a cave, and the rest of the town was left within a year. Its people moved to Hôi Diêu and have never built on bare karst since.

places.name: Hôi Diêu Thôn
places.look: A forest village of white-dusted houses beside smoking lime kilns.
places.lore: Its villagers burn the karst stone into lime for the plaster of Lạc Hà's halls. Everything in the village is white, and its children are called the ghosts of Ngư Ca.

provinces.name: Phóng Mộc
provinces.lore: Forest and bamboo on a river that runs out of the hills. Its villagers fell timber and float it down to the towns of the plain. The forest on the hills above is old and layered green.

places.name: Tằng Thúy Lâm
places.look: An old forest on the hills, its layers of green rising one above the other like stacked ranges.
places.lore: Its name comes from the old line about layered ranges rising green. The timber cutters of Phóng Mộc take only the trees at its edge.

places.name: Phóng Mộc Thôn
places.look: A river village where cut logs are rolled into the water and floated off in long chains.
places.lore: Its villagers fell timber in the hills and float it down to the plain. Each log is branded with the family's mark, and the downriver towns pay by the mark.

provinces.name: Sơn Trà
provinces.lore: Forest and high ground on a mountain river. Its villagers grow camellias for their oil and their tea. Grey wolves hunt the high forest and come down in hard winters.

places.name: Quần Lang Lĩnh
places.look: A high forested ridge where wolf trails run under the trees and howls carry at night.
places.lore: Spirit grey wolves hunt the ridge in packs. In hard winters they come down to the camellia terraces, and the villagers light fires all night.

places.name: Sơn Trà Thôn
places.look: A mountain village on a river where camellia bushes line every terrace.
places.lore: Its villagers grow camellias for their oil and their tea. The oil goes to the lamps of Lạc Hà's halls.

provinces.name: Vãn Đăng
provinces.lore: Grass and forest on the coast. Its fishers put out lamps on their boats at dusk and sing as they come home. A Water vein lies inland where the clouds break after rain.

places.name: Vân Tiêu Mạch
places.look: A grassy hollow inland where the clouds break first after rain and the light pours through.
places.lore: A Water vein runs under the hollow, named for the old line about clouds melting and rain clearing. The fishers of Vãn Đăng say the weather turns here first.

places.name: Vãn Đăng Thôn
places.look: A forest village on the coast where every boat hangs a lamp at the stern.
places.lore: Its fishers put out at dusk with lamps and come home singing. On the dusk of the mourning for 803 they light the lamps but do not put out.

provinces.name: Lăng Hoa
provinces.lore: Grass, forest and steppe along the river. Its villagers grow water chestnuts in the river ponds. A Wood vein runs under the maples on the higher ground.

places.name: Phong Ảnh Mạch
places.look: A grove of red maples on the higher ground whose shadows lie unusually sharp and still.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the maples. Lạc Hà's disciples say it is a cutting from the maples of the founder's first hall.

places.name: Lăng Hoa Thôn
places.look: A river village of grassy banks and ponds covered with the floating leaves of water chestnuts.
places.lore: Its villagers grow water chestnuts in the river ponds and gather them from small round tubs. Girls who can paddle a tub without spilling are thought to make good wives.

provinces.name: Vân Gian
provinces.lore: Forest, grass and high mountains on the uplands. Its villagers gather herbs and chestnuts in the mountain forest. Above them stands Vân Kiều Trấn, a mining town that emptied when its silver ran out and has been the seat of Lạc Hà Tông since 1185, with the Cloud Bridge Array across its gorge.

places.name: Lạc Hà Tông
places.look: Rose-tiled halls of pale stone climb two shoulders of a high mountain, with the dark ruins of the old town showing among the new terraces. A band of sunset-coloured cloud joins the two shoulders across the gorge, where the old bridge broke.
places.lore: Lạc Hà Tông, the Sect of the Drifting Sunset Clouds, is one of the seven great sects and master of the western lands; its arts lean on earth and wood, and its head Tô Vãn Chiếu carries the sword Tử Điện. The sect moved up here from the steppe in 1185, to high ground where Earth and Wood qi lie together, and its array master Quách Tiếp Vân laid the Cloud Bridge Array across the gorge. Silver miners had built Vân Kiều Trấn on this mountain in 520 under Lạc Hà; by 1040 the silver was gone and its people had moved down to Vân Gian, and the bridge broke in a storm a few years later.

places.name: Cổ Bách Mạch
places.look: A high slope of ancient cypresses whose trunks are twisted like rope.
places.lore: A Wood vein runs under the cypresses, the oldest trees in Ngư Ca Xuyên. Lạc Hà's elders go there to cultivate in solitude.

places.name: Vân Gian Thôn
places.look: A mountain village in the forest, often wrapped in cloud, with chestnut trees around its houses.
places.lore: Its villagers gather herbs and chestnuts in the mountain forest. They are descended from the miners of Vân Kiều Trấn and still keep their picks over the door.

provinces.name: Hồng Quả
provinces.lore: Forested hills rising to bare mountain on the northern edge of the plain. Its people pick hawthorn berries and make them into sweets and medicine for the markets of Thiên Quyền. A Metal vein on the mountain above draws cultivators of sword arts.

places.name: Thái Bạch Mạch
places.gloss: Vein of the Great White Star
places.look: A pale band of white quartz across a bare mountain face, bright in the evening light.
places.lore: Named for the evening star, its qi runs to Metal. Sword cultivators of the plain come to temper their blades on it.

places.name: Hồng Quả Thôn
places.look: A forest-edge village of grey roofs among hawthorn hedges red with berries in autumn.
places.lore: Its people make hawthorn sweets and medicine for the markets of Thiên Quyền. Children are paid in candied berries for picking.

provinces.name: Phong Thực Nguyên
provinces.lore: Steppe and grey badland worn into pillars and hollows by the wind, around the sulphur pans of Lưu Hoàng Khoáng. No one lives here; sulphur workers come in shifts. A Fire vein breathes under the badland floor, and its heat keeps the snow off the pans.

places.name: Lưu Hoàng Khoáng
places.look: Flat pans of yellow sulphur crust spread across a grey badland floor, broken by steaming fissures, with low stone sheds where the crust is scraped and bagged. The ground around them is stained in rings of yellow, white and rust.

places.name: Địa Hỏa Mạch
places.look: Cracked badland ground that steams in the cold and is warm to the hand.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Fire. The sulphur workers of Lưu Hoàng say its heat is why the pans never freeze.

provinces.name: Xích Thổ Nguyên
provinces.lore: Red badlands, steppe and mountain around the cinnabar terraces of Thần Sa Khoáng. Miners and alchemists come and go, but no village stands here. A warm red spring in the steppe is where the miners wash off the cinnabar dust.

places.name: Thần Sa Khoáng
places.look: In the red badlands, a hillside is cut into stepped terraces of bright vermilion spoil, with a shallow washing pool on each step where the cinnabar is rinsed. A low stone furnace house squats at the foot.

places.name: Đan Nhũ Thang
places.look: A warm, milky-red pool in a steppe hollow below the cinnabar terraces.
places.lore: Miners of Thần Sa wash the red dust off here after each shift. Alchemists warn them not to drink it.

provinces.name: Thanh Khoa
provinces.lore: High plain of lakes and a river between Củng Tinh Quán and the Pivot's mountain, at the edge of the blessed land. Its people grow highland barley and keep yaks along the river. Quartz from its mountain mine goes to the Pivot's formation masters, and an old fort above the river once guarded the seat's west road.

places.name: Bán Nguyệt Hồ
places.look: A crescent-shaped lake just east of Tinh Lạc Hồ, its reedy shallows full of nesting geese.
