places.lore: It is fed by the overflow of Tinh Lạc Hồ and is too reedy to hold the stars. Thanh Khoa's people cut its reeds for thatch.

places.name: Tinh Kính Khoáng
places.look: A high cut in bare mountain rock, glittering with clear crystal, at the edge of the seat's warded slopes.
places.lore: Rock crystal from here is ground into lenses and array crystals for the Pivot's formation masters and for the armillary of Củng Tinh Quán.

places.name: Hoa Cái Đường
places.look: A compact hall of dark stone on a forested shoulder below the seat, its chimneys trailing thin coloured smoke from the furnaces within.
places.lore: Pill refiners (luyện đan) who use the cinnabar and sulphur of the red badlands founded this hall in 1060 under Thiên Xu, naming it for the canopy of stars over the pole. Its pills are sold through Thiên Quyền Thị and weighed there like everything else.

places.name: Tây Quan Bảo
places.look: Tumbled stone walls across a forested saddle on the seat's west road, with an empty gate arch standing alone.
places.lore: It guarded the west road to the seat from 340 and held it through the War of the Pivot. After the Compact was set the garrison stood down in 520, and its stones were carried off to build Thanh Khoa.

places.name: Thanh Khoa Thôn
places.look: Flat-roofed stone houses on the river, with barley fields and yaks grazing the far bank.
places.lore: Its people grow highland barley and roast it into flour, and send yak butter up to the Pivot's kitchens. They are the highest farmers on the plain.

provinces.name: Khung Lư
provinces.lore: Wide steppe and mountain east of the Pivot's seat. Its people are herders who live in felt yurts and move with the grass, wintering by a warm spring in the hills. On a mountain shoulder stands the empty tower of Khuy Thiên Các, star-readers who joined Củng Tinh Quán long ago.

places.name: Dương Hòa Tuyền
places.look: A warm, clear spring in a sheltered hollow of the hills, ringed with green grass in the depth of winter.
places.lore: The yurt herders winter beside it. Lambs born near it are said never to take cold.

places.name: Khuy Thiên Các
places.look: A roofless stone tower on a mountain shoulder, with a stair spiralling up to an empty platform open to the sky.
places.lore: Star-readers founded it in 380, rivals of Củng Tinh Quán. In 650 its head went blind, and its disciples joined the abbey and carried their charts with them; the tower has stood empty since.

places.name: Khung Lư Thôn
places.look: A ring of white felt yurts on the steppe, with horses tethered between them and dung fires smoking.
places.lore: Its herders move with the grass and come back here each winter. The village is wherever the yurts stand, but it always returns to the same ring of stones.

provinces.name: Thiên Lang Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains, forest and high plain on the western edge of Thiên Tuyền, named for the bright Wolf Star that rises over them in winter. No village stands here; gold-washers work its streams in summer. Its pine-shadowed peak is a landmark from the plain.

places.name: Kim Sa Khoáng
places.look: Wooden sluices in a mountain stream, with gold-washers bent over pans in the cold water.
places.lore: Gold is washed from the stream gravel in summer. Every washer pays a tenth to the Pivot by weight at Thiên Quyền.

places.name: Tùng Ảnh Phong
places.look: A forested peak whose pines throw long shadows across the plain at sunset.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herders on the plain tell the hour by how far its shadow has run.

provinces.name: Thiên Cơ Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Heavenly Pearl Star
provinces.lore: High mountains south of the Pivot's seat, named for the third star of the Dipper. Iron sand is washed from its gullies and carried up to the seat's smithies. Its peak of the nine luminaries is where the Pivot's disciples go to sit alone.

places.name: Thiết Sa Khoáng
places.look: Black sand washed in a mountain gully and heaped on hide sheets to dry.
places.lore: Iron sand from here is carried up to the seat's smithies and smelted for the sect's tools.

places.name: Cửu Diệu Phong
places.look: A tall grey peak south of the seat with nine rock knobs around its summit.
places.lore: The Pivot's disciples go there to sit alone, one on each of the nine knobs, and the first to come down loses. Its qi runs to Metal, and a cultivator who sits through a night there finds the stars seem close enough to steady the spirit sense.

provinces.name: Đẩu Bính Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain, steppe and grassland south of the market, curving like the handle of the Dipper on the map. No one lives here now. A beacon fort on its slopes once passed warnings from the borders to the seat.

places.name: Câu Trần Phong
places.look: A low, curved ridge-peak bending like a hook above the steppe.
places.lore: Named for the star group that curls around the pole, it hooks round the beacon fort below it. Its qi runs to Earth, and formation masters walk its curve to learn how a ward should bend around what it guards.

places.name: Phong Toại Bảo
places.look: A small stone fort on a mountain spur, its beacon tower still standing with a blackened fire basket on top.
places.lore: From 505 its beacon passed warnings from the borders to the seat. After the truce of 805 the Pivot stood down its beacon line, and the fort was left in 806.

provinces.name: Thiên Thị Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A short mountain ridge and steppe named for the star enclosure of the Heavenly Market. Caravans cross its saddle between Thiên Quyền and the southern mines. It has no village, only a few herders' shelters.

places.name: Mã An Phong
places.look: A double-humped peak on the steppe with a deep saddle between its summits, where the caravan path crosses.
places.lore: Caravans between Thiên Quyền and the southern mines cross its saddle. Its qi runs to Earth.

provinces.name: Ngũ Xa Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains with grassy and steppe valleys, named for the five-chariot constellation. Agate is dug in its rock, and an old stockade where soldiers once farmed lies empty in a grassy valley. Herders summer their flocks here.

places.name: Đới Văn Khoáng
places.look: Banded agate nodules broken from grey mountain rock and sorted into baskets by colour.
places.lore: Banded agate is broken from the grey rock here in summer and carried to Thạch Kiều, where it is cut into beads and seals. Stones with a ring like an eye fetch the most, for star-readers set them in their charts.

places.name: Xa Luân Phong
places.look: A round-topped peak ringed by a circle of rock ribs like the spokes of a wheel.
places.lore: Herders say the five chariots of the sky rest on it at night. Its qi runs to Metal and turns slowly around the summit, and cultivators sit at its hub to circulate their own qi in the same wheel.

places.name: Đồn Điền Trại
places.look: Low stone walls around overgrown fields in a grassy valley, with a ruined barracks along one side.
places.lore: Soldier-farmers held it from 290, growing their own grain while they watched the south. After the Compact of 510 the Pivot no longer paid them, and by 530 the last had gone to Thạch Kiều.

provinces.name: Bi Phong Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare mountains and badlands on the western rim of the plain, near the old ramparts of Cố Lũy and the poisoned waste of Chiết Kích Nguyên. No one lives here. The wind moans in its gaps, and herders say it moans loudest in the season the battle was fought.

places.name: Hồi Thủ Phong
places.look: A lonely peak on the steppe rim from which the whole plain can be seen behind and the grey waste ahead.
places.lore: Soldiers going west to Cố Lũy are said to have looked back at the plain from here. Its qi runs to Metal.

places.name: Lang Yên Trại
places.look: A ring of tumbled stones on a mountain flank with a heap of scorched signal stones at its centre.
places.lore: An outpost of Cố Lũy's line from 798, where signal smoke was lit to warn the ramparts. After the battle of 803 no one came to relieve it, and it was abandoned at the truce of 805.

provinces.name: Hoàng Bách Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and mountain in the north-west, grown with cork trees whose yellow inner bark is a dye and a medicine. Bark peelers come up in summer and dry their bark on racks. No one stays through the winter.

places.name: Thứu Chủy Phong
places.look: A hooked rock beak jutting from a forested mountain.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Bark peelers use it to find their way back to their camps.

provinces.name: Tàn Kỳ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain, steppe and badland on the edge of Chiết Kích Nguyên, where the War of Broken Halberds ended in 803. No one lives here; alum is dug by day crews who leave by dusk. Shepherds will not cross its upper slopes, which run down toward the miasma.

places.name: Bạch Phàn Khoáng
places.look: White-crusted pits in grey mountain rock, with crystals drying in shallow trays.
places.lore: Alum from here fixes dyes and stops bleeding. The day crews leave before dusk and never sleep on the ridge.

places.name: Tê Mã Phong
places.look: A bare steppe peak above the grey edge of the waste, its rocks scoured by wind.
places.lore: Herders say they hear horses neighing from it on still nights, as others hear them in the miasma. Its qi runs to Earth.

provinces.name: Mao Ngưu
provinces.lore: High plain at the western edge of Thiên Tuyền, near the ramparts of Cố Lũy. Its people herd yaks and sheep on the short grass. A hot spring in the hills is where Quý Trường Kích's soldiers washed their armour in the five years they held the ramparts.

places.name: Tẩy Giáp Trì
places.look: A steaming pool in a fold of the high plain, its rim of rust-stained stones.
places.lore: Quý Trường Kích's soldiers washed their armour here in the five years they held Cố Lũy. Herders say the rust in its stones is theirs.

places.name: Mao Ngưu Thôn
places.look: Low stone houses with yak-hair tent roofs on the open high plain, the yaks grazing up to the doors.
places.lore: Its herders keep yaks and sheep on the short grass near Cố Lũy. They leave a bowl of butter on the old ramparts each spring.

provinces.name: Tô Du
provinces.lore: High plain and badland along a river in the south-west of the plain. Its herders make yak butter and cheese and sell them at Thạch Kiều. Lapis is cut in its mountains, and the walls of an old remount fort stand empty on the plain.

places.name: Thanh Kim Khoáng
places.look: A narrow, fallen-in adit in grey mountain rock, the old spoil flecked with deep blue stone.
places.lore: Lapis lazuli was once dug here in small blocks and carried down to Thạch Kiều. The adit fell in long ago, but the deep blue of the Pivot's star charts and of Củng Tinh's painted ceilings came from here.

places.name: Lão Mã Bảo
places.look: Long stone stables and a walled yard on the high plain, empty but for grass and wind.
places.lore: The Pivot bred remounts for its riders here from 600. After the battle of 803 no riders came back to claim the horses; the herds were sold and the fort was left by 806.

places.name: Thổ Long Mạch
places.look: A long ochre ridge of badland winding beside the river like a sleeping beast.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, heavy and slow like the river beside it. The herders will not dig into it or pitch tents on its back, and Earth cultivators walk its whole length to steady their foundation.

places.name: Tô Du Thôn
places.look: Stone houses on the river with butter churns at every door and cheese drying on the roofs.
places.lore: Its herders make yak butter and cheese and carry them to Thạch Kiều. Butter tea is offered to every traveller, and it is rude to refuse a third bowl.

provinces.name: Thạch Ốc
provinces.lore: High plain, steppe and badland along a river south of the Pivot's mountain. Its people build their houses of stone against the wind and farm barley and peas on the river flats. A Metal vein on the steppe is said to lie where one of the falling stars of the Wild Age struck.

places.name: Đại Giả Khoáng
places.look: A badland slope dug into red-brown terraces, with ochre cakes drying in rows.
places.lore: Its ochre is used for paint and in medicine. The diggers' hands stay red for a season.

places.name: Lưu Tinh Mạch
places.look: A shallow dish in the steppe, its rocks scorched black and glassy.
places.lore: Said to be where one of the stones of the nine days struck, its qi runs to Metal. Củng Tinh's star-readers visit it each year.

places.name: Thạch Ốc Thôn
places.look: Thick-walled stone houses huddled on a river bend, with barley and pea fields on the flats.
places.lore: Its houses are built of stone against the plateau wind. Each house keeps one stone from the falling stars of the Wild Age in its wall, or says it does.

provinces.name: Xa Ngưu
provinces.lore: Steppe and mountain along a river on the south side of the plain. Its people raise oxen for the caravans and the Pivot's carts. Amethyst is dug in the mountain above, and a Metal vein of high winds sits on a bare steppe shoulder.

places.name: Tử Thạch Khoáng
places.look: Purple crystal geodes cracked open in a mountain cut.
places.lore: Amethyst geodes are cracked from the mountain rock here and sorted by colour. The deepest purple goes into the Pivot's ceremonial seals, and the pale stones are sold to cultivators who hold them to calm the mind.

places.name: Cương Phong Mạch
places.look: A bare steppe shoulder high above the river where the wind never stops and the grass grows flat.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal, sharp as the wind. Cultivators sit here to hone their spirit sense.

places.name: Xa Ngưu Thôn
places.look: Stone cattle pens and low houses on the steppe, with herds dust-brown on the slopes.
places.lore: Its people raise oxen for the caravans and the Pivot's carts. An ox from here is sold with its weight written on its horn.

provinces.name: Hồ Dương
provinces.lore: Steppe and desert edge along a river, its banks lined with desert poplars. Its people farm the river flats and boil salt from a warm brine spring in the hills. Caravans bound for the desert water here.

places.name: Bạch Diêm Tuyền
places.look: A warm brine spring on the steppe, crusted with white salt around its rim.
places.lore: Hồ Dương's people boil its brine for salt. The salt is weighed at Thạch Kiều and sold across the heart.

places.name: Hồ Dương Thôn
places.look: A river village under gnarled desert poplars gold in autumn, with salt pans by the bank.
places.lore: Its people farm the river flats and boil salt from the warm brine spring in the hills. Caravans bound for the desert water here.

provinces.name: Hôi Vụ Hoang
provinces.lore: Mountains and high plain around Chiết Kích Nguyên, the plain poisoned by the battle of 803, and the Vạn Cốt Trủng that rose over the dead. No one lives here, and shepherds will not cross it. Thiên Xu's patrols walk its rim and do not go in.

places.name: Thủ Linh Phong
places.gloss: Peak of the Vigil for the Dead
places.look: A dark mountain standing over the grey waste, its foot lost in haze.
places.lore: Thiên Xu's patrols climb it to look over Chiết Kích Nguyên without entering it. Its qi runs to Earth, heavy and dark.

provinces.name: Thạch Điền
provinces.lore: High plain, forest and badland in the far south-west, more than fourteen hundred metres up. Its people farm small terraced fields walled with stone and keep goats. A sulphur spring and a soapstone pit give them something to sell.

places.name: Hoàng Yên Tuyền
places.look: A sulphurous spring in red badland, wrapped in yellow steam.
places.lore: It smells of eggs and heals the skin. The goatherds bathe their flocks in its runoff against mites.

places.name: Tập Trận Khoáng
places.look: A soft grey soapstone pit on the high plain, its walls smooth and greasy to the touch.
places.lore: Soapstone from here is carved into bowls and into the practice array discs of novice formation masters.

places.name: Thạch Điền Thôn
places.look: Tiny stone-walled terraces stepping up a high slope, with a village of flat roofs at their foot.
places.lore: Its people farm barley in walled terraces and keep goats. Every stone in the walls was cleared from the fields by hand.

provinces.name: Bách Linh
provinces.lore: Steppe and high plain along a river in the south of Thiên Tuyền, loud with larks in spring. Its people herd sheep and farm the river flats. A Wood vein in a forested fold and a silver sand mine in the mountain lie nearby.

places.name: Ngân Sa Khoáng
places.look: Glittering grey sand dug from a mountain pocket and washed in leather troughs.
places.lore: The silver sand is sent to the Pivot's mint. Washers are searched at the gate each night.

places.name: Tảo Xuân Mạch
places.look: A forested fold of the hills where the leaves come out a month before anywhere else.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood, quick and green. Herders bring sick lambs here in early spring, and herb gatherers find the first shoots of the year in its shade.

places.name: Bách Linh Thôn
places.look: A steppe village on the river, its fields loud with larks in spring.
places.lore: Its people herd sheep and farm the river flats. Lark cages hang at every door, and a good singer is worth a sheep.

provinces.name: Thạch Dương
provinces.lore: High steppe and mountain on the southern rim, under the hawk cliffs of Thương Ưng Đài. Its herders keep goats on the stony grass. Green jade is cut in the mountain above, and young cultivators climb the hawk cliffs for chicks.

places.name: Thương Ưng Đài
places.look: A high flat-topped stone table rises from the plateau, its cliff rim ringed with the stick nests of grey hawks and its top scoured to bare rock by the wind. The hawks circle it all day.

places.name: Lục Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A cut in a high mountain face showing veins of dark green stone.
places.lore: Green jade from here is carved at Bích Khê and sold back to the plain at twice the price.

places.name: Thạch Dương Thôn
places.look: A cluster of stone huts on high stony steppe with goats on every rock.
places.lore: Its herders keep goats under the hawk cliffs. They say the grey hawks take only the goats that stray.

provinces.name: Xuyên Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and steep mountain in the north of the plain, whose peaks stand above the cloud on most mornings. No one lives here; woodcutters from the plain climb up for timber in summer. Its white hairpin peak can be seen from Mộc Hương Thôn.

places.name: Bạch Trâm Phong
places.look: A thin, pale spire of rock standing above the forest and the morning cloud.
places.lore: It can be seen from Mộc Hương Thôn on clear days, standing above the cloud. Its qi runs to Metal, thin and bright, and sword cultivators sit on its narrow tip to train a single-pointed mind.

provinces.name: Mã Nãi
provinces.lore: Steppe, high plain and badland along a river in the south. Its herders keep horses and brew fermented mare's milk, which they trade at Thạch Kiều. An Earth vein lies under the wide steppe nearby.

places.name: Quảng Dã Mạch
places.look: A broad, gently rising stretch of steppe where the grass grows waist-high.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, spread wide and even across the steppe. Horses grazed on it grow strong and steady, and the herders of Mã Nãi keep it for their best mares.

places.name: Mã Nãi Thôn
places.look: Felt and stone houses by the river, with leather bags of fermenting milk hanging from posts.
places.lore: Its herders brew fermented mare's milk and trade it at Thạch Kiều. A guest is offered a bowl before a word is spoken.

provinces.name: Hoang Thành Nguyên
provinces.lore: Steppe, mountain and desert in the south-east of Thiên Tuyền, with no village left. Its name comes from the walls of Lục Hợp Thành on a mountain shelf, a caravan city emptied after the earthquake of 912. Herders pass through in spring and avoid the old streets.

places.name: Thạch Chung Phong
places.look: A bell-shaped peak of grey rock above the ruined city.
places.lore: Its rocks ring like bells when struck, and herders say they rang by themselves the night Lục Hợp Thành's cistern split. Its qi runs to Metal, and cultivators listen to the ringing to tune their own meridians.

places.name: Lục Hợp Thành
places.look: Long walls and a grid of empty streets on a mountain shelf, with a cracked stone cistern at the centre.
places.lore: A caravan city built on the southern road in 330, under Thiên Xu's protection. In 912 an earthquake split its cistern and dried its springs, and within a year its people had moved to Thạch Kiều.

provinces.name: Hoàng Sa Nguyên
provinces.lore: Desert and dry steppe along a river on the south-eastern edge. No one lives here but a few river fishermen in summer. Golden scorpions as big as dogs hide in its sand, and caravans do not camp in the open.

places.name: Kim Hạt Cốc
places.look: A shallow sandy valley in the steppe, its sand ridged by the tracks of many legs.
places.lore: Golden spirit scorpions as big as dogs bury themselves here. Their venom is prized by alchemists, and their hunters seldom grow old.

provinces.name: Du Mục
provinces.lore: Steppe, mountain and high plain in the south of the plain, where herders move with the grass. They winter by a warm spring in the hills. Saltpetre is scraped from a cave in the mountain and sold to Thiên Xu for fire powders.

places.name: Đông Noãn Tuyền
places.look: A steaming spring among rocks on the steppe, warm enough to bathe in during snow.
places.lore: The nomads of Du Mục winter by it and bathe in it together on New Year's night. Its warm water keeps a ring of grass green around it, and the herds graze there when the steppe is under snow.

places.name: Tiêu Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A cave in the mountain whose walls are crusted with white salt, scraped into sacks.
places.lore: Saltpetre from here is sold to Thiên Xu for fire powders, mixed with the sulphur of Lưu Hoàng.

places.name: Du Mục Thôn
places.look: A winter camp of stone-walled yurts on the steppe, with dung stacked high against the walls.
places.lore: Herders who move with the grass all summer winter here. The camp's stone walls are older than anyone can remember.

provinces.name: Liệp Ưng
provinces.lore: Steppe and mountain in the south of the plain. Its people fly hawks and falcons for hares and foxes and sell trained birds at Thạch Kiều. A frost-headed peak stands over their village.

places.name: Sương Đầu Phong
places.look: A high mountain whose summit stays white with frost and snow most of the year.
places.lore: Falconers of Liệp Ưng release their old birds from its slopes to die free. Its qi runs to Metal, cold and clear, and cultivators who sit in its frost find their thoughts slow and sharpen.

places.name: Liệp Ưng Thôn
places.look: A steppe village of stone houses with hooded hawks on perches at every door.
places.lore: Its people fly hawks and falcons for hares and foxes and sell trained birds at Thạch Kiều.

provinces.name: Nam Đẩu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains on the southern rim of Thiên Tuyền, named for the southern constellation that faces the northern Dipper. No one lives here; a few crews dig rubies in summer. Its peak of the longevity star is climbed by old cultivators near the end of their years.

places.name: Hồng Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A few narrow, long-empty adits in a high mountain face, red grains still glinting in the spoil.
places.lore: Small crews once dug rubies here in summer, the best for the Pivot and the rest for Thạch Kiều. The seam has played out, and only children climb up to sift the spoil.

places.name: Thọ Tinh Phong
places.look: A tall, broad peak on the southern rim, its summit catching the light of the southern sky.
places.lore: Old cultivators climb it near the end of their years to watch the longevity star. Its qi runs to Earth.

provinces.name: Vọng Dương Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains on the south-eastern rim, whose seaward side drops to the coast. From its grassy summit the far water can be seen. Azurite is dug in its flanks, and no village stands here.

places.name: Hải Lam Khoáng
places.look: Blue-stained rock in an old mountain cut above the coast, where a stream still runs blue past the abandoned washing floors.
places.lore: Azurite and a little malachite were dug here until the cut flooded. Smelted, the ore gave copper; ground, it gave the blue paint still on the Pivot's halls.

places.name: Lục Bình Phong
places.look: A grassy-topped mountain whose long green summit looks out over the coast.
places.lore: From its grassy summit the far water can be seen on clear days. Its qi runs to Wood and Earth, and herb gatherers find mountain gentian on its top that grows nowhere else on the rim.

provinces.name: Tùng Nhân
provinces.lore: Steppe, mountain and forest north of the Pivot's mountain. Its people gather pine nuts from the forests and herd sheep on the steppe. Its lotus-shaped peak is the first thing travellers from the north see of the seat's mountains.

places.name: Liên Hoa Phong
places.look: A ring of rock petals around a central summit north of the seat's mountains.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth. Travellers from the north see it first of all the seat's mountains.

places.name: Tùng Nhân Thôn
places.look: A forest-edge village with sacks of pine cones heaped by every door and sheep on the steppe beyond.
places.lore: Its people gather pine nuts in the forests each autumn and herd sheep on the steppe the rest of the year. The nuts are roasted in big iron pans and sold at Thiên Quyền, and the best go up to the Pivot's kitchens.

provinces.name: Đương Quy
provinces.lore: Mountain, high plain and forest in the north-west. Its people grow and dig angelica root and other herbs for the alchemists of the plain. Dark ore is dug in the mountain above the village.

places.name: Huyền Cương Khoáng
places.look: A dark adit in mountain rock with heaps of black, heavy ore at its mouth.
places.lore: Its dark iron-manganese ore is carried down by mule and smelted into a tough black steel. The plain's carpenters and herb diggers swear by tools made from it.

places.name: Tiên Nhân Phong
places.look: A forested peak topped by a rock shaped like a seated figure.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Villagers leave food at the rock for the immortal they say sits there.

places.name: Đương Quy Thôn
places.look: A forest village on a high slope, with angelica beds and roots drying on bamboo trays.
places.lore: Its people grow and dig angelica root for the alchemists of the plain. A root that grows forked is given to a newly married couple.

provinces.name: Bắc Cực Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains just north of the Pivot's seat, under the pole star in the sky. No one lives here but the seat's watchmen. Gold is dug in a small mine for the sect's own use.

places.name: Kim Tinh Khoáng
places.look: A small, guarded adit in bare mountain rock, its mouth closed with an iron grille.
places.lore: There is gold here, but the sect keeps the adit shut against its own need, and none of it has ever been weighed in the market.

places.name: Thái Nhất Phong
places.look: A sharp high peak north of the seat, lined up with the pole star at night.
places.lore: The Pivot's watchmen keep a post on its shoulder and sight the pole star over its tip each night. Its qi runs to Metal, and the sect's elders send disciples here to sit facing the pole until their minds are as still as it.

provinces.name: Hoàng Kỳ
provinces.lore: Steppe and forest on the northern edge of the plain. Its people dig milkvetch root on the steppe and sell it to alchemists and physicians. A Wood vein in the forest gives a sweet dew on its leaves at dawn.

places.name: Cam Lộ Mạch
places.look: A forest glade where a sweet dew beads on the leaves every dawn.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Children lick the leaves in spring, and the alchemists collect the dew in jars.

places.name: Hoàng Kỳ Thôn
places.look: A village at the forest edge with bundles of yellow root drying on the eaves.
places.lore: Its people dig milkvetch root on the steppe and sell it to physicians and alchemists.

provinces.name: Tầm Dược
provinces.lore: High forest, mountain and plain in the west, more than fourteen hundred metres up. Its people gather mountain herbs on the forested slopes. A Wood vein high in the forest and a realgar mine in the rock lie above the village.

places.name: Tị Xà Khoáng
places.look: Orange-red realgar crystals in grey mountain rock, untouched but for a few broken out long ago.
places.lore: The realgar here is good against snakes and for some pills, but its dust sickens those who break it out, and the cut has been left since the last crew fell ill.

places.name: Bách Tuế Mạch
places.look: A stand of enormous old trees high in the forest, the ground soft with centuries of needles.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herb gatherers say a plant that grows here lives a hundred years.

places.name: Tầm Dược Thôn
places.look: A high forest village of log houses with baskets of herbs hung from every beam.
places.lore: Its people climb the forested slopes for mountain herbs. They rope themselves together on the steep ground.

provinces.name: Xảo Tượng
provinces.lore: Forest, high plain and mountain north-west of the Pivot's mountain. Its people are carpenters who work the mountain timber into beams, carts and array frames for the plain. A warm spring on the mountain is where they rest their aching backs.

places.name: Tẩy Tâm Tuyền
places.look: A clear warm spring in a mountain cleft, its water so still it seems not to move.
places.lore: Carpenters rest their backs here. Cultivators say it calms the heart before a breakthrough.

places.name: Xảo Tượng Thôn
places.look: A forest village of fine timber houses with carved beams and workshops full of shavings.
places.lore: Its carpenters make beams, carts and array frames for the plain. The Pivot's formation masters order their frames here.

provinces.name: Cao Hàn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare, very high mountains in the north-east of Ngọc Hành, part of the great snow massif. No one lives here. Calamine is dug in a low valley at its foot and carried to the forges.

places.name: Lô Cam Khoáng
places.look: Pale, crumbly ore pits in a low valley at the mountain's foot, with ore spread to roast on stone hearths.
places.lore: Calamine from here is carried to Thối Tinh Môn and alloyed with copper into brass for fittings and array rings. The roasting fumes turn the valley's grass white.

places.name: Ngân Giáp Phong
places.look: A great snow peak of the north-eastern massif, its snowfields plated in overlapping scales like armour.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water, cold enough to bite through robes. No one has climbed it; cultivators who meditate on its lower snowfields say it hardens the body like quenched steel.

provinces.name: Thập Giáp
provinces.lore: Steppe and desert along a river, around the valley of Thiết Bối Cốc. Its people gather the iron plates the valley's beasts shed and sell them to smiths. They herd goats on the steppe and keep clear of the herd's path.

places.name: Thiết Bối Cốc
places.look: A broad highland valley whose rock walls have been gnawed and scraped, so bands of raw ore gleam like polished metal along the slopes. Big grey shapes move slowly among the boulders, their backs plated like iron.

places.name: Thập Giáp Thôn
places.look: A river village of stone houses with iron-grey beast plates stacked against the walls.
places.lore: Its people gather the plates the beasts of Thiết Bối Cốc shed and sell them to smiths. They herd goats and keep out of the herd's path.

provinces.name: Tà Dương Nguyên
provinces.lore: Dry steppe, desert and badland along a river in the west of Ngọc Hành. No village stands here. Swarms of spirit locusts rise from a ridge in late summer, and herders drive their flocks away from them.

places.name: Phi Hoàng Cương
places.look: A dry steppe ridge stripped bare of grass, the ground pocked with egg holes.
places.lore: Spirit locusts hatch here and rise in swarms in late summer. Their swarms strip fields bare, and their wings are used in talismans.

provinces.name: Thiết Ngưu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain and steppe in the middle of Ngọc Hành, crossed by the ore roads. Its name comes from the strong oxen that haul ore over it. No one lives here but the copper crews.

places.name: Lục Đồng Khoáng
places.look: Green-stained rock in a mountain cut, with a broken ore cart left on the overgrown road below.
places.lore: Its green copper ore was once hauled by ox over the ridge and weighed at Song Kiều like all the ore of Ngọc Hành, until richer cuts nearer the scales took its trade.

places.name: Đồng Trụ Phong
places.look: A tall bronze-brown pillar of rock above the ore roads, its flanks streaked green where copper weathers out.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore drivers touch its foot for luck, and cultivators of Metal arts climb its pillar to feel the ore singing in the rock.

provinces.name: Hỏa Diệm Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountain around the volcanic vent of Xích Viêm Khẩu, which Thiên Xu wards. No one may camp inside the warding ring, and no one lives here. An old fire-warden fort stands empty below the pillars.

places.name: Xích Viêm Khẩu
places.look: On a bare black cone high in Ngọc Hành Sơn, a wide red mouth glows and breathes heat, its lava cooling with a metallic sheen. A ring of carved grey warding pillars stands around the lower slope.

places.name: Thủ Hỏa Bảo
places.look: A squat stone fort below the warding pillars, its walls glazed by heat.
places.lore: From 460 a garrison kept watch on the vent here. When the warding pillars were raised in 1040 the Pivot withdrew the garrison, and the fort was left.

provinces.name: Lưu Sa Nguyên
provinces.lore: Desert, steppe and high plain along a river on the western edge. Its dunes move with every storm, and no one lives here. A warm spring in the sand is the only sure water.

places.name: Sa Nhãn Tuyền
places.look: A small warm pool among dunes, its water bubbling up through clean sand.
places.lore: It is the only sure water on the shifting plain. Travellers mark it with a tall pole so the dunes do not hide it, and replace the pole when it falls.

provinces.name: Hãn Hải Nguyên
provinces.lore: Desert and steppe along a river in the south-west. No one lives here now. A Fire and Earth vein lies on the steppe, and the cells of an ascetic sect stand empty in the mountain above.

places.name: Khổ Tu Viện
places.look: Bare stone cells cut into a mountainside above the desert, each just big enough to sit in.
places.lore: Ascetics who fasted in the desert founded it in 610. Fewer and fewer came to take up the hard life, and by 880 the cells were empty.

places.name: Liệt Nhật Mạch
places.look: A patch of steppe where the ground is hot even at night and the grass is scorched yellow.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Fire and Earth. Fire cultivators sit here at noon, and the ascetics of the mountain above once walked here barefoot as a trial.

provinces.name: Thương Mạc Nguyên
provinces.lore: Grey desert, steppe and mountain along a river in the south-west. Sand pythons hunt its dunes, and no one lives here. The empty temple of Thanh Đăng Tự stands on a mountain shoulder above the sand.

places.name: Hôi Mãng Cương
places.look: A ridge of grey dunes marked with long, smooth, curving tracks.
places.lore: Grey spirit pythons as long as boats bury themselves here and take camels. Their skins are prized for drums, and the caravans pay well for them.

places.name: Thanh Đăng Tự
places.look: A small temple on a mountain shoulder, its roof gone and a bronze lamp still hanging in the hall.
places.lore: A small sect of monks who kept a lamp burning for travellers founded it in 450. Its last abbot died in 760 with no disciple, and the lamp went out.

provinces.name: Vạn Nhận Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains rising steeply out of the desert edge. No one lives here but a few black-silver miners. Its leaning peak is a landmark across the desert.

places.name: Ô Ngân Khoáng
places.look: A narrow adit in dark mountain rock, its spoil black and heavy.
places.lore: Its black silver ore, silver darkened with sulphur, is refined at Song Kiều. The crews come up the desert edge in spring and leave before the autumn wind.

places.name: Ỷ Thiên Phong
places.look: A tall peak leaning over the desert edge, as if propping up the sky.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Caravans steer by it across the desert, and sword cultivators climb its overhang to practise against the wind.

provinces.name: Cổ Đạo Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains crossed by the oldest ore road in Ngọc Hành. Platinum is dug in its rock. On the road stands the stockade the miners' bosses held before Thiên Xu's fair weights came in 235.

places.name: Bạch Kim Khoáng
places.look: A small mine high on the mountain, with heavy grey grains washed in a cold stream.
places.lore: Its rare white metal does not rust or melt in a common forge. It goes straight to the Pivot's own forges for array anchors.

places.name: Thiên Môn Phong
places.look: Two high summits with a deep gap between them, where the old ore road passes.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore drivers call the gap the gate of heaven, and cultivators sit in it at dawn, when the wind through the gate is said to clear the meridians.

places.name: Thiết Môn Bảo
places.look: A stone stockade across the old ore road, its iron gate rusted open.
places.lore: The miners' bosses held this stockade from 140 to tax the ore at the gate. When Thiên Xu's assayers began to weigh ore in public at Song Kiều in 235, the miners stopped coming, and it was left.

provinces.name: Bát Diện Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountains whose peaks face every direction. No one lives here. Pyrite is dug on its flanks and sold for fire-strikers and sulphur.

places.name: Hoàng Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Brassy cubes of pyrite glittering in an abandoned grey mountain cut.
places.lore: No one works it now: its pyrite fetched too little as fire-strikers or roasted sulphur. Passing travellers still fill their pockets with it, thinking it gold.

places.name: Thạch Kính Phong
places.look: A peak with a smooth, polished rock face that flashes in the sun.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Miners use its flash to signal across the valleys, and cultivators gaze into its face to calm the mind before a breakthrough.

provinces.name: Lâm Uyên Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Very high mountains dropping to the inland sea in sheer walls, part of the great snow massif of the north-east. No one lives here. Fishermen see its cloud-hung peak from far out on the water.

places.name: Quải Vân Phong
places.look: A great snow peak above the sea cliffs, clouds hanging from its shoulders like banners.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Fishermen see it from far out on the inland sea, and cultivators of Water arts sit on its lower cliffs to draw on the sea mist.

provinces.name: Tiêu Thổ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with a few small volcanic vents, running down to the coast. No one lives here; its rock is burned black in places. An old sea patrol fort stands empty on the coast below.

places.name: Huân Yên Phong
places.look: A high peak streaked black by the smoke of small vents on its flanks.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Fire. The ground near its vents is warm all winter, and Fire cultivators camp beside them to temper their spirit fire.

places.name: Tuần Hải Bảo
places.look: A stone fort on a coastal headland, its seaward wall cracked and its beacon cold.
places.lore: Thiên Xu built it in 650 to watch for the pirates of Thôn Hải Môn. After the Pirate Purge destroyed them in 781 the fort was not needed, and it was stood down in 790.

provinces.name: Đà Đội
provinces.lore: Steppe and mountain on the south-western edge, on the caravan road to the desert. Its people keep camels and hire them to the caravans. Great eagles nest on the cliffs above and take lambs.

places.name: Hùng Điêu Nhai
places.look: High cliffs above the steppe, streaked white below the nests of great golden eagles.
places.lore: Spirit eagles nest here and take lambs and young camels. Their feathers are prized by fletchers, and Đà Đội's children are taught to lie flat when a shadow passes.

places.name: Đà Đội Thôn
places.look: A steppe village of stone houses with camels kneeling in the yards and bells hanging from the eaves.
places.lore: Its people keep camels and hire them to the desert caravans. Each camel's bell has its own note, and the owners know them in the dark.

provinces.name: Toái Thạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain, desert and steppe in the south-west, its slopes covered in broken stone. Rock salt is dug here and carried to the mining villages. An old grain stockade stands empty on the high plain.

places.name: Nham Diêm Khoáng
places.look: A pink-white salt cut in the mountain, with salt blocks stacked for the mule trains.
places.lore: Its rock salt goes to the mining villages of Ngọc Hành. A block of it is given to every new miner's family.

places.name: Lạc Đà Phong
places.look: A two-humped peak above the steppe, brown and bare.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, slow and enduring. Caravans know they are near Đà Đội when they see it, and Earth cultivators sit in the saddle between its humps.

places.name: Tích Lương Trại
places.look: Stone granaries inside a broken palisade on the high plain.
places.lore: It stored grain for the miners from 300. When the grain road moved to Song Kiều in 640 the stockade was left.

provinces.name: Bình Sa Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat desert and steppe along a river in the south-west. No village stands here. Caravans water their horses at a warm spring on the high ground.

places.name: Mã Ẩm Tuyền
places.look: A warm spring on the high ground above the sand, its rim trampled by hooves.
places.lore: Caravans water their horses here. It is said a horse that drinks here will not tire for a day.

provinces.name: Lam Vụ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains around Thanh Ải Phong, whose haze never lifts, running down to the coast. No sect holds the peak. Jade is cut on a lower shoulder, and pilgrims have crowded its paths since the haze lifted in 1180.

places.name: Thanh Ải Phong
places.look: The highest peak of Ngọc Hành Sơn rises above bare grey ridges, its upper slopes wrapped in a band of soft blue haze that never burns off, so the summit is never seen. Climbers say the haze looks thick from below and is gone when walked into.

places.name: Ải Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A cut on a lower shoulder of the mountain, just below the haze line, where a soft blue-grey jade shows in the abandoned face.
places.lore: The jade from here has the colour of Thanh Ải's haze. The miners never climbed above the haze line, and on the day the haze lifted in 1180 they left the cut and did not come back.

provinces.name: Hùng Quan Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains with a single pass between the western and eastern ore valleys. No one lives here. Ore trains cross the pass in summer.

places.name: Hành Vân Phong
places.look: A high bare peak with clouds always drifting across its summit.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore trains cross the pass below it in summer, and cultivators climb above the clouds to sit in the clear air.

provinces.name: Ngân Chu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains and forest on the coast, home to the sword-ore mine of Can Tương and the silver mine of Bạch Ngân. Miners live in the adits' camps, and Phượng Minh's border lies beyond the ridge. A boundary-stone peak stands over the mines, and an old silver fort lies on the shore.

places.name: Can Tương Khoáng
places.look: High on a steep slope, two adits open side by side in the grey rock, one a little larger than the other, with a small stone shrine between them blackened by forge smoke. A narrow path zigzags down toward Phất Y Cốc.

places.name: Bạch Ngân Khoáng
places.look: Below a hillside stained red with cinnabar, a fan of pale silver-grey spoil spills from the adit mouths, so the slope looks dipped in two colours. A walled smelting yard with a squat chimney sits at the foot.

places.name: Giới Bi Phong
places.look: A high peak with a stone stele on its summit facing the east.
places.lore: Thiên Xu's boundary with Phượng Minh is marked on its summit. Its qi runs to Metal and Fire, and on clear nights the glow of the cinnabar ridge can be seen from it.

places.name: Ngân Thuyền Bảo
places.look: A stone fort on the shore, its harbour silted up into a reed marsh.
places.lore: It guarded silver shipped by sea from 460. Its harbour silted up, and by 1003 the silver went overland to Song Kiều and the fort was left.

provinces.name: Bích Thảo Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain, steppe and grassland in the south-west. Herders summer their flocks on its grassy tops. No village stands here.

places.name: Mục Đồng Phong
places.look: A grassy peak with herders' stone shelters on its top.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood, mild and green. Herd boys play pipes on its summit in summer, and young cultivators find it a gentle place to first open their meridians.

provinces.name: Kim Phong Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain and steppe in the south-west, swept by a cold dry wind from the desert each autumn. No one lives here. Its white stone peak is seen from the caravan road.

places.name: Bạch Thạch Phong
places.look: A peak of white stone above the steppe, bright against the autumn sky.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. It can be seen from the caravan road, and cultivators climb it in autumn when the dry wind sharpens its qi.

provinces.name: Bạch Lãng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains along a river where it reaches the coast. No village stands here. Its sail-watching peak looks over the water.

places.name: Vọng Phàm Phong
places.look: A high peak above the river mouth, looking far over the water.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Families of sailors climb it to watch for returning sails, and leave a stone on the cairn for each one.

provinces.name: Đông Cực Nhai
provinces.lore: Steep mountains above the eastern coast, home to the star-iron mine of Thiên Ngoại Khoáng. No one lives here but Thối Tinh Môn's miners. Below its black hawk peak opens the mouth of the deep cave Cửu U Động, which the miners do not enter.

places.name: Thiên Ngoại Khoáng
places.gloss: Mine of the Iron from Beyond the Sky
places.look: A sheer mountain face streaked rust-red, with a vertical line of square adits cut one above another and iron chains hanging from each down to the ore yard below. A sorting shed with a dark roof stands at the bottom by a stream.

places.name: Hắc Ưng Phong
places.look: A dark peak above the eastern coast, black hawks wheeling around its summit.
places.lore: Below it opens the mouth of Cửu U Động, which Thối Tinh's miners do not enter. Its qi runs to Metal, and the hawks are said to hunt only those who sleep on its summit.

provinces.name: Thanh Trúc Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain with forest and bamboo on its southern flanks. No one lives here. Black magnetite sand is dug in a gully.

places.name: Hắc Sa Khoáng
places.look: Black magnetite sand washed in a gully and heaped on mats, clinging to any iron tool laid on it.
places.lore: Its magnetite sand is smelted into iron for tools. The washers pull it from the gravel with lodestones on strings.

places.name: Quân Tử Phong
places.look: A peak with bamboo on its flanks and a straight, upright rock summit.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Scholars come to paint its bamboo, and cultivators sit among the stems to practise stillness.

provinces.name: Hoàng Hoa
provinces.lore: Grassland and mountain in the south-east of Ngọc Hành, not far from Phượng Minh's border. Its people grow daylilies and graze cattle. A Wood vein lies in the grass above the village.

places.name: Lục Nhung Mạch
places.look: A grassy slope covered in soft green moss like velvet.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Cattle grazed here give rich milk, and the village keeps it for the calving cows.

places.name: Hoàng Hoa Thôn
places.look: A grassland village among fields of yellow daylilies, with cattle on the slopes.
places.lore: Its people grow daylilies for food and medicine and graze cattle. Dried flowers from here are sold in Tinh Hán as far as the quays.

provinces.name: Ngọa Vân Nguyên
provinces.lore: Mountain, grassland and badland on the southern coast. Cloud lies on its grassy plateau most mornings. No one lives here.

places.name: Cô Tháp Phong
places.look: A tower-like peak standing alone above the grassy plateau.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth. Cloud lies around its foot most mornings, and Earth cultivators sit on its top above the cloud.

provinces.name: Mục Khuyển
provinces.lore: Grassland, steppe, badland and mountain in the south-west. Its herders keep sheep and breed sheepdogs for all of Ngọc Hành. Garnets are dug in the mountain, and an Earth vein lies on the high plain.

places.name: Lựu Thạch Khoáng
places.look: Dark red garnets in grey mountain rock, picked out by hand.
places.lore: Its garnets are cut into beads, and the small ones are crushed into polishing grit for the forges of Thối Tinh.

places.name: Thạch Căn Mạch
places.look: A rock outcrop on the high plain, its grey stone veined like roots.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, deep and steady. Herders say no storm has ever knocked down a cairn built on it.

places.name: Mục Khuyển Thôn
places.look: A steppe village with sheepdogs lying at every door and flocks on the hills.
places.lore: Its herders breed sheepdogs for all of Ngọc Hành. A pup from here is paid for in silver.

provinces.name: Phi Bộc Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with bamboo and forest along a river that falls in long cascades. No one lives here. Silver is dug in thin veins in its rock.

places.name: Ngân Ti Khoáng
places.look: Thin threads of native silver in a damp mountain face beside the falls.
places.lore: Its silver is picked out by hand with fine chisels and refined at Song Kiều. Silversmiths value the threads for wire.

places.name: Ngọc Lâu Phong
places.look: A tall pale peak above the falls, its walls stacked like the floors of a tower.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Cultivators sit behind the falls at its foot to temper the body under the water's weight.

provinces.name: Trùng Loan Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains standing in rank behind rank in the south of Ngọc Hành. No one lives here. Banded marble is quarried on a low shoulder.

places.name: Cẩm Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A quarry of banded marble on a low shoulder, its blocks patterned like woven silk.
places.lore: Its marble is carved into tables and screens for the halls of Tinh Hán. Blocks are lowered down the slope on ropes from Thằng Ma.

places.name: Hồng Nhạn Phong
places.look: A high peak where wild geese rest on its ledges on their migration.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Hunters do not shoot the geese here, and cultivators read the seasons by their coming and going.

provinces.name: Lục Thủy Câu
provinces.lore: Mountain, grassland and steppe along a green river in the south. Herders summer here, and a copper mine works the gully. No village stands here.

places.name: Đồng Tỉnh Khoáng
places.look: A deep copper shaft in the gully with a windlass and leather buckets.
places.lore: Its copper ore comes up by bucket and is weighed at Song Kiều. The shaft floods every spring and must be bailed by hand.

places.name: Thanh Loa Phong
places.look: A spiral-ridged green peak above the river, like a conch shell.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herders summer below it, and cultivators climb its spiral path in one breath as a test.

provinces.name: Chu Nhai Câu
provinces.lore: Red badland, mountain and grassland along a river in the south. No one lives here. Copper ore is dug from the red cliffs by the river.

places.name: Lam Lục Khoáng
places.look: Red cliffs by the river streaked green and blue with copper ore.
places.lore: Its copper ore is broken from the cliffs and floated by river to the landing at Mã Đầu.

places.name: Xích Dực Phong
places.look: A red peak above the badland gully, its two ridges spread like wings.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Fire with a base of Earth. Fire cultivators sit between its wings at sunset, when the red rock glows.

provinces.name: Bích Tiêu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with forest and bamboo in the south. No one lives here. An old boundary stockade lies under an avalanche slope.

places.name: Cửu Tiêu Phong
places.look: A very high peak above the forest, its summit often lost in sky.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal, thin and sharp. Cultivators who reach its summit say the air there makes the spirit feel weightless.

places.name: Thủ Bi Trại
places.look: Broken walls under an avalanche slope, half buried in rock.
places.lore: From 520 a garrison guarded a boundary stele set after the Compact. An avalanche buried the stockade in 1006, and the stele was moved lower.

provinces.name: Song Tuyền Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains along a river in the south, fed by two springs from the same rock. No one lives here. Topaz is dug in its rock.

places.name: Hoàng Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: Golden crystals in grey mountain rock above the river, in a cut half full of spring water.
places.lore: Topaz from here was once cut at Tinh Hán into ring stones and seals, but the springs have not run low in the dry months for years, and the crews no longer come.

places.name: Tử Cái Phong
places.look: A peak with a cap of purple rock over the twin springs.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Herb gatherers find a purple lichen on its cap that alchemists buy for calming pills.

provinces.name: Thanh Ngạn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain and forest running down to the inland sea in the north-east. No one lives here. Its hibiscus peak flowers in pink every summer.

places.name: Phù Dung Phong
places.look: A forested peak above the shore that flowers pink each summer.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Sailors on the inland sea say summer has come when its slopes turn pink.

provinces.name: Thiên Biên Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge at the Edge of the Sky
provinces.lore: High mountains on the southern rim of Ngọc Hành, looking down toward Thính Vũ's vein of Kinh Lôi Mạch. No one lives here. An old border watch fort stands on its heights.

places.name: Tử Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A high cut showing veins of purple stone under the sheer wall.
places.lore: Its purple jade is rare and goes to the Pivot for seals. The crews work only in high summer.

places.name: Tuyệt Bích Phong
places.look: A sheer high peak on the southern rim, its walls dropping toward the south.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. From its edge the Pivot's old watchmen could see as far as Kinh Lôi Mạch, and climbers still use their iron pegs.

places.name: Nam Vọng Bảo
places.look: A stone fort on the heights, its walls broken and its watch platform facing south.
places.lore: The Pivot's border watch on the south ridge from 512, looking down toward Kinh Lôi Mạch. It was stood down in 806 after the truce.

provinces.name: Lan Khê Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain and forest along an orchid-lined brook in the south. No one lives here. A red silver mine and an old toll stockade lie on the old ore road.

places.name: Xích Ngân Khoáng
places.look: Dark red silver ore glinting in a mountain cut by the old road.
places.lore: Its red silver ore is roasted on site and refined at Song Kiều. It is richer in silver than any other mine on the old road.

places.name: Ưng Sào Phong
places.look: A peak with hawks' nests on its cliffs above the orchid brook.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Young cultivators climb its cliffs for hawk chicks to tame.

places.name: Hạp Khẩu Trại
places.look: A stockade half buried under a landslide at the mouth of a gorge.
places.lore: A toll stockade on the ore road from 300. A landslide buried it in 718, and the road was moved to the other bank.

provinces.name: Thiên Lý Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains around Cùng Mục Phong, the Peak of the Farthest Sight. Phất Y Cốc's disciples climb through it to read the sword cuts of 1130. An old bandit stockade stands empty on its heights.

places.name: Cùng Mục Phong
places.look: A narrow summit of pale granite stands above the ranges, so high that on clear days the plains and the shine of the inland sea seem to lie at its feet. Its flat top rock is criss-crossed with long, deep sword cuts that look as fresh as if they were made yesterday.

places.name: Hắc Phong Trại
places.look: A stockade of rough stone on the windy heights, its walls broken.
places.lore: A bandit hold of rogue cultivators (tán tu) from 880, who robbed the ore trains. Thiên Xu cleared it in 940.

provinces.name: Bích Lưu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains and a little bamboo along a green torrent in the south. No one lives here. Gold is washed from the torrent's gravel.

places.name: Lưu Kim Khoáng
places.look: Wooden sluices in the green torrent, with washers in leather aprons.
places.lore: Gold is washed from the torrent's gravel after the spring floods. Every washer pays a tenth to the Pivot by weight.

places.name: Ngọc Nữ Phong
places.look: A slender pale peak above the torrent, like a standing woman.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Women cultivators of Water arts come to meditate at its foot by the torrent.

provinces.name: Huyền Nham Nhai
provinces.lore: Mountain cliffs above the eastern coast, home to the deep black iron shaft of Huyền Thiết Khoáng. Miners and oxen live in the mine's camp. A massive peak stands over the winch house.

places.name: Huyền Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Deep in the mountain a single great shaft opens under a massive stone winch house, and the ramp down to the road is worn into ruts a hand deep by carts that each carry one black ingot.

places.name: Trấn Sơn Phong
places.look: A massive dark peak above the winch house of Huyền Thiết.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth and Metal, heavy as the iron below it. Body cultivators carry stones up it to temper their bones.

provinces.name: Thằng Ma
provinces.lore: Grassland, forest and steppe in the north of Ngọc Hành. Its people grow hemp and twist it into rope for the mines' winches and hoists. A Wood vein lies in the forest above.

places.name: Lục Ấm Mạch
places.look: A shady forest grove above the hemp fields where the air is always cool.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Hemp seed soaked in its spring is said to grow the strongest fibre.

places.name: Thằng Ma Thôn
places.look: A grassland village among hemp fields, with long rope walks along the lane.
places.lore: Its people twist hemp into rope for the mines' winches. A rope that breaks is traced back to its maker.

provinces.name: Khô Thảo Nguyên
provinces.lore: Grassland and badland in the north-west, dry by midsummer. No one lives here. Orpiment is dug here, and a red Earth and Fire vein lies in the badland.

places.name: Thư Hoàng Khoáng
places.look: Bright yellow orpiment in grey mountain rock.
places.lore: Its yellow pigment is sold to talisman makers and painters. It is poisonous, and the diggers wear cloth over their faces.

places.name: Xích Long Mạch
places.look: A red badland ridge winding like a dragon, warm to the touch.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth and Fire. No grass grows on its spine, and herders say it shifts a little each century.

provinces.name: Mã Đầu
provinces.lore: Steppe, badland and grassland along a river in the north-west. Its people load ore and wool onto river boats at the landing. Wild spirit bulls graze the steppe, and an old sect stands empty on the grassland.

places.name: Hắc Ngưu Cương
places.look: A steppe ridge trampled by a herd of black bulls.
places.lore: Wild spirit bulls graze here and charge anything that comes near. Their horns are carved into bows.

places.name: Hoành Đao Môn
places.look: A ruined gate and halls on the grassland, with a stone sabre rack in the yard.
places.lore: A small sect of saber fighters founded in 560. Its head left on a journey in 870 and never returned, and the disciples scattered by 872.

places.name: Mã Đầu Thôn
places.look: A river village with boats tied at a long timber landing.
places.lore: Its people load ore and wool onto river boats bound for the coast. They are paid by the load and counted by a tally stick.

provinces.name: Hải Giác Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountain and forest on a cape of the inland sea. No one lives here. Blue iron is dug on its slopes, and fishermen steer by its peak.

places.name: Thanh Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Blue-grey iron ore in a mountain cut above the sea.
places.lore: Its iron ore is carried down to boats and shipped to Tinh Hán's quays. Smiths say it takes a fine edge.

places.name: Ngư Ông Phong
places.look: A peak on the cape shaped like a fisherman bent over his line.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Water. Fishermen steer by it, and cultivators of Water arts sit on its spray-wet ledge at dawn.

provinces.name: Kiều Mạch
provinces.lore: Dry hill grass rising to bare rock in the north of the ridges, with no river to water it. Its few farmers grow buckwheat and graze goats on the high slopes. Phượng Minh's disciples cross it on their way to the northern border.

places.name: Quy Vũ Lĩnh
places.look: A long brown ridge where migrating birds rest in thousands every autumn and spring.
places.lore: The villagers say the birds come back each year to the phoenix's land. Its qi runs Thổ (earth), steady and slow.

places.name: Kiều Mạch Thôn
places.look: A handful of stone houses on a dry hillside, ringed by fields of white-flowered buckwheat.
places.lore: Buckwheat grows where the rain is short and there is no river, and the village has lived on it and on goats for generations. Its noodles are sold in Thiều Âm Thị.

provinces.name: Thiết Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A wall of high bare mountain on the western edge of the ridges, too steep for fields or villages. Only miners live here, in season, at the black iron workings below the summit. Phượng Minh calls it the western wall of its home and keeps a beacon on it.

places.name: Ô Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Adits in a black rock face high on the mountain, with a stone smelting hearth on a ledge below.
places.lore: Phượng Minh's smiths take its black iron for blades and the bronze-and-iron frames of the palace bells.

places.name: Xích Tiêu Phong
places.look: A tall bare peak of reddish rock on the western wall, often lit red at sunset while the valleys are dark.
places.lore: Phượng Minh keeps a beacon on its top, lit only in war. Its qi runs Kim (metal) through the iron in the rock.

provinces.name: Thúy Đồng Câu
provinces.lore: Steep ravines of rock and bamboo east of the palace, planted with wutong by Phượng Minh's gardeners. No one farms here; the palace keeps the slopes for its trees and its fire disciples' training climbs. Its highest peak is said to look like a phoenix's raised wing.

places.name: Phượng Dực Phong
places.look: A peak with one long sloping arm of rock and bamboo, like a raised wing, above ravines of wutong.
places.lore: Fire disciples run up its arm at dawn as a training climb. Its qi runs Mộc (wood), carried up from the bamboo.

provinces.name: Trúc Ly
provinces.lore: Bamboo hills and a river valley on the south-western slopes of the ridges. Its people weave bamboo fences, baskets and screens and grow vegetables in the valley floor. Their basket weavers make the walls that hold back the sea at Bích Lãng.

places.name: Vân Trúc Lâm
places.look: Tall pale bamboo on a steep rocky slope, its tops often hidden in low cloud.
places.lore: Its canes grow thin and strong in the thin soil, and Trúc Ly's weavers prize them for fine work.

places.name: Trúc Ly Thôn
places.look: A valley village where every yard is fenced in woven bamboo and half-finished baskets stand stacked by the doors.
places.lore: Its weavers make baskets, screens and the great stone-filled baskets of Bích Lãng's sea wall.

provinces.name: Bạch Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High pale crags and pockets of forest in the heart of the ridges, without water or villages. Silver miners come and go from a working on its eastern side. The roosting peak above it is a place of trial for Phượng Minh's wood cultivators.

places.name: Nguyệt Ngân Khoáng
places.look: A narrow silver working in pale rock, its spoil heaps glinting white in moonlight.
places.lore: Its silver goes to the palace's inlay makers. Miners say the best seams show themselves on full-moon nights.

places.name: Thê Hoàng Phong
places.look: A white crag crowned by a single old wutong growing from a crack in the summit rock.
places.lore: Phượng Minh's wood cultivators sit under the tree for trial. Its qi runs Mộc (wood), unusually for so bare a rock.

provinces.name: Cầm Huyền
provinces.lore: Bamboo, grass and forest along a river on the southern slopes, rising to the crags under the palace. Its people raise silkworms and twist zither and pipa strings for the instrument makers of Thiều Âm. High above the village stands the empty hall where Cửu Thiều's chime makers worked.

places.name: Thực Thiết Cốc
places.look: A bamboo valley stripped bare in patches, its stream banks littered with chewed cane and gnawed iron pots.
places.lore: Black-and-white spirit bears, the iron-eaters of the old books, live here on bamboo and steal any iron they can find. Villagers leave old pots at the valley mouth to keep them away from the forge.

places.name: Kích Khánh Đường
places.look: A roofless stone hall high on the crags, its floor scattered with broken L-shaped slabs of chime stone.
places.lore: Cửu Thiều Cung's chime makers cut and tuned their stone chimes here. The hall was smashed in the War of the Nine Shao in 340, and the broken chimes still ring faintly when stepped on.

places.name: Cầm Huyền Hương
places.look: A river hamlet of silkworm sheds, with skeins of twisted silk string hung to dry on long racks by the water.
places.lore: Its people twist silk into strings for zithers and pipas and sell them to Thiều Âm Thị. They boil the cocoons in river water and say it makes the strings sing true.

provinces.name: Trúc Phiệt
provinces.lore: Dense bamboo on a river that runs south from the ridges toward the coast. Its people cut cane and float it downriver in great rafts to Trúc Thực Viên and the coast. A rocky ridge east of the village holds the bamboo ode carved by Phượng Minh's founder.

places.name: Vịnh Trúc Lĩnh
places.look: A rocky ridge above the bamboo where a short poem is cut into a flat rock face.
places.lore: Phượng Minh's founder Ngô Thê Đồng is said to have cut the bamboo ode here in the palace's first years. Its qi runs Mộc (wood).

places.name: Trúc Phiệt Thôn
places.look: A riverside village among dense bamboo, its bank lined with great half-lashed rafts of cut cane.
places.lore: Its cutters float bamboo downriver to the coast every spring flood and walk home along the bank.

provinces.name: Thạch Lũy Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Almost all bare high mountain, dropping straight into the gulf on the south-east. No one lives here but copper miners at the sea's edge. Phượng Minh's fire disciples climb its tallest peak to meet the sunrise.

places.name: Xích Đồng Khoáng
places.look: Copper workings cut into the foot of the sea cliffs, the rock stained green and red where the waves wash it, with a timber landing for the ore boats.
places.lore: Miners from Thanh Khê work the seams at low tide and pull back when the sea turns. Its copper goes by boat to the port for the bronze bells of the palace and the frames of the harbour lanterns.

places.name: Vọng Dương Phong
places.look: A tall bare peak above the gulf, its eastern face scorched dark by the morning sun.
places.lore: Phượng Minh's fire disciples climb it to take in the first sun. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

provinces.name: Thanh Trúc Câu
provinces.lore: Rock ridges and bamboo ravines south-east of the palace, wet and steep. It has no village; bamboo cutters and herb gatherers pass through it. Cinnabar streaks the rock of its main peak.

places.name: Hàm Đan Phong
places.look: A bamboo-clad peak whose rock shows through in streaks of bright red.
places.lore: Cinnabar runs in thin streaks through the rock, too thin to mine. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

provinces.name: Vân Đào Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bamboo-clad mountains falling to a mangrove shore on the gulf, often lost in sea cloud. No village stands here; azurite miners work a pit by the shore. Fishers of the gulf steer by the cliff above it.

places.name: Thạch Thanh Khoáng
places.look: Shallow pits by the shore where the rock is veined bright blue.
places.lore: Its azurite is ground for blue pigment and sold to painters and to the palace's lacquer workers.

places.name: Lâm Hải Nhai
places.look: A sheer bamboo-topped cliff dropping straight into the gulf, white with sea birds.
places.lore: Gulf fishers steer by it in fog. Its qi runs Thủy (water), drawn up from the sea.

provinces.name: Sa Trúc
provinces.lore: Bamboo and rock running down to a sandy shore south of the ridges. Its people fish with bamboo traps and cut cane on the slopes. On clear evenings the ridge above glows red long after sunset.

places.name: Ngưng Hà Lĩnh
places.look: A rocky ridge above the bamboo that glows red on clear evenings long after the sun has set.
places.lore: The villagers say the sunset clouds gather here to sleep. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

places.name: Sa Trúc Thôn
places.look: A fishing village of thatched bamboo houses on a sandy cove, with rows of cone-shaped fish traps of split cane drying on the beach.
places.lore: Its people set their traps in the shallows at dusk and lift them at dawn, and cut cane on the slopes behind to sell to passing boats. When the ridge above glows red after sunset, they say the next day's catch will be good.

provinces.name: Trà Pha
provinces.lore: Grass hills and patches of forest in the north-east, rising to bare rock, without a river. Its people grow tea on the slopes and send it down to Mạch Điền and the plain. A warm pool in the woods above the village is carpeted with fallen wutong leaves every autumn.

places.name: Ngô Diệp Trì
places.look: A warm pool in a wood above the tea slopes, its surface carpeted every autumn with broad yellow wutong leaves.
places.lore: Tea pickers bathe here at the end of the season. The leaves are never cleared; the villagers say the phoenix likes the pool as it is.

places.name: Trà Pha Thôn
places.look: A hill village of grey roofs above rows of dark green tea bushes clipped into waist-high hedges.
places.lore: Its tea is carried down to Mạch Điền and the plain; the first picking of spring goes to the palace's dawn rites.

provinces.name: Thạch Duẩn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Karst towers, bamboo and rock along the gulf, facing the spotted-bamboo isle of Tương Phi Đảo. No one lives here; alchemists' miners take stalactite from the caves. Boatmen fall silent passing the cliffs, as they do passing the isle.

places.name: Tương Phi Đảo
places.look: A small steep island off the coast, covered from shore to crown in dense bamboo whose canes are flecked with purple-brown spots, like old tear stains. There is no landing and no roof; the bamboo comes right down to the rocks.

places.name: Chung Nhũ Động
places.look: A sea-facing karst cave hung with pale dripping stalactites, many broken off at the tips.
places.lore: Alchemists' miners take the stalactite milk-stone for pills of the bones and lungs. Phượng Minh allows only fallen and broken pieces to be taken from the inner hall.

provinces.name: Lôi Hậu
provinces.lore: A storm coast of bamboo, jungle and rock below the thunder peaks, where Lôi Ngô Lâm takes the lightning. Its people gather the struck wutong for Phượng Minh's workshops, and fish when the sky is clear. The palace has guarded the wood closely since the Thunder Vein War.

places.name: Lôi Ngô Lâm
places.look: In the lowland jungle under the storm peaks, a wood of tall wutong trees stands split and scarred by lightning, green crowns still living above trunks streaked with white burn scars and black splits. The air smells of rain and scorch, and the ground is littered with fused, glassy sand.

places.name: Lôi Hậu Thôn
places.look: A bamboo-walled fishing village on the storm shore, its sheds stacked with scarred wutong logs under palace seals.
places.lore: After each storm clears, its gatherers go into Lôi Ngô Lâm for fallen struck wood and carry it out for Phượng Minh's workshops; on cloudy days they fish instead.

provinces.name: Hi Quang Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest mountains of the south, rising to Cao Cương Phong above the coast, with a little volcanic ground. No one lives here; pilgrims and Phượng Minh's disciples climb to the crest at dawn. Realgar is dug on the flank of the old volcanic cone.

places.name: Cao Cương Phong
places.look: A high bare ridge-top above the wutong hills ends in a flat crest of pale gold stone that takes the first light of dawn before anything else in the south. A single stone pillar stands on the crest, worn at its top into the shape of a perch.

places.name: Đan Hoàng Quật
places.look: Orange-red workings on the flank of an old volcanic cone high above the sea, the spoil bright as rust.
places.lore: Its realgar is used in alchemy and in charms against snakes and poison. Miners work with cloth over their faces and never stay past noon.

provinces.name: Tiêu Giang
provinces.lore: A warm river plain of grass and jungle opening on the southern sea. Its people grow bananas and rice and fish the river mouth. A spirit vein lies in its open fields, and the farmers plant rice around it first.

places.name: Thanh Hòa Mạch
places.look: A low rise in the open fields where the rice grows taller and greener than anywhere around it.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein close under the soil. The farmers of Tiêu Giang plant the rise first each year, and the palace takes a share of its grain for seed.

places.name: Tiêu Giang Thôn
places.look: A river-mouth village on stilts among banana groves, fish weirs set across the brown water below.
places.lore: Its people grow bananas and rice and fish the river mouth, and send dried fish up to Trúc Thực Viên for its beasts.

provinces.name: Bạch Lộ
provinces.lore: Grass shore, jungle and rocky hills along the southern coast. Its people fish the shallows and keep buffalo. Wild elephants come down from the hills to its grass in the dry season.

places.name: Cuồng Tượng Nguyên
places.look: Tall grass under the hills trampled into broad paths, with broken trees along its edge.
places.lore: Wild spirit elephants come down from the jungle hills to graze here in the dry season, and a bull in musth will charge anything that moves. Hunters come for tusks; few come twice.

places.name: Bạch Lộ Thôn
places.look: A shore village of thatched houses where white egrets stand in the shallows among the moored boats.
places.lore: Its people fish the shallows and keep water buffalo on the shore grass, and bar their gates in the dry season when the elephants come down.

provinces.name: Hôi Tẫn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High volcanic mountains on the south coast, grey with ash around Niết Hỏa Khẩu. No one lives here; the burned wutong sprout again after every outburst. Phượng Minh's fire disciples come to the vent for trial and leave before dark.

places.name: Niết Hỏa Khẩu
places.look: High in the wutong hills, a fire vent opens in a slope of black ash, ringed by burned wutong stumps that have sprouted fresh green shoots from their charred trunks. Heat shimmers over the mouth, and the ash around it is warm underfoot.

provinces.name: Đằng Khê
provinces.lore: Low jungle and mangrove on a river near the southern sea, some of it below the tide line. Its people cut rattan and camphor and fish the brook. Camphor from its forest goes to Thanh Khê's healers.

places.name: Long Não Lâm
places.look: A lowland forest of tall smooth-trunked trees whose air smells sharp and cool even at noon.
places.lore: Its trees give borneol camphor, which Thanh Khê's healers use for wounds and fevers.

places.name: Đằng Khê Thôn
places.look: A jungle village on a slow brook, coils of cut rattan soaking in the water beside the houses.
places.lore: Its people cut rattan and camphor and weave rattan mats and chairs for the ports.

provinces.name: Ô Mộc
provinces.lore: Deep jungle on the southern coast, much of it at or below the sea. Its people cut ebony and fish from the mangrove edge. In the jungle stand the burned stockades of a Thôn Hải shore camp, destroyed in the Pirate Purge.

places.name: Ẩn Phàm Trại
places.look: Charred stockade posts in the jungle above a hidden creek, where a boat slip has rotted into the mud.
places.lore: Thôn Hải Môn's shore camp, where its pirates hid boats and stores within reach of the southern coast. Phượng Minh's fleet burned it in 780, a year before the Purge ended at Thôn Hải's own islet.

places.name: Ngô Căn Mạch
places.look: A wild wutong in the jungle with roots spread over a slab of mossy rock, the ground around it springy and warm.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein runs under the tree. No one knows who planted a wutong so far into the jungle.

places.name: Ô Mộc Thôn
places.look: A village on low mangrove ground behind an earth bank, with black ebony logs stacked under its eaves.
places.lore: Its people cut ebony in the jungle and fish from the mangrove edge; the wood goes to Thiều Âm for flutes and zither pegs.

provinces.name: Khổng Tước
provinces.lore: Jungle and rock on a small stretch of southern coast. Its people trap fish and gather the feathers shed by wild peacocks, which they sell to fan makers and talisman makers. Black crocodiles hold the mud shore beyond the village.

places.name: Hắc Ngạc Chử
places.look: A mud shore between jungle and sea, scored with long drag marks and the dark backs of basking crocodiles.
places.lore: Black spirit crocodiles hold the shore and take anything that comes to drink. The village's fishers launch their boats well beyond it.

places.name: Khổng Tước Thôn
places.look: A small jungle-edge village by the sea, bundles of long green-and-gold feathers hanging in its doorways.
places.lore: Its people fish and gather the feathers wild peacocks shed in the jungle, and sell them to fan makers and to Bách Vũ Các.

provinces.name: Hoang Đằng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and jungle held by the dark apes of Huyền Viên Lâm, too wild for villages. Only miners of red stone come here, and only in the morning. Phượng Minh's disciples hunt the jungle edge for practice, and the apes remember them.

places.name: Huyền Viên Lâm
places.look: A dense jungle below the wutong hills, where huge strangler figs rise above the canopy, their crowns knotted with the dark apes' woven sleeping platforms of branch and vine. Calls and crashing branches carry from inside, but nothing shows at the edge.

places.name: Kê Huyết Khoáng
places.look: A small quarry at the jungle's foot where the pale stone is splashed with blood-red cinnabar.
places.lore: Its chicken-blood stone is carved into seals for Phượng Minh's elders. The miners come only in the morning and leave fruit at the jungle edge for the apes.

provinces.name: Thạch Lựu
provinces.lore: Upland grass and forest on a river in the north-west of the ridges. Its people grow pomegranates and millet on river terraces. Red sandstone outcrops on the hill above hold a fire vein.

places.name: Đan Hà Huyệt
places.look: A cleft in a red sandstone outcrop on the hill, its rock warm to the touch even in the rain.
places.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein comes close to the surface here. Phượng Minh's young fire disciples are sent to sit in the cleft for their first winter.

places.name: Thạch Lựu Thôn
places.look: A river village of grey roofs above terraced pomegranate orchards, red with flowers in early summer.
