places.lore: Its pomegranates go down to the palace and the markets, and a bride of the village carries one on her wedding day for many children.

provinces.name: Hải Giác
provinces.lore: A tiny grassy cape at the southern tip of the ridges' coast. Its people fish and gather salt. A spirit vein on the shore rises and falls with the tide.

places.name: Triều Tịch Nhãn
places.look: A round rock pool on the shore that fills and empties with the tide, ringed by smooth white stones.
places.lore: A Thủy (water) vein that swells at high tide and fades at low. The fishers say it breathes with the sea, as the lake at Hồ Tâm does.

places.name: Hải Giác Thôn
places.look: A handful of fishing huts on a grassy cape at the end of the coast, with shallow salt pans cut into the flat rock below and boats pulled up in a cleft.
places.lore: Its people fish the currents off the point and boil sea salt in the dry season, and say they live at the corner of the sea. They read the tide by the rock pool on the shore, which fills and empties a little before the sea does.

provinces.name: Đan Kiều
provinces.lore: Dry steppe, red badlands and grass along a river in the north of the ridges, the one dry country of Thê Ngô Lĩnh. Its people graze horses and goats and trade hides at the town by the red bridge. A hot spring in the badlands stains bathers' skin rust-red.

places.name: Xích Thổ Thang
places.look: A hot spring in a hollow of red badland clay, its water opaque and rust-coloured, with gullies of bare red earth running down to it.
places.lore: Herders from Đan Kiều soak their stiff joints here after the horse fairs, and its water stains skin red for days. Phượng Minh's fire disciples say the iron in the clay warms the blood, and come in winter.

places.name: Đan Kiều Trấn
places.look: A walled river town on the edge of the steppe, its two halves joined by a humped bridge lacquered bright red.
places.lore: Herders bring horses, goats and hides to its market, and Phượng Minh's disciples cross the bridge on the road north. The palace relacquers the bridge every ten years.

provinces.name: Mục Dương
provinces.lore: Upland grass and forest on a river in the north-western hills. Its people herd sheep and goats and sell wool down the river. Red wolves den in the forest below, and the shepherds keep big dogs.

places.name: Hồng Lang Cương
places.look: A forested ridge where rust-red wolves can be seen at dusk slipping between the trees.
places.lore: Packs of red spirit wolves hunt the forest and the sheep. They whistle to each other instead of howling, and the shepherds listen for it.

places.name: Mục Dương Thôn
places.look: Stone sheepfolds and low houses by a river on the upland grass, big dogs lying at every gate.
places.lore: Its shepherds sell wool down the river and keep their dogs against the red wolves.

provinces.name: Ngô Miêu
provinces.lore: Grass, bamboo and forest climbing from a river to the ridges just north of the palace. Its people raise wutong seedlings for the palace terraces, as they have since the founding. A peak above the village is where Phượng Minh's disciples practise their first sword cries.

places.name: Thanh Minh Lĩnh
places.look: A bare ridge above the bamboo where any shout comes back clearly three times.
places.lore: Young disciples of Phượng Minh practise their first sword cries here. Its qi runs Kim (metal).

places.name: Ngô Miêu Thôn
places.look: A village by the palace road ringed by beds of young wutong in neat rows, each tagged with a strip of red cloth.
places.lore: Since Phượng Minh's founding its people have raised the wutong for the palace terraces. Every sapling that leaves the village has a red tag tied by the child who watered it.

provinces.name: Minh Tuyền Câu
provinces.lore: A high ravine of rock and forest on the western ridges, cut by a cold mountain stream. No one lives here; the springs whistle through the rocks in the wind. Phượng Minh's elders discourage disciples from lingering to listen.

places.name: Huyền Tiêu Phong
places.look: A thin spire of rock above the singing ravine, pierced near its top by a hole the wind whistles through.
places.lore: Its whistle carries far on stormy nights, and the palace's elders tell disciples not to follow it. Its qi runs Kim (metal).

provinces.name: Thê Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains west of the palace, nearly always in cloud, with forest in the hollows. No villages stand here; miners dig red jade below the summit. The palace gathers fallen feathers on its peak as a rite.

places.name: Xích Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A narrow cut in grey rock high under the clouds, its floor scattered with chips of red-veined jade.
places.lore: Its red jade is carved into the palace's rite vessels and the pendants of its elders.

places.name: Lạc Vũ Phong
places.look: A high cloud-wrapped summit where a flat ledge is strewn with feathers blown up from the valleys.
places.lore: Once a year Phượng Minh's disciples climb to gather the feathers for the palace's rites. Its qi runs Thổ (earth).

provinces.name: Nhục Quế
provinces.lore: Jungle, bamboo and rock on the eastern slopes of the ridges, wet and without a river. Its people strip cinnamon bark and sell it to the ports. Above them stand the walls of a mountain market town that emptied when Cửu Thiều fell.

places.name: Hồng Bích Nhai
places.look: A long cliff of red rock above the jungle, streaked black where the rain runs down, with a ledge near its top where the old mountain road once ran.
places.lore: The cinnamon cutters of Nhục Quế steer home by it when the jungle closes in, and the road along its ledge once led to the empty market town of Tiêu Sơn. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire), warm in the red rock.

places.name: Tiêu Sơn Thị
places.look: Grass-grown walls on a high shoulder of rock, with rows of stone stall bases lining a single street.
places.lore: A mountain market town of Cửu Thiều Cung where pipes and flutes were sold to the palace and the plain. After the palace fell in 340 its people left within a year, like those of Vân Môn, and the town was never resettled.

places.name: Nhục Quế Thôn
places.look: A jungle village where rolled strips of bark dry on racks in every yard and the air smells sweet and hot.
places.lore: Its people strip cinnamon from the hill trees and sell it in Thanh Khê to the ships.

provinces.name: Hồng Thổ Hoang
provinces.lore: High mountains and red badlands at the north-western corner of the plain, dry and bare. No one lives here but copper miners in season. Its red peak is said to have grown from a single fallen feather.

places.name: Chu Đồng Khoáng
places.look: Open copper workings stepped into red badland rock below the peak, the spoil heaps streaked green and a line of mule tracks winding down toward the plain.
places.lore: Miners come up from the plain in the dry season and leave before the rains wash the badlands out. Its copper goes to Lai Nghi, where it is cast into the bronze bells of the nine tiers.

places.name: Xích Vũ Phong
places.look: A bare red peak above the badlands, its rock shading from orange to deep crimson, its summit split into thin blades like the feathers of a raised wing.
places.lore: The copper miners below say a red bird dropped one feather here and the mountain grew from it. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire), dry and fierce, and Phượng Minh's fire disciples cross the badlands to sit on it in the hottest month.

provinces.name: Hoàng Lương
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grass on the inland hills west of Lai Nghi, without a river. Its people grow millet and herd goats. Jackal packs den on a rise near the village.

places.name: Quần Sài Cương
places.look: A low grassy rise pocked with dens, where gaunt red-brown jackals watch the road.
places.lore: Spirit jackals hunt in packs here and follow travellers at a distance. The goatherds bring their flocks in before dark.

places.name: Hoàng Lương Thôn
places.look: A dry hill village of mud-walled houses among fields of tall yellow millet.
places.lore: Its people grow millet and herd goats. Travellers who nap at its inn while the millet cooks are teased that they will dream a whole life before supper.

provinces.name: Thủ Mạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains running to the coast at the plain's western border with the heart, where Đan Sơn Mạch lies. No villages stand here; Phượng Minh's guards and cinnabar miners are its only people. The palace has kept the ridge guarded since Thính Vũ Lâu's attack in 1150.

places.name: Đan Sơn Mạch
places.look: A steep mountain flank of vermilion rock is split by a long seam that glows a deeper crimson at dusk, where the vein's qi runs close to the surface. Along the ridge above stand the scorched stone footings of watch platforms from the last war.

places.name: Đan Sa Quật
places.look: A guarded grotto in red rock below the ridge, its walls glittering crimson in torchlight.
places.lore: Phượng Minh digs cinnabar here near the vein, under guard since the war of 1150. Its cinnabar goes to the palace's alchemists.

provinces.name: Phong Mật
provinces.lore: Hill meadows and forest above the plain, cool and flowery. Its people keep bees and sell honey and wax to the towns. Golden eagles nest on the cliff above the village.

places.name: Liệp Điêu Nhai
places.look: A cliff above the meadows whitened with droppings, great stick nests on its ledges.
places.lore: Spirit golden eagles nest here and take lambs and goats from the hills. Young cultivators climb for the chicks and seldom manage it.

places.name: Phong Mật Thôn
places.look: A hill village among flowering meadows, its walls lined with log beehives.
places.lore: Its beekeepers sell honey and wax to Lai Nghi and Hoàng Vân, and Lễ Tuyền buys its honey for wine.

provinces.name: Tử Thái
provinces.lore: Flat steppe and grass on the southern gulf shore, barely above the sea. Its people gather laver from the rocks and fish the shallows. The burned walls of a salt town stand on the shore, destroyed by Thôn Hải in 764.

places.name: Hàm Ôn Tuyền
places.look: A warm spring on the flat steppe, its rim crusted white with salt.
places.lore: Its water is salt and warm, and the laver gatherers soak their cracked hands in it.

places.name: Hải Diêm Trấn
places.look: Burned walls on the shore among old salt pans, the pans cracked and grown over with samphire.
places.lore: A salt town of the southern gulf, burned by Thôn Hải's pirates in 764, two years after Châu Lệ Cảng. Its salt makers never came back, and their pans lie dry.

places.name: Tử Thái Thôn
places.look: A low shore village where dark sheets of laver dry on bamboo frames along the beach.
places.lore: Its people gather laver from the rocks at low tide and sell it pressed and dried.

provinces.name: Hàm Trạch
provinces.lore: Low steppe and grass on the southern gulf, some of it below the tide. Its people make salt in shallow pans and herd a few cattle. Red ants the size of a hand build mounds on the grass behind the pans.

places.name: Xích Nghĩ Nguyên
places.look: Grassland studded with red earth mounds taller than a man, the grass around them stripped bare.
places.lore: Spirit red ants the size of a hand build here, and a column of them can strip an ox to bone. The salt makers burn the grass between their bank and the mounds each dry season.

places.name: Hàm Trạch Thôn
places.look: A village behind an earth bank below the tide line, its salt pans shining white beyond the houses.
places.lore: Its people make salt in shallow pans and sell it up the coast; the bank is raised a little every winter.

provinces.name: Thúy Bình Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with forest and bamboo on the western edge of the plain, rising like a screen behind Hoàng Vân. No one lives here; jade miners come up in summer. The plain's farmers read the weather by the cloud on its peak.

places.name: Ô Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A summer working high on the mountain where black jade is cut from grey rock.
places.lore: Its ink-black jade is carved into seals and inkstones for Phượng Minh's scribes.

places.name: Bích Tiêu Phong
places.look: A high grey peak behind the plain, its forested shoulders rising to bare rock and its top usually wrapped in a single white cloud.
places.lore: The rice farmers of Hoàng Vân read the weather by its cloud: when it lifts, they cut; when it thickens, they cover the threshing floors. Its qi runs Kim (metal) through the hard grey rock.

provinces.name: Tùng Ngạn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and forest falling to a small stretch of western coast. No village stands here; marble is quarried at the shore. Its peak looks like an ox lying down, and the herders of Hoàng Ngưu bow to it.

places.name: Vân Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A marble quarry at the shore, its white blocks veined with grey like clouds.
places.lore: Its cloud stone paves the courts of Hoàng Vân's counting hall and goes by boat along the gulf.

places.name: Ngọa Ngưu Sơn
places.look: A broad forested mountain shaped like an ox lying with its head on its forelegs.
places.lore: The herders of Hoàng Ngưu bow to it when they drive their oxen west. Its qi runs Thổ (earth).

provinces.name: Điệp Loan Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Fold after fold of high mountain and forest on the western coast, empty of villages. Woodcutters and herb gatherers work its lower slopes. Its tallest peak carries the sound of Lai Nghi's dawn bells back across the plain.

places.name: Thần Chung Phong
places.look: A tall peak above folded forest, its bare top shaped like an upturned bell.
places.lore: On still mornings the bells of Lai Nghi's nine tiers echo back from it across the plain. Its qi runs Kim (metal).

provinces.name: Nhật Xuất
provinces.lore: Grass and steppe at the far eastern end of the plain, facing the open sea. Its people fish and are the first on the plain to see the sun each morning. A fire vein in the grass is warmest at dawn.

places.name: Đông Thăng Nhãn
places.look: A round patch of bare earth in the grass, warm at dawn and cold by noon.
places.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein that is strongest at sunrise. Phượng Minh's fire disciples come to sit in it before dawn.

places.name: Nhật Xuất Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on the far eastern shore, every door facing the sea.
places.lore: Its fishers launch at first light and say they see the sun before anyone else on the plain.

provinces.name: Liệt Nhật Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains on the western gulf coast, hot and bare on their sunward side. No one lives here. Phượng Minh's fire disciples sit on its peak at noon in summer.

places.name: Kim Ô Phong
places.look: A bare peak above the western gulf whose sunward face of pale rock shines gold at noon, too hot to touch in summer.
places.lore: It is named for the golden crow that lives in the sun, and gulf sailors use its noon glare to find the coast. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire), and Phượng Minh's fire disciples sit on its sunward face at midday until they can bear it no longer.

provinces.name: Hải Mục
provinces.lore: Wide grass and steppe on the gulf coast east of Lai Nghi, some of it below the tide. Its people graze cattle on the salt grass and fish the shore. Wild iron-horned buffalo roam the grass inland.

places.name: Thiết Giác Nguyên
places.look: Wide grass where a herd of huge dark buffalo grazes, their horns grey as iron.
places.lore: Wild spirit buffalo whose horns can split a cart. Hải Mục's herders keep their cattle well away from the herd's bulls.

places.name: Hải Mục Thôn
places.look: A shore village behind a low dyke, its cattle grazing the salt grass right down to the tide.
places.lore: Its herders say salt grass makes the sweetest beef, and they fish when the cattle are in.

provinces.name: Thâm Tỉnh
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grass inland on the eastern plain, without river or coast. Its people live by deep wells and graze sheep and oxen. An earth vein runs under the steppe near the village.

places.name: Hậu Thổ Huyệt
places.look: A low earth mound in the steppe topped by a small altar of piled stones.
places.lore: A Thổ (earth) vein. The shepherds of Thâm Tỉnh pour the first water of every new well on its altar.

places.name: Thâm Tỉnh Thôn
places.look: A steppe village gathered round a single deep stone well with a long sweep pole.
places.lore: Its people live by the well and their sheep. The well is so deep that a dropped stone is counted to ten before it splashes.

provinces.name: Thú Hải Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and grass on the western gulf coast, overlooking the plain. No village stands here; the broken fort that watched for Thôn Hải's sails sits on its seaward side. Its peak looks down on the rice fields like a bowed head.

places.name: Phủ Điền Lĩnh
places.look: A high ridge of grass and rock whose crest bends forward over the rice plain like a bowed head, with the broken sea fort on its far side.
places.lore: Farmers say it bows to the first rice that Thủy Điền plants each spring, and they bow back. Its qi runs Thổ (earth), heavy and slow, and the fort's old garrison said it was the steadiest ground on the coast.

places.name: Liệu Phàm Bảo
places.look: A broken stone fort on the seaward slope, its signal tower toppled and its seaward wall gone into the gulf.
places.lore: Phượng Minh raised it in the pirate years to watch for Thôn Hải's sails. After the Purge the garrison was withdrawn in 790, and the empty fort crumbled.

provinces.name: Tận Vũ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare red ridges and badlands at the northern rim of Tiêu Vũ Lâm, where the rain clouds off the sea tear apart on the crests and drop their water before they cross. No one lives here; iron prospectors come up in the dry months and leave before the storms. Herders call it the place where the rain ends.

places.name: Thiết Vũ Khoáng
places.look: Shallow pits and spoil heaps scar a steep mountain flank, where the rain has washed loose iron ore down the rock in dark streaks.
places.lore: Seasonal miners dig red iron ore here in the dry months and carry it down to the Tower's smiths. The pits close when the storms come, and the ore each season's rain washes down is gathered first the next year.

places.name: Chu Nham Đỉnh
places.look: A blunt summit of vermilion rock rises over the northern badlands, banded red and ochre and bare of any plant.
places.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies heavy on this crest. Herders say the rain stops at its foot, and prospectors use its red crown to find the iron workings below.

provinces.name: Vũ Ảnh Nguyên
provinces.lore: High dry steppe in the rain shadow of the mountains west of the Tower, grass on the flats and grey rock on the ridges. Herders drive goats through it in spring, but it has no village and no water that lasts the summer. An old watch fort of Khải Lôi Môn still stands on a spur over the western pass, and a silver mine works the ridge below it.

places.name: Ngân Lộ Khoáng
places.look: Narrow adits enter a grey mountain wall above the steppe, the rock around their mouths beaded with grey drops of weathered silver ore.
places.lore: Silver has been dug here since 520. The miners say the seam sweats fresh silver like dew each night, so they work only before sunrise.

places.name: Vọng Vũ Phong
places.look: A tall, lone grey peak stands up out of the dry steppe, its summit wrapped in cloud while the grass below it is brown.
places.lore: Herders of the rain-shadow steppe watch this peak to know when rain will reach them, and drive their flocks toward it when its cloud darkens. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

places.name: Hưởng Lôi Bảo
places.look: On a mountain spur above the western pass, a square fort of dark stone stands broken open, a round drum platform still raised over its gate.
places.lore: Khải Lôi Môn built this watch fort over its western approach, and its drum answered the thunder of the peaks. When the Tower was raised on this ground in 380 the garrison went home to the Gate, and the Tower never manned it again.

provinces.name: Hạn Thạch Hoang
provinces.lore: Red badlands, stony steppe and patches of desert between the mountains, crossed by one thin river that runs only after storms on the peaks. Nothing is farmed here, and travellers go round it. A lone stone pillar on its ridge is the only landmark.

places.name: Thạch Nhân Phong
places.look: A tall pillar of weathered rock on a steppe ridge, shaped from the west like a man standing with his head bowed against the wind.
places.lore: Travellers crossing the dry waste steer by it and leave a mouthful of water at its foot for luck. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

provinces.name: Phong Sa Nguyên
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and sand at the foot of the western mountains, swept by a hot wind for most of the year. Herders from Hạn Tỉnh graze it in the short wet season and leave before the dust storms. The yellow summit above it is the only landmark for a day's walk.

places.name: Hoàng Sa Đỉnh
places.look: A broad summit over the steppe, its upper slopes heaped with wind-blown yellow sand that drifts like snow against the rocks.
places.lore: The hot wind of the plain carries sand all the way up and piles it on the crest. Loose cultivators of Earth (Thổ) qi climb it to sit out the sandstorms.

provinces.name: Xích Nham Hoang
provinces.lore: Red crags and badlands with patches of grass, rising to the forested ridge where the black bears of Hắc Hùng Lĩnh den. Woodcutters and honey hunters come up from the forest in autumn, when the bears go down, and never stay the night. It has no village and no road.

places.name: Hắc Hùng Lĩnh
places.look: A forested highland ridge above the rain forest, its slopes broken by boulders. At the mouth of a dark cave stands a tilted slab of grey rock scored with deep parallel claw marks, the black bears' scratching stone.

provinces.name: Thảo Lư
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and grassland sloping from the Tower's mountains toward the coast, beside the grey lake Tàn Hà Hồ. Its herders keep goats and hill horses and sell felt, milk and dung fuel to the Tower and to Hạnh Hoa Thị. They live close enough to hear the Tower's rain-chains ring in storms.

places.name: Kính Thủy Đàm
places.look: A small clear pool in the steppe grass, fed by a channel from the larger grey lake nearby, so still that it holds the Tower's cone upside down.
places.lore: Unlike Tàn Hà Hồ beside it, no lotus has ever grown in this pool. The herders of Thảo Lư water their goats here, and the Tower's disciples come to look at the reflection rather than the Tower.

places.name: Thảo Lư Thôn
places.look: A scatter of low thatched huts and stone goat pens on the steppe slope below the Tower's cone, with felt rugs drying on every roof.
places.lore: Herders settled here in 620 to sell milk and felt to the Tower. Since 906 they keep the lamp shutters closed on the side that faces the cone, though no one has ever told them to.

provinces.name: Chương Thụ
provinces.lore: Mixed country of badlands, grass and broadleaf forest below the western ridges. Its people fell camphor trees and boil the wood in copper stills, and its camphor is sold to every sect that keeps books or robes against insects. A quiet spirit vein in the grass above the village draws a few loose cultivators who rent rooms from the distillers.

places.name: Bích Thảo Mạch
places.look: A long fold of hillside stays a deep blue-green all year, with a faint shimmer over the grass on still mornings.
places.lore: A modest Wood (Mộc) vein above the camphor village. Loose cultivators (tán tu) rent rooms from the distillers to sit here and pay in labour at the stills.

places.name: Chương Thụ Thôn
places.look: A forest village of steep-roofed houses around a smoking row of copper stills, the air so sharp with camphor that insects will not cross the fence.
places.lore: The camphor distillers of Chương Thụ have worked here since 590. Sect libraries across the south keep their books in camphor chests, and the village sells to the Tower first.

provinces.name: Trúc Chỉ
provinces.lore: Broadleaf forest, grass and bamboo on low hills inland, wet nearly every night of the year. Its village makes paper from bamboo pulp, and the oiled-paper awnings of Thu Trì's Night Rain Market come from here. Wild boars raid the pulp pits, and a ruined abbey in the woods is all that is left of a school that lasted eight years.

places.name: Dã Trư Cương
places.look: A low forested ridge whose earth is turned over everywhere as if ploughed, with mud wallows in every hollow.
places.lore: A herd of spirit-touched wild boars led by a great tusker roots across this ridge and raids the pulp pits of Trúc Chỉ in the wet season. Hunters prize the tusker's bristles for brushes and have never taken him.

places.name: Phi Anh Quán
places.look: In the broadleaf forest the low walls of a small abbey stand among wild peach trees, its stone courtyard carpeted with petals each spring.
places.lore: When Lạc Anh Phái broke apart in 610, a handful of its disciples came inland and founded this abbey in its name. It lasted eight years: Lạc Hà and Thính Vũ disciples passed through in the Petal Shore fighting, and when they had gone the abbey was empty. Its peach trees still flower.

places.name: Trúc Chỉ Thôn
places.look: Stone pulp pits and drying frames hung with sheets of pale paper fill the clearing around a village of bamboo houses.
places.lore: Paper has been made here from bamboo pulp since 650, and since the Night Rain Market opened its oiled awnings have come from Trúc Chỉ. The papermakers oil each sheet twice, for the market's rain must never touch the goods.

provinces.name: Mộc Miên
provinces.lore: Grassland and broadleaf forest on rolling hills in the middle of Tiêu Vũ Lâm. Its people grow rice on the bottoms and gather kapok floss from the tall red-flowering trees for quilts and padded jackets. A spring of spirit water above the village brims in the plum-rain season and is nearly dry by autumn.

places.name: Mai Vũ Tuyền
places.look: On a grassy hilltop a ring of stones holds a shallow spring that overflows in the plum-rain season and shrinks to a damp hollow by autumn.
places.lore: A Water (Thủy) vein that waxes and wanes with the rains. Cultivators time their retreats to the early summer rains, when its qi runs strongest.

places.name: Mộc Miên Thôn
places.look: A hill village of grey-tile houses under huge kapok trees, whose red flowers fall on the roofs in spring and whose white floss blows through the lanes in summer.
places.lore: The village gathers kapok floss for quilts and padded jackets, and the Tower's servants winter in jackets stuffed here. A bride of Mộc Miên brings a quilt as her dowry, and its weight is talked about for years.

provinces.name: Vũ Tiền
provinces.lore: Open grassland and bamboo on low hills, with dry steppe at its northern edge toward the Tower. Its tea gardens are picked in the days before the spring rains, and Vũ Tiền tea is drunk in the Tower itself. On the steppe at its edge stand the ruins of the lamp-makers' town that lost its trade when the Tower went dark.

places.name: Thanh Đăng Trấn
places.look: On the steppe below the Tower's mountains lie the walls and empty lanes of a small town, its doorways still fitted with rusted iron lamp hooks.
places.lore: Thanh Đăng was the lamp-makers' town that lit the Tower's windows with blue-glazed lamps for five centuries. When the lamps went dark in 906 its trade died with them, and by 930 the last families had moved to Hạnh Hoa Thị.

places.name: Xuân Nha Nhãn
places.look: On a hillside above the tea gardens a single wild tea bush grows taller than a house, and the ground around it puts out new buds even in winter.
places.lore: A small spirit eye of Wood (Mộc) qi. Its leaves are picked once a year and sent to the Tower, and the pickers of Vũ Tiền may not drink them.

places.name: Vũ Tiền Thôn
places.look: Neat tea gardens climb the grassy hills in green steps around a village of whitewashed houses and charcoal roasting sheds.
places.lore: Since 700 the village has picked its first tea in the days before the spring rains, and Vũ Tiền tea is drunk in the Tower itself. A picker who lets rain touch the first leaves gives up her share of the season.

provinces.name: Tượng Lộ
provinces.lore: Grass and bamboo hills with patches of jungle in the heart of the forest, crossed by a timber road. Its villagers keep working elephants that haul logs to the rivers, and the elephants are worth more than the houses. A spirit vein in the bamboo above the village is a resting place for the Tower's outer disciples on the road south.

places.name: Trúc Căn Huyệt
places.look: In a bamboo grove on a hill a hollow opens among the roots, and the stems around it lean inward as if toward a fire.
places.lore: A Wood (Mộc) vein that runs through the root mat of the whole grove. The Tower's outer disciples stop here on the road south, and each leaves a cut bamboo tally with a name on it.

places.name: Tượng Lộ Thôn
places.look: A village of tall stilted houses along a broad, deeply rutted road, with elephant stalls of heavy timber larger than the houses.
places.lore: The village has kept working elephants since 730, hauling logs from the forest to the rivers. Each child is given a calf to grow up with, and the two work together all their lives.

provinces.name: Lãnh Vụ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains and cold broadleaf forest in the far north-east of Tiêu Vũ Lâm, nearly always in cloud. No one lives here; the forest is too steep to cut and the summits too cold to graze. The Tower's disciples climb its highest peak to train in the mist.

places.name: Ủng Vân Phong
places.look: A forested summit in the far north-east, its moss-hung upper slopes buried in a slow cloud that clings even on clear days.
places.lore: Water (Thủy) qi gathers in the mist on its crown. Thính Vũ's disciples climb it to train their hearing blind, learning to fight by the drip of the mist from the leaves.

provinces.name: Lạc Triều
provinces.lore: Low jungle, grass and mangrove at a river mouth on the south coast. Its villagers net fish and crabs in the tidal channels and dry them on racks above the mud. A wood of great banyans stands just inland, and the village carries its dead there.

places.name: Dung Thụ Lâm
places.look: Just inland from the river mouth a handful of enormous banyans have spread into a whole wood, their hanging roots grown into a maze of grey pillars.
places.lore: Lạc Triều carries its dead here and ties their names to the hanging roots. When a new root reaches the ground, the villagers say an ancestor has come home.

places.name: Lạc Triều Thôn
places.look: Stilt houses of bamboo and thatch stand over the mud at a river mouth, with fish-drying racks and crab traps stacked along the walkways.
places.lore: The villagers go out at every ebb to work the channels and come back before the flood. They mark the tides on a carved post, and anyone who moves it must feast the whole village.

provinces.name: Da Âm
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass along the south coast, with a few limestone knolls. Its people grow coconuts and twist coir rope for the ships at Thu Trì. An agarwood forest inland is the province's real treasure, and Hồng Đậu Trang buys its resin by weight in silver.

places.name: Hương Lệ Lâm
places.look: Inland from the coast, old agarwood trees stand in the grass, many scarred with cuts that weep dark, fragrant resin.
places.lore: Agarwood forms only in wounded trees, and the cutters of Da Âm wound them carefully and wait decades. Hồng Đậu Trang buys the resin by weight in silver, and the village does not ask what it is burned for.

places.name: Da Âm Thôn
places.look: A shore village of palm-thatched houses under tall coconut palms, with long coils of brown coir rope drying on frames along the beach.
places.lore: The village has twisted coir rope since 680 and sells it to the ships at Thu Trì. Its children climb palms before they can swim, and its boats are sewn together with its own rope.

provinces.name: Lăng Đường
provinces.lore: Dense coastal jungle edged with mangrove in the south-west of Tiêu Vũ Lâm. Its village farms water chestnuts and fish in the brackish ponds behind the shore. Great poison toads breed in the jungle pools, and Hồng Đậu Trang pays the villagers for their skins.

places.name: Độc Thiềm Lâm
places.look: A wet jungle hollow full of black pools, loud at night with a deep croaking, the leaves around the water spotted with yellow slime.
places.lore: Toads the size of dogs breed in these pools, and the largest, a spirit beast the villagers call the Old Mother, has not been seen in years but still sings. Their venom is a staple of Hồng Đậu Trang's poisons.

places.name: Lăng Đường Thôn
places.look: A coastal village of low houses on banks between brackish ponds, the water dark green with floating water-chestnut leaves.
places.lore: Villagers harvest water chestnuts from tubs pushed across the ponds and fish the channels to the sea. They also bring in poison-toad skins from the jungle for Hồng Đậu Trang, wearing gloves of oiled leather.

provinces.name: Liệt Địa Hoang
provinces.lore: Cracked red badlands and steppe below the northern mountains, without a tree or a running stream. A hot pool stained red with iron and a malachite mine are the only reasons to come. The miners walk in from Hạn Tỉnh and carry their own water.

places.name: Thiết Tú Trì
places.look: In the cracked badlands a steaming pool of rust-red water lies in a basin of iron-stained rock, crusted orange at its edges.
places.lore: The water tastes of iron and is said to harden the bones of those who bathe in it. Miners from the malachite workings soak here after each shift.

places.name: Lục Vũ Khoáng
places.look: Open trenches in the red badlands expose seams of banded green malachite, bright as peacock feathers against the rock.
places.lore: The mine yields copper and malachite, which is ground into the green paint of the south's temple roofs. Its miners walk in from Hạn Tỉnh and carry their water.

provinces.name: Lôi Kích Nhai
provinces.lore: A short range of bare mountains and badland cliffs north of the Tower, where the storms off the sea break first and lightning strikes the same crests night after night. The rock is scarred black along the ridgelines. No one lives here, and herders keep their flocks off the high ground in the storm months.

places.name: Lôi Cốt Phong
places.look: A narrow, jagged peak of dark rock above the badland cliffs, its crest scored with black lightning tracks like veins.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs in the dark rock, and the lightning finds it every storm. The Tower's sword disciples leave their blades on the crest overnight in thunderstorms.

provinces.name: Đồng Nham Câu
provinces.lore: Ravines cut through green-stained and red rock in the mountains north-east of the Tower, with a little grass in the bottoms. Prospectors have dug test pits all over it and found the copper too thin to mine. One grey peak stands over the ravines and throws the thunder back.

places.name: Hồi Lôi Phong
places.look: A grey peak over a ring of ravines, its walls curved so that each thunderclap rolls back from it two and three times.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi lies in its grey rock. The Tower's disciples test their hearing here by counting the echoes, and say a master can hear five.

provinces.name: Mã Lan
provinces.lore: High, dry steppe under the northern mountains, nearly treeless. Its people breed the small, hardy hill horses that carry the Tower's messengers, and winter the herds in stone pens. Grey wolves den in the rocks above and take a foal or two each spring.

places.name: Hôi Lang Cương
places.look: A rocky spur above the steppe, its boulders worn smooth where wolves have lain, with bones scattered in the grass below.
places.lore: A pack of grey wolves under a spirit-touched leader dens here and takes foals from Mã Lan each spring. The herders leave the leader alone and hunt only the young wolves.

places.name: Mã Lan Thôn
places.look: A high steppe village of stone houses and long dry-stone horse pens, with herds of small shaggy horses grazing the slope below.
places.lore: Mã Lan has bred hill horses since 560, and the Tower's messengers ride them on the mountain roads. Each spring the best foal is led up to the Tower.

provinces.name: Khô Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare mountains and badlands just north of the Tower, where clouds that have already rained on the cone drift over thin and white. It is dry, windy and empty. A twin-horned peak marks its centre.

places.name: Vũ Giác Phong
places.look: Two bare horns of rock rise side by side from one mountain shoulder north of the Tower, the gap between them just wide enough to walk through.
places.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi gathers between the horns. Herders say whoever walks through the gap in a storm comes out a year older.

provinces.name: Lạc Lôi Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and red badlands east of the Tower's cone, with grass in the hollows. Lightning falls here nearly as often as on the thunder peaks to the east, and a copper mine works the red rock. The Tower's smiths come down to the mine in storms to quench their castings in the rain.

places.name: Vũ Đồng Khoáng
places.look: Terraced cuts in a red badland slope expose dull red copper ore, with a small smelting floor of blackened stone below.
places.lore: The Tower's smiths take copper from here for their bronze rain-chains and bells. They quench the castings in storm rain, and say bronze quenched dry will not sing.

places.name: Thụ Lôi Đỉnh
places.look: A rounded summit east of the Tower's cone, its crown fused into black, glassy rock by countless strikes.
places.lore: The Metal (Kim) qi in its rock draws lightning more often than any other summit in Tiêu Vũ Lâm. The Tower's disciples sit just below the crown in storms to feel the strikes through the stone.

provinces.name: Hạn Tỉnh
provinces.lore: Dry steppe and high mountains in the north-west of Tiêu Vũ Lâm, in the rain shadow behind the ridges. Its village lives around one very deep well, keeps goats and a little millet, and sends its young men to the mines in the hills. Jade from the black jade mine above it is carved in Thu Trì.

places.name: Dạ Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A cramped tunnel mouth in a grey mountain wall, its spoil heap glittering with chips of black, glossy stone.
places.lore: Black jade (mặc ngọc) has been cut here since 820 and carved in Thu Trì into seals and sword fittings. Since the lamps went dark the Tower's masters favour it, because it holds no gleam of lamp or moon.

places.name: Thụy Ngưu Sơn
places.look: A long, humped mountain over the steppe, shaped like a resting ox, with grass on its back and bare rock on its flanks.
places.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies deep in it. The herders of Hạn Tỉnh say that if the ox ever stands up, the well will run dry.

places.name: Hạn Tỉnh Thôn
places.look: A steppe village of flat-roofed stone houses around a single wide well, its rope so long that a mule turns the windlass.
places.lore: The well was dug in 610, and it takes a mule half the morning to raise a day's water. The village keeps goats and millet and sends its young men to the mines in the ridges.

provinces.name: Tàng Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains at the north-western end of Kinh Trập Sơn, with a little steppe and badland on the lower spurs. Clouds pile into its high valleys and sit there for days. No one lives here; miners dig lodestone on one slope in the dry season.

places.name: Hấp Thiết Khoáng
places.look: A cut in a grey mountain flank where rusted iron tools still cling to the rock face, and the old spoil heaps bristle with filings.
places.lore: Lightning has made the ore here into lodestone, fit for compasses and array-makers' needles. Few know the cut; the miners who found it left their iron tools stuck to the rock and never came back with bronze.

places.name: Ngưng Lôi Phong
places.look: A heavy grey summit at the head of the cloud valleys, often hidden under a lid of dark cloud that flickers from inside.
places.lore: Storms gather over it for hours before they break. Its rock holds Metal (Kim) qi, and herders on the steppe take its flicker as the warning to drive their flocks down.

provinces.name: Tiêu Thổ Hoang
provinces.lore: Badlands and bare mountain on the northern side of the thunder range, the rock blackened and fused in patches by lightning. Nothing grows on the scorched ground, and herders call it the Tower's anvil. Diggers come for the red-veined stone of its one mine.

places.name: Hồng Văn Khoáng
places.look: Shallow galleries in a mountain foot expose pale stone shot through with bright red veins, like blood in milk.
places.lore: Chicken-blood stone (kê huyết thạch) is cut here for seals, and a seal of it is a gift fit for an elder. The red is cinnabar, and the cutters wear masks against the dust.

places.name: Hắc Diệu Phong
places.look: A blunt peak over the scorched badlands, its crown fused by lightning into black glass that gleams after rain.
places.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its fused crown. Herders say a storm that does not strike it is not a real storm.

provinces.name: Lôi Minh Cương
provinces.lore: Mountains and high grassland on the northern ridge of the range, where thunder rolls along the crest for hours after each storm. A silver mine works the lower slope. Herders graze the high grass in the dry season and never sleep on the ridge.

places.name: Lôi Ngân Khoáng
places.look: Adits in a mountain slope above the high grass, their spoil sparkling with flakes of bright silver ore.
places.lore: The silver here is found in seams that lightning has opened, so the miners follow the storms. Silver from it is used in the Tower's warding talismans.

places.name: Lôi Chủy Phong
places.look: A hooked spur of bare rock juts from the northern ridge like the beak of a stooping eagle.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi gathers at its tip, and the lightning strikes the beak first. Eagles nest under its hook and are said to fly out into the storms.

provinces.name: Hôi Thành Nguyên
provinces.lore: Steppe, desert and bare mountain beside the Tower's cone and above Hạnh Hoa Thị, dry in the rain shadow. Ash-grey soil fills its hollows, and in the hills lie the buried walls of a city Khải Lôi Môn lost before the Tower was built. A spirit eye of Earth qi on the steppe is kept by the Tower's outer disciples.

places.name: Hạ Lôi Thành
places.look: In the mountain hollows beside the cone, the tops of thick walls and gate towers stick up out of grey ash hardened to stone.
places.lore: Khải Lôi Môn built this upland city on the cone's flank as its western market. In 352 the cone woke and buried it in ash, and the Gate never rebuilt; the cone fell quiet again, and in 380 Phó Tiêu Tương raised her tower on it.

places.name: Hậu Thổ Nhãn
places.look: On the dry steppe beside the Tower's cone, a round hollow of ash-grey soil lies warm to the touch, with tough grass growing in rings around it.
places.lore: A spirit eye of Earth (Thổ) qi rising through the old ash of the cone. The Tower's outer disciples keep it, and sit here in the dry months when the rain on the cone is too loud for them.

provinces.name: Vũ Thủy Câu
provinces.lore: Steep mountain and steppe cut by ravines that run full after every storm and dry within a day. A river threads the largest of them toward the coast. Goatherds use the ravines in spring, and its one peak is named for the clear days after rain.

places.name: Thanh Minh Phong
places.look: A clean grey summit over the ravines, its rock washed pale and sharp by the storms.
places.lore: In the clear days after a storm it stands out so sharp that the farmers on the coast can count its ledges. Its rock holds Metal (Kim) qi.

provinces.name: Thạch Lũng Nguyên
provinces.lore: Mountain and steppe in equal parts, the steppe ribbed with long ridges of stone like a ploughed field. A river crosses it toward the sea at Lãng Hoa. Herders from the coast graze it, and its peak tells the farmers below when spring has begun.

places.name: Lập Xuân Phong
places.look: A broad peak above the stone-furrowed steppe, where the first green of the year shows on its southern face.
places.lore: Farmers below begin the year's work when its southern face turns green. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

provinces.name: Thiên Nhận Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A block of sheer mountain rising from near sea level to a high crest. There is no level ground on it to build on, and no one lives here. A soapstone mine at its foot sends its stone down to Lãng Hoa.

places.name: Thanh Hoạt Khoáng
places.look: A low quarry face at the mountain's foot, its pale green stone so soft that the walls shine where hands have rubbed them.
places.lore: Soapstone from here is carved into seals and pill boxes and ground for alchemists' powders. It is carried down to Lãng Hoa on mules.

places.name: Vũ Bút Phong
places.look: Three sheer points of rock stand in a row on the high crest, like the points of a scholar's brush rest.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs in the cliffs. Scholars in Lãng Hoa say a student who can see all three points from the city on the morning of an examination will pass.

provinces.name: Ám Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High, bare mountains in the middle of the range, where storm clouds gather dark on the crest before they break over the south. No one lives here. Miners dig a black ore on its slopes and leave when the clouds sink low.

places.name: Ám Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Narrow cuts in a high slope expose seams of dull black ore, and the spoil stains the scree black down to the valley.
places.lore: The dark iron ore here is smelted for blades that do not shine. The Tower's masters have favoured it since 906.

places.name: Thùy Liêm Phong
places.look: A tall summit in the middle of the range from which dark clouds seem to hang like curtains on its southern side.
places.lore: Water (Thủy) qi gathers in the clouds that hang on it. The Tower's disciples read the coming weather of the whole south from its curtains.

provinces.name: Khởi Trập Nguyên
provinces.lore: A high mountain upland with grass in its basins, where the tiger-kind beasts of Phục Hổ Cương roam and the first spring thunder is said to wake every creature in the hills. A banded iron mine works the slope near the ridge. The Tower's fort on the highland road has lain in ruins since the beasts took it.

places.name: Phục Hổ Cương
places.look: A long, low ridge on the Kinh Trập highland, shaped like a great cat crouched with its head on its paws. Its exposed rock is banded in yellow and dark grey stripes, and the grass on it is flattened into long paths.

places.name: Ban Văn Khoáng
places.look: A cut in the highland slope exposes ore banded yellow and dark grey, like the stripes of the crouching ridge nearby.
places.lore: The banded iron ore is good, but the beasts of Phục Hổ Cương make it dangerous, and miners come only in large parties. They leave a goat at the ridge's foot before each season's work.

places.name: Thanh Thạch Bảo
places.look: A small fort of blue-grey stone on the highland road, its gate torn off and its walls scored with deep claw marks.
places.lore: The Tower kept this fort on the highland road for five centuries. In 1041 its garrison was called east to the Thunder Vein War, and the tiger-kind beasts of Phục Hổ Cương came down and took it; it was never manned again.

provinces.name: Phích Lịch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and badlands around Kinh Điện Khoáng, where lightning strikes the ore so often that the smiths forge in the storms. Its only people are miners and smiths, who come for the storm season. A peak above the mine draws the lightning down toward the forges.

places.name: Kinh Điện Khoáng
places.look: A mine on a bare ridge of Kinh Trập Sơn, where open-air forges stand on the rock beside the pit mouths, each with a tall iron rod raised above it to catch the lightning. The rock around them is streaked with burn marks.

places.name: Dẫn Lôi Phong
places.look: A sharp, bare peak above the forges of Kinh Điện, its crest bristling with old iron rods driven into the rock.
places.lore: Khải Lôi's smiths drove rods into its crest to lead the lightning down to the forges, and Thính Vũ's smiths keep them. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on it with every storm.

provinces.name: Miên Trùng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High, nearly bare mountains in the eastern range, where the cave of Tàng Trập Động opens and the sleeping creatures wake at the first spring thunder. Hunters gather at the cave mouth each year on the day of Kinh Trập. Above the cave stand the broken walls of Khải Lôi's old cave watch.

places.name: Vân Hải Đỉnh
places.gloss: Summit Above the Sea of Clouds
places.look: A high summit in the eastern range that stands above the clouds on most mornings, an island of grey rock in a white sea.
places.lore: Water (Thủy) qi gathers in the cloud sea around it. The hunters of Tàng Trập Động climb it on the eve of Kinh Trập to watch for the first thunder.

places.name: Thủ Động Trại
places.look: On a ledge near the cave of Tàng Trập Động, the low dry-stone walls of a stockade enclose a hearth and a row of collapsed huts.
places.lore: Khải Lôi Môn kept wardens here to watch the cave mouth and keep order among the hunters on the day of Kinh Trập. When the Gate fell, its wardens went home, and the hunters have kept their own order since.

provinces.name: Phấn Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Grey mountains and badlands at the north-western edge of the range, close to the Tower. Its rock is pale and crumbling, and a blue vitriol mine works the foot of the slope. Herders cross it to reach the steppe and do not linger.

places.name: Đảm Phàn Khoáng
places.look: Wet galleries at the foot of the grey slope drip blue water, and crusts of bright blue crystal coat their walls.
places.lore: Blue vitriol is scraped from the galleries for dyers, alchemists and the poison-makers of Hồng Đậu Trang. The miners' hands are stained blue for life.

places.name: Hạc Đầu Phong
places.look: A peak of pale, crumbling rock whose top is white as an old man's head against the grey ridges around it.
places.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its pale rock. Herders say it turned white the night Khải Lôi's last head fell, though older songs already call it white.

provinces.name: Hải Vụ Nhai
provinces.lore: Mountains that drop straight into the sea, wrapped in sea mist most mornings. There is no harbour and no village; fishers below steer by its peak when the mist lifts. A rock crystal mine is cut into the lower cliff.

places.name: Thủy Tinh Khoáng
places.look: Low, abandoned galleries cut into the cliff above the surf, their walls studded with clear six-sided crystals beaded with sea damp.
places.lore: Rock crystal from here would make array focuses and scholars' lenses, but the rope path to the galleries broke in a gale and no digger has gone down since.

places.name: Vọng Triều Phong
places.look: A steep peak rising straight from the sea cliffs, its upper rocks streaked white by the nesting seabirds.
places.lore: Fishers along the coast watch its foot to read the tides when the mist lifts. Water (Thủy) qi rises to it off the sea.

provinces.name: Kinh Đào Nhai
provinces.lore: Sheer coastal mountain where storm waves boom in the sea caves under the cliffs. No one lives here. Its cape peak is the last land the Lãng Hoa fishers see when they sail east.

places.name: Hải Giác Phong
places.look: A sheer headland peak over booming sea caves, the waves breaking white on its foot even in calm weather.
places.lore: It is the last land the Lãng Hoa fishers see when they sail east, and they bow to it on leaving. Water (Thủy) qi gathers in its spray.

provinces.name: Hoa Vũ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains around the rain-flower pebble beds of Vũ Hoa Khoáng. Its only people are the Tower's pickers and guards, who sort the pebbles in the rain. The peak above the mine is named for the sermon under which the flowers are said to have fallen.

places.name: Vũ Hoa Khoáng
places.look: The highest mine in the thunder mountains, a stony upland where the stream beds have been dammed into long wooden sluices. In them lie heaps of smooth pebbles of every colour, red, agate-banded, green and white, gleaming wet in the rain.

places.name: Giảng Đạo Phong
places.look: A flat-topped peak above the pebble sluices, its summit a broad bare platform like a preaching terrace.
places.lore: The pickers of Vũ Hoa say the master whose sermon made the flowers fall as rain preached from this summit. Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its rock, and pebbles washed down from it are said to be the brightest.

places.name: Hộ Khoáng Bảo
places.look: Low on the slope below the pebble beds, the walls of a guard fort lie half buried under a great tongue of fallen rock and mud.
places.lore: The Tower built the fort in 505 to guard the road to Vũ Hoa Khoáng. A storm in 1102 brought the slope down on its lower court, and the guard moved up to the mine itself.

provinces.name: Tử Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Steep mountains above the purple-gold seams of Tử Kim Khoáng, where storm clouds glow violet at dusk. Miners work the cliffs and leave when the seams glow. A high peak above the mine gathers the lightning.

places.name: Tử Kim Khoáng
places.look: A mine on a steep mountain slope, its tunnel mouths set in cliffs streaked purple and gold. Below them long fans of purple-tinted spoil spill down the hillside.

places.name: Phi Lôi Phong
places.look: A high, sharp summit over the purple-gold cliffs, where the lightning seems to leap from it to the clouds rather than fall.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs through it from the purple-gold seams below. Miners of Tử Kim watch its crest and leave the tunnels when the leaping lightning starts.

provinces.name: Cửu Tiêu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest ground of Kinh Trập Sơn, around the split summit of Liệt Khuyết Phong. Nothing lives on its upper slopes, and storm clouds sit on it most days. The Tower's disciples drill here in thunderstorms, past the ruin of Khải Lôi's storm camp and a fulgurite mine.

places.name: Liệt Khuyết Phong
places.look: The highest summit of Kinh Trập Sơn, a sheer grey peak split from crown to shoulder by a deep vertical rift, as if cut by one stroke. The rock along the rift is fused black and glassy, and storm clouds gather on it more often than on any other summit.

places.name: Lôi Tinh Khoáng
places.look: On a high slope below the split summit, diggers break open the sand and scree to pull out glassy, branching tubes fused by lightning.
places.lore: Thunder crystal (lôi tinh), sand fused by lightning, is gathered here for thunder talismans and arrays. The diggers come only between storms and leave their iron at the bottom of the trail.

places.name: Nghênh Lôi Trại
places.gloss: Stockade Where the Lightning Is Welcomed
places.look: High on the shoulder of Liệt Khuyết Phong, a ring of fire-blackened stone walls encloses the hearths of a camp, open to the sky.
places.lore: Khải Lôi's disciples camped here to wait for the storms before climbing the summit to invite the lightning. When the Gate fell in 480 the camp was left to the weather, and the Tower's disciples now pass it on their way to drill.

provinces.name: Thiểm Điện Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains around the Thunder vein Kinh Lôi Mạch, close to Thiên Xu's border. Lệ Tiêu Hồn keeps the vein, and no one comes here without the Tower's leave. An amethyst mine on the ridge is worked under guard.

places.name: Kinh Lôi Mạch
places.look: High on a bare black ridge of Kinh Trập Sơn, seams of violet light run through the rock like veins under skin, brightening whenever thunder rolls. Nothing grows on the ridge, and the air above it smells of a struck flint.

places.name: Tử Tinh Khoáng
places.look: A guarded cut in a bare high ridge, its walls lined with violet crystal that brightens faintly when thunder rolls.
places.lore: The amethyst grows along the edges of the Thunder vein and takes some of its colour. Lệ Tiêu Hồn allows the mine to be worked only under the Tower's guard, and every stone is counted.

provinces.name: Đấu Lạp
provinces.lore: Grassland and bamboo between the mountains and the coast, below the Tower. Its people grow rice and weave conical rain hats of bamboo and palm leaf, sold in every market of the south. A spirit vein in the meadows is kept for the Tower's outer disciples.

places.name: Tân Lục Mạch
places.look: A strip of meadow above the hat village where the grass is always the bright green of a new spring.
places.lore: A Wood (Mộc) vein kept for the Tower's outer disciples. Villagers cut palm leaf on its edge and say hats woven from it never fade.

places.name: Đấu Lạp Thôn
places.look: A bamboo village where every porch is stacked with conical hats of split bamboo and palm leaf, drying in rows like mushrooms.
places.lore: The village has woven rain hats since 640, and a Đấu Lạp hat is said to keep its wearer dry for twenty rainy seasons. The Tower's servants wear them, and their brims are left plain and undyed.

provinces.name: Hàm Phong Nguyên
provinces.lore: Mountain, steppe and grass sloping to the coast, swept by a salt wind that stunts every tree. Herders and salt-gatherers pass through, but no one stays. An old fort from the pirate years watches the shore from a spur.

places.name: Lạc Nhật Phong
places.look: A peak of red badland rock above the salt-wind plain that burns crimson at sunset.
places.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its red rock. Salt-gatherers on the coast stop work when its crown goes dark.

places.name: Vọng Phàm Bảo
places.look: On a mountain spur above the coast, the square walls of a fort look out to sea, with a fallen signal tower at one corner.
places.lore: The Tower built the fort in the pirate years to watch for Thôn Hải's sails. After the Pirate Purge there was nothing left to watch for, and its garrison was sent home in 810.

provinces.name: Bạo Vũ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Very high mountains in the eastern range, where storms empty in sudden cloudbursts that send torrents down every gully. No one lives here. The earthquake of 1199 split the stockade on its pass, and it has stood empty since.

places.name: Lôi Trụ Phong
places.look: A very tall, slender summit of pale grey-green rock rising like a pillar above the gullies of the eastern range.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs up it like water up a reed. Cloudbursts break on it first, and the torrents from its flanks are heard for miles.

places.name: Sơn Khẩu Trại
places.look: A stockade of stone and timber at the mouth of a high pass, split in two by a fresh crack in the ground that runs straight through its gate.
places.lore: The Tower kept a small guard here on the eastern pass for six centuries. The earthquake of 1199 that raised the isle at Hà Châu split the stockade from end to end, and the guard has not been sent back.

provinces.name: Liên Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains whose crests run so close together that the clouds over them join into one roof. Nothing settled lives here. Its tall peak can be seen from Xuyên Lâm Môn's gate.

places.name: Tình Tiêu Phong
places.look: A high summit that rises above the joined clouds of its ridge into clear blue sky on most afternoons.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its clear crown. Xuyên Lâm's guides take it as their mark, for it can be seen from the gate above every cloud.

provinces.name: Vân Thảo Nguyên
provinces.lore: High grassland and mountain on the northern edge of the range, its meadows often under low cloud. Deer graze the high grass, and herders bring cattle up in summer. There is no village, only summer huts of stone.

places.name: Lão Lộc Phong
places.look: A grassy summit above the cloud meadows, where deer graze up to the very top.
places.lore: Herders say an old white stag has grazed this summit for longer than anyone remembers. Wood (Mộc) qi lies in its high grass.

provinces.name: Chấn Thiên Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains beside Kinh Lôi Mạch, where the thunder is loud enough to shake stones loose. Gold sand washes out of its streams after storms. The ruin of the fort that guarded the vein in the Thunder Vein War stands on its lower ridge, and on the drum-shaped summit of Thần Cổ Phong above it stands Thính Vũ Lâu, which carried its halls here from the cone in 1166-1170.

places.name: Sa Kim Khoáng
places.look: Stream beds below the drum peak are dammed with rock into little pools, and pans of black sand glitter with gold flakes.
places.lore: The storms cut into the gold-bearing rock above, and the streams wash the gold down. Panners work only after storms and pay a tithe to the guards of the vein.

places.name: Thính Vũ Lâu
places.look: Black halls stand on a bare grey peak with a drum-shaped crown, a bronze rain-chain hanging from every eave and running down into the rock, and lightning running down the chains in a storm. The hollow rock of the peak still booms like a drum when thunder strikes.
places.lore: Thính Vũ Lâu, a great sect (đại tông môn) of the ma đạo (demonic path), ruled by Mạnh Dạ Vũ, who holds the Tương Phi Tán, has held this summit since 1166-1170, when it carried its halls east from the cone; its old seat is now the Rain Tower. The Tower had built its guard here in 1046 above the ashes of Thủ Lôi Bảo, and the canon's second half wants the Thunder qi that the cone lacks. In 1170 Thạch Liên Hoàn and Lệ Tiêu Hồn laid the Iron Rain array, a bronze chain from the peak down to Kinh Lôi Mạch, and the soul vaults moved into the vein. The guards of Kinh Lôi Mạch say the peak warns them of storms a day before they come.

places.name: Thủ Lôi Bảo
places.look: On a lower ridge near the vein stands the burned shell of a fort, its gate tower collapsed and its stones cracked by fire.
places.lore: The Tower built this fort to guard Kinh Lôi Mạch soon after it took the thunder mountains. In 1042, during the Thunder Vein War, Phượng Minh's disciples took it and burned it, and when the vein was kept the Tower built its new guard higher on the ridge.

provinces.name: Lâm Vụ Câu
provinces.lore: Mountain ravines filled with broadleaf forest and mist, cut by a river running south. Charcoal burners and agate diggers work its lower slopes. Its forested peak is green to the top.

places.name: Vũ Hoàn Khoáng
places.look: Pits in the riverbank at the mountain's foot turn up nodules of grey stone that split open into banded red and white agate.
places.lore: Agate from here is polished in Không Mông for beads and the counters of games. Diggers say the bands are the rings of old storms.

places.name: Bích Loa Phong
places.look: A small round peak above the misty ravines, forested green to its top like a coiled snail shell.
places.lore: Wood (Mộc) qi gathers in its forest. Charcoal burners never cut on it, saying it is the forest's own pillow.

provinces.name: Ô Diêu
provinces.lore: Forest, mountain and grass in the hills east of Không Mông, with charcoal kilns smoking in every clearing. The charcoal feeds the smelters of the iron mine above the village. A peak shaped like a cockscomb stands over the kilns.

places.name: Huyết Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Open cuts in a mountain slope expose blood-red iron ore, and a smelter below sends up a column of grey smoke.
places.lore: The red ore is smelted with charcoal from Ô Diêu and sent down to the Tower's smiths. The miners' clothes are red with dust, and they are called the red men in Không Mông.

places.name: Hỏa Quan Phong
places.look: A ragged crest of red-brown rock rises over the kilns in a row of points like a rooster's comb.
places.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its red rock. The kiln village says a fire lit when its comb glows at dawn will burn clean.

places.name: Ô Diêu Thôn
places.look: A hill village of soot-darkened houses around a row of domed earth kilns, smoke drifting through the trees in every direction.
places.lore: The village has burned charcoal since 680 for the smelters of the iron mine above. Its children are said to be born grey, and they wash in the stream only at New Year.

provinces.name: Thanh Chướng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forested mountains standing in rows like green screens above the bamboo country. No one lives here, but woodcutters climb its lower slopes for hardwood. Rain comes to it every evening.

places.name: Mộ Vũ Phong
places.look: A forested peak among the green screens, gathering a cloud each afternoon that breaks into rain at dusk.
places.lore: Wood (Mộc) qi gathers in its forest. Woodcutters work its slopes only until the cloud forms, and are home by the first drops.

provinces.name: Xuân Duẩn
provinces.lore: Bamboo forest and grass in the low eastern hills. Its villagers dig bamboo shoots in spring and dry them for the cities, and cut nanmu timber in the forest above. Xuyên Lâm's guides pass through on the forest road.

places.name: Nam Mộc Lâm
places.look: On the grassy hills above the village stand tall, straight nanmu trees with golden-grained trunks, widely spaced like the pillars of a hall.
places.lore: Nanmu timber does not rot in the rain, and the Tower's halls are framed with it. Each tree cut must be marked with the Tower's seal first.

places.name: Xuân Duẩn Thôn
places.look: A bamboo village where racks of split bamboo shoots dry over smoky fires under every eave.
places.lore: Each spring the whole village digs bamboo shoots before they break the soil and dries them for the cities. A shoot left to grow by mistake is tied with a red cord and never cut.

provinces.name: Dẫn Lộ
provinces.lore: Bamboo forest below the high shoulder where Xuyên Lâm Môn keeps its gate. The households of the school's guides live here, and children learn the forest roads before they can read. The giant centipedes in the bamboo above are the first danger every guide is taught.

places.name: Xích Túc Cốc
places.look: A damp bamboo valley where the leaf litter rustles constantly, and red-legged centipedes as long as a man's arm move under it.
places.lore: Spirit-touched centipedes breed in the rotting bamboo, and their master is said to be longer than a boat. Xuyên Lâm's apprentices learn here to strike with the staff before they see what moves.

places.name: Dẫn Lộ Thôn
places.look: A village of bamboo houses at the foot of Xuyên Lâm's long stair, with worn guide staffs leaning by every door.
places.lore: The households of Xuyên Lâm's guides have lived here since the school was founded. When a guide does not come home, the family hangs the returned staff over the door and leaves it there.

provinces.name: Phạt Trúc
provinces.lore: Almost pure bamboo forest on low hills around Đả Diệp Lâm. Its villagers cut and sell bamboo poles but leave alone the clearing of stumps where Xuyên Lâm's disciples train. The rain on the leaves is so loud that in a downpour the villagers talk in hand signs.

places.name: Đả Diệp Lâm
places.look: A grove of tall green bamboo on low hills, so dense that rain on the leaves roars like surf. In its heart is a clearing filled with cut bamboo stumps of different heights, standing in rows like a field of posts.

places.name: Phạt Trúc Thôn
places.look: A bamboo village on a low hill, its yards stacked high with cut poles and its paths ringing with the sound of blades.
places.lore: Bamboo cutters have lived here since 700 and sell poles in every town of the coast. They leave the clearing of stumps in Đả Diệp Lâm alone, and in a downpour they talk in hand signs.

provinces.name: Cố Trạch
provinces.lore: Low coastal grass, bamboo and jungle at the river mouth where the ruins of Lôi Trạch Thành stand in the marsh. Eel fishers and reed cutters live here; most of the old city's families moved up the valley to Không Mông long ago. The bamboo inland grows over the graves that Thu Phần Các keeps.

places.name: Lôi Trạch Thành
places.look: On a marshy river mouth by the sea, among old forest, stand the broken walls of a city whose stones are fused black and glassy, as if fired in a kiln. Over the old gate rises the shattered stump of a great drum tower, split down its middle. Reeds grow through the streets.

places.name: Hải Trúc Lâm
places.look: A grove of tough, salt-stunted bamboo on the shore, its stems silvered by the sea wind.
places.lore: The salt-hard bamboo makes the best fish traps on the coast. Cố Trạch cuts it in winter and soaks it in the marsh for a year.

places.name: Cố Trạch Thôn
places.look: A huddle of reed-thatched houses on stilts at the edge of the marsh, with the black walls of Lôi Trạch Thành visible across the water.
places.lore: Eel fishers settled here in 760, three centuries after the city burned. They do not enter the ruin after dark, and on the thunder-day they beat drums with the people of Không Mông.

provinces.name: Tảo Điền
provinces.lore: Coastal grass and jungle on a sheltered shore. Its villagers farm laver on bamboo frames in the shallows and dry it in purple sheets. A spirit spring in the meadows rises and falls with the tide.

places.name: Triều Tịch Tuyền
places.look: In the meadow behind the shore a stone-rimmed spring rises and sinks twice a day, in time with the sea out of sight.
places.lore: A Water (Thủy) vein that breathes with the tides. Cultivators sit here at high water, when its qi is strongest, and leave at the ebb.

places.name: Tảo Điền Thôn
places.look: A shore village where rows of bamboo frames stand in the shallows, hung with dark seaweed, and purple sheets dry on mats along the beach.
places.lore: The village has farmed laver since 820, and its dried sheets are sold in Không Mông and Lãng Hoa. Children here are taught to read the tides before their letters.

provinces.name: Tiêu Viên
provinces.lore: Jungle, grass and bamboo in the low inland hills. Its people grow bananas and plantains and weave mats from the fibre. A lychee grove on the hill above is the pride of the province.

places.name: Lệ Chi Lâm
places.look: On the grassy hill above the village, a grove of old lychee trees hangs heavy with red fruit in early summer.
places.lore: The first lychees of the grove are carried to the Tower each year by relay runners so that they arrive fresh. The village eats the rest and gets fat for a month.

places.name: Tiêu Viên Thôn
places.look: A jungle village under the tattered leaves of banana gardens, its houses roofed with banana leaf and its paths lined with fibre drying on lines.
places.lore: The village grows bananas and plantains and weaves mats from the fibre. Its people say the rain on banana leaves is the first sound a child of Tiêu Viên hears.

provinces.name: Thiên Mục Nguyên
provinces.lore: High grassland among mountains on the northern rim of the range. Herders bring cattle up in summer and leave before the storm season. A white jade mine works the ridge, and the peak above it glows in storms.

places.name: Vũ Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A narrow quarry high on the ridge, its floor littered with chips of milky white stone that shine in the rain.
places.lore: White jade from here is carved into seals and hairpins in Không Mông. The quarry is worked only in summer, when the herders are on the pasture to carry the stone down.

places.name: Thiên Đăng Phong
places.look: A tall summit above the sky pastures, on which a pale blue light flickers along the crest in storms.
places.lore: Herders call the storm light the sky's lantern, and say it is the only lamp lit in the Tower's mountains. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its crest.

provinces.name: Đạo Hoa
provinces.lore: Low jungle and paddy grass inland from the coast, flat and wet. Its villagers grow two rice harvests a year and fish the paddies. A forest of hanging vines fills the wet ground above the village.

places.name: Đằng La Lâm
places.look: A wet jungle where vines hang from every branch in curtains so thick that the forest is dim at noon.
places.lore: Villagers cut rattan and vine here for baskets and rope. Children are warned not to play in the curtains, for some vines close on whatever touches them.

places.name: Đạo Hoa Thôn
places.look: A low village of thatched houses among flat green paddies, with fish traps set in every channel between the fields.
places.lore: The village takes two rice harvests a year and raises fish in the flooded fields. When the rice flowers, no one in Đạo Hoa may sing, lest the blossom fall.

provinces.name: Ôn Sa
provinces.lore: Jungle, grass and a small volcanic mountain on the coast. Its beaches are warm underfoot from the fire below, and the villagers fish and gather sulphur. On the volcano's flank lies the sulphur town the mountain buried in 1013.

places.name: Hoàng Diễm Trấn
places.look: On the volcano's flank, roof lines and a market gate stick up out of a field of grey ash and yellow sulphur crusts.
places.lore: Hoàng Diễm was a town of sulphur gatherers, named for the yellow flames of its vents. In 1013 the small volcano woke and buried it in ash; most of its people escaped to the shore and founded Ôn Sa.

places.name: Địa Hỏa Huyệt
places.look: In a rocky fold at the volcano's foot a hollow glows a dull red from cracks in its floor, and the rain turns to steam before it reaches the ground.
places.lore: A Fire (Hỏa) vein rising from the small volcano, rare in the Tower's wet lands. Few of the Tower's disciples can use it, and it is rented to visiting cultivators of fire.

places.name: Ôn Sa Thôn
places.look: A fishing village on a black-sand beach that steams faintly after rain, below the slopes of a small volcano.
places.lore: Villagers bury eggs in the warm sand to cook them and gather sulphur from the vents above. They moved down to the shore after the mountain buried their old town.

provinces.name: Tống Mộc
provinces.lore: Dense jungle along a river mouth on the south coast. Its people float timber rafts down the river to the sea and sell them at Phong Đăng and Không Mông. Old elephants come out of the jungle to die on a barrow ridge in the grass.

places.name: Tượng Trủng Cương
places.look: A low grassy ridge strewn with the bleached bones and tusks of elephants, guarded by a herd of huge grey bulls.
places.lore: Old wild elephants walk out of the jungle to die on this ridge, and a herd of spirit-touched bulls guards their bones. The raftsmen of Tống Mộc say no ivory from it has ever reached a market and come to good.

places.name: Tống Mộc Thôn
places.look: A jungle village at a river mouth, its landing crowded with long timber rafts lashed together and the huts of the raftsmen built on them.
places.lore: The raftsmen float hardwood down from the forest and sell the timber at Phong Đăng and Không Mông. A raftsman who loses his raft walks home, and is not allowed to sleep under a roof until he has built another.

provinces.name: Phù Ốc
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass along a river near the coast, flooded every wet season. Its villagers live in houses built on rafts that rise with the floods. A Wood vein in the jungle above is wrapped in wisteria.

places.name: Tử Đằng Nhãn
places.look: In the jungle above the river an ancient wisteria has climbed a dead tree and covered a whole clearing in hanging purple flowers.
places.lore: A spirit eye of Wood (Mộc) qi under the wisteria. The villagers of Phù Ốc bring their newborns here for a single breath of its air.

places.name: Phù Ốc Thôn
places.look: A village of houses built on bamboo rafts moored along a jungle river, rising and falling with the water.
places.lore: Floods come every wet season here, and since 840 the villagers have simply floated with them. A family's raft is its land, and it is divided among the children by cutting the lashings.

provinces.name: Yên Vũ
provinces.lore: Wide coastal grassland with jungle and bamboo at the eastern end of the Tower's coast. Its town trades fish, grain and bamboo by sea. Wild buffalo roam the grass behind the town, and the herders follow them rather than drive them.

places.name: Cự Giác Nguyên
places.look: A broad stretch of tall coastal grass trampled into wallows, where great dark buffalo stand with only their horns showing above the grass.
places.lore: A herd of spirit-touched wild buffalo led by a bull with horns wider than a cart roams this plain. The herders of Yên Vũ keep their own cattle well clear of the herd, and no one crosses the bull.

places.name: Yên Vũ Trấn
places.look: A walled harbour town on a wide grass coast, its grey roofs and sea wall softened by a fine rain that drifts in from the sea most afternoons.
places.lore: Yên Vũ grew up in 860 as a harbour for the grain and bamboo of the eastern coast. Its people say the misty rain is the sea's breath, and its sailors will not leave harbour on a clear day.

provinces.name: Mãn Võng
provinces.lore: Coastal jungle and grass at the western end of the Kinh Trập shore. Its fishers bring in full nets most days and dry the catch on the beach. Crocodiles lie on the wet flats behind the shore.

places.name: Lão Ngạc Chử
places.look: Low waterlogged grass flats behind the shore, where long dark shapes lie motionless in the shallow channels.
places.lore: Great saltwater crocodiles bask here, led by a spirit beast the fishers call the Old Log. The fishers leave it their fish heads and say it has never taken a villager.

places.name: Mãn Võng Thôn
places.look: A shore village of palm-thatched huts in the jungle edge, its beach covered in nets spread to dry and racks of split fish.
places.lore: The fishers of Mãn Võng have brought in full nets since 790, and they credit the crocodiles behind the shore for scaring off thieves. Every catch begins with one fish thrown back for the sea.

provinces.name: Dạ Chúc
provinces.lore: Jungle down to the shore on the south coast. Its fishers go out at night with torches on their boats, and the lights of the fleet are the brightest thing on the dark coast below the Tower. Bats roost by the thousand in the jungle above the village.

places.name: Dạ Bức Lâm
places.look: A stretch of jungle whose trees hang with thousands of roosting fruit bats, the ground beneath white with droppings.
places.lore: Huge spirit-touched fruit bats roost here, and at dusk they pour out over the coast like smoke. The fishers of Dạ Chúc say the bats follow their torches out to sea.

places.name: Dạ Chúc Thôn
places.look: A jungle shore village whose boats are drawn up on the sand by day, each with an iron torch basket fixed at the bow.
places.lore: The fishers of Dạ Chúc fish at night by torchlight, and the lights of their fleet are the brightest thing on the dark coast below the Tower. The Tower has never forbidden them, and the village takes care never to ask.

provinces.name: Phong Hỏa Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and steppe at the western end of the range, close to the Tower, with old beacon sites on every spur. A realgar mine works the lower slope. The fort that watched the western road has stood empty since the lightning drove its garrison out.

places.name: Khu Xà Khoáng
places.look: A short gallery in a mountain slope where the walls glow orange-red with realgar crystals.
places.lore: Realgar is dug here for medicines, festival wine and the poisons of Hồng Đậu Trang. The miners work short shifts and drink milk after each.

places.name: Lang Yên Phong
places.look: A steppe-flanked peak whose summit carries the ruined platform of an old beacon, blackened by long-dead fires.
places.lore: Khải Lôi's signallers lit smoke here to warn of trouble on the western road, and the Tower kept the beacon for a time after. Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its rock.

places.name: Tây Vọng Bảo
places.look: A small stone fort on a mountain spur over the western road, its towers split and blackened by lightning.
places.lore: The Tower built the fort to watch the western road after it let the old stockade below go. Lightning struck it so often that by 980 its garrison begged to leave, and the Tower let it stand empty.

provinces.name: Tiễu Bích Lĩnh
