provinces.lore: A wall of bare mountain in the north of the range, all cliff and scree. No one lives here; miners reach its one mine by rope. Its summit is one of the first to catch the storms.

places.name: Vô Tú Khoáng
places.look: A gallery mouth high on a cliff, its rope ladders long rotted away, where the ore lies in dark seams cold to the touch even at noon.
places.lore: The cold iron of this mine keeps an edge through rain and does not rust. Miners were once lowered to it on ropes to live in it a month at a time, but no crew has gone down in living memory.

places.name: Kình Thiên Phong
places.look: A sheer, square-topped summit of grey rock that seems to hold up the storm clouds on its flat crown.
places.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs in its cliffs. It is one of the first summits in the range to catch the storms, and herders on the northern steppe watch it for them.

provinces.name: Trầm Lôi Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A broad mountain mass in the middle of the range, its valleys forested and its crest bare. Thunder here is low and long, more felt than heard. An azurite mine on its flank and a high peak are its only marks.

places.name: Thiên Thanh Khoáng
places.look: A cut in the mountainside where the rock is crusted deep blue with azurite, bright against the grey scree.
places.lore: Azurite from here is ground for blue paint and smelted for copper. The painters of Không Mông buy the deepest blue for their skies.

places.name: Muộn Lôi Phong
places.look: A massive summit over forested valleys, its bare crest shaped like the head and shoulders of a giant.
places.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies deep in its bulk. The thunder rolls around it low and long, and herders say the giant is grumbling in its sleep.

provinces.name: Huyền Bộc Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with a little forest, where storm water pours off the cliffs in falls that blow sideways in the wind. No one lives here. Its tallest peak sends down a dozen falls after every storm.

places.name: Thiên Bộc Phong
places.look: A high peak whose cliffs pour a dozen waterfalls after every storm, blown into white veils by the wind.
places.lore: Water (Thủy) qi runs down its cliffs with the falls. The Tower's disciples stand under its falls after storms to train their footing.

provinces.name: Bắc Thú Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and high grass on the northern edge of Kinh Trập Sơn, facing the lands of Thiên Xu. The Tower once kept a watch fort here against the Pivot and gave it up at the truce. Herders graze the high grass and keep away from the fort.

places.name: Tinh Kỳ Phong
places.look: A tall peak on the northern edge of the range, its crest still marked by a stone socket where a great banner once flew.
places.lore: The Tower once flew its banner here in sight of Thiên Xu's lands. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its crest.

places.name: Vọng Xu Bảo
places.look: A stone fort on a high spur facing north, its walls pulled down to knee height on purpose and its gate stones laid flat.
places.lore: The Tower built this fort to watch Thiên Xu's border. When the North Star Compact was sworn again at the truce, the Tower pulled its walls down as a sign of good faith, and they have never been raised.

provinces.name: Bắc Đài Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat lichen tundra on the far northern shore, frozen most of the year and broken only by stands of stunted larch. No one lives here; reindeer herders cross it in summer and leave before the first snow. White bears den along its shore, and Tùng Đào sends no patrols past the larches.

places.name: Bạch Hùng Nguyên
places.look: Flat white tundra near the shore, pocked with snow dens and old seal bones, where great white shapes rise and lie down again in the wind.
places.lore: White bears come ashore here each autumn and den through the winter. Herders cross the plain only in midsummer, when the bears are out on the water.

provinces.name: Hàn Sam Nguyên
provinces.lore: Dark fir forest thinning into tundra and bog, with no road and no village. Trappers enter it only in winter, when the bogs freeze and the wolf packs are easier to hear. Its timber is too far from any water to be worth the cutting.

places.name: Quần Lang Lâm
places.look: A dark fir wood on low wet ground, its trails beaten hard by many paws, with gnawed antlers scattered under the trees.
places.lore: Several wolf packs share this wood and fight over it in winter, and their howling carries to the tundra. Trappers take pelts from its edge and never camp inside.

provinces.name: Tùng Chi
provinces.lore: Rolling inland pine forest whose people tap resin from the old trees and boil it into pitch for the lake boats. A quiet spirit vein of wood qi runs under its oldest roots. The empty fur town in its hills is a reminder of what happens when a forest is trapped bare.

places.name: Điêu Bì Trấn
places.look: On a wooded hill, the log walls of a small town have fallen inward, and rusted traps still hang on pegs inside the roofless fur store.
places.lore: Fur traders built Điêu Bì Trấn when sable fur was worth its weight in silver. By 1020 the sables were trapped out of the hills, and within two years the last traders left for the lake towns.

places.name: Lão Căn Mạch
places.look: On a rise in the forest, a tangle of huge exposed pine roots arches over bare ground that hums faintly when pressed with a palm.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the roots of the oldest pines here. Resin from these trees is said to stay soft for a hundred years.

places.name: Tùng Chi Thôn
places.look: Log houses among old pines, each trunk scarred with neat V-shaped cuts above a clay cup, and pitch kettles smoking in the yard.
places.lore: The village taps resin and boils it into pitch for the lake boats, cutting no living tree. Its pitch-makers say the best resin comes from trees older than Tùng Đào Cung.

provinces.name: Ngư Đăng
provinces.lore: Forest and reed swamp along the shore, its people fishing by lantern light on autumn nights. They sell smoked fish to Quy Điểu Trấn and pay their dues to Tùng Đào in pitch and dried fish. Great owls hunt the swamp edge and the villagers will not go into it after dark.

places.name: Dạ Kiêu Lâm
places.look: A swampy pine wood where pellets of fur and bone lie thick under hollow trees, and at dusk great pale owls drift between the trunks.
places.lore: Owls as big as children nest in its hollow trees and hunt the swamp edge at night. Villagers say an owl that follows a boat home means a death in the house.

places.name: Ngư Đăng Thôn
places.look: A shore village of low grey roofs where dozens of boat lanterns hang from poles along the beach, lit together on autumn nights.
places.lore: Its fishers draw fish to their nets with lantern light in autumn, and from the far shore the boats look like a second string of stars. They sell their smoked catch at Quy Điểu.

provinces.name: Tùng Than
provinces.lore: Pine forest running down to a long pale beach at the western end of the region. Its people fish, build small boats and gather pine pitch to caulk them. The forest behind the beach is thick enough that Tùng Đào's surveyors once counted its trees and gave up.

places.name: Vạn Tùng Lâm
places.look: An endless stand of straight red-brown pines on gentle ground, so even that the trunks seem to repeat to the edge of sight.
places.lore: Tùng Đào's surveyors once tried to count its trees and stopped at ten thousand, which gave the forest its name. Woodsmen get lost in it because every view looks the same.

places.name: Tùng Than Thôn
places.look: Grey-roofed houses along a pale beach under tall pines, boats drawn up on log rollers and pitch pots smoking by the water.
places.lore: Its people build small boats from windfallen pine and caulk them with their own pitch. Lake fishers from all along the shore come here to buy a hull.

provinces.name: Hồi Lưu
provinces.lore: Low forest where a river turns back on itself before it meets the shore, leaving still backwaters full of eels. Its people set eel traps and strip birch bark. They pay Hàm Nguyệt Trang in smoked eel each autumn.

places.name: Tố Hoa Lâm
places.look: A pale, quiet birch wood on flat ground, its white trunks peeling in long curls and the floor carpeted with yellow leaves.
places.lore: The villages strip bark here for boxes and writing sheets, never more than one strip from a tree in a year. Hàm Nguyệt Trang's records are kept on its bark.

places.name: Hồi Lưu Thôn
places.look: Stilt houses stand over a still backwater where the river meets the shore, wicker eel traps stacked on every porch.
places.lore: The villagers trap eels in the river's backwaters and smoke them over birch. Hàm Nguyệt Trang takes its dues in eel each autumn and serves them at its moon feast.

provinces.name: Thán Diêu
provinces.lore: Unbroken inland forest of larch and pine, smoky with charcoal kilns. Its burners make charcoal from fallen and dead wood only, by Tùng Đào's rule, and sell it to the lake towns for the winter. The kiln smoke can be seen for a day's walk.

places.name: Lạc Diệp Lâm
places.look: A larch forest that turns gold in autumn and drops every needle, leaving the trunks bare and the ground soft and bright.
places.lore: Larch is the one conifer here that sheds its needles, and the burners gather the fallen wood for their kilns. In winter the bare forest is the easiest place in the north to track game.

places.name: Thán Diêu Thôn
places.look: A clearing ringed by earth-covered charcoal mounds, smoking day and night, with soot-black houses and stacks of deadwood.
places.lore: The burners make charcoal only from dead and fallen wood, as Tùng Đào requires, and haul it to the lake towns before the snow. Their children are black to the elbows by the age of five.

provinces.name: Nguyệt Tân
provinces.lore: Forest along the river where it runs down toward the long lake, with a small side lake of its own. Nguyệt Tân Trấn ferries timber, pitch and pearls between the lake and the inland villages. It is the busiest crossing in Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm outside the pearl towns.

places.name: Tẩy Nguyệt Đàm
places.look: A small, clear lake in the pines near the river, its pebble bed visible far out from the shore.
places.lore: Fishers say the moon comes down to wash here before it rises over the long lake. Hàm Nguyệt Trang's disciples once kept spirit fish in it, and a few still swim there.

places.name: Nguyệt Tân Trấn
places.look: A timber-walled town on the river bank, its ferry stair running into the water beside rows of pitch-black barges.
places.lore: Nguyệt Tân Trấn ferries timber, pitch and pearls between the long lake and the inland villages. Its ferry runs only by moonlight in the busy season, so the day stays free for loading.

provinces.name: Sái Võng
provinces.lore: Wide pine forest and lake shore whose fishers hang their nets to dry on frames along every path. A small cold lake lies inland among the trees. The province sends fish and net cord to Quy Điểu Trấn and to Hàm Nguyệt Trang's pearl beds.

places.name: Hàn Kính Hồ
places.look: A dark, round forest lake that freezes clear as glass in winter, the trees and sky reflected perfectly in its ice.
places.lore: Its ice is so clear that the fish can be seen moving under it. Young cultivators of Hàm Nguyệt Trang come to sit on the ice and still their minds.

places.name: Sái Võng Thôn
places.look: Every path in this forest village is lined with tall frames of drying nets, so walking through it is like walking through a maze of grey lace.
places.lore: Its people twist net cord from nettle and birch bast and sell nets to fishers all along the lake. A net from Sái Võng is said to last ten winters.

provinces.name: Liệp Hộ
provinces.lore: Higher inland forest of spruce and pine where hunters' families trap marten, fox and deer. A green-canopied spirit vein of wood qi lies under the ridge. Furs from here are sold at the winter ice market of Quy Điểu.

places.name: Thúy Cái Mạch
places.look: On a forested ridge, a ring of spruces with unusually dense, deep-green crowns closes overhead like a roof, and the ground beneath stays dry in any rain.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi rises under the ridge and feeds the spruces above it. Tùng Đào's wardens visit it each spring and keep the hunters from camping inside the ring.

places.name: Liệp Hộ Thôn
places.look: A cluster of log houses with racks of stretched pelts, antlers nailed over every door and hounds sleeping in the snow.
places.lore: Its families have trapped marten, fox and deer here for generations and sell their furs at the winter ice market. Every hunter swears never to take a beast's young.

provinces.name: Phóng Phiệt
provinces.lore: Forest on a river near the long lake, where loggers bind dead and windfallen trunks into rafts and float them down. A quiet pool by the river hides its own small pearl bed. Tùng Đào's foresters mark every raft before it leaves.

places.name: Tàng Châu Đàm
places.look: A deep, reed-fringed pool beside the river, its dark water ringed with white mussel shells on the shore.
places.lore: A small bed of pearl mussels lives here, hidden from the Băng Tâm skiffs during the Long Lake War. Hàm Nguyệt Trang now keeps it as seed stock for its beds.

places.name: Phóng Phiệt Thôn
places.look: On a river bank, bound log rafts lie in rows on the mud, each branded with the pine mark of Tùng Đào's foresters.
places.lore: The villagers float windfallen and dead trunks down to the lake towns in spring flood. No raft leaves without a forester's brand, and a raft without one is burned.

provinces.name: Bạch Mang Hoang
provinces.lore: Bare tundra on the northern shore, white for nine months of the year. No one lives here; the cold wind off the water keeps even herders away. A spirit vein of water qi lies frozen in a hollow near its middle, and Tùng Đào's cultivators come to it in summer.

places.name: Hàn Lộ Huyệt
places.look: A shallow hollow in the tundra where frost forms on every blade of lichen even at midsummer noon, and the air smells of snow.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi surfaces here, cold enough to freeze dew on a summer day. Tùng Đào's water cultivators come in the short summer, when the walk is possible.

provinces.name: Tịch Ba
provinces.lore: Shore forest whose fishers go out when the evening waves calm. Its people fish, cut ice in winter and hunt lynx in the woods behind. On the shore lie the broken walls of Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn, crushed by the ice shove of 1033.

places.name: Sơn Miêu Cương
places.look: A rocky knoll in thick pine, its boulders scratched and its snow marked by broad, furred tracks.
places.lore: Lynxes den among its boulders and hunt hares through the forest. Villagers say a lynx can see through a wall, and hang their meat high.

places.name: Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn
places.look: On the shore, the stone walls of a town lean inland, pushed over in long rows, with heaps of boulders shoved up among the house footings.
places.lore: The town greeted the moonrise over the water from its harbour wall for six centuries. In the spring of 1033 a storm drove the breaking ice ashore in a wall, flattening the harbour and half the town, and its people never rebuilt.

places.name: Tịch Ba Thôn
places.look: A row of grey-roofed houses facing the water, boats pulled up at the tide line and nets set out on poles in the evening calm.
places.lore: Its fishers go out only when the evening waves settle, a habit learned after the ice shove that crushed Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn. They sell their catch and winter ice at Quy Điểu.

provinces.name: Tạc Băng
provinces.lore: Pine and cedar forest on the shore near Hàn Yên and Noãn Ốc. Its people cut blocks of lake ice in winter and pack them in sawdust to keep fish through the summer. Tùng Đào's stewards buy the ice for the granaries of the north.

places.name: Tuyết Tùng Lâm
places.look: A wood of broad cedars with layered branches that hold the snow in flat white shelves.
places.lore: Its cedar is fragrant and resists rot, and the lake villages build their shrines from it. Only a fallen cedar may be taken, by Tùng Đào's rule.

places.name: Tạc Băng Thôn
places.look: A shore village where great blocks of ice lie stacked under sawdust in long sheds, and saws and ice picks hang on every wall.
places.lore: In winter its people saw ice from the frozen shore and pack it in sawdust to keep fish all summer. Tùng Đào's stewards buy ice for the northern granaries.

provinces.name: Tùng Kiều
provinces.lore: Upland pine forest on a river, crossed by a long bridge of whole pine trunks. Woodsmen and pine-nut gatherers live here, and the wood above the river is a favourite place for listening to the pines. Tùng Đào has let Sương Tùng Các build its pavilion in the higher woods.

places.name: Thính Tùng Lâm
places.gloss: Wood Where One Listens to the Pines
places.look: An upland pine wood where flat stones have been set among the trunks as seats, and the wind in the crowns sounds like distant surf.
places.lore: Tùng Đào's disciples of the north come here to hear the pine waves when they cannot travel to the seat. The stones are said to have been set by the first steward of the north.

places.name: Sương Tùng Các
places.look: A three-roofed pavilion of dark pine stands on a frosty rise among old trees, and from every branch around it hang small paper lanterns painted with talismans.
places.lore: Sương Tùng Các is a small sect of talisman makers sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, who write their talismans on paper made from birch bark and pine resin. Its ward lanterns hang in the lake villages to keep beasts and frost spirits off the doors in winter.

places.name: Tùng Kiều Thôn
places.look: A village on both banks of a river, joined by a long bridge of whole pine trunks pinned with wooden pegs.
places.lore: The bridge was built from pines felled by one storm, and each family mends its own trunk. Pilgrims cross it on their way up to the listening wood.

provinces.name: Thạch Than
provinces.lore: Inland spruce forest along a stony river. Its people fish the shallows, gather spruce gum and float small loads of wood downstream. The river is too shallow for boats above the village, so goods go on by mule.

places.name: Vân Sam Lâm
places.look: A dark, dense spruce forest whose tall spires vanish into low cloud on grey days.
places.lore: Spruce from here is light and strong and goes to make zither soundboards in the pine sea. Gum gatherers work its edge in summer.

places.name: Thạch Than Thôn
places.look: Grey-roofed houses above a wide, stony river where children wade the shallows with spears and mules wait on the bank.
places.lore: The river is too shallow for boats above the village, so goods come and go by mule. Its people spear fish in the shallows and gather spruce gum.

provinces.name: Hồ Khẩu
provinces.lore: Forest where a river opens into the long lake, rich with fish and reeds. Hồ Khẩu Thôn lives by fishing and by the boats that pass in and out of the river. Its red pine woods give the best mast timber in the north.

places.name: Hồng Tùng Lâm
places.look: A wood of tall, straight pines with reddish bark, their crowns far above a clear floor.
places.lore: These red pines give the best mast timber in the north, and only windfalls may be taken. Shipwrights from the lake towns come to choose their trunks in person.

places.name: Hồ Khẩu Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs where a river opens into the long lake, its jetties busy with fishing boats and timber barges.
places.lore: Every boat going up the river passes Hồ Khẩu, and the village lives by fish, reeds and the boatmen's custom. Tùng Đào keeps a toll post on its jetty.

provinces.name: Tùng Tử
provinces.lore: Rolling forest of old pines whose people live by gathering pine nuts each autumn. An ancient spirit vein of wood qi lies under a single huge tree. Pine-nut oil from here is pressed for lamps all over the north.

places.name: Cổ Mộc Nhãn
places.look: In a clearing stands a single colossal pine, its trunk hollow at the base, and inside the hollow the air shimmers faintly green.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi comes to the surface inside the old pine's hollow. Tùng Đào allows one disciple at a time to sit in it, for a month at most.

places.name: Tùng Tử Thôn
places.look: A hill village where pine cones lie drying in heaps on every roof and the smell of roasted nuts hangs in the air.
places.lore: Its people live by gathering pine nuts each autumn and pressing them for lamp oil. They leave one cone in ten for the squirrels, saying the squirrels plant the next forest.

provinces.name: Sơn Ổ
provinces.lore: The first real hills of the southern forest, climbing above five hundred metres. Villagers gather mushrooms and wild honey in the hollows and keep a few goats. The ruin of Tà Dương Trấn on the slope warns them not to build where the hillside is soft.

places.name: Bàn Căn Lâm
places.look: On a steep hillside, pines grow from bare rock, their roots coiling over the stones like ropes.
places.lore: The roots hold the slope together, and the villages forbid cutting here. After Tà Dương Trấn slid away, no one argues with the rule.

places.name: Tà Dương Trấn
places.look: A raw scar of earth runs down a hillside, and at its foot the timbers and roofs of a small town lie broken in a heap of mud and stones grown over with birch.
places.lore: A hill town of honey and timber traders, built on a sunny western slope. In the long rains of 1104 the hillside slid away and buried half the town in a night, and the rest was left.

places.name: Sơn Ổ Thôn
places.look: Houses tucked into a sheltered hollow in the hills, log beehives on the slope and baskets of mushrooms drying on the eaves.
places.lore: Its people gather mushrooms and wild honey and keep a few goats. They remember Tà Dương Trấn and build only on rock.

provinces.name: Hệ Bì
provinces.lore: Forest on a river at the edge of Phản Cảnh Lâm. Its people are woodcutters and guides who tie bark strips to the trees so the lost can follow the light out of the forest. Tùng Đào's patrols rest here before skirting the forest edge.

places.name: Phản Cảnh Lâm
places.look: From outside it is a dark sea of old spruce and larch rising gently to a low crown. At its heart a hollow ringed by giant trees holds a patch of amber evening light that lingers long after the rest of the forest has gone grey.

places.name: Hệ Bì Thôn
places.look: A river village at the edge of Phản Cảnh Lâm, where bundles of birch bark strips hang by every door, ready to be tied to trees.
places.lore: Its woodcutters and guides tie bark strips on the ways into Phản Cảnh Lâm so the lost can follow the light out. Tùng Đào's patrols rest here and ask the guides what they have seen.

provinces.name: Song Thụ
provinces.lore: Deep river forest of mixed pine and birch. Its villagers fish and gather herbs, and tend the overgrown terraces of the fallen Lãnh Hương Viện for the cold-flower incense herbs that still grow there. Tùng Đào took the old academy's disciples in when it fell.

places.name: U Thúy Lâm
places.look: A deep wood of pine and fir where moss covers every stone and fallen log in a thick green fleece.
places.lore: The forest is so damp and quiet that herb gatherers find mosses here that grow nowhere else. Its paths lead up to the old academy's terraces.

places.name: Lãnh Hương Viện
places.look: On a wooded rise, terraces of overgrown herb beds climb to the roofless halls of an academy, its incense burners still standing in the moss.
places.lore: A small sect of incense makers who burned cold-flower herbs to calm the mind in cultivation. Its last master died in seclusion in 890 with no heir named, and Tùng Đào took in its disciples; its herbs still grow on the terraces.

places.name: Song Thụ Thôn
places.look: A river village gathered around two huge pines that grew from one root, their trunks splitting apart above the roofs.
places.lore: Villagers fish the river and gather incense herbs from the old terraces of Lãnh Hương Viện. Couples are married under the twin pines.

provinces.name: Phong Khẩu
provinces.lore: High forested hills at the region's southern edge, cut by a windy gap where the old post road once ran. Its people keep goats and gather pine nuts, and brown bears hold the crags above. The empty post town on the gap fell out of use when the road moved.

places.name: Tông Hùng Nhai
places.look: A forested crag above the gap, its caves marked by stripped bark and claw-torn stumps.
places.lore: Brown bears den in its caves through the winter and raid the beehives below in spring. The villagers leave a pot of honey at the foot of the crag each autumn, hoping to be left alone.

places.name: Dịch Lộ Trấn
places.look: High on a hill, the stone stables and inn walls of a post town stand roofless beside a paved road that runs into the forest and vanishes.
places.lore: Tùng Đào built the post town when it took Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm, on the hill road from the pine sea. When the lake road along the water was finished, the hill road was abandoned, and the town emptied by 868.

places.name: Phong Khẩu Thôn
places.look: Low stone-walled houses huddle in a windy gap in the hills, roofs weighted with rocks, goats sheltering in the lee.
places.lore: The wind through the gap never stops, and its people keep goats and gather pine nuts. They still keep the old post road's well, though few travellers come.

provinces.name: Đống Thổ Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat, frozen tundra on the northern shore, wet in the short summer and iron-hard in winter. No one lives here. A deep vein of water qi lies under the frost, and it never thaws.

places.name: Vĩnh Đống Huyệt
places.look: A sunken pit in the tundra lined with blue ice that never thaws, breathing cold mist even in summer.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here so cold that the ground has not thawed in living memory. Tùng Đào's disciples who cultivate in it wrap themselves in fur and stay a day at most.

provinces.name: Tàn Tuyết Câu
provinces.lore: Tundra and stunted forest in shallow gullies where snow lies until midsummer. No one lives here now, though the stones of the old Bắc Minh Quán still stand on the shore. A cold spring of water qi runs from the gullies.

places.name: Bắc Minh Quán
places.look: On a bare shore, a ring of low stone cells stands around a fallen hall, its doorways facing the northern water.
places.lore: Hermits of water arts built this abbey to watch the northern water through the long dark. They never took more than a handful of disciples, and when Tùng Đào came north in 330 the last of them went to the palace and left the abbey empty.

places.name: Bạch Dạ Tuyền
places.look: A cold spring wells up among stunted larches and runs in a clear thread over the tundra, catching the low light of the summer nights.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds this spring, strongest in the white nights of midsummer. The hermits of Bắc Minh Quán drank only from it.

provinces.name: Thương Mang Nguyên
provinces.lore: Grey tundra and thin larch woods stretching to the northern shore. Only herders in summer cross it. A vein of frost-bound water qi lies under a low rise, and Tùng Đào's disciples come to temper themselves in its cold.

places.name: Ngưng Sương Mạch
places.look: A low rise in the tundra is crusted with thick white frost in a long line, as though a frozen river ran just under the lichen.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs under the rise and draws frost out of the air. Tùng Đào's disciples come to temper their bodies in its cold.

provinces.name: Mục Lộc
provinces.lore: Inland forest giving way to tundra in the north, where reindeer families of the same stock as Tuyết Lộc's herders keep their winter grounds. They trade hides, antler and smoked meat south. The forest is bowed under snow for half the year.

places.name: Tuyết Áp Lâm
places.look: A pine forest whose young trees are bent into arches under heavy snow, making tunnels across the paths.
places.lore: Snow lies so heavy here that the trees grow crooked, and the herders drive their reindeer through the arches. Bent pine from here makes the best sled runners.

places.name: Mục Lộc Thôn
places.look: Log houses and hide tents at the forest edge, reindeer corralled behind fences of split pine and antlers piled by the doors.
places.lore: Its herders are cousins of Tuyết Lộc's and keep their winter grounds here. They trade hides, antler and smoked meat south to the lake towns.

provinces.name: Bắc Ngạn
provinces.lore: A broad forest running up to the cold northern shore. Its people hunt seals on the ice and fish through holes in winter, and cut timber in summer. Giant boars root in the inland woods, and villagers fence their stores against them.

places.name: Cự Thỉ Cương
places.look: A knoll in the forest torn up as if ploughed, with trees rubbed bare at shoulder height and wallows of black mud.
places.lore: Boars the size of oxen root here and raid the village stores in lean winters. Hunters go after them only in groups of ten.

places.name: Bắc Ngạn Thôn
places.look: Grey-roofed log houses on the cold northern shore, sleds and harpoons stacked by the doors and seal hides stretched on frames.
places.lore: Its people hunt seals on the ice and fish through holes in winter. Seal oil from here lights the lamps of the northern villages.

provinces.name: Băng Võng
provinces.lore: Forest, bog and tundra on the northern shore, where fishers set long nets under the ice. Golden eagles nest on a rock table inland and take hares and young deer. Its people pay Tùng Đào in dried fish and eagle feathers.

places.name: Kim Điêu Đài
places.look: A flat-topped rock rises out of the forest, its edges heaped with great stick nests and the bones of hares and fawns.
places.lore: Golden eagles nest on the rock and hunt the forest and tundra for miles. Their fallen feathers are prized by fletchers, and villagers gather them under the cliff.

places.name: Băng Võng Thôn
places.look: A shore village where long lines of holes cut through the ice lead out from the beach, each with a net cord frozen to a stake.
places.lore: Its fishers feed long nets under the ice from hole to hole and haul them at dawn. They pay Tùng Đào in dried fish and eagle feathers.

provinces.name: Ô Nê Trạch
provinces.lore: A cold black-mud marsh on the shore, frozen half the year and stinking in summer. No one lives here; the poison toads of its shoals are reason enough. Alchemists' collectors come for toad venom in late summer.

places.name: Độc Thiềm Chử
places.look: Low mud shoals in a black marsh, their surface covered in warty toads the size of a man's head, croaking in a deep drone.
places.lore: Poison toads breed on the shoals in summer, and their venom blisters the skin. Alchemists' collectors come in late summer with gloves and jars.

provinces.name: Tân Sinh
provinces.lore: Steppe and grass on the north coast below the red cliffs of Xích Thành Môn. Its people herd goats and dry fish, and do not graze the cliffs. The village was rebuilt on the ashes of one of the eleven villages Xích Thành burned.

places.name: Xích Thành Môn
places.look: On the coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, cliffs of deep red rock rise in rounded tiers like banks of rosy cloud above the sea. Into them are cut the broken terraces and gutted halls of the old gate, their fire-blackened walls open to the sky, with fresh pale quarry scars where stone has lately been taken away.

places.name: Tàn Hỏa Mạch
places.look: A patch of grass where the earth is cracked and faintly warm, a short walk from the ruined gate.
places.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein that once fed Xích Thành's fire arts. Phượng Minh keeps an eye on anyone who sits here too long.

places.name: Tân Sinh Thôn
places.look: A coast village of red-stone houses on steppe below the red cliffs, a blackened old hearthstone set at its centre.
places.lore: It was rebuilt on the ashes of one of the eleven villages Xích Thành burned, and its people keep the old hearthstone as a shrine. They herd goats and dry fish, and never graze the cliffs.

provinces.name: Thạch Tượng
provinces.lore: Jungle, grass and red hills on the west coast around the quarry of Đan Thạch. Its people are quarrymen and masons who cut and dress the red stone. The burned walls of Xích Thành's old quarry town stand on the hillside above.

places.name: Đan Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A quarry cut into a red mountain, its face stepped in tall terraces of raw vermilion rock. Rough-cut red blocks lie in rows on the quarry floor, waiting to be dragged down the road.

places.name: Đan Mộc Lâm
places.look: A grove of small thorny trees on the grass below the red quarry, their cut stumps showing heartwood as bright red as the stone above.
places.lore: Its sappan wood is chipped and boiled for red dye and sold to the silk dyers of Tang Điền. The masons of Thạch Tượng say the trees drink the colour out of the red mountain.

places.name: Tạc Thạch Trấn
places.look: Burned walls on a red hillside above the quarry, the ground strewn with broken chisels.
places.lore: Xích Thành Môn's quarry town for Đan Thạch, burned in 588 in the War of the Vermilion Caves when the gate's men fired it rather than leave it. The quarrymen who stayed built Thạch Tượng below.

places.name: Thạch Tượng Thôn
places.look: A village of red-stone houses below the quarry, its yards full of half-dressed blocks and chisel sheds.
places.lore: Its masons dress the red stone of Đan Thạch for Phượng Minh's builders, and their own houses are made of the blocks that cracked.

provinces.name: Thu Võng
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass on the southern coast, low and wet. Its people fish with nets and gather agarwood in the forest. Agarwood from here is burned in Phượng Minh's halls.

places.name: Trầm Hương Lâm
places.look: Dark jungle where some trunks are scarred and oozing black resin, and the air smells of incense.
places.lore: Its agarwood is burned in Phượng Minh's halls. The gatherers wound a tree and wait twenty years before they cut it.

places.name: Thu Võng Thôn
places.look: A low shore village of stilted houses at the jungle's edge, long seine nets hanging on poles before every door and canoes drawn up on the grey sand.
places.lore: Its people haul seine nets from the beach at dawn, whole families on each rope, and in the dry season go into the forest behind for agarwood. The resin they bring out is burned in Phượng Minh's halls.

provinces.name: Hải Sâm
provinces.lore: Deep jungle down to a mangrove shore on the southern coast. Its people dive for sea cucumbers and dry them for the cities. A great python holds the jungle valley behind the village.

places.name: Đại Mãng Cốc
places.look: A jungle valley where broad smooth tracks run through the undergrowth and shed skins hang from the branches.
places.lore: A python longer than a boat lives here and takes deer, pigs and the occasional diver. Alchemists pay well for its shed skin.

places.name: Hải Sâm Thôn
places.look: A village on the mangrove edge where dried sea cucumbers hang in strings under the eaves.
places.lore: Its divers bring sea cucumbers up from the shallows and dry them for the city kitchens.

provinces.name: Tân Lang
provinces.lore: Jungle, grass and mangrove on the south coast. Its people grow areca palms and sell the nuts along the coast road. A wood vein lies in the jungle behind the groves.

places.name: Thâm Lục Mạch
places.look: A hollow in the jungle where the leaves grow so thick and dark that it is green twilight at noon.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein. Wood cultivators come to sit in the hollow and leave covered in moss.

places.name: Tân Lang Thôn
places.look: A coast village under tall straight areca palms, their nut clusters drying on mats.
places.lore: Its people sell areca nuts along the coast road; every guest is offered one at the door.

provinces.name: Hương Liệu
provinces.lore: Low jungle on the south coast around a small spice market town. Its people gather and trade spices and resin from the jungle. Old banyans crowd the forest behind the town.

places.name: Cổ Dung Lâm
places.look: A jungle of vast banyans whose hanging roots have grown into whole new trunks, so that one tree looks like a forest.
places.lore: The town's traders leave a coin in the roots of the oldest banyan before a voyage.

places.name: Hương Liệu Thị
places.look: A small walled market town on the shore, its streets lined with sacks of pepper, cardamom and resin under awnings.
places.lore: The spice villages of the south coast bring their harvest here, and boats carry it on to Ngũ Thải and Thạch Cơ.

provinces.name: Sa Nhân
provinces.lore: Jungle and grass on the southern shore. Its people grow cardamom under the trees. On the shore stand the ruins of a sea hall of Xích Thành Môn, abandoned in 590.

places.name: Viêm Hải Quán
places.look: Broken red-stone halls on the grassy shore, their sea wall blackened as if by fire.
places.lore: A sea hall of Xích Thành Môn, where its disciples practised fire arts over the water. It was abandoned when the gate fell in 590, and Phượng Minh never reopened it.

places.name: Tử Đàn Huyệt
places.look: A ring of old rosewood trees in the jungle, their fallen leaves deep and dark underfoot.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein lies under the ring. Phượng Minh forbids cutting the rosewood here.

places.name: Sa Nhân Thôn
places.look: A shore village of thatched houses beside cardamom gardens planted in the shade of the jungle trees, with pods drying on woven trays in every yard.
places.lore: Its people grow cardamom under the canopy and sell the dried pods at Hương Liệu Thị. They will not walk on the grass shore by the old Xích Thành sea hall after dark.

provinces.name: Nam Tân
provinces.lore: A small, steep stretch of jungle and forest on the south-western coast with a good harbour. Its people work the boats that sail to the far south. Kapok trees flower red on the hill behind the town.

places.name: Mộc Miên Lâm
places.look: A hillside of tall kapok trees that burst into huge red flowers on bare branches every spring.
places.lore: The coast calls them hero trees. Their floss stuffs the town's pillows and sails' seams.

places.name: Nam Tân Trấn
places.look: A small walled harbour town on a steep shore, its quay crowded with deep-sea boats.
places.lore: Boats sail from here to the far south and the islands. Its sailors say the great Bằng's wind starts at their quay.

provinces.name: Đậu Khấu
provinces.lore: Jungle hills and mangrove on the far southern coast, near Thôn Hải's old islet. Its people grow nutmeg and fish. A spice town on the shore was burned by the pirates in 771.

places.name: Hương Phàm Trấn
places.look: Charred walls among jungle on the shore, a burned quay running into the sea.
places.lore: A spice port of the south coast, burned by Thôn Hải's pirates in 771. The Purge came ten years too late for it, and its trade moved to Hương Liệu.

places.name: Huyết Đằng Mạch
places.look: A jungle hilltop knotted with vines as thick as an arm, which bleed dark red sap where they are cut.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein runs under the hill and the vines grow fastest over it. Healers of the coast tap the sap to stop bleeding, and wood cultivators who sit here say they can feel the vines growing.

places.name: Đậu Khấu Thôn
places.look: A shore village among nutmeg trees on the jungle hills, brown seeds wrapped in red lace drying on mats in every yard.
places.lore: Its people grow nutmeg and mace and fish within sight of Thôn Hải's old islet. Their grandparents' grandparents came from the burned spice town of Hương Phàm, and every house keeps a charred plank from it over the hearth.

provinces.name: Bằng Trình
provinces.lore: A small jungle coast in the far south-west facing the southern sea. Its fishers sail further south than any others on the coast. A water vein on the hill looks out toward where the great Bằng is said to fly.

places.name: Nam Minh Mạch
places.look: A rocky hilltop in the jungle with a clear spring that looks out over the open southern sea.
places.lore: A Thủy (water) vein named for the southern deep where the Bằng flies in the old book. The spring always runs a little south.

places.name: Bằng Trình Thôn
places.look: A jungle-edge fishing village whose long deep-sea boats are drawn up with their prows all pointing south.
places.lore: Its fishers sail further south than any others on the coast and say they follow the great Bằng's road.

provinces.name: Hồ Tiêu
provinces.lore: Jungle hills on the southern coast. Its people grow pepper vines on the trees and sell the dried berries to the ports. Dragon's blood trees grow on the slope above.

places.name: Long Huyết Lâm
places.look: Squat umbrella-shaped trees on a jungle slope, their cut bark weeping dark red resin.
places.lore: Its resin, dragon's blood, is a medicine for wounds and a red varnish for the palace's zithers.

places.name: Hồ Tiêu Thôn
places.look: A hill village above the sea where pepper vines climb every tree, and red and black berries dry on mats along the paths.
places.lore: Its people tend the vines on the jungle slope and carry the dried pepper down to the shore boats, which take it to Hương Liệu Thị and on to the cities. Every bride is given a vine to plant on her first day.

provinces.name: Lô Hội
provinces.lore: Grass, jungle and bamboo on the east coast just south of Phần Vũ Đường. Its people grow aloe and sell the salve to the hall's burned disciples. A fire vein in the grass still holds the warmth of the vents.

places.name: Dư Ôn Mạch
places.look: A low grassy hill where snow-white ash shows in the soil and the ground is warm after dark.
places.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein running out from the vents to the north. Phần Vũ's disciples rest here between sittings.

places.name: Lô Hội Thôn
places.look: A coast village of grass-roofed houses among rows of spiky grey-green aloe.
places.lore: Its people boil aloe into salve and sell it to Phần Vũ Đường for disciples burned in the vents.

provinces.name: Hồng Sa
provinces.lore: A tiny grassy headland on the south coast with beaches of red sand. Its people fish and boil salt. A hot pool by the shore is warmed by the waves breaking over volcanic rock.

places.name: Lãng Ôn Trì
places.look: A rock pool on the shore where hot water wells up through black rock and mixes with the breaking waves.
places.lore: At high tide it is warm, at low tide scalding; the villagers time their baths by the moon.

places.name: Hồng Sa Thôn
places.look: A few fishing huts on a beach of red volcanic sand, boats drawn up above the tide.
places.lore: Its people fish and boil salt. Bathers come for the red sand, said to draw out fever.

provinces.name: Thiên Nhai
provinces.lore: A tiny grassy cape at the south-western end of the coast. Its people run the last harbour before the open sea. Fire lizards hold the cliff beyond the town.

places.name: Hỏa Tích Nhai
places.look: A black sea cliff beyond the town, its ledges crowded with great lizards basking in the sun.
places.lore: Spirit monitor lizards that spit burning spittle nest here. The town's children are told never to climb it, and some do.

places.name: Thiên Nhai Trấn
places.gloss: Town at the Edge of the Sky
places.look: A small walled harbour town on a grassy cape, with nothing beyond it but sea.
places.lore: The last port before the open southern sea; ships take water here, and sailors carve their names on the quay before they leave.

provinces.name: Bằng Sàng
provinces.lore: The isle of Đồ Nam Đảo in the southern sea: jungle on its flanks and a little volcanic ground, a grassy crown pressed into the great Bằng's hollow, and the blood-red spring Chu Sa Tuyền steaming in a clearing. Seabirds nest here in their thousands, and wild pigs and monitor lizards root in the jungle. No one has ever settled it; fishers from the mainland land only to leave fish in the hollow for a fair wind south, and fire cultivators sometimes row out to soak in the red spring and leave the same day.

places.name: Đồ Nam Đảo
places.look: A low grassy island in the southern sea, its crown pressed into a vast shallow hollow, as if something enormous had lain there. The grass in the hollow grows in long swirled streaks like the print of feathers, and seabirds wheel over it in their thousands.

places.name: Chu Sa Tuyền
places.look: In a jungle clearing, a single round hot spring boils up blood-red from the ground, steaming hard, and its overflow runs away through the trees in a bright vermilion stream. The jungle around is pale with rising steam.

provinces.name: Viêm Châu
provinces.lore: A volcanic isle in the southern sea, its jungle flanks rising to a smoking cone, its shores strewn with grey pumice after every outburst. Fruit bats, crabs and snakes are its only lasting inhabitants. Xích Thành Môn once kept a fire pavilion on its slope, abandoned in 590 and half buried by lava since; no village has ever stood here, and Phượng Minh's fire disciples come by boat only to temper themselves at the vent.

places.name: Luyện Vũ Huyệt
places.look: A red-glowing crack high on the volcano's flank, breathing heat over a bare slope of black rock.
places.lore: Phượng Minh holds it; its fire disciples come to temper their arts in the heat and say the vent forges feathers into flame. Its fire is Hỏa (fire) at its fiercest.

places.name: Lưu Hỏa Các
places.look: The upper halls of a red-stone pavilion jutting out of a tongue of black lava on the jungle slope.
places.lore: A fire hall of Xích Thành Môn, abandoned when the gate fell in 590. In 845 lava from the vent above ran down over its lower courts, and only its roofs still show.

provinces.name: Dương Cốc
provinces.lore: The far south-eastern isle of Dục Nhật Đảo, jungle and volcanic ground facing the open ocean, with the snake forest of Vạn Xà Lâm deep in its interior and the sea arch of Phù Tang Cảnh's gate on its eastern shore. It has no village and no harbour; its only dweller is the hermit Mạc Quy Khư in his thatched hut by the gate, as he has been since 700. Pilgrims and fishers come by boat from the mainland to ask him their one question or to bow to the sunrise, and leave before the snakes come out at dusk.

places.name: Dục Nhật Đảo
places.look: A forested island in the far south-eastern sea, its eastern shore facing open ocean where the sun rises straight out of the water. On that shore stands a great ring of sea-worn rock, an arch open to the sunrise, by which the gate of Phù Tang Cảnh opens. A single thatched hut sits under the trees above it.

places.name: Vạn Xà Lâm
places.look: Deep jungle at the far end of Đan Huyệt Châu, where giant strangler figs have wrapped and swallowed older trees. Their grey roots coil over a black, still pool like nests of snakes, and real snakes lie sunning on them.

provinces.name: Phá Lãng
provinces.lore: Jungle on the far southern coast, facing the islet of Thôn Hải Môn. Its boatmen row treasure seekers out to dig in the burned hold, and some of them do not row back. Palms line the shore.

places.name: Thôn Hải Môn
places.look: A small forested islet in the southern gulf, ringed by rocks. At the waterline gapes the black mouth of a sea cave large enough to take a ship, its rim scorched and the stumps of a broken log boom still standing across it. Charred timbers of the old hold lie heaped inside the entrance.

places.name: Thanh Da Lâm
places.look: A coastal grove of tall leaning coconut palms above a white beach.
places.lore: Its palms give the village rope, oil and roofing; the boatmen say no pirate ever hid in it.

places.name: Phá Lãng Thôn
places.look: A jungle shore village of boatmen, its beach lined with small strong rowing boats.
places.lore: Its boatmen row treasure seekers out to Thôn Hải's islet to dig in the ash for Kình Nha, and charge for the trip both ways in advance.

provinces.name: Trúc Lâu
provinces.lore: Wide grass and bamboo on the eastern coast. Its people live in raised bamboo houses and grow rice and mulberry. A young hall of fire-silk weavers has risen on the shore, and the elders of Phượng Minh watch it with interest and some unease.

places.name: Chức Hà Các
places.look: A long red-timber pavilion on the grassy shore, its open halls hung with bolts of silk that glow red at dusk.
places.lore: A minor sect of weavers sworn to Phượng Minh, founded in 1150, which weaves fire-silk robes and banners from Tang Điền's worms without the vents. It says it has rediscovered Xích Thành's lost craft by other means, and the palace has not yet decided whether that pleases it.

places.name: Thanh Can Mạch
places.look: A bamboo grove near the shore whose green canes grow twice as thick as any around it, creaking in the sea wind.
places.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein lies under the grove. The villagers of Trúc Lâu cut its canes only for the main posts of their houses, and the weavers of Chức Hà Các come here to sit before a new loom is strung.

places.name: Trúc Lâu Thôn
places.look: A coast village of raised bamboo houses on stilts among rice and mulberry plots.
places.lore: Its people grow rice and mulberry, and lately sell their cocoons to the weavers on the shore.

provinces.name: Cam Giá
provinces.lore: Low grass and jungle on the south coast near the river. Its people grow sugarcane and boil it into brown sugar for the cities. A boiling spring in the fields is used to start the cane fires.

places.name: Phí Thạch Thang
places.look: A spring in the cane fields that boils hard among white stones, steaming day and night.
places.lore: The villagers start the cane boiling with its water and cook eggs in it for travellers.

places.name: Cam Giá Thôn
places.look: A shore village surrounded by tall sugarcane, with an ox-driven cane press and a smoking boiling shed at its centre.
places.lore: Its people crush the cane in the press, boil the juice down into cakes of brown sugar and ship them to Ngũ Thải and the cities. They start the boiling with water from the hot spring in the fields, which saves a day's firewood.

provinces.name: Lam Điện
provinces.lore: Grass and jungle on the south coast. Its people grow indigo and dye cloth and silk blue for the coast. A drowned town lies on the shore, lost to a storm tide in 913.

places.name: Lục Phàn Trì
places.look: A warm pool in the grass whose water is a cloudy green and whose rim is crusted with green crystals.
places.lore: The dyers scrape its green vitriol to fix their colours, and alchemists buy it too.

places.name: Kim Sa Trấn
places.look: Sand-drifted walls on the shore, the lower streets under the sea at high tide.
places.lore: A fishing and trading town on the golden beach, drowned by a great storm tide in 913. Its people moved inland, and their grandchildren became the dyers of Lam Điện.

places.name: Lam Điện Thôn
places.look: A shore village where vats of blue dye stand in every yard and cloth dries in long blue banners.
places.lore: Its people grow indigo and dye cloth and silk; their hands are blue to the wrist.

provinces.name: Lệ Chi
provinces.lore: Grass and jungle on the south-eastern coast. Its people grow lychees and send them to the cities by fast boat. A forest of flame trees burns red on the grass every summer.

places.name: Phượng Vĩ Lâm
places.look: A stand of spreading flame trees on the grass, their crowns blazing scarlet every summer.
places.lore: The coast calls them phoenix-tail trees. Phượng Minh's disciples collect the fallen flowers for the summer rites.

places.name: Lệ Chi Thôn
places.look: A shore village among lychee orchards, its trees hung with red fruit in early summer.
places.lore: Its lychees are rushed to the cities by fast boat, since they spoil in three days.

provinces.name: Quế Viên
provinces.lore: Jungle with a mangrove shore on the south-eastern coast. Its people grow longans and dry them for the markets. A mangrove town on the shore was burned by Thôn Hải in 767.

places.name: Phi Hồ Cốc
places.look: A jungle valley where the trees hang black with thousands of roosting giant bats.
places.lore: Spirit flying foxes with wings wider than a man's arms roost here by day and strip the orchards by night.

places.name: Bàn Căn Trấn
places.look: Burned stilts and walls among mangrove roots on the shore, half swallowed by the tide.
places.lore: A mangrove town of fishers and charcoal burners, burned by Thôn Hải's raiders in 767. The mangroves have taken it back.

places.name: Quế Viên Thôn
places.look: A jungle village in a clearing of longan orchards, the brown fruit drying over smoky charcoal racks under long open sheds.
places.lore: Its people dry longans into the sweet brown rounds sold in every market of the coast, and burn the pruned wood into charcoal. They keep torches lit in the orchards at night against the flying foxes of the valley nearby.

provinces.name: Bạch Diêm
provinces.lore: Grass and jungle on the flat eastern coast. Its people make salt in pans and fish the shallows. A water vein lies among the mangrove roots inland.

places.name: Triều Căn Nhãn
places.look: A clear pool among mangrove roots inland, where the water rises and falls with no channel to the sea.
places.lore: A Thủy (water) vein. Phượng Minh's scholars have added it to the puzzle of Hồ Tâm's lake.

places.name: Bạch Diêm Thôn
places.look: A flat coast village beside a grid of salt pans gleaming white in the sun.
places.lore: Its people make salt and fish the shallows; its salt is whiter than any on the coast.

provinces.name: Huyết Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A block of high red mountain on the west coast of Đan Huyệt Châu, too steep for villages. Only quarrymen and fire cultivators climb it. Its summit is said to be where the five-coloured bird was seen over the vermilion caves.

places.name: Thải Phượng Phong
places.look: A tall red crag above the west coast, its rock banded in red, yellow and grey.
places.lore: It is said the five-coloured bird was seen over this peak in the old days, and the coast was named for it. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

provinces.name: Thiên Bạch Nguyên
provinces.gloss: Plain Where the Sky Is White
provinces.lore: Flat frozen tundra along the northern sea, where snow and sky meet without a line between them. No one lives here; sealers come in summer and leave before the first snow. Herds of frost elephants cross it each year and leave tusk-scored ice behind.

places.name: Hàn Tượng Nguyên
places.look: Wide frozen flats are scored with long grooves where frost elephants have dragged their tusks through the ice.
places.lore: Herds of woolly frost elephants cross the plain each year on the same path. Sealers say the herd will trample anything that stands in it, tent or cultivator.

provinces.name: Bồ Diệp
provinces.lore: Low woods and wide cattail marsh along the cold north shore. Its people weave cattail mats and baskets, fish the shallows and sell both in Yên Ba. Great otters fish the same channels, and the villagers share the catch with them rather than fight.

places.name: Đại Thát Chử
places.look: Mud banks in the marsh channels are crossed by slides and heaped with fish bones where great otters feed.
places.lore: Otters as large as a man fish these channels and fight anything that takes their catch. The villagers of Bồ Diệp leave them a share of each net.

places.name: Bồ Diệp Thôn
places.look: Low houses roofed with cattail thatch stand on stilts at the edge of a marshy bay, mats drying on every rail.
places.lore: The villagers weave cattail mats and baskets and fish the shallows. Their mats line the floors of half the houses in Yên Ba.

provinces.name: Thiêu Thán
provinces.lore: Deep inland forest, unbroken for days of walking, with no coast and no river. Charcoal burners live in it and send their charcoal to the furnaces of Hồng Lô Cốc. Among the trees lie the burnt ruins of a resin town lost to fire.

places.name: Thâm Bích Lâm
places.look: Old broadleaf forest so dense that the light under it is green even at noon.
places.lore: The charcoal burners cut only at its edges and leave the old heart alone. Lost travellers are told to walk downhill until they smell smoke.

places.name: Tùng Chi Trấn
places.look: Blackened stone footings and charred stumps lie among young trees, the outline of a small town still visible in the moss.
places.lore: Resin tappers built the town and sold pitch for boats and torches. In the dry summer of 1061 a fire caught the resin stores and burned the town and the forest around it in one night; the tappers did not rebuild.

places.name: Thiêu Thán Thôn
places.look: A clearing of turf-domed kilns smokes among the trees, with black-faced burners and stacks of cut wood around it.
places.lore: Its charcoal goes by cart to Hồng Lô Cốc, which pays well for wood that burns even. The burners say a good kiln is tended like a pill furnace.

provinces.name: Bích Tân
provinces.lore: Forest running down to a sheltered landing on the north coast, where timber is floated out to sea. The town of Bích Tân Trấn lives by timber and the coast trade, and its old firs are the tallest on the cape. Inland stand the empty walls of a town emptied by the coughing sickness of 760.

places.name: Bách Niên Lâm
places.look: Ancient firs stand far apart above a floor of moss, each wider than a cart.
places.lore: The town of Bích Tân cuts a tree here only once a century, for the main beam of its hall. Woodcutters say each tree knows when its year has come.

places.name: Hoàng Bá Trấn
places.look: Roofless houses of grey stone stand in a ring around an empty market, yellow-barked cork trees growing through their floors.
places.lore: The town sold the yellow cork bark used against fevers, and grew rich on it. The coughing sickness of 760 killed most of its people, and the rest left before the cure of Lâm Tuyền was found.

places.name: Bích Tân Trấn
places.look: A walled timber town of grey roofs stands at a sheltered landing, log rafts tied along its shore.
places.lore: Timber from the cape's northern forests is floated here and shipped out along the coast. Its harbour masters are paid in logs as often as in coin.

provinces.name: Dã Mật
provinces.lore: Linden and maple forest on the coast east of Hồng Lô Cốc. Its villagers gather wild honey and wax, and sell the wax to the alchemists for sealing pill jars. Honey bears compete with them for every hive.

places.name: Mật Hùng Lâm
places.look: Lindens scored with claw marks stand over broken hives and trampled undergrowth.
places.lore: Honey bears raid the hives here every summer, and some of them have eaten enough spirit honey to grow cunning. Hunters of Dã Mật go in pairs.

places.name: Dã Mật Thôn
places.look: Hollow-log hives hang from every tree around a small village of grey roofs, and bees fill the air above the paths.
places.lore: The villagers gather wild honey and wax from the linden woods. Their wax seals the pill jars of Hồng Lô Cốc.

provinces.name: Hàn Loan
provinces.lore: Birch forest around a cold, low-lying bay on the western shore of the cape. Fishers and birch-bark weavers live by the water. In winter the bay half freezes and the boats are hauled up into the birches.

places.name: Hoa Thụ Lâm
places.look: A white-trunked birch forest grows on low ground behind the bay, bright even under grey skies.
places.lore: The villagers of Hàn Loan strip its bark for baskets, boxes and roofing, taking only a strip from each tree. Peeled trunks heal into dark rings that mark the families who cut them.

places.name: Hàn Loan Thôn
places.look: A few grey-roofed houses stand on a low cold bay, boats drawn up among the birches behind them.
places.lore: Its fishers haul their boats into the birch wood when the bay half freezes in winter. The women weave baskets of birch bark while they wait for the thaw.

provinces.name: Hải Đới
provinces.lore: Elm forest along a coast rich in kelp beds. Its people cut and dry kelp and sell it inland for food and for the alchemists' salt washes. Kelp dries on racks along the shore for most of the summer.

places.name: Du Thụ Lâm
places.look: Tall elms with spreading crowns cover low ground just inland of the kelp shore.
places.lore: In famine years the cape's poor eat elm seeds and inner bark from these woods, and the villagers of Hải Đới never forbid it. The custom dates from the winter of 860.

places.name: Hải Đới Thôn
places.look: Long racks of drying kelp line the shore in front of a small village, dark ribbons stirring in the wind.
places.lore: The villagers cut kelp from the offshore beds and dry it for food. Hồng Lô Cốc buys the ash of burnt kelp for its salt washes.

provinces.name: Thái Dược
provinces.lore: Forest rising into steep high ground in the east of the cape, far from the sea. Herb gatherers live here and sell roots and leaves to Hồng Lô Cốc and to Thúy Vi's terraces. Mountain lynxes keep the upper slopes.

places.name: Đoản Vĩ Cương
places.look: A rocky wooded ridge is crossed by narrow game trails and marked with claw-scored trunks.
places.lore: Short-tailed spirit lynxes, the bobtails of the ridge's name, den in the rocks and hunt the herb gatherers' paths at dusk. The gatherers say a lynx will follow you for a day before it decides.

places.name: Thái Dược Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs on a forested slope, its yards full of baskets of roots and bundles of drying leaves.
places.lore: Its people climb the high ground for roots and sell them to Hồng Lô Cốc and Thúy Vi's terraces. Every gatherer carries a bell so the others can find them in the haze.

provinces.name: Thuyền Ổ
provinces.lore: Old pine forest on a low western coast, where boats are built from its own timber. Most cape fishing boats were laid down here. On the shore stand the burnt halls of a small sect destroyed by Thôn Hải's pirates.

places.name: Lão Tùng Lâm
places.look: Tall old pines with red bark grow on low hills behind the shipyards, the ground soft with needles.
places.lore: The boatwrights choose keel trees here years before they cut them and bind a red cord around each one. No one else may cut a corded tree.

places.name: Lam Triều Các
places.look: On a rocky point the burnt shell of a stone pavilion faces the sea, its upper floors gone and its steps green with weed.
places.lore: A small sect of water cultivators sworn to Thúy Vi studied the tides from this point. In 744 Thôn Hải's pirates landed at night, burned the pavilion and carried off its disciples; the boatwrights still light a fire on the point on that night.

places.name: Thuyền Ổ Thôn
places.look: Half-built hulls stand on wooden slips along a low shore, with pine logs stacked behind a village of grey roofs.
places.lore: Most fishing boats on the cape were laid down here, from pines of the forest behind. A boat is launched only at high tide on a still day, and the whole village pushes.

provinces.name: Tùng Nhung
provinces.lore: Rolling inland pine hills, the highest and driest forest of the cape's interior. Its villagers gather pine mushrooms in autumn and dry them for the markets of Yên Ba. Silver martens live in the high woods, and their pelts are the hills' other wealth.

places.name: Ngân Điêu Đài
places.look: A flat rocky terrace above the pines is riddled with dens, and silver-furred martens watch from the stones.
places.lore: Silver martens with spirit-bright fur den on the terrace, quick enough to steal from a cultivator's sleeve. Their pelts fetch a high price in Yên Ba.

places.name: Tùng Nhung Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs in high pine woods, with mushrooms drying on flat baskets on every roof.
places.lore: Each family knows its own mushroom grounds and tells no one, not even its neighbours. The dried mushrooms go to Yên Ba in autumn.

provinces.name: Tất Thụ
provinces.lore: Inland forest with a few marshy hollows, where lacquer trees grow wild among the oaks. Its villagers tap the sap and sell raw lacquer to the craftsmen of Yên Ba. A belt of the forest is so often lost in Thúy Vi's haze that travellers go around it.

places.name: Mê Vụ Lâm
places.look: A low forest of hollows where the blue-green haze lies so thick that the trees fade a few steps away.
places.lore: Travellers go around it, for paths there turn back on themselves. Thúy Vi's disciples are sent in to walk out without a guide, as a lesser Haze Walk.

places.name: Tất Thụ Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs among oaks and lacquer trees, the lacquer trunks scored with neat rows of cuts and cups.
places.lore: The villagers tap raw lacquer and sell it to the craftsmen of Yên Ba. Newcomers break out in rashes for a year, and the villagers say that is the trees deciding.

provinces.name: Vĩnh Đông Hoang
provinces.lore: Frozen coastal tundra whose ground never thaws more than a hand deep. No one lives here. A spirit vein of black ice lies under the snow, and Thúy Vi's alchemists come for its cold water.

places.name: Huyền Băng Nhãn
places.look: A round pool of black ice lies in the white tundra, so clear that one can see deep into the dark below.
places.lore: Water qi rises through the ice, and alchemists cut blocks from it to cool their furnaces. The pool refreezes overnight however much is taken.

provinces.name: Man Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest and marsh where a river reaches the sea on the cape's eastern shore. Eel fishers live at the river mouth and smoke their catch for Yên Ba. Water vipers fill the marsh, and no one wades in it barefoot.

places.name: Thủy Hủy Chử
places.look: Low muddy islets in the marsh are covered with shed snake skins and coiled shapes in the reeds.
places.lore: Water vipers swarm here, and the largest are said to have spirit venom. Hồng Lô Cốc pays for their venom glands.

places.name: Man Ngư Thôn
places.look: Wicker eel traps hang drying on poles at a river mouth, beside smokehouses and a village of grey roofs.
places.lore: The villagers trap eels in the river mouth and smoke them for Yên Ba. Smoked eel from here is a winter gift along the whole cape.

provinces.name: Thạch Công
provinces.lore: Forested hills climbing into bare mountain in the east of the cape. Stonecutters quarry the grey rock for the walls and quays of Yên Ba. Higher up lies an empty copper town, abandoned when its seams gave out.

places.name: Thúy Cái Lâm
places.look: On the hill slopes broad crowns of oak and lime meet overhead in an unbroken green roof.
places.lore: Under its canopy the haze gathers green, and Thúy Vi's herb-gatherers find shade herbs here. The stonecutters do not quarry above it.

places.name: Đồng Sơn Trấn
places.look: On a wooded mountain shoulder empty stone houses stand around green-stained spoil heaps and the black mouths of old adits.
places.lore: Miners built the town on a copper seam and cast bells and pots for the cape. When the seam gave out in 1094 the town emptied within a few years.

places.name: Thạch Công Thôn
places.look: A village of grey stone houses sits below a quarried hillside, blocks stacked by the road for the carts.
places.lore: Its stonecutters quarry grey rock for the walls and quays of Yên Ba. Every house is built from stones its owner rejected.

provinces.name: Hải Thúy
provinces.lore: Forest along the western coast where the sea runs green over shallow sand. The town of Hải Thúy Trấn trades fish and timber with Mục Ca and the white sands. Its woods are thick with oak and maple that shed every autumn.

places.name: Mãn Diệp Lâm
places.look: A low oak and maple forest stands behind the town, knee-deep in fallen leaves each autumn.
places.lore: The townsfolk rake its leaves for compost and bedding. Children say whoever walks through it in autumn without a sound will have a year of luck.

places.name: Hải Thúy Trấn
places.look: A small walled town of grey roofs stands above a bay where the sea runs pale green over sand.
places.lore: It trades fish, timber and hemp rope with Mục Ca and Bạch Sa. Its people say the green of the water is Thúy Vi's haze sunk into the sea.

provinces.name: Thằng Tác
provinces.lore: Inland forest broken by clearings of hemp. Its villagers make rope and sailcloth for the boatwrights and sailors of the coast. In the deep woods the trees are so still that birds seem quiet there.

places.name: Tĩnh Mộc Lâm
places.look: A dense inland forest where the air is so still that leaves do not stir even on windy days.
places.lore: Birds are quiet here, and the hemp farmers avoid it. Thúy Vi sends restless disciples to sit in it, as it sends others to Vân Khởi Quán.

places.name: Thằng Tác Thôn
places.look: Tall hemp stands in clearings around a small village, retting pools and rope walks between the houses.
places.lore: The villagers make rope and sailcloth for the boatwrights of Thuyền Ổ and the sailors of Phong Phàm. A cape sailor will tell you whose rope he trusts.

provinces.name: Phù Kiều
provinces.lore: River forest in the middle of the cape, crossed by its main road at a bridge of boats. Phù Kiều Trấn lives by the road and the river trade. In the woods east of the town stands Vụ Ẩn Môn, a gate sworn to Thúy Vi that guards the cape's roads in mist.

places.name: Hắc Tùng Lâm
places.look: Dark black pines crowd the flat ground east of the river, their trunks streaked with resin.
places.lore: Travellers on the cape road hurry through it, for robbers once hid there. Since Vụ Ẩn Môn was founded nearby, the road has been safe.

places.name: Vụ Ẩn Môn
places.look: Low grey halls stand in the forest east of the river, nearly invisible inside a ring of standing stones that breathes out a thin green mist.
places.lore: A neutral gate of formation masters sworn to Thúy Vi, who lay mist arrays along the cape's roads to hide travellers and confuse robbers. Its founder learned the Haze Walk at Thúy Vi and left to make the haze useful.

places.name: Phù Kiều Trấn
places.look: A walled river town of grey roofs, its two halves joined by a bridge of boats chained across the stream.
places.lore: The cape's main road crosses the river here, and the town lives on tolls, inns and river trade. The bridge is taken apart before every spring flood and rebuilt after.

provinces.name: Mẫu Lệ
provinces.lore: Low forest on a western coast of mudflats and oyster beds. Its villagers rake oysters and burn the shells for lime. Sea eagles nest on the cliffs above the beds and take fish from the rakers' baskets.

places.name: Hải Điêu Nhai
places.look: A wooded cliff above the oyster beds is crowned with huge stick nests and splashed white below them.
places.lore: Sea eagles with wings longer than a boat nest here and snatch fish from the rakers' baskets. One took a child in 1170, and the village has hated them since.

places.name: Mẫu Lệ Thôn
places.look: A low village of grey roofs stands on the mudflats, with white heaps of oyster shells and lime kilns along the shore.
places.lore: The villagers rake oysters at low tide and burn the shells for lime. Lime from here whitewashes the walls of Bạch Sa.

provinces.name: Hàm Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest on a western coast where fish is salted and dried for the whole cape. Its village lives by the catch and the salt pans. Inland lie the empty halls of a healers' sect that ended without an heir.

places.name: Tùng La Lâm
places.look: Grey-green lichen hangs in long beards from every branch of a damp coastal pine forest.
places.lore: Healers gather the lichen for wounds and coughs. The healers of the ruined hall nearby first taught the villagers its use.

places.name: Thanh Nang Đường
places.look: A walled compound of low halls stands empty in the woods, its herb beds gone wild and its medicine cabinets standing open.
places.lore: A small sect of healers sworn to Thúy Vi tended the cape's sick here for three centuries. Its last head died in closed-door cultivation in 1101 without naming an heir, and its disciples went to Hồng Lô Cốc.

places.name: Hàm Ngư Thôn
places.look: Rows of split fish dry on racks along a shore of salt pans, beside a village of grey roofs.
places.lore: Fish is salted and dried here for the whole cape, and the smell carries a long way out to sea. Sailors say they can find the village in fog by nose.

provinces.name: Lô Từ
provinces.lore: Forest with a few high ridges along a coast of rocky inlets. Its fishers fish with tame cormorants. Iron boars root in the lowland woods, and the village fences its fields with stone.

places.name: Thiết Trư Lâm
places.look: Churned earth and tusk-gashed trunks fill a lowland wood, with wallows of black mud between the roots.
places.lore: Iron boars with hide like plate root here and charge anything that comes near. The villagers fence their fields with stone because wood does not stop them.

places.name: Lô Từ Thôn
places.look: Bamboo rafts with tethered cormorants line a rocky inlet below a village of grey roofs.
places.lore: Its fishers fish with tame cormorants, a ring on each bird's neck. Every bird has a name, and old birds are buried in the village graveyard.

provinces.name: Lăng Giác
provinces.lore: Forest and marsh down to the sea west of Yên Ba. Its villagers grow water chestnuts in the marsh ponds and sell them in the city. Old vines hang so thick in its woods that they make walls between the trees.

places.name: Cổ Đằng Lâm
places.look: Thick old vines hang from tree to tree in a low forest, making green walls and dark rooms.
places.lore: The vines are cut for baskets and rope, but grow back faster than anyone can cut them. Hunters say a man lost in it can be found a year later, sitting quietly, not knowing the time.

places.name: Lăng Giác Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs stands among square marsh ponds covered in water-chestnut leaves, small tub boats floating between them.
places.lore: Villagers kneel in round tubs to pick the chestnuts and sell them in Yên Ba. A boiled bag of them is the cape's autumn street food.

provinces.name: Trà Viên
provinces.lore: Forested hills rising to bare heights north of Yên Ba, inland and misty. Its villagers grow tea on terraced clearings, and the haze is said to give the leaves their green. Thúy Vi buys the best of the picking for its seat.

places.name: Ngưng Lục Lâm
places.look: A forest of evergreen oaks on high ground, where moss covers every trunk and stone in deep green.
places.lore: Wood qi gathers here thickly enough to be felt, and Thúy Vi disciples come to meditate under the trees. The tea farmers take their seedlings from its edges.

places.name: Trà Viên Thôn
places.look: Neat rows of tea bushes climb the cleared hillsides around a village of grey roofs, half in the haze.
places.lore: The villagers say the haze gives their leaves their green. Thúy Vi buys the first picking for its seat and leaves the rest for Yên Ba.

provinces.name: Lạc Tuyết Nguyên
provinces.lore: Tundra and scattered forest on the north-west shore, where snow falls on more days than not. No one lives here now. On the coast stand the snowed-in halls of a sword sect older than Thúy Vi's claim on the cape.

places.name: Sương Kiếm Môn
places.look: On the cold shore the stone walls of a small sect stand half-buried in drifted snow, a row of rusted sword racks along the yard.
places.lore: A small sect of sword cultivators trained here in the cold before any great sect held the cape. The winter of 468 buried its halls to the roofs, and the disciples who lived went south and did not return.

places.name: Hàn Lộ Tuyền
places.look: A small spring rises among frozen tussocks, never freezing, with frost feathers thick on every stem around it.
places.lore: Water qi rises with the spring, and alchemists carry its water south for pills that cool the blood. In the coldest winter its steam can be seen a day's walk away.

provinces.name: Hỏa Tích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A short spine of high mountains and volcanic cones on the south coast, snow above and warm rock below. No one lives here, but Thúy Vi's alchemists climb to Tuyết Để Tuyền for its water. Miners cut black glass from the cones.

places.name: Tuyết Để Tuyền
places.look: A smooth snowfield lies high on the cape's mountains, white except for one blue ice cave at its foot. Steam pours from the cave mouth day and night, and the meltwater runs out warm and faintly green over the stones.

places.name: Hắc Diệu Khoáng
places.look: Black glassy rock glints from the flank of a volcanic cone, broken into sharp terraces where miners pry out blocks.
places.lore: Miners cut obsidian for blades, mirrors and furnace windows. Hồng Lô Cốc buys the clearest pieces to watch its fires without opening the furnace.

provinces.name: Nhũ Lạc
provinces.lore: Forest on a narrow coast below the fire spine, rising steeply to bare rock. Its villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below. Giant scorpions live in the warm cliffs, and the goats know to stay off them.

places.name: Cự Yết Nhai
places.look: A warm rocky cliff below the fire spine is pocked with crevices, and pale husks of shed shells lie at its foot.
places.lore: Giant scorpions shelter in the warm rock, kept alive in the cold by the heat underground. The goats will not climb it, and the herders trust the goats.

places.name: Nhũ Lạc Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs clings to a narrow coast below steep slopes, goats picking along the rocks above it.
places.lore: The villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below. Goat cheese from here is rubbed with volcanic salt and keeps all winter.

provinces.name: Viêm Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains and an active cone on the south coast, with forest only at their feet. No one lives here. Lava still flows from a vent near the summit, and Hồng Lô's alchemists come to it for fire they need not carry from the isles.

places.name: Lưu Hỏa Khẩu
places.look: High on a volcanic cone a crack glows orange, and a slow tongue of lava creeps from it down the black slope.
places.lore: Fire qi pours from the vent, and Hồng Lô Cốc's alchemists come to light furnaces from it without sailing to the isles. They carry the fire home in clay pots packed with ash.

provinces.name: Lật Thụ
provinces.lore: A small forested coast at the south end of the cape. Its villagers gather chestnuts and fish. Seals haul out on the rocks below the village.

places.name: Hải Báo Chử
places.look: Grey seals crowd the flat rocks of a shoal below wooded cliffs, barking at passing boats.
places.lore: A colony of seals hauls out here every winter, among them a few great spirit seals. Fishers leave them alone, for the big bulls have sunk boats.

places.name: Lật Thụ Thôn
places.look: Old chestnut trees shade a small village of grey roofs on the southern shore.
places.lore: The villagers gather chestnuts in autumn and fish the rest of the year. Their roasted chestnuts are sold in the streets of Yên Ba at the first frost.

provinces.name: Tận Giác
provinces.lore: The far western tip of the cape: grass, woods and one high hill over the sea. Tận Giác Trấn trades wool, fish and the passage around the point. On the shore are the sanded ruins of the older town the sea took.

places.name: Hải Lăng Trấn
places.look: On the shore stand the tops of old walls half-buried in sand, a stone quay running out into nothing.
places.lore: The old port of the cape's end stood on a mound by the sea. A great storm in 1152 broke its harbour and filled it with sand, and its people moved up the coast to Tận Giác.

places.name: Sơn Lam Huyệt
places.look: In a wooded hollow on the hill above the town, a green haze wells up from the ground and spills over the rim.
places.lore: Wood qi rises with the haze, and Thúy Vi disciples stationed at the cape's end cultivate here. The townsfolk read the weather in how far the haze spills.

places.name: Tận Giác Trấn
places.look: A walled town of grey roofs stands on grass at the far western tip, a stone beacon tower on the point beside it.
places.lore: Ships rounding the cape stop here for water and pilots, and the town trades wool and fish. Its beacon is lit on stormy nights at the town's cost.

provinces.name: Dương Quyển
