provinces.lore: A small strip of dry steppe on the western coast. Its people keep sheep in stone folds and sell wool to Tận Giác. It is the driest land on the cape, and its water comes from wells.

places.name: Dương Quyển Thôn
places.look: Round stone sheepfolds and well-heads dot a dry coastal steppe around a few low houses.
places.lore: The villagers keep hardy sheep and sell their wool in Tận Giác. Every family digs its own well and guards it.

provinces.name: Vân Tước
provinces.lore: Grass and a little steppe along the south-western coast. Its village keeps flocks and bees and watches skylarks rise over the grass. A spirit vein of earth qi lies in the grass near the shore.

places.name: Hoàng Thổ Nhãn
places.look: A round patch of bare yellow earth lies in the green grass near the shore, warm to the touch even in winter.
places.lore: Earth qi rises here, and nothing but a fine yellow moss grows on it. Thúy Vi disciples of the earth arts sit here barefoot.

places.name: Vân Tước Thôn
places.look: A small village of grey roofs sits in open grass by the sea, with beehives along its walls and skylarks singing overhead.
places.lore: The villagers keep flocks and bees. They say a year without skylarks is a year without rain, and remember three.

provinces.name: Tàn Tuyết Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra with fringes of forest along the north coast, where the snow lingers into summer. No one lives here; fire foxes den on its plain of Hỏa Hồ Nguyên. Brave hunters come for their pelts.

places.name: Hỏa Hồ Nguyên
places.look: A flat white tundra under a low sky, broken by scattered round patches of bare, thawed brown earth. Each patch marks a fire fox den, its snow melted away by the beast's heat, and trails of melted prints run between them.

provinces.name: Thương Đài Nguyên
provinces.lore: Tundra of grey moss and frozen pools on the north coast. No one lives here. Snow owls hunt over it, and on the coast lie the whale-bone halls of a sect of sea hunters.

places.name: Tuyết Hiêu Đài
places.look: A low flat rise in the tundra is scattered with white feathers and owl pellets, and pale shapes sit motionless on its stones.
places.lore: Snow owls large enough to take a fox roost here. Hunters say they see a cultivator's qi as easily as a hare's heat.

places.name: Kình Cốt Đường
places.look: On the cold shore stands a long hall framed in whale ribs, its hide roof long gone and snow drifted inside.
places.lore: A small sect of sea hunters sworn to Thúy Vi hunted sea beasts from this shore. In 884 its head went out after a great spirit whale and never came back, and the remaining disciples joined Hồng Lô Cốc.

provinces.name: Hàn Thạch Nguyên
provinces.lore: Stony tundra rising to bare rock in the north-east of the cape. No one lives here. White bears come ashore from the ice in winter and den on its ridges.

places.name: Bạch Hùng Cương
places.look: A low stony ridge in the tundra is dug with snow dens and scattered with seal bones.
places.lore: White bears come ashore from the sea ice in winter to den here. Sealers count the dens each spring and keep their camps far away.

provinces.name: Sương Trạch
provinces.lore: Tundra, thin forest and frozen marsh behind the north coast. No one lives here. Ptarmigan flocks winter on it, and their wings sound like thunder when they rise.

places.name: Lôi Điểu Nguyên
places.look: A white plain of frozen marsh where flocks of white ptarmigan burst up at a step.
places.lore: The flocks winter here in thousands, and their wings crack like thunder when they rise. Hunters net them, and some say a few birds carry thunder qi.

provinces.name: Trùng Sương Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains above the coast north of Hồng Lô Cốc, frosted most of the year. No one lives here. A peak of grey iron-bearing rock stands at its heart.

places.name: Thiết Cốt Phong
places.look: A bare dark peak streaked with rust-red stone rises above the frosted ridges.
places.lore: Metal qi gathers in its iron-bearing rock, and sword cultivators climb it to temper their blades. Lightning strikes it more often than any other peak on the cape.

provinces.name: Liệp Hải
provinces.lore: Forest and tundra on the north-west coast, the largest settled land in the cape's north. Its people hunt seals and fish, as sealers have on this coast since the Wild Age. Great elk move through its woods in autumn.

places.name: Cự Mi Lâm
places.look: An open forest of birch and pine is crossed by broad trails, the bark stripped high where great elk feed.
places.lore: Great elk with antlers as wide as a cart gather here in autumn to fight for mates. The sea hunters leave the woods alone in that season.

places.name: Liệp Hải Thôn
places.look: Grey-roofed houses stand on the cold shore, skin boats upturned on racks and seal hides stretched along the walls.
places.lore: The villagers hunt seals and fish, as sealers have on this coast since the Wild Age. They say their forebears were the ones who named the cape of snow and fire.

provinces.name: Bạch Mang Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat frozen tundra on the far northern sea, white in every direction. No one lives here. A deep cold spirit vein lies under the ice, and Thúy Vi's alchemists come for its water.

places.name: Hàn Uyên Nhãn
places.look: A dark round hole in the tundra ice opens onto deep water that never freezes, breathing a thin mist.
places.lore: Water qi wells up from far below, cold enough to numb a hand in a moment. Alchemists lower jars on long cords to fill them.

provinces.name: Phiệt Công
provinces.lore: River forest in the north-east, where logs are tied into rafts and floated downstream. Raftsmen and loggers live along the river. Beavers dam the side streams and the raftsmen break the dams each spring.

places.name: Hà Ly Chử
places.look: Stick dams and lodges choke a side stream into a chain of still ponds among gnawed stumps.
places.lore: Spirit beavers build dams strong enough to hold a flood. The raftsmen break them every spring and the beavers rebuild them every summer.

places.name: Phiệt Công Thôn
places.look: Log rafts lie lashed along a forest river below a village of grey roofs, with stacked timber on the bank.
places.lore: The raftsmen float logs downstream to the coast. A raftsman's rank is counted by how many springs he has ridden the flood.

provinces.name: Tân Cư
provinces.lore: River forest inland of the Cold Ford, settled by fishers who left the coast under Tùng Đào's resin tax. Its people farm, fish the river and remember the tax with jokes. Deep in its woods lies a forest so quiet that it seems Không Sơn's.

places.name: Vô Thanh Lâm
places.look: A forest of moss-hung trees where no bird sings and footsteps make no sound on the deep moss.
places.lore: Villagers say the quiet of Không Sơn Viện drifted north and settled here. Vân Khởi Quán sometimes sends novices to sit in it for a day.

places.name: Tân Cư Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs stands on a river bend in the forest, each door with a jar of pine resin by it.
places.lore: Fishers of the Cold Ford who left the coast under Tùng Đào's resin tax founded it in 675. It is still called the new homes, and the resin jars are a joke about the tax.

provinces.name: Hồ Đào
provinces.lore: Inland forest of walnut and oak in the north of the ridges. Its villagers gather walnuts and press walnut oil for lamps and ink. In early summer white butterflies fill the woods.

places.name: Phấn Điệp Lâm
places.look: In early summer clouds of white butterflies rise from an open oak forest, settling on every leaf.
places.lore: They come for a week and are gone, and the villagers say a soul rides on each one. No one sweeps the dead butterflies from the paths.

places.name: Hồ Đào Thôn
places.look: Tall walnut trees shade a village of grey roofs, with nut husks drying in black heaps in every yard.
places.lore: The villagers press walnut oil for lamps and sell husk dye to the scribes of Lam Yên. Each child is given a walnut tree at birth.

provinces.name: Thủy Ma
provinces.lore: River forest in the north-east, where mills grind grain for the north. Its villagers mill, farm and fish the river. In its woods stands Hộ Lâm Đường, whose wardens keep the northern forests for Thúy Vi.

places.name: Độc Phong Cốc
places.look: A wooded hollow is hung with grey paper nests as big as barrels, and the air hums.
places.lore: Spirit hornets nest here, and their sting can kill a mortal. The forest wardens of Hộ Lâm Đường take their nests for poison.

places.name: Hộ Lâm Đường
places.look: A hall of dark timber stands on a wooded rise, its roof grown over with moss and a tall lookout platform in the oak beside it.
places.lore: A righteous hall of forest wardens sworn to Thúy Vi, who guard the northern woods and gather herbs and spirit wood for its furnaces. It was founded after the Cold Ford came home, to keep the northern forests for the sect.

places.name: Thủy Ma Thôn
places.look: A row of waterwheels turns along a forest river beside a village of grey roofs, sacks of flour stacked on the banks.
places.lore: The mills grind grain for all the northern villages. Millers are paid in a tenth of what they grind, and the scoop is kept in the village shrine.

provinces.name: Tạo Chỉ
provinces.lore: River forest and marsh in the north-east, where bark and hemp are beaten into paper. The village's paper goes to Lam Yên Thị for copied scripture. Brown bears fish the river beside the papermakers' vats.

places.name: Tông Hùng Lâm
places.look: A riverside forest of marsh and alder is torn with claw marks, fish carcasses scattered along the banks.
places.lore: Brown bears fish the river in autumn beside the papermakers' vats. The village keeps a drum to frighten them off.

places.name: Tạo Chỉ Thôn
places.look: Sheets of paper dry on wooden frames along a river village, beside vats of soaking bark.
places.lore: The villagers beat mulberry bark and hemp into paper for the copied scripture of Lam Yên Thị. A sheet that tears in the vat is never sold.

provinces.name: Phục Linh
provinces.lore: Pine forest on the road north from Lam Yên, gently rising toward the mountains. Its villagers dig poria fungus from pine roots for Thúy Vi's furnaces. The old post town of Cổ Dịch Trấn, left behind when the road was moved, has been Thúy Vi Tông's seat since 1001-1006, its halls standing in deep forest and haze.

places.name: Thương Thúy Lâm
places.look: Old grey-green pines stand on rising ground, thick with lichen and hung with haze.
places.lore: Its oldest pines grow the best poria, and the villagers guard the roots jealously. Thúy Vi disciples walking the road north rest in its shade.

places.name: Thúy Vi Tông
places.look: Wooden halls with green-glazed roofs stand in deep forest with no wall around them, half drowned in a blue-green haze, and herb terraces climb the forest edge. Inn gardens grow too well along the old post town's overgrown streets.
places.lore: Thúy Vi Tông, the Sect of the Emerald Haze, is a righteous (chính đạo) great sect of alchemists, and has kept its halls in the old post town of Cổ Dịch Trấn since 1001-1006. The inns had closed one by one after the road was moved east in 975, and in 1000 Ngu Lam Sơn ended his hundred days in the haze at the empty inns and gave his first order as head: 'We go down.' The town sat on a root-vein nobody had noticed, the green haze the sect is named for pools thickest here, and Tất Hành Vụ laid the Spring Return array over the vein in 1006. Úy Thanh Diễm carried the Green Furnace down from the ridge still burning.

places.name: Phục Linh Thôn
places.look: A small village of grey roofs in pine forest, with baskets of white poria lumps drying under the eaves.
places.lore: The villagers dig poria fungus from old pine roots and sell it to Thúy Vi's furnaces. They plant a pine for each one they dig.

provinces.name: Bạch Lạp
provinces.lore: Inland forest of ash trees north of the seat. Its villagers raise wax insects on the ash and scrape white wax for candles and pill coatings. The forest is loud with birds at dawn.

places.name: Sơ Hiểu Lâm
places.look: A mixed forest of ash and oak echoes with birdsong from dawn until mid-morning.
places.lore: Bird-catchers come here for songbirds to sell in Lam Yên. Thúy Vi forbids nets in the spring nesting season.

places.name: Bạch Lạp Thôn
places.look: Ash trees around a village of grey roofs are crusted white with insect wax on their branches.
places.lore: The villagers raise wax insects and scrape white wax for candles and pill coatings. Thúy Vi buys most of it for its furnaces.

provinces.name: Bối Độ
provinces.lore: River forest in the east, where the river runs wide over stone shallows. Its villagers fish and ford travellers across. A wood vein rises in the forest above the shallows.

places.name: Thanh Mộc Mạch
places.look: A line of unusually tall trees runs straight through the forest, greener than the woods on either side.
places.lore: Wood qi runs along the line under the ground, and trees planted on it outgrow all others. Thúy Vi's disciples follow the line to cultivate.

places.name: Bối Độ Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs sits beside a wide river that runs thin and white over flat stones.
places.lore: Its people fish the shallows and carry travellers across on their backs. They know every stone of the ford by name.

provinces.name: Tử Tô
provinces.lore: River forest east of the seat, where perilla and other herbs grow in riverside plots. Its villagers grow herbs for the alchemists. In its woods lie the ruins of a herb academy destroyed by its own pill fire.

places.name: Bách Thảo Viện
places.look: The scorched shell of an academy stands among wild herb beds, its central furnace hall blown open from inside.
places.lore: A small herb academy sworn to Thúy Vi kept a hundred kinds of herbs in its beds. In 932 a cauldron of untamed pill fire burst and destroyed the halls; Thúy Vi took its herb books to the seat.

places.name: Linh Lộ Tuyền
places.look: A spring in the forest floor seeps into a mossy hollow where heavy dew lies on every leaf all day.
places.lore: Wood qi rises with the water, and herbs gathered there with the dew on them are prized. Alchemists come before dawn to collect the dew itself.

places.name: Tử Tô Thôn
places.look: Plots of purple perilla and other herbs line the river below a small village of grey roofs.
places.lore: The villagers grow herbs for the alchemists and learned their plots from the ruined academy nearby. Its purple leaves are dried for tea along the coast.

provinces.name: Tỏa Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and high mountain west of the seat, where cloud gathers in the valleys and stays. No one lives here but a few hermits. A pale stone pillar of a peak rises from the cloud.

places.name: Ngọc Trụ Phong
places.look: A tall pale pillar of stone rises out of the cloud that fills the valleys around it.
places.lore: Earth qi gathers in its pale rock. Hermits live in caves halfway up and come down only when the clouds lift.

provinces.name: Vô Thụ Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra on the northern coast with only a few stunted trees at its southern edge. No one lives here. Snow hares in their thousands feed the foxes and owls of the north.

places.name: Tuyết Thố Nguyên
places.look: A white tundra plain crossed by countless small tracks, hares bounding away at every step.
places.lore: Snow hares breed here in their thousands, and a few spirit hares are as quick as a sword cut. Foxes and owls hunt them from all over the north.

provinces.name: Cửu Điệp Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Folded high ridges and forest just east of Thúy Vi Tông's seat. No one lives here but miners and the sect's watchers. An empty fort above the north road dates from the years the Cold Ford was lost.

places.name: Bạch Tinh Khoáng
places.look: A narrow adit on a mountain slope spills white tailings glittering with crystal.
places.lore: Miners dig clear quartz for formation stones and pill vials. Vụ Ẩn Môn buys its best crystals for its mist arrays.

places.name: Tê Hạc Phong
places.look: A grey rocky peak east of the seat, its ledges dotted with roosting cranes.
places.lore: Metal qi gathers in the rock, and the cranes return to it each spring. Thúy Vi disciples climb it to practise sword forms among the birds.

places.name: Vọng Bắc Bảo
places.look: A small stone fort stands on a wooded spur above the north road, its walls intact and its gate gone.
places.lore: Thúy Vi built it the year Tùng Đào took the Cold Ford, to watch the road north. After the Cold Ford came home in 905 it was left empty.

provinces.name: Hoa Mạch
provinces.lore: A wide forest east of the seat, running to the coast, with clearings of buckwheat. Its villagers farm the clearings and sell flour to Lam Yên. A great tree at the forest's heart holds a wood vein.

places.name: Thụ Tâm Nhãn
places.look: A vast old tree stands alone in a clearing, a hollow at its heart glowing faintly green at night.
places.lore: Wood qi rises through the tree's hollow heart. Villagers leave buckwheat cakes at its roots, and Thúy Vi disciples sit inside the hollow.

places.name: Hoa Mạch Thôn
places.look: Clearings of white-flowering buckwheat surround a village of grey roofs deep in the forest.
places.lore: Buckwheat grows where rice will not, and its flour goes to Lam Yên for noodles. The villagers bless the fields when the flowers open.

provinces.name: Lãm Thúy
provinces.lore: Coastal forest on the eastern shore of the ridges. Lãm Thúy Trấn trades timber, fish and herbs along the coast. Inland stand the burnt halls of a sect whose head died in his tribulation.

places.name: Thâm U Lâm
places.look: A dense coastal forest so dark under its canopy that moss grows on the paths.
places.lore: Herb gatherers from the town find shade herbs here that grow nowhere else. They tie cords to the trees to find their way back.

places.name: Minh Kính Đường
places.look: A burnt hall stands in a ring of lightning-split trees, a cracked bronze mirror still hanging over its door.
places.lore: A small sect of heart-mirror cultivators sworn to Thúy Vi. In 1066 its head tried to break through to Nguyên Anh, and his tribulation burned the hall and killed him; the disciples scattered.

places.name: Lãm Thúy Trấn
places.look: A walled town of grey roofs on the eastern shore, its quay stacked with timber and bales of herbs.
places.lore: It trades timber, fish and herbs from the eastern forests along the coast. Its herb buyers are said to grade a root by smell alone.

provinces.name: Trầm Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountain and forest in the west of the ridges, where clouds sink into the valleys at dusk. No one lives here now. High on a shoulder lie the buried streets of a mountain town lost to an avalanche.

places.name: Nhạn Hồi Phong
places.gloss: Peak Where the Geese Turn Back
places.look: A sharp grey peak stands so high that migrating geese turn aside around it.
places.lore: Metal qi gathers in its bare rock. Its south face is said to be too cold even for the geese.

places.name: Vân Gian Trấn
places.look: High on a mountain shoulder the roofs of a small stone town poke out of a slope of old rubble and grass.
places.lore: A mountain town of herb growers and porters on the path to the western ridges. An avalanche in 1019 buried its upper street, and the survivors went down to Lam Yên Thị.

provinces.name: Bích Chướng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Steep high mountains clad in forest on their lower slopes, west of the seat. No one lives here but miners. Blue-green jade is dug below a cliff that cuts the clouds.

places.name: Thương Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A cut in the mountain below the cliff shows bands of blue-green stone, with a ramp down to the road.
places.lore: Thúy Vi opened it long after Bích Ngọc Khoáng, to dig a bluer, harder jade. Its stone is carved into talismans and furnace lids.

places.name: Đoạn Vân Nhai
places.look: A sheer grey cliff rises above the forest, and drifting clouds part around its edge.
places.lore: Metal qi gathers in its sharp rock. Sword cultivators say the cliff cut the clouds before they learned to.

provinces.name: Tuyệt Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest bare walls of rock south of the seat, with only a little forest in the clefts. No one lives here. Miners dig cold iron from its flanks for Thúy Vi's furnace fittings.

places.name: Lãnh Thiết Khoáng
places.look: A dark mine mouth on a sheer slope, with frost on the iron ore heaped outside even in summer.
places.lore: Its iron stays cold to the touch long after forging. Thúy Vi uses it for furnace fittings that must not grow hot.

places.name: Lăng Không Đỉnh
places.look: A bare summit of grey rock juts out over a drop so deep that its foot is lost in haze.
places.lore: Metal qi gathers in its rock. Thúy Vi elders stand on the edge to test their nerve before breakthrough.

provinces.name: Lưu Thúy Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forest and mountain cut by a river running south, its slopes green with moss and fern. A few miners cut inkstone here for the scholars of Lam Yên. A peak holds the cloud on its shoulder most mornings.

places.name: Nghiên Thạch Khoáng
places.look: Small pits along a river bank show fine dark stone, with half-cut inkstones drying on the rocks.
places.lore: Its fine black stone makes inkstones for the scholars of Lam Yên. Miners test each block by grinding ink on it before they sell.

places.name: Hàm Vân Phong
places.look: A rounded forested peak with a band of cloud resting on its shoulder most mornings.
places.lore: Earth qi gathers in its stone, and the cloud seldom leaves. The monks of Vân Khởi say it holds what their own mountain lets go.

provinces.name: Ngọa Ngưu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A short ridge of mountain and forest by a river, shaped like an ox lying down. No one lives here. Herdsmen from below say the ridge breathes on cold mornings.

places.name: Ngưu Bối Phong
places.look: A long rounded peak by the river, shaped like the back of a lying ox.
places.lore: Earth qi gathers along its spine. Herdsmen below say a cultivator who sleeps on it wakes heavier and calmer.

provinces.name: Vô Nhân Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridges Where No One Is Seen
provinces.lore: High mountain above the south coast where Không Sơn Viện stands empty and unlooted. No one lives here, and Thúy Vi keeps it so. A soapstone pit at the foot of the ridge is the only work done in the land.

places.name: Không Sơn Viện
places.look: High on a ridge above the haze a cluster of old halls stands silent, their doors open, the roof of the great lecture hall sagging and its small pagoda missing its top tier. Beside the path a raw landslide scar runs down the slope, and in it a stone gate carved with lines of poetry stands half-buried, its opening blocked with newer stone.

places.name: Nhuyễn Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A small pit at the foot of the ridge by the shore shows soft pale grey stone, with carved bowls drying on a rack.
places.lore: Villagers dig soapstone here for bowls, moulds and pill moulds. They dig only at the foot, far below the academy.

places.name: Độc Tọa Phong
places.look: A narrow rocky peak above Không Sơn Viện, with a single flat stone at its top big enough for one person.
places.lore: Earth qi gathers in its stone, and Không Sơn's masters sat on it alone. Thúy Vi lets no one climb it, and the stone is still clean.

provinces.name: Thiên Thúy Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest mountains of the ridges, south-east of the seat, falling to the coast through forest. No one lives here. From its sunrise peak one can see both the cape and the eastern sea.

places.name: Quan Nhật Phong
places.look: The highest bare peak of the ridges, its summit catching the first light long before the valleys.
places.lore: Metal qi gathers in its rock. From its top one can see the cape and the eastern sea at once.

provinces.name: Lẫm Phong Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra and bare high rock on the north coast, swept by wind off the ice. No one lives here. Ice rhinoceroses cross it on the plain of Băng Tê Nguyên.

places.name: Băng Tê Nguyên
places.look: A frozen tundra plateau is crossed by deep trenches worn in the snow by heavy beasts. Great grey boulders stand scattered over it, scored with long gouges and polished smooth where ice rhinoceroses rub their horns.

provinces.name: Tùng Yên
provinces.lore: Forested mountains west of Vân Khởi, inland and steep. Its villagers burn pine for soot and press it into ink for the scholars of three sects. A peak of pines above the village gives the wood.

places.name: Vạn Tùng Phong
places.look: A high peak covered to its top in pines, dark green against the bare mountains around it.
places.lore: Wood qi gathers in its pines. The soot burners of Tùng Yên cut only the dead trees on it.

places.name: Tùng Yên Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs on a forested slope, with long brick soot kilns climbing the hill behind it.
places.lore: The villagers burn pine in long kilns and press the soot into ink. Their ink goes with the inkstones of Lưu Thúy to the scholars of three sects.

provinces.name: Hải Đường
provinces.lore: Coastal forest south of the seat with orchards of crabapple. Its villagers fish and sell blossom and fruit in Lam Yên. Giant centipedes live in a damp valley above the orchards.

places.name: Ngô Công Cốc
places.look: A damp wooded valley above the orchards, with rotting logs crawling with red centipedes.
places.lore: Giant centipedes live in its rot, and the biggest are as long as a man. Hồng Lô Cốc pays for their venom.

places.name: Hải Đường Thôn
places.look: Pink crabapple orchards surround a village of grey roofs on the coast.
places.lore: The villagers fish and sell crabapple blossom and fruit in Lam Yên. The blossom is pressed into the pages of scripture beside Thu Diệp's leaves.

provinces.name: Đồng Du
provinces.lore: Inland forest of the far south-east, rising to wooded hills. Its villagers press tung oil for boats, paint and lamps. Grey wolves run on the hill ridge above.

places.name: Thanh Lang Lĩnh
places.look: A wooded hill ridge where packs of grey wolves have worn paths along the crest.
places.lore: Grey wolves hunt the ridge in packs, and the oldest are said to be clever as men. Villagers do not walk it after dark.

places.name: Đồng Du Thôn
places.look: Tung trees with white blossoms ring a village of grey roofs, and oil presses stand in every yard.
places.lore: The villagers press tung oil for boats, paint and lamps. Every boat on the coast is sealed with it.

provinces.name: Thiêu Hôi
provinces.lore: Forest and limestone karst in the south-east. Its villagers burn limestone for lime and sell it to builders along the coast. A gorge so narrow that only a thread of sky shows cuts the karst.

places.name: Tuyến Thiên Hạp
places.gloss: Gorge of the Thread of Sky
places.look: A limestone gorge so narrow and deep that only a thin line of sky shows overhead.
places.lore: The lime-burners take a short cut through it to the coast. In the noon light alone the gorge floor is lit, and then only for a moment.

places.name: Thiêu Hôi Thôn
places.look: White lime kilns smoke among limestone knolls beside a small village of white-dusted grey roofs.
places.lore: The villagers burn limestone for lime and sell it to builders along the coast. Their houses are the whitest in the ridges.

provinces.name: Sương Tùng Nguyên
provinces.lore: Tundra and pine forest on the northern coast. No one lives here. On its shore stand the ruins of a sect that went out on the ice after a mirage.

places.name: Thận Lâu Các
places.look: On the frozen shore the stone base of a tall pavilion stands empty, its upper floors fallen onto the beach.
places.lore: A small sect that studied the mirages of the northern sea built its pavilion here. In 497 its head walked out on the sea ice after a mirage of a city and never returned, and the disciples left.

places.name: Lăng Hàn Huyệt
places.look: In the frozen tundra a small hollow of open water steams among frosted pines.
places.lore: Water qi wells up and keeps the hollow ice-free all winter. Thúy Vi disciples of the water arts sit beside it through the coldest month.

provinces.name: Hắc Thủy Trạch
provinces.lore: Forest, tundra and black peat marsh in the north. No one lives here. Frost toads sing in the marsh pools all summer.

places.name: Hàn Thiềm Chử
places.look: Black peat pools are ringed with frosted moss, and pale toads sit motionless at the water's edge.
places.lore: Frost toads sing here all summer and sleep frozen in the mud all winter. Their skin is a cooling medicine.

provinces.name: Nghịch Triều
provinces.lore: Forest, tundra and marsh where a river reaches the north coast. Its villagers fish the river and the backwaters. On the coast stand the snowed-in walls of a temple of snow-sitters.

places.name: Dã Ngưu Chử
places.look: A trampled marsh island in the forest, its mud churned by heavy hooves.
places.lore: Herds of wild forest bison graze here in summer. The villagers hunt one each autumn and no more.

places.name: Tĩnh Tuyết Tự
places.look: Low stone halls stand half-buried in snow on the cold shore, a row of flat meditation stones before them.
places.lore: Monks sat in the snow here and cultivated stillness. The last monk died in 455 with no novices, and the temple was left to the snow.

places.name: Nghịch Triều Thôn
places.look: A village of grey roofs stands on a river where the tide turns the current back upstream twice a day.
places.lore: The villagers fish the river and its backwaters and time their boats by the returning current. Children learn the tides before they learn to count.

provinces.name: Đông Hà Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra and thin forest where a river freezes solid down to the sea. No one lives here. Snow roe deer winter along the frozen banks.

places.name: Tuyết Bào Nguyên
places.look: A tundra plain along a frozen river, crossed by the light tracks of roe deer.
places.lore: Snow roe deer winter along the frozen banks. Hunters say they can run on thin ice without breaking it.

provinces.name: Cô Tùng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Tundra, forest and a few high crags on the north-west coast. No one lives here. A pine-spirit vein lies in its forest, and an old abbey ruin stands on the crag.

places.name: Bão Nhất Quán
places.look: On a high crag a few roofless stone halls stand around a dry spring, prayer stones scattered on the ground.
places.lore: A small Daoist abbey older than Không Sơn Viện kept its hermits here. Its spring dried, and the last abbot went down to Không Sơn Viện as a guest in 488.

places.name: Tùng Linh Mạch
places.look: A grove of very old pines stands among the tundra, its needles greener than any other trees on the coast.
places.lore: Wood qi rises under the grove. Hunters say the oldest pine has a spirit, and they leave a little food at its roots.

provinces.name: Việt Quất
provinces.lore: Northern forest with a little tundra at its edges. Its villagers pick lingonberries and trap fur. Its old town stands empty since the river moved.

places.name: Phi Thử Lâm
places.look: A tall forest where flying squirrels glide from trunk to trunk at dusk.
places.lore: Spirit flying squirrels nest here, and their skins make light gloves. They steal berries from the villagers' roofs.

places.name: Hoành Kiều Trấn
places.look: A stone bridge spans a dry hollow in the forest beside the empty walls of a small town.
places.lore: The town grew around a bridge on the river. A flood in 1148 moved the river west and left the bridge over dry ground, and the town followed the water.

places.name: Việt Quất Thôn
places.look: A small village of grey roofs in northern forest, with red berries spread on mats on every roof.
places.lore: The villagers pick lingonberries and trap fur. Berry jam from here keeps all winter and travels to Hàn Tân.

provinces.name: Hàn Than Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra, bog and thin forest on the northern coast, with cold shoals offshore. No one lives here now. The fallen pavilion of Vọng Triều Các stands on the shore, and a spring of water qi rises in the woods behind.

places.name: Vọng Triều Các
places.look: On a bare shore, the stone base of a pavilion faces the sea, its steps running down into the water.
places.lore: A small sect of water arts that cultivated the rhythm of the tide. Its last master walked into the winter sea in 468 to cultivate the tide and never came back; within two years its disciples went to Tùng Đào Cung.

places.name: Lãnh Triều Tuyền
places.look: In the woods behind the shore a cold spring wells up into a stone basin, its water salt-cold and smelling faintly of the sea.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring, its flow strongest at the high tide. The tide-watchers of Vọng Triều Các drew their water from it for two centuries.

provinces.name: Tùng Mặc
provinces.lore: Inland pine forest in the north of the pine sea, where villagers burn pine to soot and press it into ink cakes. Tùng Mặc ink is sold in every sect library of the north. The misty wood beside the village gives the softest soot.

places.name: U Lam Lâm
places.look: A pine wood in a hollow where mist lies all morning, the trunks fading into grey.
places.lore: The ink-makers say pine from the misty wood gives the softest soot. Travellers lose the path here easily.

places.name: Tùng Mặc Thôn
places.look: Low sheds with long clay flues climb a slope, black soot coating every roof, and rows of ink cakes dry on boards in the shade.
places.lore: Villagers burn pine in long flues, scrape the soot and pound it with glue into ink cakes. Tùng Mặc ink is sold in every sect library of the north.

provinces.name: Phạt Mộc
provinces.lore: Pine forest rising from the coastal lowland into hills. Its woodcutters fell only trees marked by Tùng Đào's foresters and send the logs down to Tùng Gian Thành. A spirit vein of budding wood qi lies in its hills.

places.name: Manh Nha Mạch
places.look: A hillside where young pines grow thick and fast, and the snow melts weeks before anywhere else.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi wakes the hill early each spring. Tùng Đào's foresters gather seedlings here for replanting the cut slopes.

places.name: Phạt Mộc Thôn
places.look: A woodcutters' village with log slides running downhill and stacks of marked logs by the road.
places.lore: Its woodcutters fell only trees marked by Tùng Đào's foresters. A tree cut without a mark costs the cutter a year's work.

provinces.name: Tùng Mật
provinces.lore: Forested hills climbing toward high mountain west of the palace. Its villagers keep bees in log hives and sell dark pine honey on the palace road. Above them a cloud forest climbs nearly to a thousand metres.

places.name: Lăng Vân Lâm
places.look: On high slopes, tall firs rise through drifting cloud, their tops showing above it like masts.
places.lore: The forest is often above the clouds, and Tùng Đào's disciples climb to cultivate in its thin air. The beekeepers will not go higher than its edge.

places.name: Tùng Mật Thôn
places.look: Hollow-log hives hang in the pines around a small village, and the air hums with bees.
places.lore: Its beekeepers make a dark, resinous pine honey sold on the palace road. They say their bees learn the pine waves too.

provinces.name: Hương Khuẩn
provinces.lore: Forest and rocky high ground on the western edge of the pine sea. Its people gather and dry fragrant mushrooms that grow on fallen pine. Black leopards den on the crags, and gatherers go out in pairs.

places.name: Huyền Báo Nhai
places.look: A dark crag in the forest, its ledges strewn with bones and its rock marked with black hairs.
places.lore: Black leopards den in its caves and hunt the forest by night. The mushroom gatherers carry bells to warn them off.

places.name: Hương Khuẩn Thôn
places.look: Racks of drying mushrooms line every house, and the village smells of earth and woodsmoke.
places.lore: Its people gather mushrooms from fallen pine and dry them for the markets. They go out in pairs, for the leopards above.

provinces.name: Cát Chi
provinces.lore: Forest rising from low valleys into steep hills. Its people tap pine resin for incense and varnish, under foresters' rules on how many cuts a tree may bear. A heavy vein of earth qi lies under the hill above the village.

places.name: Hậu Thổ Mạch
places.look: On a steep hillside, a broad shelf of dark earth holds no trees, only thick grass and a few heavy boulders.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Earth qi runs under the shelf, heavy and slow. Tùng Đào's disciples who lean to earth come here, though few of them do.

places.name: Cát Chi Thôn
places.look: A valley village whose pines bear neat cuts above clay cups, and pots of golden resin cool on the doorsteps.
places.lore: Its people tap pine resin for incense and varnish. The foresters count the cuts on every tree each autumn.

provinces.name: Hương Khách
provinces.lore: Hill forest south of the palace ridge, on the pilgrims' road. Its village lives by lodging and feeding pilgrims, who climb on to the ridge to listen to the pines. The wood above the village sounds so like the sea that pilgrims sometimes stop there and go no further.

places.name: Hải Vận Lâm
places.look: A pine wood on a hill whose crowns roar in the wind exactly like surf on a beach.
places.lore: Pilgrims who stop here sometimes never go on to the palace, saying they have heard enough. Tùng Đào's disciples call it the near sea.

places.name: Hương Khách Thôn
places.look: A village of inns and tea stalls on the pilgrims' road, incense smoke drifting from every door.
places.lore: It lives by lodging pilgrims bound for the palace ridge. Innkeepers sell pine cones as keepsakes.

provinces.name: Tiều Phu
provinces.lore: High forest and rock above the ravines, home to woodsmen who sell firewood and charcoal to Vạn Hác. White apes hold the ridge above a thousand metres. The ginseng town of Thải Sâm Trấn was driven out by those apes in 979.

places.name: Bạch Viên Lĩnh
places.look: A high ridge of fir and rock where white-furred apes sit on the boulders, watching the valley.
places.lore: White apes hold the ridge and throw stones at anyone who climbs. They drove out the ginseng diggers of Thải Sâm Trấn in 979.

places.name: Thải Sâm Trấn
places.look: On a high slope, the stone walls of a small town are tumbled and grown with ferns, and dug pits pock the ground around it.
places.lore: Ginseng diggers built this town when the roots were plentiful. As the ginseng ran out they dug higher, into the apes' ridge, and in 979 the apes drove them out.

places.name: Tiều Phu Thôn
places.look: A hamlet of log houses on a high slope, firewood stacked to the eaves.
places.lore: Its woodsmen sell firewood and charcoal to Vạn Hác. They keep clear of the white apes above.

provinces.name: Dương Lan
provinces.lore: High forest climbing to bare rock above a thousand metres. Its shepherds graze goats and sheep in the clearings and on the high meadows, and pen them in dry-stone folds at night. Dwarf pines crouch on the summits where nothing else grows.

places.name: Ải Tùng Lâm
places.look: On bare high rock, a low forest of dwarf pines no taller than a man crouches against the wind.
places.lore: The dwarf pines are said to be as old as the palace. Shepherds shelter their flocks among them in storms.

places.name: Dương Lan Thôn
places.look: A high village of dry-stone sheepfolds, goats and sheep spread over the meadows above it.
places.lore: Its shepherds graze goats and sheep in the clearings and high meadows and pen them at night against the apes and leopards. They make hard cheese for Vạn Hác.

provinces.name: Phù Mộc
provinces.lore: River forest south-east of the palace, its river carrying driftwood down from the mountains. Villagers gather the driftwood and float logs to the lowlands. The red-barked pines above the river are among the oldest in the pine sea.

places.name: Xích Bì Lâm
places.look: A wood of old pines with bright red bark, glowing in the evening sun.
places.lore: These are among the oldest pines in the pine sea. Tùng Đào's foresters mark none for cutting.

places.name: Phù Mộc Thôn
places.look: A river village whose beaches are heaped with driftwood, bleached and sorted by size, and log booms tied along the bank.
places.lore: Its people gather driftwood from the river and float logs downstream to the lowland towns. They build their houses only from wood the river has brought them.

provinces.name: Biên Trúc
provinces.lore: High forest where the first bamboo of the south creeps in among the pines. Villagers weave bamboo fences, baskets and mats for the markets of Cổ Độ. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under a still grove on the slope.

places.name: Thanh Hư Mạch
places.look: A still grove of pine and bamboo on a high slope, where no wind moves the leaves.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi rises in the grove, and the stillness helps cultivators empty their minds. Vạn Hác's students come to rest their ears.

places.name: Biên Trúc Thôn
places.look: A village enclosed by woven bamboo fences, baskets and mats drying in every yard.
places.lore: Its people weave bamboo goods and sell them at Cổ Độ. The bamboo here is the first of the south, and the villagers cut only stems older than three years.

provinces.name: Liệp Hồ
provinces.lore: Forest, tundra and bog on the northern coast. Its people hunt foxes and trap for furs and fish the coast in summer. Grey wolves hold a knoll inland and take a share of every winter's catch.

places.name: Thương Lang Cương
places.look: A forested knoll with wolf trails worn into the moss and bones scattered at its foot.
places.lore: Grey wolves den here and hunt the forest and tundra. The fox hunters leave them carcasses each winter to keep the peace.

places.name: Liệp Hồ Thôn
places.look: A northern village of log houses, fox pelts stretched on every wall.
places.lore: Its hunters trap foxes and fish the coast in summer. They pay the grey wolves a share of every winter's catch by leaving carcasses on the knoll.

provinces.name: Bán Sơn
provinces.lore: Forested mountain climbing to over sixteen hundred metres south-east of the palace. Its village sits halfway up and lives by goats, herbs and the disciples who climb to the peak. The peak's metal qi draws Tùng Đào's disciples in summer.

places.name: Bích Lạc Phong
places.look: A bare rock peak above the pines, its summit standing in clear blue sky above the clouds.
places.lore: A peak of Metal qi rises over sixteen hundred metres here. Tùng Đào's disciples climb it in summer to temper their arts in its thin, cold air.

places.name: Bán Sơn Thôn
places.look: A village of stone houses halfway up a forested mountain, terraced herb beds below it.
places.lore: It lives by goats, herbs and the disciples who climb to the peak. Its people guide them up for a fee.

provinces.name: Vân Ổ
provinces.lore: High mountain and forest on the eastern edge, often sunk in cloud. Its villagers herd goats and gather mountain herbs. A slender green-grey peak rises above the hollow like a hairpin.

places.name: Thúy Trâm Phong
places.look: A slender, green-grey spire of rock rises above the forest like a hairpin thrust into the clouds.
places.lore: A peak of Earth and Metal qi, its rock streaked with pale green. Climbers say it sings faintly in the wind, and the goat herders of Vân Ổ will not climb past its shoulder.

places.name: Vân Ổ Thôn
places.look: A village in a high hollow, often sunk in cloud, with goat pens and stone huts.
places.lore: Its villagers herd goats and gather mountain herbs. They can find their way in cloud by the sound of goat bells.

provinces.name: Lạc Thạch
provinces.lore: High forest under crags that shed stones every spring. Villagers quarry the fallen stone and carve millstones. The avalanche that buried Hàn Thạch Trấn in 1151 is still remembered in every house.

places.name: Thâm Vụ Lâm
places.look: A high fir forest swallowed by mist most days, its trunks dripping.
places.lore: The mist never lifts for long, and the villagers will not enter it without a rope. Mosses here are prized by alchemists.

places.name: Hàn Thạch Trấn
places.look: On a high mountain shelf, the roofs of a stone town poke out of a field of tumbled rock and old snow.
places.lore: A quarry town that cut stone for Tùng Đào's halls. In the winter of 1151 an avalanche buried it, and the survivors moved down to Lạc Thạch.

places.name: Lạc Thạch Thôn
places.look: A village of stone houses among boulders under the crags, millstones stacked by the road.
places.lore: Villagers quarry the stones that fall in spring and carve millstones. They remember Hàn Thạch Trấn.

provinces.name: Thảo Pha
provinces.lore: Forested hills opening into grassy slopes in the south. Its people graze cattle on the slopes and cut yew in the woods for bows. It is the warmest land in the pine sea.

places.name: Tử Sam Lâm
places.look: A dark wood of old yews with red, peeling bark and poisonous red berries.
places.lore: The bowyers take only fallen branches. Cattle that stray in sicken from the berries.

places.name: Thảo Pha Thôn
places.look: A village on a grassy slope, cattle grazing around it and yew bows drying under the eaves.
places.lore: Its people graze cattle and make yew bows. It is the warmest village in the pine sea.

provinces.name: Thạch Tỉnh
provinces.lore: Forest and high rock in the south-east, its village gathered around a deep stone well. Its people herd goats and dig a little copper from the hill. Giant flying squirrels glide over the crags at dusk.

places.name: Phi Thử Nhai
places.look: A high crag above the forest where big furred shapes glide from ledge to ledge at dusk.
places.lore: Giant spirit flying squirrels nest in the crag and steal from the village stores. Villagers hang their food in sealed jars.

places.name: Thạch Tỉnh Thôn
places.look: Stone houses with slab roofs ring a deep well cut through the rock, its rim worn smooth by ropes, and green-stained copper diggings scar the slope above.
places.lore: The village grew around the well, which has never run dry even in the drought years, and its people herd goats and dig a little copper ore for the smiths of Cổ Độ. Every family hangs a bell over the well on the night a child is born.

provinces.name: Hôi Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountain near the border of the heart, rising to over eighteen hundred metres. No one lives here but Tùng Đào's watch on Thương Tùng Mạch and the miners of the grey iron mine. The rock is grey like the pines on the summit.

places.name: Thương Tùng Mạch
places.look: On a high summit above the pine sea stands a grove of pines with bark the colour of ash, older and paler than any around them. An old fence of stone posts and timber rails rings the grey grove, and the air inside is still even when the forest below is roaring.

places.name: Hôi Thiết Khoáng
places.look: On a bare mountain slope, small mine mouths open in grey rock under the grey pines.
places.lore: The mine digs grey iron ore from the high rock. Tùng Đào's watch on Thương Tùng Mạch guards it too.

provinces.name: Tửu Phường
provinces.lore: River forest in the far south, where villagers brew pine-needle wine and sell it on the road to Cổ Độ. Venom hornets nest in the woods behind. The wine is said to taste of the wind in the pines.

places.name: Độc Phong Lâm
places.look: A wood humming with hornets, their paper nests hanging from the branches like lanterns.
places.lore: Venom hornets as long as a finger nest here. Alchemists pay well for their venom.

places.name: Tửu Phường Thôn
places.look: A village of brewhouses and wine jars, the air sharp with pine.
places.lore: Its brewers make pine-needle wine and sell it on the road to Cổ Độ. The wine is said to taste of the wind in the pines.

provinces.name: Quan Hạ
provinces.lore: High mountain, forest and grassland around the broken walls of Thiết Tỏa Quan. Its village lives by goats and the iron mine above. Tùng Đào's elders bring disciples here to see what breaking the peace cost.

places.name: Thiết Tỏa Quan
places.look: On a forested bluff above the river road stand the broken walls of a fort, its gate towers cracked and one fallen. At the bluff's edge a massive stone anchor-block still holds a great iron ring, snapped open, from which the chain once ran across the river.

places.name: Tỏa Thiết Khoáng
places.look: On a high slope, black spoil heaps run down from a timbered adit, and rusted ore carts lie where the old track ends.
places.lore: The mine digs dark iron ore; old miners say iron from here went into the chain of Thiết Tỏa Quan, which gave the mine its name. It is worked again today by the people of Quan Hạ.

places.name: Đoạn Liên Phong
places.look: A bare peak above the fort, from which the river road can be seen far below.
places.lore: A peak of Metal qi, named for the chain that broke below it in 508. Tùng Đào's elders bring disciples to its summit to look down at the river.

places.name: Quan Hạ Thôn
places.look: A village of stone houses under the broken walls of Thiết Tỏa Quan.
places.lore: Its people herd goats and work the iron mine above. They guide Tùng Đào's elders and disciples to the fort.

provinces.name: Thủ Mộ
provinces.lore: Quiet northern forest around the fallen temple of Khô Mộc Tự. Its villagers keep the temple's graves and gather firewood and fungus. The forest beside it is so still that birdsong carries for a mile.

places.name: Tịch Tĩnh Lâm
places.look: A still pine forest where the wind seems to stop at the edge.
places.lore: Birdsong carries for a mile here. The monks of Khô Mộc Tự meditated among its trees.

places.name: Khô Mộc Tự
places.look: In the forest, the halls of a temple stand roofless around a huge dead tree, grey and bare.
places.lore: A small sect that cultivated the stillness of withered wood. In 641 its abbot's art turned on him and he withered with his tree; his monks scattered, and the village kept the graves.

places.name: Thủ Mộ Thôn
places.look: A quiet village at the edge of an old temple's graveyard, its people sweeping the stones.
places.lore: Its villagers keep the graves of Khô Mộc Tự and gather firewood and fungus. They were the temple's servants once.

provinces.name: Hắc Nhĩ
provinces.lore: Damp northern forest where black wood-ear fungus grows thick on fallen logs. Its people gather and dry it for the markets of Tùng Gian. The forest is green and misty even in late autumn.

places.name: Lục Vân Lâm
places.look: A misty green forest where moss hangs from every branch.
places.lore: The fungus gatherers find their best logs here. It is green and misty even in late autumn.

places.name: Hắc Nhĩ Thôn
places.look: A damp village where logs stacked by the houses are crusted with dark wood-ear fungus, and baskets of it dry on the eaves.
places.lore: Its people grow and gather black wood-ear fungus on fallen logs. Their dried fungus is sold at Tùng Gian Thành, and the best of it goes up to the palace kitchens.

provinces.name: Tùng Hoa
provinces.lore: Inland pine forest that turns the air yellow with pollen each spring. Villagers collect the pollen for cakes and medicine. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under a wave of green hills.

places.name: Thúy Ba Mạch
places.look: Rolling green hills where the pines ripple like waves in the wind.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the hills. Tùng Đào's disciples cultivate here in spring.

places.name: Tùng Hoa Thôn
places.look: A village whose roofs turn yellow with pollen each spring, and cloths spread to catch it.
places.lore: Villagers collect pine pollen for cakes and medicine. Tùng Đào's alchemists buy most of it.

provinces.name: Mộc Tập
provinces.lore: River lowland in the north-east of the pine sea, where the timber of the north is gathered and sold. Mộc Tập Trấn holds a timber fair each spring. Dawn redwoods grow along the river.

places.name: Thủy Sam Lâm
places.look: A grove of tall dawn redwoods along the river, their feathery needles turning red in autumn.
places.lore: These trees grow only by the river and are protected by the foresters. Their wood is light and floats well.

places.name: Mộc Tập Trấn
places.look: A river town of timber yards and log ponds, its wharves stacked with marked logs.
places.lore: The timber of the north is gathered here and sold at a fair each spring. Tùng Đào's foresters check every brand.

provinces.name: Lâu Thuyền
provinces.lore: Coastal forest whose town builds ships from straight pine. Lâu Thuyền Trấn launches Tùng Đào's coastal ships and Lãng Đào's sea-going barges. Its mast pines are guarded by foresters.

places.name: Trực Cán Lâm
places.look: A forest of tall, straight pines like ship masts.
places.lore: The mast pines are guarded by foresters and cut only for the shipyards. A crooked tree here is a rare sight.

places.name: Lâu Thuyền Trấn
places.look: A coastal town of shipyards and slipways, half-built hulls rising like ribs.
places.lore: It builds Tùng Đào's coastal ships and Lãng Đào's sea-going barges. Its shipwrights are the best in the north.

provinces.name: Thải Tân
provinces.lore: Inland forest of mixed pine and broadleaf. Its villagers gather firewood and sell it to the coast towns. It is the plainest land in the pine sea, and its people are proud of it.

places.name: Tạp Mộc Lâm
places.look: A rolling wood where pines stand among oak, birch and maple, the floor deep in acorns and broad fallen leaves.
places.lore: The firewood gatherers of Thải Tân take its deadwood, and its acorns fatten the wild boar that the villagers hunt each autumn. Tùng Đào's foresters leave it unmarked, since its timber is too crooked for ships or halls.

places.name: Thải Tân Thôn
places.look: A plain village with firewood stacked along every road.
places.lore: Its villagers gather firewood and sell it to the coast towns. They are proud of their plain lives.

provinces.name: Triều Thanh
provinces.lore: Coastal forest dipping below the sea in places. Its fishers listen to the tide from their houses. The sea wind bends the pines along the shore.

places.name: Hải Phong Lâm
places.look: On the low coast, a pine forest stands bent inland by the wind, its seaward trees dwarfed and salt-burned and its inner trees tall and straight.
places.lore: The fishers of Triều Thanh read the weather by the sound of the wind in its crowns, and they gather pine pitch here to caulk their boats. Its windbreak keeps the salt off the village gardens.

places.name: Triều Thanh Thôn
places.look: A fishing village of grey roofs by the sea.
places.lore: Its fishers listen to the tide to know when to sail. The sea wind bends the pines around it.

provinces.name: Sóc Phong Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat tundra on the northern coast, scoured bare by the north wind. No one lives here; reindeer cross it in summer and leave before the first snow. A cold spring of water qi rises in its middle.

places.name: Hàn Tinh Tuyền
places.look: A cold spring in the open tundra, its still pool so clear that on winter nights it holds the stars like a second sky.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring. Tùng Đào's disciples come in summer, the only season the walk is possible.

provinces.name: Điếu Đài
provinces.lore: River forest on the lower river, its people fishing from stone terraces on the bank. A spirit vein of soft water qi lies near the river. The drowned abbey of Tĩnh Thủy Quán stands in the woods, its walls still marked by the flood of 700.

places.name: Tĩnh Thủy Quán
places.look: In the woods, the mud-filled halls of an abbey stand with water marks high on their walls.
places.lore: A small sect that cultivated the stillness of water. The great flood of 700 drowned it along with three villages, and the survivors went to Tùng Đào two years later.

places.name: Nhu Thủy Mạch
places.look: A hollow near the river where a spring seeps through moss into a pool so soft that stones on its bed are worn round as eggs.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here, gentle and slow. Tùng Đào's water cultivators come to learn patience at it, and the drowned monks of Tĩnh Thủy Quán once did the same.

places.name: Điếu Đài Thôn
places.look: A river village whose bank is stepped with flat stone terraces, each with a fisher sitting on it and a long rod over the current.
places.lore: Each family owns its own terrace and passes it down with the house. The village sells its catch at Đào Thanh, and the oldest terrace is said to be older than the levees.

provinces.name: Lô Chu
provinces.lore: River forest where villagers fish with trained cormorants on the slow reaches. They sell their catch at Đào Thanh. The maples behind the village turn red each autumn.

places.name: Phong Thụ Lâm
places.look: A maple forest behind the village that turns red in autumn.
places.lore: The villagers tap maple sap in spring and boil it into syrup for the river towns. Cormorant fishers judge the autumn fish run by how red the leaves have turned.

places.name: Lô Chu Thôn
places.look: A river village of grey roofs where black cormorants perch on the gunwales of narrow boats, rings around their necks.
places.lore: Its people fish the slow reaches with trained cormorants that bring back fish they cannot swallow. They sell their catch at Đào Thanh and give each bird the seventh fish.

provinces.name: Phủ Tạc
provinces.lore: Inland forest whose villagers are carpenters, building boats, carts and houses for the river towns. Wild oxen graze the clearings. Its carpenters are hired as far as Tùng Gian.

places.name: Dã Ngưu Nguyên
places.look: A broad clearing in the forest, its grass grazed short and churned by hooves, where shaggy dark oxen stand in a wary herd.
places.lore: Wild oxen graze here and charge anyone who comes between them and their calves. Hunters of Phủ Tạc take one or two in winter, and the carpenters buy their horn for glue.

places.name: Phủ Tạc Thôn
places.look: A forest village of open-sided workshops where boat ribs, cartwheels and roof beams lie half-shaped in the wood shavings.
places.lore: Its carpenters build boats, carts and houses for the river towns and are hired as far as Tùng Gian. Each apprentice carves his own mallet before he may touch a chisel.

provinces.name: Mạch Hương
provinces.lore: River lowland where villagers grow barley and wheat on the flood flats. Its grain goes to the granaries of Lâm Hạ. An old elm wood shelters its fields from the north wind.

places.name: Du Âm Lâm
places.look: A strip of old elms between the fields and the north wind, their broad crowns throwing deep shade.
places.lore: The elms shelter the fields of Mạch Hương from the wind. In hard years the villagers eat the young elm seeds, and they call the wood their second granary.

places.name: Mạch Hương Thôn
places.look: A river village of grey roofs among fields of barley and wheat on the flood flats, with threshing floors by every house.
places.lore: Its people sow the flats as soon as the spring flood drains and send their grain to the granaries of Lâm Hạ. At harvest the whole bend smells of bread.

provinces.name: Hoành Độ
provinces.lore: Low river forest at a crossing of the Nine-Bend River. Its people run a ferry and fish. Lãng Đào takes a share of its fares.

places.name: Hắc Hoa Lâm
places.look: A damp riverside wood of dark-barked birches, their trunks grey-black and shaggy with curling bark.
places.lore: Black birch bark is stripped here for roofing the riverside houses. The ferrymen cut their poles from its straight young trees.

places.name: Hoành Độ Thôn
places.look: A river village where a broad flat ferry hauls across the river on a rope, and carts wait in line at the landing.
places.lore: Its people run the ferry across the Nine-Bend River here and fish between crossings. Lãng Đào takes a share of the fares and keeps the rope in repair.

provinces.name: Giá Ngưu
provinces.lore: Inland forest and clearings where villagers breed and drive oxen for the river towns' carts. Giant badgers dig their burrows on a knoll nearby. Oxen from here haul the timber down to the river.

places.name: Cự Hoan Cương
places.look: A knoll dug full of badger burrows, their mouths ringed with heaps of fresh earth.
places.lore: Giant badgers dig here and raid the ox feed. Their burrows can break an ox's leg.

places.name: Giá Ngưu Thôn
places.look: A village of ox pens and yoke sheds in a forest clearing, its lanes deep in hoof-churned mud.
places.lore: Its people breed and drive oxen for the river towns' carts. Oxen from here haul the timber down to the river.

provinces.name: Hà Đê
provinces.lore: River lowland behind a long earth levee, raised after the flood of 700. Its people farm the flats and mend the levee every spring. A spirit vein of water qi runs beside the river.

places.name: Bích Lưu Mạch
places.look: A green pool beside the river, fed by a current that runs clear and jade-green even when the river beside it is brown with flood.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here, and the villagers of Hà Đê say it never floods. Tùng Đào's disciples cultivate on the levee above it.

places.name: Hà Đê Thôn
places.look: A village behind a long earth levee, its houses below the level of the river in flood.
places.lore: Its people farm the flats and mend the levee every spring. The levee was raised after the flood of 700.

provinces.name: Thủy Xa
provinces.lore: River forest where villagers lift water to their fields with tall waterwheels. Its people farm and grind grain. The frost-leaf forest behind turns red early.

places.name: Sương Diệp Lâm
places.look: A wood of oak and maple behind the village whose leaves turn red with the first frost, weeks before the rest of the river.
places.lore: The villagers watch it to know the season: when its leaves turn early, they say, the winter will be hard. Its fallen oak wood feeds the mill fires.

places.name: Thủy Xa Thôn
places.look: A river village where tall bamboo waterwheels creak on the bank, lifting buckets of water into wooden troughs that run to the fields.
places.lore: Its people lift river water to their fields with the wheels and grind grain with a smaller wheel by the mill. Each wheel is rebuilt every ten years from the same pattern.

provinces.name: Bối Dược
provinces.lore: Inland hill forest where villagers gather wild herbs and carry them on their backs to Thải Chi Cốc. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under the hill. Herb gatherers come from all over the basin.

places.name: Bách Thảo Mạch
places.look: A hillside clearing so thick with herbs of every kind that its air smells bitter and sweet at once.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi feeds the herbs, and plants grow here that grow nowhere else in the basin. Thải Chi Cốc's alchemists prize them and send a gatherer each spring.

places.name: Bối Dược Thôn
places.look: A hill village where tall carrying baskets hang by every door and herbs dry in bundles from the eaves.
places.lore: Its people gather wild herbs on the hills and carry them on their backs down to Thải Chi Cốc. Herb gatherers come from all over the basin.

provinces.name: Thạch Lũy
provinces.lore: Inland forest and hills where villagers build stone walls around their fields. Its people farm and gather firewood. A grey cypress wood climbs the hill.

places.name: Thương Bách Lâm
places.look: A wood of grey-green cypresses on the hill above the village, their scent sharp in the cold air.
places.lore: Cypress from here is used for coffins and shrine beams. The villagers of Thạch Lũy bury their dead under its trees.

places.name: Thạch Lũy Thôn
places.look: A village with stone walls around its fields, built from the stones they cleared.
places.lore: Its people build stone walls from the stones they clear. They farm and gather firewood.

provinces.name: Hoang Tự Câu
provinces.lore: Forest and tundra in the north, with gullies where a temple stood before Tùng Đào came. No one lives here now. A northern birch wood shelters the ruins.

places.name: Bắc Hoa Lâm
places.look: A thin birch wood on the tundra's edge, its trees bent low by the north wind and its floor white with lichen.
places.lore: The birches shelter the ruins of Tuyết Thiền Tự. Reindeer herders camp here in summer and strip bark for their tents.

places.name: Tuyết Thiền Tự
places.look: In a gully, the stone halls of a temple stand roofless under snow.
places.lore: A small sect of monks who meditated in the snow. In the hard winter of 261 most of them starved, and the last walked south to Tùng Đào Cung the next spring.

provinces.name: Tân Lưu
provinces.lore: River forest on the new course of the river, near the dry bed of Đông Lưu Thành. Tân Lưu Trấn grew on the new current, and its people fish, farm and trade. Children dig for coins on the old bed since the flood of 1198.

places.name: Đông Lưu Thành
places.look: A long stone quay wall runs through an empty meadow, its rusted iron mooring rings hanging over grass where boats once tied up. Behind it stand the roofless stubs of warehouses, and a fresh scar of sand shows where a spring flood has opened up an old paved street. The living river runs past at a distance, along the edge of the bed.

places.name: Cựu Đạo Lâm
places.look: A long, narrow wood of willow and alder growing in a winding line across the meadow, following the dry bed of the old river.
places.lore: The trees took root on the bed the river left in 280, and their line still shows its old bends. Since the flood of 1198, children from Tân Lưu dig among the roots for coins of Đông Lưu Thành.

places.name: Tân Lưu Trấn
places.look: A river town on the new course of the river, its wharves busy with boats.
places.lore: It grew on the new current after the river left Đông Lưu Thành. Its people fish, farm and trade.

provinces.name: Độc Mộc
provinces.lore: River forest whose villagers cross the river on a single great log. Its people fish and carve dugout canoes. Ospreys nest on a rock above the river.

places.name: Ngư Ưng Đài
places.look: A rock above the river where ospreys nest, their great stick nests piled on its ledges.
places.lore: Ospreys nest here and fish the river. The villagers watch them for the fish runs.

places.name: Độc Mộc Thôn
places.look: A river village on both banks, joined by one huge pine trunk laid across a narrow, rocky stretch of the river, with dugout canoes pulled up below.
places.lore: Its people cross the river on the log and carve dugout canoes from single trunks. When the log rots, the whole village goes up the hill together to fell the next one.

provinces.name: Sài Môn
provinces.lore: Hill forest where villagers live quietly behind brushwood gates. Its people gather firewood and pine nuts. A cloud pine forest climbs the hill.

places.name: Vân Tùng Lâm
places.look: A pine forest high on the hill, its crowns lost in low cloud on most mornings and dripping with mist.
places.lore: Tùng Đào's disciples climb here to cultivate in the mist among the pines. The villagers of Sài Môn gather pine nuts only on its lower edge.

places.name: Sài Môn Thôn
places.look: A quiet hill village of thatched houses, each with a gate of woven brushwood and a pine-nut tree in the yard.
places.lore: Its people gather firewood and pine nuts and keep to themselves. Retired outer disciples of Tùng Đào sometimes settle here to grow old in quiet.

provinces.name: Tùng Lộ
provinces.lore: Inland hill forest where villagers dig pine truffles with trained pigs. The truffles sell well in Đào Thanh. A forest of tall pines like a thousand pillars rises behind.

places.name: Thiên Trụ Lâm
places.look: A forest of tall, straight, branchless pines standing like the pillars of an endless hall, their crowns far overhead.
places.lore: The pines are so straight that Tùng Đào's builders once came here for hall pillars, and the stumps of that cutting still show. The truffle diggers of Tùng Lộ work its roots.

places.name: Tùng Lộ Thôn
places.look: A hill village with truffle pigs in pens.
places.lore: Its people dig pine truffles with trained pigs. The truffles sell well in Đào Thanh.

provinces.name: Cung Tiễn
provinces.lore: Hill forest where villagers make bows and arrows for hunters and Tùng Đào's guards. Its people hunt and craft. Sacred old trees stand on the hill above.

places.name: Thần Mộc Lâm
places.look: On the hilltop, a grove of colossal old trees whose trunks are wrapped with red cords and hung with small votive boards.
places.lore: The bowyers of Cung Tiễn hold the trees sacred and never cut them, and they bring each new bow here to be blessed before it is sold. They say an arrow fletched with a feather found in the grove never misses.

places.name: Cung Tiễn Thôn
places.look: A hill village of bowyers, bow staves seasoning under every roof.
places.lore: Its people make bows and arrows for hunters and Tùng Đào's guards. They hunt too.

provinces.name: Thạch Lâu
provinces.lore: Forest climbing into high mountain near a thousand metres. Its people herd goats and gather herbs. The burned pavilion of Lăng Tiêu Các stands high on the mountain.

places.name: Thanh Ngưu Cốc
places.look: A high valley of mountain meadow where massive oxen with dark green-tinged coats graze among the boulders.
places.lore: Spirit oxen live here, gentle unless their calves are threatened; then they charge like a landslide. Herbalists gather the rare grasses they leave ungrazed.

places.name: Lăng Tiêu Các
places.gloss: Pavilion That Rises to the Sky
places.look: High on the mountain, the burned shell of a pavilion stands against the sky.
places.lore: A small sect of alchemists. A fire in its pill hall in 1066 burned the pavilion, and its disciples scattered.

places.name: Thạch Lâu Thôn
places.look: A mountain village of goat pens and stone huts gathered under a squat stone watchtower with a fire basket on top.
places.lore: Its people herd goats and gather herbs on the high slopes. The tower is lit when the green oxen come down the valley, so the herders can drive their flocks clear.

provinces.name: Ma Bố
provinces.lore: High forest where villagers grow hemp and weave cloth. Its people farm and weave. Hemlock forest climbs the mountain above.

places.name: Thiết Sam Lâm
places.look: A dark hemlock forest climbing the mountain, its drooping branches heavy with snow half the year.
places.lore: Hemlock wood here is hard and does not split, and the weavers of Ma Bố make their loom frames from it. Few go deeper than the woodcutters' paths.

places.name: Ma Bố Thôn
places.look: A high village of narrow hemp fields and stone houses where looms clack in every doorway and retting pits steam in the stream.
places.lore: Its people grow hemp on the slopes and weave a coarse, hard-wearing cloth for sails and sacks. They sell it at Đào Thanh.

provinces.name: Lâm Khẩu
provinces.lore: Forest climbing into hills, its village at the forest's mouth. Its people hunt and gather. Sabre-toothed cats roam a ridge nearby.

places.name: Kiếm Xỉ Lĩnh
places.look: A forested ridge whose trunks are scored with deep claw marks, and deer bones lie cracked in its hollows.
places.lore: Sabre-toothed cats den on the ridge and hunt deer in the valley below. Hunters of Lâm Khẩu go in groups of six, and a fang from here buys a cow.

places.name: Lâm Khẩu Thôn
places.look: A village of log houses at the mouth of a forest valley, a tall palisade on the forest side.
places.lore: Its people hunt and gather in the valley behind. They keep the palisade high because of the sabre-toothed cats on the ridge.

provinces.name: Vân Biên
provinces.lore: High forest and rock near the clouds. Its people herd goats and gather herbs. Hawks nest on a crag, and the cliff-cut halls of Đoạn Vân Viện stand broken nearby.

places.name: Ưng Sào Nhai
places.look: A grey crag above the village, its ledges crowned with stick nests and whitened by droppings.
places.lore: Great hawks nest on the crag and take young goats from the slopes. Vân Biên's herders climb up each spring to take chicks for taming, and the hawks remember them.

places.name: Đoạn Vân Viện
places.look: On a cliff, the cut halls of an academy lie broken.
places.lore: A small sect that cut its halls into the cliff. An earthquake in 1134 broke them, and the survivors went to Tùng Đào.

places.name: Vân Biên Thôn
places.look: A high village of stone huts on a shelf above the forest, where the clouds often lie below the houses like a white sea.
places.lore: Its people herd goats and gather herbs on the crags. They guard their kids against the hawks of the crag above.

provinces.name: Hổ Bối Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountain and forest around Hổ Khiếu Cương. The tiger and the thin ore drove the miners out of Thạch Khẩu Trấn, and since 1162 the swordsmen of Ngạo Tuyết Phái have kept their sword hall in its empty houses. Tùng Đào's riders go around the ridges, not over them.

places.name: Hổ Khiếu Cương
places.look: A long bare ridge rises between the river's bends, its crest banded with dark and pale rock like a tiger's flank. The wind funnels through a notch in the crest with a low growl, and now and then a real roar answers it from the boulders below. No path crosses it.

places.name: Hổ Văn Khoáng
places.look: A mine in banded rock like a tiger's stripes, its adit now dark and silent.
places.lore: The mine dug banded iron ore. The tiger of Hổ Khiếu Cương drove the miners out.

places.name: Ngạo Tuyết Phái
places.look: A sword hall with a freshly tiled roof stands among the grey stone houses of an old mining town, about a hundred and twenty of them repaired and the rest roofless, with a forge smoking beside it. Behind the town the spoil heaps of the ore lie banded like a tiger's flank.
places.lore: Ngạo Tuyết Phái is a small school of sword cultivators sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, founded in 1105 by a swordsman who learned his art watching the plum bloom through the snow; it takes only children with Metal in their root. In 1162, a month after the tiger of Thạch Khẩu killed his daughter Lăng Nhược Mai, the founder Lăng Đạp Tuyết hunted it to Hổ Khiếu Cương, killed it, and moved the sword hall into the town's empty smelting houses. His sworn brother Trác Thiết Cán, a miner's son of the town, relit the forge. The miners had left because the tiger-stripe ore ran thin and the tiger took them, and the town was empty by 1161.

provinces.name: Thương Lô Trạch
provinces.lore: Swamp and forest on the northern coast, thick with grey reeds. No one lives here. Mud dragons hold its shoals.

places.name: Nê Giao Chử
places.look: Low mud shoals among grey reeds where long, ridged backs lie half sunk like logs, and the mud is scored with drag marks.
places.lore: Mud dragons (giao) lurk in the shoals and drag deer and stray reindeer down into the mud. No one cuts reeds within sight of them, and the coast fishers row wide of the marsh mouth.

provinces.name: Tầng Điền
provinces.lore: High forest and rock where villagers farm terraces on the slopes. Its people grow barley and buckwheat. The sealed abbey of Cô Hạc Quán stands high above.

places.name: Quải Đài Lâm
places.look: A high, misty forest of old firs hung so thick with grey-green lichen that the branches look like bearded old men.
places.lore: The lichen grows only where the air is clean and damp, and alchemists of Thải Chi Cốc buy it for wound salves. The villagers of Tầng Điền gather it in autumn.

places.name: Cô Hạc Quán
places.look: A sealed abbey high on the mountain, its main door still closed under a faded seal.
places.lore: A small sect of hermits. Its abbot died in closed-door cultivation in 1010, and no one could break his seal; the disciples scattered.

places.name: Tầng Điền Thôn
places.look: A high village under stair-stepped terraces of barley and buckwheat, held up by dry-stone walls that climb the whole slope.
places.lore: Its people farm the terraces and rebuild a wall or two each spring after the frost heaves them. They carry earth up in baskets to replace what the rains wash down.

provinces.name: Lẫm Phong Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The highest mountains of the basin, rising to nearly two thousand metres. No one lives here but miners. From its peak the whole river can be seen.

places.name: Ngân Tuyết Khoáng
places.look: A timbered adit high on bare rock, its spoil heaps glittering with silver ore under the snow.
places.lore: The mine digs silver from the high rock in the short summer and closes in winter. Tùng Đào posts a guard on the ore road down to Đào Thanh.

places.name: Vọng Xuyên Phong
places.look: The highest peak of the basin, a bare grey summit near two thousand metres, from which the whole river shines in its nine bends.
places.lore: A peak of Metal qi, cold and sharp. Tùng Đào's disciples climb it to cultivate, and river pilots say a man who has counted all nine bends from its top will never lose his way on the water.

provinces.name: Tùng Tâm
provinces.lore: Inland pine forest in the north of the basin. Its people split resinous pine heartwood for torches. Porcupines roam a wood nearby.

places.name: Tiễn Trư Lâm
places.look: A wood of gnawed pines, bark stripped in rings and the ground scattered with long black-and-white quills.
places.lore: Porcupines as big as dogs live here and kill the young pines by gnawing their bark. Their quills are gathered for arrows and fish lures.

places.name: Tùng Tâm Thôn
places.look: A pine forest village where bundles of split, resin-soaked heartwood stand drying against every wall.
places.lore: Its people split the resinous heartwood of fallen pines into torches that burn for hours. They sell them at Đào Sa for the night washers.

provinces.name: Ô Bồng
provinces.lore: Forest and swamp on the coast, where villagers fish from boats with black awnings. Its people fish and gather reeds. A flooded wood lies behind the village.

places.name: Tẩm Thủy Lâm
places.look: A swamp wood of alder and willow standing knee-deep in still brown water, the trunks stained dark to the flood line.
places.lore: The villagers of Ô Bồng pole their boats between the trees and set eel traps among the roots. In spring the water rises to the low branches.

places.name: Ô Bồng Thôn
places.look: A coastal village of reed houses where narrow boats with arched black-tarred awnings lie in rows at the water's edge.
places.lore: Its people fish the coast and the marsh channels from the awninged boats and sleep in them in the fishing season. They gather reeds for thatch and mats.

provinces.name: Băng Thảo Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra on the northern coast, its grass frozen most of the year. No one lives here. A vein of water qi lies under the ice.

places.name: Băng Lưu Huyệt
places.look: A hollow in the tundra where a frozen stream of blue ice pours out of the ground and spreads in a fan that never melts.
places.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi rises here, so cold it freezes its own water as it flows. Tùng Đào's disciples sit on the ice to temper their bodies in the summer.

provinces.name: Bạch Thạch
provinces.lore: Forest on the coast, its village built of white stone. Its people fish and quarry. Blue martens roam the woods.

places.name: Thanh Điêu Lâm
places.look: A coastal pine wood where blue-grey martens flicker through the branches, and stripped pine cones litter the ground.
places.lore: Blue martens hunt squirrels here, and their pelts are prized in the winter markets. Trappers of Bạch Thạch take them only in deep winter, when the fur is thickest.

places.name: Bạch Thạch Thôn
places.look: A coastal village of white stone houses on a pale rocky shore, boats drawn up between the quarry heaps.
places.lore: Its people fish and quarry the white stone of the shore, which goes by boat to Đào Thanh for steps and quays. The whole village glows at sunset.

provinces.name: Đà Công
provinces.lore: River forest where villagers serve as helmsmen for Lãng Đào's ferries. Its people know every bend of the river. Weeping willows line its banks.

places.name: Thùy Dương Lâm
