places.look: A wood of weeping willows along the river bank, their long branches trailing in the current.
places.lore: The willows hold the bank against the spring floods. The helmsmen of Đà Công rest in their shade between voyages and cut withies here for baskets.

places.name: Đà Công Thôn
places.look: A river village of helmsmen, steering oars racked by every door.
places.lore: Its people serve as helmsmen for Lãng Đào's ferries. They know every bend of the river.

provinces.name: Ngọa Ngưu
provinces.lore: River forest named for a hill shaped like a resting ox. Its people farm and fish. The fallen gate of Phân Thủy Môn stands in the woods.

places.name: Hồi Thanh Lâm
places.look: A pine forest in a ring of low hills, where every call comes back twice, a little later each time.
places.lore: Sounds echo strangely among its trees. The villagers of Ngọa Ngưu come on the night of the dead to call their dead by name and listen for the answer.

places.name: Phân Thủy Môn
places.look: In the woods, the fallen gate of a sect.
places.lore: A small sect of boatmen. Its boats sank in a feud in 788, and the survivors joined Lãng Đào Môn two years later.

places.name: Ngọa Ngưu Thôn
places.look: A river village under a low hill shaped exactly like an ox lying down, its fields reaching to the bank.
places.lore: Its people farm and fish, and they leave a bundle of hay on the hill's head each new year. They say the day the ox rises, the river will flood.

provinces.name: Hải Tùng
provinces.lore: Low forest coast of pines that grow right down to the shingle. A few fishing families and resin tappers live here, and their boats sell catch and pitch at Khai Dương. Inland the pines grow so close that the coast road has never been cut through them.

places.name: Mật Tùng Lâm
places.look: A dense forest of black-barked pines, so close-grown that it is dusk under them at noon.
places.lore: The coast road has never been cut through it, and travellers go round by the shore. Resin tappers work only its edges and say the middle is full of fallen trunks no one has ever cleared.

places.name: Hải Tùng Thôn
places.look: A handful of tarred timber houses on the shingle under leaning pines, with resin pots smoking by the boats.
places.lore: Its families fish the coast and tap the pines for pitch, which they sell to the boatyards. Every boat here is caulked with pitch from the family's own trees.

provinces.name: Cao Mục
provinces.lore: Forest on the lower slopes, open steppe above and a knot of bare mountain to the west. Shepherds drive their flocks up to the summer grass and down to the woods for winter. They say the high ground here was found warm under the snow by the first shepherds of Dao Quang.

places.name: Tức Ngưu Sơn
places.look: A broad round-backed mountain of grey rock above the forest, shaped like an ox lying down to rest.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, slow and steady, and shepherds say flocks grazed on its flanks never stray. Cultivators of Earth arts sit on its back to settle their foundations.

places.name: Cao Mục Thôn
places.look: Stone sheepfolds and low turf-roofed houses on an open steppe shoulder, with flocks spread over the slope below.
places.lore: Its shepherds drive their sheep to the high grass each summer and down into the woods for winter. Wool and cheese go down to Bích Khê on market days.

provinces.name: Lâm Biên
provinces.lore: A wide, dark forest of the inner ridges with no river, crossed by timber tracks. Woodcutters live at its edges and seldom go deep, for the boars of the high woods are big and short-tempered. In the middle stand the burned walls of Chi Hương Trấn, the resin town lost to fire.

places.name: Sơn Trư Cương
places.look: A wooded ridge rooted bare in great furrows, with trees scarred waist-high by tusks.
places.lore: Spirit boars as big as oxen live here and dig up the forest floor for roots. Their bristles make fine brushes, and hunters who take them seldom try twice.

places.name: Chi Hương Trấn
places.look: Blackened stone walls and the stumps of a gate tower in a clearing of young pines, with charred beams still lying in the lanes.
places.lore: A resin town that boiled pitch for the coast from 330. In the dry summer of 712 a fire began in its pitch yards and burned the town and the forest around it; no one rebuilt.

places.name: Lâm Biên Thôn
places.look: Log houses where the timber tracks leave the forest, with stacked trunks and sawpits along the lane.
places.lore: Woodcutters live here and work the edge of the deep forest. They go into the high woods only in groups, with dogs, because of the boars.

provinces.name: Nhân Sâm
provinces.lore: Broad forest of the ridge country, rising to fir woods on the higher ground. Its people dig wild ginseng and other roots under the trees and sell them to Thiên Xu's alchemists at Khai Dương. Root diggers keep their patches secret even from their own children until they are too old to climb.

places.name: Cung Sam Lâm
places.look: Tall dark firs on the high ridge, often wrapped in cloud, their trunks bearded with grey lichen.
places.lore: The fir here is light and springy, and the Pivot's bowyers and formation masters buy it for bows and frames. Cloud sits in the forest most mornings until noon.

places.name: Nhân Sâm Thôn
places.look: A forest village of bark-roofed houses with racks of drying roots under every eave.
places.lore: Its people dig wild ginseng and sell it to Thiên Xu's alchemists at Khai Dương. A digger's patch passes only from parent to child, shown once, on the parent's last climb.

provinces.name: Hữu Bật Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Right Assistant Star
provinces.lore: Steep mountains with a strip of forest along a river, empty but for hunters and patrols. It is named for the hidden star said to stand beside the Dipper, as Phụ Tinh stands on the other side. Herb hunters climb its cold ridges for mountain flowers, and the Pivot's patrols pass through on the way to Tinh Tủy Mạch.

places.name: Ẩn Tinh Phong
places.look: A narrow grey peak above the river forest, whose summit is lost in cloud on most nights.
places.lore: It is named for the hidden assistant star of the Dipper, which star-readers say can only be seen from here on one night a year. Its qi runs to Metal, sharp and cold.

provinces.name: Sương Kích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High ice-capped mountains dropping straight into the northern sea, with no farmland and no village. It takes its name from the rusted iron stakes on Phụ Tinh Phong, where Phá Quân Môn drilled at night, which the frost coats white every winter. Only Thiên Xu's patrols and a few bold herb hunters come here.

places.name: Phụ Tinh Phong
places.look: A glacier peak stands beside taller neighbours, white ice over dark rock. Its broad shoulder holds a flat terrace cut into the ice, still bristling with rows of rusted iron stakes where weapon racks once stood. At night a single faint star hangs just above its summit.

provinces.name: Phóng Mã
provinces.lore: Forested hills with open steppe glades where horses are turned out to graze. Its people breed sturdy forest horses for Thiên Xu's couriers and the northern road. Wolf packs hunt the wooded ridges east of the pastures, and the herders ride in pairs.

places.name: Quần Lang Cương
places.look: A wooded ridge of broken rock with dens under every boulder and old bones scattered in the leaves.
places.lore: Grey spirit wolves den here in packs of twenty or more and hunt the horse herds in winter. Phóng Mã's riders burn torches along the pasture edge on the longest nights.

places.name: Phóng Mã Thôn
places.look: Timber stables and paddock fences on a steppe glade ringed by forest, with herds grazing loose beyond.
places.lore: Its people breed sturdy forest horses for Thiên Xu's couriers on the northern road. The herds are turned out loose in summer and rounded up by riders working in pairs.

provinces.name: Mặc Yên
provinces.lore: Rough upland of forest, steppe and red badland gullies at the southern edge of the forests. Its people burn pine in closed kilns for soot and press it into the ink sticks Thiên Xu's clerks write with. Great bears live in the high woods, and the ink-makers leave a cake of honey at the forest edge each autumn.

places.name: Đại Hùng Lâm
places.look: Old forest high on the ridge, with trunks clawed bare and beehives torn open in the branches.
places.lore: Great spirit bears live here, named by the villagers for the stars of the Dipper, which they call the Great Bear. Each autumn the ink-makers leave a cake of honey at the forest edge, and the bears have not come down in living memory.

places.name: Mặc Yên Thôn
places.look: Soot-black houses around long brick kilns that smoulder day and night, with ink cakes drying on boards in the sun.
places.lore: Its people burn pine in closed kilns, gather the soot and press it into ink sticks for Thiên Xu's clerks. The best sticks are scented with musk and stamped with the Dipper.

provinces.name: Lý Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest and mountain flank along a river that comes down from the high ranges. Villagers fish the river for carp and float timber down it. A vein of Wood and Metal qi in the woods above the village draws the Pivot's ironworkers, who come to temper tools there.

places.name: Thiết Mộc Mạch
places.look: A wooded slope where the trees grow slow and black, their wood so hard that axes ring off it.
places.lore: A vein whose qi runs to Wood and Metal together. Thiên Xu's ironworkers bring their tools here to be tempered, and the ironwood is cut only for array frames.

places.name: Lý Ngư Thôn
places.look: A river village of grey roofs with fish traps of woven willow set in the shallows and log rafts tied along the bank.
places.lore: Its people trap carp and guide timber rafts down the river. A carp that leaps the weir in spring is let go, for luck.

provinces.name: Lộc Tồn Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Lộc Tồn Star
provinces.lore: Forested mountains along a river, named for the third of the Dipper's star-lords in Thiên Xu's reckoning. No village stands here; miners come up the river to the red iron diggings and go down again before the snow. Its red-crested peak is a landmark for crane riders.

places.name: Giả Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Rust-red pits in the mountainside above the river, with ore heaps and a log slide down to the water.
places.lore: Crews dig red iron ore here in summer and slide it to the river for rafting to Cự Môn. They leave before the snow and never winter on the ridge.

places.name: Xích Quan Phong
places.look: A ridge-top of jagged red-grey rock teeth standing above the forest like a rooster's comb.
places.lore: Crane riders steer by it on the way to Tinh Tủy Mạch, and rest their mounts on its teeth in bad weather. Its qi runs to Metal, and cultivators who sit among the teeth find their sword intent grows keen and quick to anger.

provinces.name: Trường Canh Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountains of black rock below Trích Tinh Phong, where the evening star is first seen over the ridge. Nothing grows here but lichen, and no one lives here but the guard of Tinh Tủy Mạch. The guard has stood since 470 and was doubled in 1189; its fires are the only lights on the ridge at night.

places.name: Tinh Tủy Mạch
places.look: High on a black rock face near Trích Tinh Phong, seams of silver-white star marrow thread through the stone and glitter like frost even at noon. A low stone breastwork and a guards' fire pit sit on a ledge in front of the face. Cranes wheel over it in slow rings.

provinces.name: Mộc Phiệt
provinces.lore: Deep river forest in the west of the ridge country. Its people fell timber and float it down the river to the coast in great rafts each spring. Walnut groves on the drier ground give them a second harvest in the autumn.

places.name: Hồ Đào Lâm
places.look: Broad walnut trees on the drier hills, their ground thick with husks in autumn.
places.lore: The walnut harvest is Mộc Phiệt's second crop. The trees are counted and owned by families, and some have been owned by the same family since before the Pivot came.

places.name: Mộc Phiệt Thôn
places.look: Long timber sheds and log booms on a river bend, with great rafts being lashed together on the bank.
places.lore: Each spring its people float the winter's timber down to the coast on huge rafts and walk home along the bank. A raftsman who loses his raft walks home without speaking.

provinces.name: Chiên Mao
provinces.lore: Open steppe and thin forest above red badlands on the southern edge of Dao Quang. Herders keep sheep and goats and beat their wool into felt for tents and boots. An Earth vein lies under the steppe nearby, and its warm ground keeps the grass green into winter.

places.name: Noãn Thổ Mạch
places.look: A low swell of steppe where the grass stays green through winter and frost never lies on the ground.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, warm and deep, like the ground the first shepherds of Dao Quang found. Herders bring their flocks here in the hardest winters, and the Pivot lets them.

places.name: Chiên Mao Thôn
places.look: Round felt-roofed houses on the open steppe, with wool spread on mats and women beating it with sticks.
places.lore: Its herders make felt for tents, boots and saddle cloths and sell it down the northern road. Felt from here is said to keep out rain for ten years.

provinces.name: Liêm Trinh Nguyên
provinces.gloss: Plain of the Liêm Trinh Star
provinces.lore: Broken country of steppe, mountain, forest and badland named for the fifth of the Dipper's star-lords. Nobody farms it; herders pass through in summer, and prospectors come for the Metal vein hidden in its woods. The land is dry and the springs are few and far apart.

places.name: Tàng Kim Mạch
places.look: A forested hollow among bare hills where thin gold seams glint in a rock face under the roots.
places.lore: A vein whose qi runs to Metal, found by a prospector who could not dig the gold out. The gold, the Pivot's assayers say, is the qi itself made visible, and will not come away.

provinces.name: Vũ Khúc Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Vũ Khúc Star
provinces.lore: High forested mountains named for the Dipper's warrior star. In Phá Quân Môn's day its forts watched the southern roads, and their walls still stand on the heights. Today only woodcutters and patrols climb it, and they do not camp in the old forts.

places.name: Xích Sam Phong
places.look: A forested peak whose red-barked firs grow almost to the summit rock.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood, unusual so high in the ranges. Woodcutters who climb it to cut firs leave the topmost tree standing.

places.name: Vọng Tinh Bảo
places.look: A square stone fort on a forested height, its gate burned and its walls still standing to the parapet.
places.lore: Phá Quân Môn built it in 742 to watch the southern roads. When the rebellion was crushed in 874 its garrison surrendered without a fight, and the fort was burned and left.

provinces.name: Tham Lang Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Tham Lang Star
provinces.lore: Steep mountains and forest on the eastern side of the ranges, named for the first of the Dipper's star-lords. Lead and silver are dug here by a few hard crews. In 871 Thiên Xu camped here to besiege Phá Quân Môn, and the siege lines can still be traced on the slopes.

places.name: Duyên Ngân Khoáng
places.look: Grey spoil heaps below a few adits, with a small smelting hearth and a heap of lead pigs by the path.
places.lore: Lead and a little silver are dug here and smelted on the spot. The crews are paid in Thiên Xu's silver coin, which they like to say they dug themselves.

places.name: Khiếu Lang Phong
places.look: A sharp white-grey fang of rock above the eastern forests, where the wind howls in the cracks.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Metal, keen and restless. Sword cultivators climb it to sharpen their intent.

places.name: Vi Thành Trại
places.look: Earth banks and rotted palisade stakes in a ring on a mountain shoulder, with fire pits still black inside.
places.lore: Thiên Xu raised this camp in 871 to besiege Phá Quân Môn and abandoned it when the rebel gate fell in 874. Soldiers' names scratched on its stones can still be read.

provinces.name: Văn Khúc Lĩnh
provinces.gloss: Ridge of the Văn Khúc Star
provinces.lore: Tall bare mountains named for the Dipper's star of letters. Tin is dug on its lower slopes and carried down to the coast. Scholars of the Pivot climb its brush-shaped peak to compose poems, and most of the poems are about how cold it is.

places.name: Bạch Tích Khoáng
places.look: A few small adits on a low mountain slope, with ore washed in a cold stream and spread to dry on flat stones.
places.lore: Tin from here is carried to Khai Dương and alloyed into bronze for the Pivot's bells and mirrors.

places.name: Chấp Bút Phong
places.look: A slender rock summit standing upright above the ridge like a brush held to paper.
places.lore: Scholars of the Pivot climb it to write poems on the summit. Its qi runs to Metal.

provinces.name: Thiên Thê Lĩnh
provinces.lore: The high spine of Dao Quang, crowned by Trích Tinh Phong and its thousand rock-cut steps. Pilgrims climb the stair all summer; no one lives here but the keepers of a few rest huts. On a shoulder below the summit lie the broken gate and walls of Phá Quân Môn.

places.name: Trích Tinh Phong
places.gloss: Peak Where One Picks the Stars
places.look: The roof of the heartland: a dark rock peak rising clear of the clouds, its summit ending in a thin stone needle. Strips of white cloth tied around the needle stream in the wind, and below it a pilgrims' road of a thousand rock-cut steps runs up the spine of the ridge. On clear nights the stars seem to rest on the needle's tip.

places.name: Phá Quân Môn
places.look: On a high mountain shoulder, a gate arch split clean down the middle still stands, each half leaning away from the other, with seven iron star-studs running across its broken lintel. Behind it, scorched walls and the stump of a watchtower climb the slope. Grass grows in the old parade ground, and little else.

provinces.name: Hàn Đẩu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A wall of glaciered peaks east of Trích Tinh Phong, part of the same massif. Jade is cut from the rock high on its flanks, in a short summer season. Herders say the Dipper hangs lowest over these peaks in winter, as if it had come down to rest.

places.name: Tuyết Ngọc Khoáng
places.look: A small cut high on a bare slope near the ice, with blocks of pale stone roped on sledges.
places.lore: White jade is cut here in a short summer season and sledged down over the snow. The Pivot's seal-cutters take the best of it.

places.name: Thị Tinh Phong
places.look: A great white glacier peak standing just east of Trích Tinh Phong, a little lower, like an attendant beside a throne.
places.lore: Pilgrims call it Trích Tinh's servant. Its qi runs to Metal and Water, cold as its ice.

provinces.name: Hồng Thạch Câu
provinces.lore: Red badland gullies and bare mountain south of the forests. Copper is dug from the red rock, and the copper crews are the only people here. Rain is rare, and when it comes the gullies run red with mud for a day.

places.name: Hồng Câu Khoáng
places.look: Green-stained pits in red rock, with a line of water jars carried up from far below.
places.lore: Copper is dug here and carried north by mule. Water is so short that the crews bring every drink up the gully.

places.name: Chu Bình Phong
places.look: A long flat-faced red cliff peak above the badland gullies, glowing at sunset.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Earth with a warmth of Fire. Copper crews read the time of day by the colour of its face.

provinces.name: Bằng Dực Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountain and badland under the cliffs of Bằng Sào Nhai, where a roc nests. No one lives here, and herders keep their flocks well away. Lodestone is dug on the ridge by crews who work under rock overhangs, out of sight of the sky.

places.name: Bằng Sào Nhai
places.look: A sheer cliff of pale rock towers over the forest, and on a ledge near its top sits a nest the size of a farmhouse, woven from whole pine trunks bleached grey. Feathers longer than a man lie in the scree below. Nothing else nests within sight of it.

places.name: Chỉ Nam Khoáng
places.look: A dark adit under a rock overhang, its mouth bristling with iron nails that have flown to the stone and stuck.
places.lore: Lodestone from here goes to the Pivot's formation masters and to compass makers. The crews work under the overhang, out of sight of the roc.

provinces.name: Hoang Đài Nguyên
provinces.lore: Stepped badland terraces and low mountain at the southern edge of Dao Quang. The ground is too dry to farm, and only herders cross it in spring when the grass comes. Its stone drum peak is said to boom when storms come off the heartland.

places.name: Thạch Cổ Phong
places.look: A round, drum-shaped knob of rock on the badland terraces, hollow at its base.
places.lore: Wind in its hollow booms before storms, and herders drive their flocks to shelter when it sounds. Its qi runs to Earth.

provinces.name: Huyền Chi
provinces.lore: Damp forest along a river, thick with old logs and fungus. Its people gather wood-ear and dark lingzhi and dry them on racks for the markets of Khai Dương. The pine woods on the high ground are tapped for resin by the same families.

places.name: Chu Tùng Lâm
places.look: Tall red-trunked pines on the high ground above the river, their bark peeling in papery strips.
places.lore: The pine nuts and resin feed Huyền Chi through the winter. Talisman (phù lục) makers buy the resin to fix their ink.

places.name: Họa Tinh Đường
places.look: A low hall of dark timber in a forest clearing, its walls hung with long paper strips painted with the Dipper and drying in the wind.
places.lore: Talisman makers who paint the stars of the Dipper onto paper founded this hall in 910 and swore to Thiên Xu. They grind their ink from Mặc Yên soot and fix it with pine resin, and a talisman from here will not run in the rain.

places.name: Huyền Chi Thôn
places.look: Damp bark-roofed houses in the forest with mushroom logs stacked under the trees and drying racks along the lanes.
places.lore: Its people grow and gather wood-ear and dark lingzhi and sell them dried at Khai Dương. They tap the pines above the village for resin in the dry months.

provinces.name: Mặc Thạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Dark mountains and forest whose black slate splits into fine inkstones. A small quarry crew cuts the slate and sends it to Thiên Xu's clerks and scholars. No farms stand here; the crews eat what comes up the mule path.

places.name: Mặc Nghiên Khoáng
places.look: A small quarry of black slate on the mountainside, with split slabs stacked and rough inkstones lined up to dry.
places.lore: Its slate makes the inkstones Thiên Xu's clerks grind their ink on. A stone from here is said to grind ink without a sound.

places.name: Huyền Vũ Phong
places.look: A dark, heavy peak of black slate above the forests, shaped like a tortoise's shell.
places.lore: It is named for the northern constellation of the Black Warrior. Its qi runs to Water and Metal.

provinces.name: Hàn Mạch
provinces.lore: High mixed country of forest, steppe and red badland in the south-east of Dao Quang. Its people grow buckwheat on the cold upland where wheat will not ripen, and keep goats on the rest. Stone lizards bask on the badland ledges, and children are taught not to climb there.

places.name: Thạch Tích Đài
places.look: A red badland ledge where lizards the size of dogs lie unmoving in the sun, grey as the rock.
places.lore: Stone lizards bite and do not let go, and their skin turns arrows. Their shed skins are used to line armour.

places.name: Hàn Mạch Thôn
places.look: Stone houses among small walled fields of pink-flowering buckwheat on a high forest edge.
places.lore: Its people grow buckwheat where wheat will not ripen and keep goats on the badland slopes. Their buckwheat noodles are sold as far as Thanh Bách.

provinces.name: Thiết Lăng Câu
provinces.lore: Sharp-edged badland ridges and mountain at the southern edge of the region. No one lives here, but turquoise is dug from the copper-stained rock and carried north. The gullies are bitter cold at night and hot by noon.

places.name: Bích Lăng Khoáng
places.look: Shallow pits in copper-stained mountain rock, with sky-blue turquoise chips glittering in the spoil.
places.lore: Turquoise from here is carved into beads and inlays at Bích Khê. The crews keep the best chips in their cheeks until they are paid.

places.name: Hồng Nha Phong
places.look: A lone red rock tooth standing out of the badland gullies, its base worn hollow by the wind.
places.lore: Travellers steer by it across the gullies, and the turquoise crews camp in its shade. Its qi runs to Earth, dry and stubborn, and Earth cultivators who sit in its hollow find their foundation settles slowly but does not crack.

provinces.name: Liệt Thạch Câu
provinces.lore: Mountain and badland where frost has split the rock into fields of broken blocks. It is empty of people and nearly empty of water. Travellers crossing to the heartland follow the cairns and do not leave them.

places.name: Hợp Giác Phong
places.look: Two sharp horns of grey rock rising from one mountain above the split-stone fields.
places.lore: Herders say the horns lean a little closer each century, and that the world ends when they touch. Its qi runs to Metal, split between the two summits, and a cultivator who sits in the gap between them feels pulled two ways at once, a hard test of a steady mind.

provinces.name: Ẩn Lộc Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forested mountain with high grassy clearings on the southern ranges. Deer that leave the park at Lộc Uyển are said to come here to die, and hunters will not shoot in its woods. Herb gatherers come up in summer and sleep in bark huts.

places.name: Lộc Giác Phong
places.look: A forested peak with branching rock ribs at its summit, like a stag's antlers.
places.lore: Hunters will not shoot within sight of it, for the deer of Lộc Uyển are said to climb it to die. Its qi runs to Wood, and herb gatherers find antler moss and deer-horn mushrooms among its rock ribs that alchemists buy for healing pills.

provinces.name: Hải Đê
provinces.lore: Low forest coast, part of it lying below the level of the sea behind an old earth dike. Its people farm and fish behind the dike and keep it in repair together each autumn. Inland, the wind off the sea has bent the pines flat to the ground.

places.name: Phục Tùng Lâm
places.look: Pines bent flat along the ground by the sea wind, their trunks crawling over the dunes.
places.lore: The wind off the northern sea has laid these trees down. Hải Đê's people gather driftwood and pine cones here and nothing else.

places.name: Hải Đê Thôn
places.look: Thatched houses on low ground behind a long grassy earth dike, with fishing boats drawn up on the seaward side.
places.lore: Its fields lie below the level of the sea, and the whole village mends the dike together each autumn. A child born in a storm is called a dike child and is first to carry earth.

provinces.name: Tạo Chu
provinces.lore: Forest coast west of Khai Dương, where the firs grow tall and straight down to a sheltered bay. Its people build boats and ships of fir and sell them along the northern coast. The yards work for Khai Dương's merchants, and every keel is laid facing the dawn.

places.name: Long Cốt Lâm
places.look: Tall, straight hemlock firs on the flat behind the bay, with skid roads cut down to the water.
places.lore: Its hard firs make the keels of Tạo Chu, and its name is the shipwrights' word for a keel. A tree is marked for a keel ten years before it is cut.

places.name: Tạo Chu Trấn
places.look: A walled town on a sheltered bay with ship hulls on slipways along the shore and fir logs seasoning in great stacks.
places.lore: Its yards build fishing boats and coasters of fir for the northern coast and for Khai Dương's merchants. Every keel is laid facing the dawn, as in Khai Dương.

provinces.name: Mật Phong
provinces.lore: Wide forested hills in the west of Dao Quang, with no great river. Its people keep bees in log hives and sell honey and wax as far as Thạch Kiều Thành. A Wood vein lies in the hills, and the bees that forage near it make a honey prized by alchemists.

places.name: Thanh Đằng Mạch
places.look: A hillside wrapped in green vines thick as arms, flowering out of season.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. The vines grow back overnight when cut, and the Mật Phong beekeepers set their hives at its edge.

places.name: Mật Phong Thôn
places.look: A forest village whose walls are lined with hollow-log hives, the air humming all summer.
places.lore: Its people sell honey and wax as far as Thạch Kiều Thành. Bees that forage on the vein above the village make a darker honey that alchemists buy by weight.

provinces.name: Tích Thán
provinces.lore: Forested hills between the western woods and the coast, smoky with charcoal kilns. Its people burn oak and poplar into charcoal for the smiths of Khai Dương and Thanh Bách. They cut in a ring and let each part of the forest grow back for twenty years.

places.name: Ngân Dương Lâm
places.look: Pale-barked poplars on the hillsides, their leaves flashing silver in the wind.
places.lore: Charcoal-burners let this wood grow back between cuttings. Its fast-growing poplar is the cheapest fuel in Dao Quang.

places.name: Tích Thán Thôn
places.look: Smoky clay kilns among the trees, with sacks of charcoal piled by the lane and every face streaked black.
places.lore: Its people burn charcoal for the smiths of Khai Dương and Thanh Bách, cutting the forest in a twenty-year ring.

provinces.name: Cự Môn
provinces.lore: Forest coast backed by the first steep mountains of the east, named for the second of the Dipper's star-lords. Its town ships timber and ore and serves the patrols bound for the high ranges. Above the town stand the empty streets of Hắc Thạch Trấn, a mining town of Phá Quân Môn that was never resettled.

places.name: Hắc Thạch Trấn
places.look: Empty stone houses of dark slate stepped up a bare mountain slope, their doors gone and their hearths cold.
places.lore: Phá Quân Môn's miners built this town in 760. When the rebel sect was destroyed in 874 the town passed to Cửu Cao Phái with the other holdings, but its people had already fled to Cự Môn, and none came back.

places.name: Hải Vụ Mạch
places.look: A forested hollow near the coast where sea fog gathers and lies all day, beading every leaf.
places.lore: Its qi runs to Water. Fishermen of Cự Môn say the fog here never lifts until the tide turns.

places.name: Cự Môn Trấn
places.look: A stone-walled harbour town between the forest and the cliffs, its gate set between two great boulders.
places.lore: Named for the Dipper's second star-lord, it ships timber and red iron and supplies the patrols bound for the high ranges. Its people took in the miners of Hắc Thạch Trấn after 874.

provinces.name: Kình Bối Nhai
provinces.lore: Steep mountains that rise straight out of the northern sea in long humped cliffs. There is no anchorage and no farmland, only seabirds and wind. Fishermen of Cự Môn read the weather by the cloud on its tide-watching peak.

places.name: Quan Triều Phong
places.look: A steep grey peak over the sea cliffs, often capped with a single cloud.
places.lore: Fishermen of Cự Môn read the weather by its cloud: a white cap means fair seas, a grey one a storm by night. Its qi runs to Water, rising and falling with the tide below, and cultivators of Water arts sit on its sea face to time their breathing to the waves.

provinces.name: Cực Băng Nguyên
provinces.gloss: Ice Plain at the World's End
provinces.lore: A flat tongue of glacier at the very top of the continent, pushed into a frozen sea. No one lives here; the ice cracks too often to camp on. Băng Tâm sends novices here for a night alone to see if the cold breaks them.

places.name: Băng Trụ Phong
places.look: A lone pillar of blue ice stands above the flat glacier, streaked white by the wind.
places.lore: Its Water qi is cold and clean, and novices sent to the plain sit at its foot. Those who last the night carve a mark in its base.

provinces.name: Lịch Thanh
provinces.lore: Inland pine forest on low ground, far from the sea. Its people tap the pines for resin, which they boil into pitch and sell for boats and torches. A strong Wood vein lies under the oldest stand of trees.

places.name: Thụ Tâm Mạch
places.look: A vast hollow pine stands in the oldest grove, green light seeping from cracks in its bark.
places.lore: A Wood vein rises through the heart of the old tree. The resin tappers never cut it, and they say its sap heals burns.

places.name: Lịch Thanh Thôn
places.look: Log houses stand in a clearing of scarred pines, the air thick with the smoke of pitch kettles.
places.lore: The villagers tap pines for resin and boil it into pitch. Every pitch kettle in the village is lit from the same fire, which has not gone out since the village was founded.

provinces.name: Băng Khổng
provinces.lore: Fir forest on a cold coast where the sea freezes close to shore every winter. Its fishers set nets under the ice and live on the catch. The ruin of a small abbey stands in the woods inland.

places.name: Mặc Sam Lâm
places.look: Firs so dark they look black stand close together, and little light reaches the snow below them.
places.lore: Băng Khổng cuts its boat timber here. Children are told the ruined abbey's ghosts walk under these trees.

places.name: Tuyết Ẩn Quán
places.look: Three roofless stone halls stand in a forest clearing, with a meditation platform heaped with snow in the middle.
places.lore: A small band of ice hermits founded this abbey in 520. In 690 its last master went into seclusion and never came out; his few disciples went down to the coast, and the abbey fell in.

places.name: Băng Khổng Thôn
places.look: Wooden houses stand on a cold shore lined with racks of nets, and in winter a row of fishing holes runs out across the sea ice.
places.lore: Its fishers set nets under the sea ice and haul them through holes. They learned the craft from Hàn Giang's fishers long ago and still say a word for them before each haul.

provinces.name: Sương Trạch Hoang
provinces.lore: Birch woods, frozen bog and tundra run to a bleak shore. It is empty now; the fur town on its coast was given up when the sable were gone. Hunters cross it in winter when the bogs bear weight.

places.name: Hoa Bì Lâm
places.look: White birches stand in frozen bog, their peeling bark bright against the snow.
places.lore: Hunters cut the bark to roof shelters and make canoes. The wood is the last before the open tundra.

places.name: Điêu Cừu Trấn
places.look: A row of collapsed log warehouses lines an iced-in harbour on the tundra shore, a rusted fur press still standing among them.
places.lore: This fur town grew from 620 on the sable trade of the north coast. By 1065 the sable were trapped out and the harbour iced in each year, and the last families moved south to Hòe Âm.

provinces.name: Hải Báo
provinces.lore: Wind-bent forest on a coast of low rocks where seals haul out. Its people hunt seals for oil, meat and hide, and they sell the oil as lamp fuel as far as Hòe Âm. Some tundra and bog lie behind the village.

places.name: Ngọa Tùng Lâm
places.look: Pines bent flat by the sea wind crawl over the ground, their crowns all pointing inland.
places.lore: The sea wind is so steady here that Hải Báo's hunters steer by the pointing pines when fog hides the shore. Seals drag themselves up under the low branches to give birth, and the village does not hunt inside the wood.

places.name: Hải Báo Thôn
places.look: Low stone houses roofed with turf crowd a rocky shore, seal hides stretched on frames between them.
places.lore: The villagers hunt seals for oil, meat and hide. A seal skull is nailed above every door, and the village takes no more seals than it can eat in a winter.

provinces.name: Côn Bố
provinces.lore: Low coastal forest on ground that sinks below the sea in places. Its people cut kelp from the cold shallows and dry it on racks, eating it and selling it as fodder and medicine. The drowned wood inland floods every spring.

places.name: Trầm Mộc Lâm
places.look: Dead grey trunks stand in still black water below sea level, with living firs on the higher ground around them.
places.lore: The wood floods with snowmelt every spring. Its sunken logs are cut out for timber that never rots.

places.name: Côn Bố Thôn
places.look: Long racks of drying kelp line a low shore, and the houses behind them smell of the sea.
places.lore: The villagers cut kelp from the cold shallows and dry it for food, fodder and medicine. Băng Tâm's alchemists buy the finest blades for cold pills.

provinces.name: Bộc Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest and fog-bound swamp on the west coast. Its people salt and dry cod for the long winter and for Băng Tâm's tax. The mist of the swamp woods is so thick that the village rings a bell at dusk to call its people home.

places.name: Trầm Vụ Lâm
places.look: Firs and swamp pools vanish into a white fog that lies low on the ground and rarely lifts.
places.lore: People who wander from the path here are found days later, if at all. The fishers of Bộc Ngư go in only roped together.

places.name: Bộc Ngư Thôn
places.look: Racks of split cod hang drying along a foggy shore in front of plank houses, and a bell hangs on a post at the village edge.
places.lore: Its people salt and dry cod for the winter and for the tax. The bell is rung at dusk so no one is lost in the swamp fog.

provinces.name: Phiệt Mộc
provinces.lore: Fir forest and swamp along a sheltered shore. Its people fell timber and float it down the coast in great rafts to Hòe Âm and beyond. A great elk lives in the woods behind the village, and loggers cut around its paths.

places.name: Mi Lộc Lâm
places.look: A swampy wood with broad trails trampled through it and young trees stripped of bark at head height.
places.lore: A spirit elk with antlers wide as a cart lives here. Loggers cut around its trails, and when it bellows in autumn they stay out of the wood.

places.name: Phiệt Mộc Thôn
places.look: Great rafts of fir logs lie moored along the shore below a village of loggers' huts.
places.lore: The villagers fell timber and float it down the coast in rafts. A raft master must make the trip to Hòe Âm ten times before he may build his own raft.

provinces.name: Hải Nhai Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A short range drops straight into the eastern sea in cliffs. No one lives here now, but iron is dug where the rock meets the water. A ruined fort on the cliffs once watched for pirates.

places.name: Hải Thiết Khoáng
places.look: Adits open in a rust-red cliff just above the surf, beside the rotted stumps of a wooden chute and landing.
places.lore: Iron ore was once loaded straight onto boats here. The salt wind rusted every tool, and the last miners left saying the iron was rust before it was dug.

places.name: Kình Bối Phong
places.look: A long, smooth grey summit humps over the sea like the back of a surfacing whale.
places.lore: Metal and Water qi meet on its bare rock above the sea. Sailors on the eastern coast steer by it.

places.name: Vọng Triều Bảo
places.look: A broken tower of grey stone stands on a cliff edge above the sea, its seaward wall gone.
places.lore: Băng Tâm built this watch fort around 650 against the pirates of Thôn Hải Môn. After the Pirate Purge of 781 it was not needed, and the garrison was withdrawn in 790; storms have broken it since.

provinces.name: Thanh Hàn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Forested foothills and bare ridges with a clear river running to the sea. Nobody farms it; hunters from Hòe Âm work its slopes. The old pines on its cliffs are said to be older than Băng Tâm.

places.name: Khô Tùng Nhai
places.look: A sheer cliff of pale rock with a single dead pine hanging upside down from a crack near the top.
places.lore: Its Metal qi gathers in the bare rock. Hunters of Hòe Âm say the pine was already dead when Băng Tâm came.

provinces.name: U Nguyệt Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountains over the eastern coast, home to Băng Phách Mạch, the Ice Soul vein. Băng Tâm keeps the land empty except for its vein keepers and a moonstone mine. Ice beasts drawn by the vein's cold roam the passes.

places.name: Băng Phách Mạch
places.look: Below the ice mountains, a round cave mouth opens in a cliff, rimmed with ice so white it glows faintly blue, like the moon seen through mist. Inside, pillars of ice give off a cold light of their own. Frost feathers grow on the rocks for a long way around the entrance.

places.name: Nguyệt Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A small mine on a mountainside above the sea, its spoil heap glittering faintly blue at night.
places.lore: Băng Tâm digs moonstone here, a cold milky stone that holds the qi of Băng Phách Mạch nearby. Miners work in pairs because of the beasts that roam toward the vein.

provinces.name: Tuyết Giác Hoang
provinces.lore: A small cape of glacier ending in a single white hill above the sea. Nothing grows and nothing is mined. Seal hunters use the hill as a sea mark and do not land.

places.name: Bạch Thủ Phong
places.look: A round white hill of ice rises at the tip of the cape like an old man's head.
places.lore: Seal hunters steer by it and call it the old man. Its weak Water qi draws nothing but seabirds.

provinces.name: Tích Tuyết Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains rising from the coast where snow lies deep until midsummer. Cold iron is mined in a single shaft, and the miners winter at Hoàng Oanh. Nothing else lives here but goats.

places.name: Hàn Thiết Khoáng
places.look: A single shaft opens in a snowfield under a timber shed, with frost thick on the ore carts.
places.lore: The iron here takes and keeps cold, and Băng Tâm's smiths use it for sword cores. The miners leave before the first snow.

places.name: Hàn Ưng Phong
places.look: A hooked summit of dark rock juts out over the valley like an eagle's beak.
places.lore: Metal qi gathers in its hard rock. Eagles nest under the hook and attack anyone who climbs near.

provinces.name: Liệt Phong Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High bare mountains where the wind off the sea never stops. A stockade from Hồ Thiên's age lies in the lower pass. No one lives here, and Băng Tâm disciples come only to train in the wind.

places.name: Bão Tuyết Phong
places.look: A high peak whose two arms of rock curve around a deep bowl of snow.
places.lore: Water qi gathers in the snow bowl. Băng Tâm disciples train their sword forms in the wind on its rim.

places.name: Lũng Đầu Trại
places.look: A ring of fallen stone walls stands at the head of a pass, with the burned stumps of timber gates.
places.lore: Hồ Thiên Phái built this stockade around 260 to guard the pass to its coast. After the eruption of 425 buried the school, the garrison went home and never came back.

provinces.name: Hàn Khê
provinces.lore: A river valley of maple and fir between the mountains. Its people fish trout, burn charcoal and grow a little barley on the warm slopes. It is the last farming valley before the high ice.

places.name: Phong Diệp Lâm
places.look: A wood of maples climbs the valley side and turns blood red for a few weeks each autumn.
places.lore: Hàn Khê's charcoal burners work here. The red leaves are said to mark the last warm ground before the ice.

places.name: Hàn Khê Thôn
places.look: Stone houses and barley strips line a fast clear river, with charcoal mounds smoking on the slopes above.
places.lore: Its people fish trout, burn charcoal and grow barley. They send their charcoal down to Hòe Âm and their sons up to the mines.

provinces.name: Thương Sam Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Grey fir forest climbs to bare rock here. Silver is mined at the foot of the ridge. No village stands in it; the miners come from Hàn Khê.

places.name: Ngân Lũ Khoáng
places.look: A small mine at the forest edge, where thin silver veins show like threads in the quarried rock.
places.lore: Miners from Hàn Khê work the silver in summer. The threads are thin, and the mine has never made anyone rich.

places.name: Kiếm Tích Phong
places.look: A thin, sharp ridge of grey rock runs up to a narrow summit like the spine of a blade.
places.lore: Its Metal qi draws Băng Tâm's sword cultivators, who walk the edge as a test of balance.

provinces.name: Băng Hà Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains where slow glaciers grind down into the valleys. A Băng Tâm fort that once guarded the road to Băng Phách Mạch lies broken in the pass. The land is empty.

places.name: Bích Trâm Phong
places.look: A slender spire of green-grey rock rises above a glacier like a hairpin.
places.lore: Metal qi gathers in the spire. Lê Hoa Am's nuns say the first abbess dropped her hairpin from here.

places.name: Thủ Tuyết Bảo
places.look: A square stone fort in a high pass, its gate torn off and long claw marks scored down its walls.
places.lore: Băng Tâm built this fort in 760 to guard the road to Băng Phách Mạch. In 1102 ice beasts drawn by the vein's cold overran it, and the Pavilion did not rebuild.

provinces.name: Ngân Tuyết Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains whose snow shines silver at dusk. An ice-crystal cavern is worked in the lower rock. Only miners and a few Băng Tâm sword cultivators stay here, and only in summer.

places.name: Băng Tinh Quật
places.look: A cave mouth in grey rock opens onto a hall lined with clear rock crystal.
places.lore: Clear crystal is cut here for formation plates. The miners say the crystal is ice that froze so long ago it forgot how to melt.

places.name: Băng Kỳ Phong
places.look: A high peak that trails a long plume of blown snow from its top like a banner.
places.lore: Water qi streams off its summit with the snow. Climbers read the weather from the banner's direction.

provinces.name: Vân Tiêu Lĩnh
provinces.lore: A wall of high mountains rising almost from the western shore to nearly four thousand metres. Tin is mined in the low valleys. No one lives above the clouds.

places.name: Tích Thạch Khoáng
places.look: Small pits and a stream sluice dot a valley floor below the great peak, the gravel black with tinstone.
places.lore: Tin is washed from the stream gravel here. Băng Tâm's smiths mix it into bronze for bells and mirrors.

places.name: Thùy Thiên Phong
places.look: An immense white peak rises nearly four thousand metres from the sea, its top usually lost in cloud.
places.lore: Its Metal and Water qi are strong and cold. Few have climbed it, and none have come down with the same face.

provinces.name: Lam Hỏa Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains with a small volcanic heart, where Hàn Diễm Khẩu breathes cold blue flame through the glacier. Alchemists come for its heat and leave quickly. The ice here is treacherous, and no one lives on it.

places.name: Hàn Diễm Khẩu
places.look: High on the ice mountains, a crack in the glacier breathes out pale blue flames that dance over the snow without melting it. The ice around the vent is glassy and scorched dark at the lip. Downwind, sulphur stains the snow yellow.

provinces.name: Hàn Thạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Bare high mountains in the heart of the range. Silver is mined at the edge of the ice. No one lives here; the cold splits stone in a single night.

places.name: Hàn Ngân Khoáng
places.look: A cluster of stone huts and an adit sit at the foot of a glacier.
places.lore: Silver is mined here at the edge of the ice. Miners say the ore is coldest in summer, when the glacier sweats.

places.name: Kim Quan Phong
places.look: A high peak with a ring of rock towers at its top, which catches the first sun and glows gold.
places.lore: Its Metal qi is strongest at dawn. Băng Tâm's sword cultivators climb to greet the first light on it.

provinces.name: Đoạn Vân Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains where the clouds from the sea break on the summits. A lodestone mine is worked here for compass needles and formation plates. No one stays the winter.

places.name: Từ Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A mine on a bare slope where tools left on the rock creep slowly toward the adit mouth.
places.lore: Lodestone is mined here for compass needles and formation plates. Miners carry no iron underground.

places.name: Huyền Băng Phong
places.look: A high peak sheathed in old dark ice, so dense it looks black.
places.lore: Its Water qi is heavy and old. Ice cultivators cut cores from the black ice for their meditation.

provinces.name: Vĩnh Đống Nguyên
provinces.lore: A broad sheet of ice that climbs from the shore to a lone summit. It has never thawed in living memory, and no one lives on it. Ice cultivators of Băng Tâm walk out here to sit where the Water qi is purest and the wind is worst.

places.name: Phong Tuyết Đỉnh
places.look: A broad ice summit always wrapped in blowing snow, its top seen only on a few still days a year.
places.lore: Băng Tâm's ice cultivators sit here for the pure Water qi of the endless freeze. The wind has taken more than one careless disciple off the top.

provinces.name: Cửu Chuyển Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains around Hồi Lộ Phong and its winding ice stair. No one lives here. Băng Tâm disciples climb the stair roped together, and the ridge is named for its turns.

places.name: Hồi Lộ Phong
places.look: A steep ice peak is wrapped in a switchback stair carved into its flank, the steps doubling back so often that the stair looks like white thread wound around a spindle. Wind-scoured snow fills the turns. From below, climbers on it seem to vanish and reappear at random.

provinces.name: Băng Bích Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Sheer high mountains above the desert side of the range. A gold vein is worked high on the rock, and a pass fort lies buried by snow. No one lives here.

places.name: Hàn Kim Quật
places.look: A cave high on a cliff face, reached by a ladder of iron spikes, with gold showing in the quartz of its walls.
places.lore: Băng Tâm works the gold vein only in high summer. Two miners fell from the ladder in its first year, and their names are cut at its foot.

places.name: Vô Điểu Phong
places.look: A sheer high peak of pale rock where no bird flies and no wind sound carries.
places.lore: Its Metal qi is so strong that birds turn away from it. Sword cultivators come here to sit in its silence.

places.name: Đoạn Tuyết Quan
places.look: Only the top of a gatehouse roof and one watch tower show above a slope of old avalanche snow.
places.lore: Băng Tâm built this fort in 530 to hold the high pass from the desert into the ice mountains. An avalanche buried it with its garrison in the winter of 1012, and it was never dug out.

provinces.name: Vọng Tinh Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains on the border with Thiên Xu's land, looking down on the wild vein Tinh Tủy Mạch. No one lives here, and Băng Tâm has kept its people off the ridge since its claim to the vein was rejected in 1188. An agate cavern is still worked on the near side.

places.name: Mã Não Quật
places.look: A cave mouth in a cliff of banded rock, its floor scattered with chips of red and white agate.
places.lore: Agate is cut here for seals and ornaments. Miners come from Băng Tâm's side only and never cross the ridge.

places.name: Hàn Tinh Phong
places.look: A high peak whose ice glitters like stars on clear nights.
places.lore: Its Metal qi runs toward the vein in the valley below. From the top one can see Tinh Tủy Mạch and the cranes that circle it.

places.name: Khuy Tinh Bảo
places.look: A small stone watch fort on the ridge, its doors sealed with plain wooden bars.
places.lore: Băng Tâm built this watch fort around 1100 to look down on Tinh Tủy Mạch. After its claim to the vein was rejected and Thiên Xu doubled its guard in 1189, the Pavilion withdrew the watchers and barred the doors so as not to look like it was preparing a war.

provinces.name: Băng Giản Câu
provinces.lore: Mountains cut by an icy river that runs down toward the desert, with red rock at their southern foot. Copper is mined in the gully. A beacon fort broken in the Desert Road War still stands on a spur.

places.name: Đồng Lục Quật
places.look: Red and green stained adits open in the gully wall above the icy brook.
places.lore: Copper is mined here where the mountain meets the desert. The ore goes down to the desert towns by camel.

places.name: Túc Nhạn Phong
places.look: A high peak above a southern gully, where migrating geese rest on its snowfields in spring.
places.lore: Its Metal qi gathers in the bare upper rock. Hunters say geese that land here in autumn never fly on.

places.name: Lang Yên Bảo
places.look: A beacon fort on a spur above the gully, its walls glazed black by fire and its beacon tower split.
places.lore: Băng Tâm built this beacon fort in 520 to pass warnings along the caravan road. Phượng Minh's fire broke it in 726, the same year Cô Thành fell.

provinces.name: Bách Nhận Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains falling to the southern sea in great cliffs. No one lives here and no road crosses it. Seabirds nest on its walls in their thousands.

places.name: Ngân Bình Phong
places.look: A long wall of snow-covered summit stands like a silver screen above the southern sea.
places.lore: Its Metal and Water qi meet over the sea cliffs. Seabirds nest on its walls in their thousands.

provinces.name: Chúc Âm Nguyên
provinces.lore: Glacier and black lava fields lie around the cone of Chúc Long Sơn, with a frozen lake and its coiled flood-dragon beyond. Hồ Thiên Phái stood here until the eruption of 425 buried it; since 470 Băng Tâm Các has kept its seat on the ruin, with the Jade Vessel Array laid over the buried vent. Băng Tâm leaves the ruin as it lay and forbids digging, and since the mountain rumbled in 1199 even the ice hunters stay away.

places.name: Chúc Long Sơn
places.look: A black cone rises out of the ice fields, its flanks streaked with old lava under a skin of snow. In its crater a dull red glow shows through a lid of ice, like the half-open eye of something asleep. Steam drifts from cracks around the rim and freezes into feathers of rime.

places.name: Băng Tâm Các
places.look: Băng Tâm Các's white halls climb a black lava mountain on a sheet of blue glacier ice, raised on the ruin of Hồ Thiên Phái, with a great Vessel Hall on the summit and a tall white pagoda behind it. At the mountain's foot the green-tiled tip of one old pagoda roof still stands out of a bare field of black lava, and a ring of jade-green light glows up through the ice.

places.name: Hàn Giao Chử
places.look: Out on a frozen tundra lake, a lone low islet of black rock is ringed by a coiling pressure ridge of ice that wraps around it like a serpent's body. In the thaw the ridge cracks and groans. Bones of deer and wolves lie bleached on the rock.

provinces.name: Hàn Đài Nguyên
provinces.lore: A small spur of ice and moss tundra on the north coast. Reindeer cross it in summer, and a few hunters follow them. In winter it is left to the wind.

places.name: Băng Bích Nhai
places.look: A cliff of grey rock sheathed in a curtain of ice faces the sea.
places.lore: Its Water qi gathers in the ice curtain. Hunters shelter at its foot in summer storms.

provinces.name: Hàn Phong Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat moss tundra along the northern shore, swept by the north wind for most of the year. The only people are hunters who come for fur and walrus ivory in summer. A broken city of Hồ Thiên's age lies on its coast, and a frozen Water vein lies inland.

places.name: Bắc Đình Thành
places.look: Low stone walls trace a square on the tundra shore, half buried in moss, with the stump of a gate tower facing the sea.
places.lore: Hồ Thiên Phái built this fur and ivory city on the northern shore around 260. After the eruption of 425 buried the school, the trade died and the last families left within a few years.

places.name: Đống Thủy Nhãn
places.look: A perfectly round pool in the moss tundra that never fully freezes, its black water steaming faintly in the cold.
places.lore: A Water vein rises here through the frozen ground. Băng Tâm has never built over it, and hunters drink from it only after making an offering.

provinces.name: Khúc Tùng Lâm
provinces.lore: Stunted, wind-twisted pine forest thins out here into open tundra. No village stands in it, because the snow owls of the plain take lambs, dogs and sometimes children. Trappers from Hàn Trạch work its edges in winter.

places.name: Tuyết Hiêu Nguyên
places.look: Open tundra dotted with boulders, each one crowned with white droppings and small bones.
places.lore: Snow owls as big as eagles hunt here, led by a spirit owl that flies by day. Trappers never cross the plain in the open.

provinces.name: Hàn Trạch
provinces.lore: Fir forest broken by wide peat bogs on the edge of the tundra. Its people cut peat for fuel, pick cranberries and trap fur, and they sell all three to the coast. It is the northernmost village that pays Băng Tâm's tax in coin rather than fish.

places.name: Hoàng Tùng Lâm
places.look: A thin wood of larches on wet ground that turns bright gold every autumn and stands bare all winter.
places.lore: Hàn Trạch's trappers set their lines here. Larch wood does not rot, and the village's bog paths are laid with it.

places.name: Hàn Trạch Thôn
places.look: Turf-roofed houses on a dry rise above the bog, with stacks of black peat drying beside every door.
places.lore: The villagers cut peat, pick cranberries and trap fur. They say the bog keeps everything, and now and then they cut out a perfectly kept bone or blade.

provinces.name: Tích Tuyết Nguyên
provinces.lore: Half fir forest and half open tundra, where snow falls on more days than not. No one lives here, but a Wood vein in the forest draws Băng Tâm's herb gatherers in summer. The coast is low and drowned in ice for half the year.

places.name: Tùng Tuyết Mạch
places.look: A ring of tall pines stands green in a land of stunted trees, and snow melts in a circle around them.
places.lore: A Wood vein feeds the ring of pines. Băng Tâm's herb gatherers pick the cold-root that grows only here.

provinces.name: Xích Nham Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Red-rocked mountains between the ice range and the desert. No one lives here now; turquoise is mined in the hills. The burned stockade of Dạ Quang's raider days still stands in a side valley.

places.name: Tùng Thạch Khoáng
places.look: Small pits dot a red hillside, with chips of blue-green stone in the spoil.
places.lore: Turquoise is dug here for ornaments and caravan trade. Desert people say it guards a rider from falling.

places.name: Thạch Kiếm Phong
places.look: A tall blade of red rock stands upright on the ridge.
places.lore: Its Metal qi draws Băng Tâm's sword cultivators. The raiders of Dạ Quang used it as a lookout.

places.name: Huyết Đao Trại
places.look: A burned stockade of red stone and timber in a side valley, its walls blackened and its gate burned out.
places.lore: Dạ Quang's raiders hid their loot here from 975. Băng Tâm burned it in 1121, at the end of the campaign, and Hạng Dạ Bôi knelt soon after.

provinces.name: Hạn Sa Nguyên
provinces.lore: Dry steppe that turns into open dunes in the south. No village stands here; caravans cross it in two days and do not stop. Golden scorpions hunt in the dunes.

places.name: Kim Hạt Cương
places.look: A ridge of yellow dunes pocked with holes, and golden shells glinting in the sand at noon.
places.lore: Spirit scorpions with golden shells hunt here at night. Their poison is sold to alchemists, and the men who catch them rarely live to old age.

provinces.name: Sạn Đạo Lĩnh
provinces.lore: High mountains, badlands and desert cut by the gorge of Viên Đề Hạp and its plank road. No sect holds the road and no one lives here; caravans cross with wax in their ears. Copper-red rock and dry slopes surround the gorge.

places.name: Viên Đề Hạp
places.look: A narrow gorge cuts through the high mountains, its walls hung with vines and its river loud below. A timber plank road pinned to the cliff face runs the length of one wall, and gibbons swing above it, crying on both banks without end. Mist fills the gorge floor at dawn.

provinces.name: Hãn Hải Mạc
provinces.lore: Open desert with a few bare hills and badland ridges. No one lives here but at a boiling spring in the sand, where caravans water their beasts. Băng Tâm keeps a cairn of water jars there for travellers.

places.name: Phí Sa Thang
places.look: Hot water bubbles up through the sand into a shallow pool ringed with white crust.
places.lore: Fire qi rises with the water. Caravans water their camels here after it cools, and Băng Tâm keeps a cairn of water jars beside it.

provinces.name: Lưu Sa Câu
provinces.lore: Desert cut by a thin river whose bed shifts every year. Wild camels graze the river edge, and no one settles here. Caravans follow the river and pay for guides who know where the sand is soft.

places.name: Dã Đà Nguyên
places.look: Flat sand along the river, tracked by broad two-toed hoofprints and dotted with dung.
places.lore: Wild spirit camels graze the river edge, led by a white bull. Caravan breeders try to catch its calves.

provinces.name: Chiên Trướng
provinces.lore: Wide steppe with some desert and badland to the south. Its herders live in felt tents, move with their flocks and make felt for the seat and the caravans. A Fire vein lies in the desert edge.

places.name: Liệt Dương Huyệt
places.look: A bowl of red rock in the desert where the air shimmers even in winter.
places.lore: A Fire vein rises here. Băng Tâm's disciples come to train the ice heart against heat.

places.name: Chiên Trướng Thôn
places.look: A ring of round felt tents on the steppe, with felt drying on frames and flocks grazing all around.
places.lore: The herders move the village twice a year. They make felt for the seat's winter halls and the caravans.

provinces.name: Chử Diêm
provinces.lore: Coastal steppe running down to a salt shore. Its people boil sea water into salt over dung fires and sell it to the caravans and to Hồi Lan. A bitter hot spring rises inland.

places.name: Khổ Thủy Trì
places.look: A warm pool in the steppe, its water cloudy and its edges stained white and yellow.
places.lore: Its water is too bitter to drink, but salt-boilers soak their cracked hands in it. Its Fire qi is weak and its Water qi bitter.

places.name: Chử Diêm Thôn
places.look: Low mud houses on a salt shore, with iron pans steaming over dung fires along the waterline.
places.lore: The villagers boil sea water into salt and sell it to caravans and to Hồi Lan. Every child learns to tend a pan before they can read.

provinces.name: Hàn Tùng Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Pine-covered mountains on the north edge of the desert. Coal is dug here for the seat's forges. The ruin of a small sect that died in the Desert Road War lies in the pines.

places.name: Hắc Môi Khoáng
places.look: Black spoil heaps and a timber headframe stand among pines at the foot of the mountain.
places.lore: Coal is dug here for the forges of the seat. The miners' faces are always black, and they are called the crows.

places.name: Hạc Lập Phong
places.look: A slim grey peak rises alone above the pines like a crane standing on one leg.
places.lore: Its Metal qi is mild and steady. The ruined sect below once held its morning practice here.

places.name: Lãnh Hương Các
places.look: A small ruined pavilion among pines, its roof fallen and a grove of wild plum gone feral around it.
places.lore: A small sect of plum-blossom sword cultivators founded this pavilion in 600. In 724 all its disciples rode to break the siege of Cô Thành and none came back.

provinces.name: Mộc Kiều
provinces.lore: A river valley of forest and steppe below the mountains. Its people log, farm a little and keep the timber bridge on the road from the seat to the coast. Silver foxes live in the woods above.

places.name: Ngân Hồ Lâm
places.look: A forested slope with fox earths between the roots and silver hairs caught on the bark.
places.lore: Silver spirit foxes live here and steal from the village. Mộc Kiều's people leave them a share of grain to keep them from the houses.

places.name: Mộc Kiều Thôn
places.look: Log houses on both banks of a river, joined by a long timber bridge on stone piers.
places.lore: The village keeps the bridge on the road from the seat to the coast, and Băng Tâm pays it in grain. Its loggers fell timber in the hills above.

provinces.name: Ngọc Môn Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Very high mountains, over four and a half thousand metres, at the west end of the desert. White jade is mined at their foot. The old poem of Cô Thành looks toward the jade gate, and caravan drivers say this is it.

places.name: Dương Chi Khoáng
places.look: A mine in a dry stream bed where white stones like congealed fat lie in the gravel.
places.lore: White jade is dug from the stream bed and the cliffs above. Băng Tâm carves its seals from it.

places.name: Tuyết Tôn Phong
places.look: A massive white summit over four and a half thousand metres high, towering above the western desert.
places.lore: Its Metal and Water qi are fierce. Few have reached the top, and Băng Tâm's elders climb it before a breakthrough.

provinces.name: Đà Linh
provinces.lore: Steppe and desert along a river under the mountains, where caravans gather before the long crossing. Camel breeders, harness makers and innkeepers live in its town. A sandstorm-swept Earth vein lies to the west.

places.name: Phong Sa Nhãn
places.look: A ring of standing stones in the desert, where small whirlwinds of sand rise even on still days.
places.lore: An Earth vein lies under the ring. The caravan drivers of Đà Linh say storms are born here.

places.name: Đà Linh Trấn
places.look: A river town of mud-brick inns and camel yards, ringing with camel bells.
places.lore: Caravans gather here before the long crossing. The town makes the bronze bells every caravan camel wears.

provinces.name: Lạc Nhật Nguyên
provinces.lore: Half steppe and half desert along a long river, where the lone smoke of caravan fires rises straight in still air. No one settles here. A Fire vein lies where the sun sets over the river.

places.name: Viên Nhật Huyệt
places.look: A round hollow on the steppe by the river, its red earth glowing as if the setting sun lay in it.
places.lore: A Fire vein rises here. The old caravan song says the long river and the round setting sun meet in this hollow.

provinces.name: Dương Bằng
provinces.lore: Steppe with patches of desert and red badland in the east. Its people herd sheep and goats and sell wool to the seat and to Hồi Lan. An Earth vein lies under a low rise.

places.name: Thạch Tháp Mạch
places.look: A flat slab of yellow rock as big as a courtyard lies on a steppe rise, bare of snow and warm to the touch even on frost nights.
places.lore: An Earth vein rises under the slab and keeps it warm. The shepherds of Dương Bằng bed their ewes on it in the lambing frosts, and Băng Tâm's earth cultivators come to sit on it in summer when the flocks are away.

places.name: Dương Bằng Thôn
places.look: Stone pens and low houses on the steppe, ringed by grazing sheep.
places.lore: The shepherds sell wool to the seat and to Hồi Lan. They count sheep at dusk with a song that no outsider understands.

provinces.name: Tuyết Hải Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Huge mountains with small glaciers rise over the west of the desert. No one lives here. The empty fort of Băng Tâm's first ice keepers stands in a pass.

places.name: Băng Quan Phong
places.look: A huge peak capped with a crown of ice above the desert.
places.lore: Its Water qi gathers in the ice. Băng Tâm's ice cultivators come to sit in its cold.

places.name: Ngưng Băng Bảo
places.look: Low mounds of slumped ice and stone stand in a high pass, the shape of walls still visible.
places.lore: Tần Ngưng Sương's first disciples built this fort of ice blocks in 450 to guard the pass, keeping it frozen with their arts. When she died in 1010 no one renewed the ice, and the walls slumped.

provinces.name: Liệt Thạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains and red badlands split by heat and frost. No one lives here, and the old caravan fort lies under sand. Snakes and scorpions shelter in the cracks.

places.name: Hồng Thạch Phong
places.look: A cracked red peak rises over the badlands, split into great blocks by summer heat and winter frost, with fallen slabs heaped at its foot.
places.lore: Its Earth qi is heavy and dry and gathers in the split rock. Sand vipers shelter in its cracks, and caravan drivers who climb it for a lookout tap every handhold with a stick first.

places.name: Mai Sa Bảo
places.look: Only the top of a watch tower shows above a dune in a mountain pass.
places.lore: Băng Tâm built this caravan fort in 600. The sandstorm of 1050 that buried Mã Minh's wells buried it too, and it was not dug out.

provinces.name: Thiên Bắc Hoang
provinces.lore: Tundra, glacier and bare rock at the northern tip of the frost coast. No one lives here now. A city of Hàn Giang's age lies empty on the shore.

places.name: Cực Quang Phong
places.look: A glacier peak at the top of the frost coast, under green curtains of light on winter nights.
places.lore: Its Water qi is strongest under the aurora. Ice cultivators come here on the longest nights.

places.name: Sóc Phương Thành
places.look: Stone walls and empty houses stand in a rocky bay, with seal-oil vats rusting on the quay.
places.lore: Hàn Giang Môn built this seal-oil city around 340. After the War of the Frost Coast, Băng Tâm moved its people south to Liên Giang in 498 and it was left empty.

provinces.name: Chưng Vụ Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Tundra and hills around the snow-capped cone of Sương Diễm Sơn. No sect holds the mountain, and no one lives on its slopes. Fire and water cultivators both come here, each wary of the other.

places.name: Sương Diễm Sơn
places.look: A broad snow-capped volcanic cone rising alone out of the forest. Down one flank runs a crimson fissure that never freezes, glowing through the snow and trailing a thin plume of steam.

provinces.name: Bích Thạch Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Mountains with a small volcanic heart where Noãn Ngọc Tuyền steams. Băng Tâm's disciples come to warm their meridians. Warm green stone is quarried here.

places.name: Noãn Ngọc Tuyền
places.look: High in the snowy mountains, a chain of steaming pools spills down a rocky slope. The stones around them are a pale jade green and warm to the touch, and snow never settles on them.

places.name: Noãn Thạch Khoáng
places.look: A quarry of jade-green stone on a snowy slope, where snow melts as it touches the cut faces.
places.lore: Băng Tâm quarries warm stone here to floor its cave abodes. The stone is the same as at Noãn Ngọc Tuyền nearby.

provinces.name: Tàn Tuyết Nguyên
provinces.lore: Tundra, hills and forest where snow lingers into summer. No one lives here since the city on its coast was abandoned in 655. Broken ice cliffs face the sea.

places.name: Đoạn Băng Nhai
places.look: A cliff of grey rock capped with old ice rises over the tundra, split by cracks wide enough to walk into.
places.lore: Its Water qi gathers in the cracks of the old ice. Every thaw great blocks break off and roll onto the plain, and hunters camp well away from its foot.

places.name: Lẫm Đông Thành
places.look: Empty stone streets on a tundra shore, with the ribs of crushed ships frozen in the harbour.
places.lore: This port city was founded around 420. In the winter of 655 the sea froze to the horizon and crushed its ships in the harbour, and its people moved to Mộc Lan.

provinces.name: Ngân Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest and swamp on the north coast. Its people net silver ice-fish in winter and sell them in Mộc Lan. The ruin of the Gate of Ice and Fire lies inland.

places.name: Thùy Băng Lâm
places.look: Firs hung with icicles from every branch, tinkling in the wind.
places.lore: The icicles stay until late spring. Ngân Ngư's children are told not to shout here.

places.name: Băng Hỏa Môn
places.look: A ruined sect in the forest, half its halls burned and half split by frost.
places.lore: A small sect founded in 710 to cultivate both the fire and frost of Sương Diễm Sơn. Its fire and water disciples quarrelled until the sect split and burned itself out in 980.

places.name: Ngân Ngư Thôn
places.look: Plank houses on the shore, with silver ice-fish drying on racks.
places.lore: The villagers net ice-fish under the winter ice and sell them in Mộc Lan. They learned the craft from Hàn Giang's fishers.

provinces.name: Mộc Thán
provinces.lore: Inland forest far from the sea. Its people burn charcoal for the coast cities and the forges. Old Korean pines stand in the deep woods.

places.name: Quả Tùng Lâm
places.look: Tall red-barked pines stand in deep snow, pine cones as big as fists on the ground.
places.lore: The charcoal burners do not cut these pines. Squirrels and bears feed on their nuts.

places.name: Mộc Thán Thôn
places.look: Log houses in a forest clearing, surrounded by smoking charcoal kilns.
places.lore: The villagers burn charcoal for the coast cities and the forges. Their faces and houses are black with soot.

provinces.name: Bì Thuyền
provinces.lore: Forest around Vô Tung Lâm running to the sea. Its people build hide boats and hunt seals along the coast. A logging town swallowed by the forest lies inland.

places.name: Vô Tung Lâm
places.look: A dark, rolling forest of spruce and fir under deep snow, its crowns bowed white. Through it runs a frozen stream like a white ribbon, and not one track crosses it or the snow on either bank.

places.name: Mê Tung Trấn
places.look: Collapsed log houses in the forest, young firs growing through their roofs.
places.lore: Loggers built this town in 560 at the edge of Vô Tung Lâm. Too many of its people were lost in the forest, and by 1012 the last families had moved to Tiều Lộ.

places.name: Bì Thuyền Thôn
places.look: Hide boats lie upturned on the shore in front of log houses.
places.lore: The villagers build hide boats and hunt seals along the coast. Trạc Anh's sea hunters buy their boats.

provinces.name: Ám Sam Lĩnh
provinces.lore: Fir forest, bare hills and tundra on the west coast. No one lives here. Snow leopards hunt from its cliffs.

places.name: Tuyết Báo Nhai
places.look: A cliff of grey rock above the fir forest, with paw prints in the snow on its ledges.
places.lore: Snow leopards den on the ledges and hunt deer in the forest below. Their pelts fetch a high price in Mộc Lan.

provinces.name: Lãnh Ngạn
provinces.lore: Forest on the west coast where sea fog rolls in. Its people gather mussels and seabird eggs from the cliffs. Fog-bound woods lie behind the village.

places.name: Hải Vụ Lâm
places.look: Firs hung with grey moss stand in a sea fog that rarely lifts.
places.lore: The moss is gathered for bedding and wound dressing. The fog makes the wood easy to get lost in.

places.name: Lãnh Ngạn Thôn
places.look: Stone houses on a foggy shore under cliffs white with seabirds.
places.lore: The villagers gather mussels from the shore and seabird eggs from the cliffs. They climb on ropes of twisted hide.

provinces.name: Tuyết Đăng
provinces.lore: Forest and swamp on the north-east coast around a timber town. Its people ship logs and furs down the coast. Wild plums bloom in the woods in late winter.

places.name: Lạp Mai Lâm
places.look: Wild plums bloom white among the firs in late winter.
places.lore: Tuyết Đăng's people come to see the plums when the snow is still deep. The fruit is made into sour wine.

places.name: Tuyết Đăng Trấn
places.look: A timber town on the north-east coast, with snow lanterns lit along its quay on winter nights.
places.lore: The town ships logs and furs down the coast. Each winter its people carve lanterns from snow to guide boats home.

provinces.name: Vọng Phàm
provinces.lore: Forest, tundra and hills on the west coast. Its people fish and watch for sails from the cliffs. A town abandoned after Sương Diễm Sơn's week of fire lies on the coast.

places.name: Tuyết Điêu Lĩnh
places.look: A ridge above the forest with huge nests on its crags.
places.lore: Snow eagles nest here and take lambs and seals. Vọng Phàm's people keep their children indoors when the eagles fly low.

places.name: Hắc Ngạn Trấn
places.look: Empty stone houses on a shore of black ash, their wells filled with grey silt.
places.lore: This fishing town was founded in 505. When Sương Diễm Sơn breathed fire for a week in 700, ash fell on it and its wells went bitter, and its people left.

places.name: Vọng Phàm Thôn
places.look: Stone houses on the west coast, with a lookout platform on the cliff above.
places.lore: The villagers fish and watch for sails from the cliff. They light a fire on the platform to guide boats home.

provinces.name: Vô Thụ Nguyên
provinces.lore: Flat tundra on the north-east coast without a single tree. Reindeer herders cross it in summer. A Water vein lies in its centre.

places.name: Bắc Minh Nhãn
places.look: A deep round pool in the tundra, its black water never freezing.
places.lore: A Water vein rises from the deep. Reindeer herders avoid it, saying it has no bottom.

provinces.name: Thái Cô
provinces.lore: Inland forest with low wet hollows. Its people gather wood-ear fungus and mushrooms and sell them dried. A Wood vein lies in the forest.

places.name: Xuân Manh Huyệt
places.look: A hollow in the forest where green shoots push up through the snow even in midwinter.
places.lore: A Wood vein rises under the hollow and keeps the ground soft through the winter. The mushroom pickers of Thái Cô cut its shoots for medicine and sell them to Băng Tâm's alchemists in spring.

places.name: Thái Cô Thôn
places.look: Log houses in the forest, with strings of dried fungus hanging from the eaves.
places.lore: The villagers gather wood-ear fungus and mushrooms and sell them dried. They know every rotting log in the forest.

provinces.name: Triều Bình
provinces.lore: Forest on a sheltered east coast where the tide runs gently. Its people fish and farm a little barley. A silted-up harbour town lies on the shore.

places.name: Chiết Liễu Phố
places.look: Rotting piers in a silted bay, with empty warehouses behind them.
places.lore: This harbour town was founded in 650, and travellers broke willow twigs here in farewell. Its harbour silted up and the ships went to Liên Giang, and by 1140 it was empty.

places.name: Sam Âm Mạch
places.look: A stand of tall firs behind the shore where the ground under the trees stays green with moss while snow lies all around.
places.lore: A Wood vein lies under the firs. Băng Tâm's herb gatherers pick a cold green moss here that stops bleeding, and Triều Bình's people will not cut a single tree in the stand.

places.name: Triều Bình Thôn
places.look: Wooden houses on a sheltered shore, with barley strips behind them.
places.lore: The villagers fish and farm a little barley. The gentle tide here lets them fish all year.

provinces.name: Lư Ngư
provinces.lore: Forest on the east coast between Liên Giang and Tuyết Đăng. Its people fish for perch in the river mouths and sell them in Liên Giang. Cold green woods lie inland.

places.name: Hàn Lục Lâm
places.look: A dense fir forest on the slopes above the coast that stays dark green under the snow.
places.lore: Lư Ngư's people cut straight firs here for boat keels and masts. Red deer winter in its shelter, and the village takes only what it needs for the year's boats.

places.name: Lư Ngư Thôn
places.look: Plank houses on the east coast, with perch drying on racks.
places.lore: The villagers fish for perch in the river mouths and sell them in Liên Giang. Perch soup is their pride.

provinces.name: Tàng Sâm
